dpe deb 'di ma dpe ngos 'dzin kha gsal thog bskyar du dpar bskrun gnang na dgag bya med/ bod kyi gtsug lag gces btus pod phreng / 28 gso ba rig pa'i khog 'bugs baiDUR+ya'i me long / mdzad pa po/ sde srid sangs rgyas rgya mtsho/ (1653-1705) brjod bya/ bod kyi gso ba rig pa dang 'brel ba'i lo rgyus/ bod kyi gtsug lag zhib dpyod khang nas phyogs dang dpar bskrun zhus/ spyi lo 2008_lor ldi lir dpar thengs dang po bskrun/

dpal ldan gso ba rig pa'i khog 'bugs legs bshad baiDUR+ya'i me long drang srong dgyes pa'i dga' ston/
Mirror of Beryl: A WELL-EXPLAINED HISTORY OF THE GLORIOUS SCIENCE OF MEDICINE, A FEAST TO DELIGHT THE RISHIS
sde srid sangs rgyas rgya mtsho/
Desi Sangyé Gyatso
Introduction
shis brjod phyag
1. Homage and Verses of Auspiciousness[30]

d.div: [30] The first object of veneration in these verses is the Fifth Dalai Lama, mentor and father figure to the author. This is followed by homage to Śākyamuni Buddha in his aspect of Medicine Buddha. The other figures are the five rishis, in particular Vidyājñāna and Manasija, speaker and requestor of the tantra, respectively; the Buddhist and non-Buddhist audience of the original teaching of Four Tantras; Jivaka, the famous physician at the time of the Buddha; Nāgārjuna, as a writer of medical texts; the Indian master Śūra, identified as the author of the renowned Treatise of the Eight Branches; his grandson Candranandana; Padmasambhava, the tantric adept who visited Tibet; Tsongkhapa, the great scholar practitioner; Vairocana the translator; his contemporary King Trisong Detsen; and Muné Tsenpo, the king’s son. For identifications of the remaining figures, see corresponding notes.

!_sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i bdag nyid ye shes khyab 'jug lte ba'i 'dab brgyar mngon rdzogs byang chub dus gsum kun mkhyen pad+ma'i rigs gyur de bzhin gshegs pa lha yi lhas/ / mtshan dpe'i 'od zer 'jig rten kun tu 'phags pa'i mod la mchog gi go 'phang snang ba'i sgo 'byed dpal brtsegs rgyal po snyigs ma lnga yi gdung bas nyer gtses lus can khams/ / spyi dang khyad par gangs can 'gro ba'i phan bde'i byed por brtse bas ngur smrig gar rol sdom brtson rgyal po'i tshul bstan rtsa ba'i bla ma ngag dbang blo bzang rgya mtsho'i zhabs/ / bsams bzhin bstan 'gro'i don du slar yang lhas gnang smyos kyi rigs phebs drug pa chen pos 'dis mtshon skye bar gong mas zhal bzhes bzhin du rjes bzungs srid zhi'i dge legs stsol/ /[*]

Of the nature of every buddha, an exalted gnosis all-pervading, on the hundred-petal lotus of the navel, in complete and perfect enlightenment, omniscient of past, present, and future, of the lotus family, tathāgata, god of gods, light from your enlightened features arises everywhere in all worlds, immediately opening the gates to shine on the supreme level, great king of glory upon glory[31] for the realms of sentient beings in general, tormented by the five degenerations, and specifically for those of the snowy land of Tibet, you are the creator of all happiness and welfare. With great compassion you perform the dance of the red-robes, a vow-holding monk and king, my root guru, Ngawang Losang Gyatso, deliberately come again for the doctrine and sentient beings, Great Sixth born of the celestially descended Nyöpa lineage, in this life, as promised by your previous incarnation, care for us and grant us all the happiness of samsara and nirvana.
[*] (shis pa brjod pa'i rim pa tshangs pa'i sngon byung gi gtam dang sbyar ba'i sbyar gzugs sogs kyi rab spel/)
[31] Words in bold are the name of the Great Fifth immortalized as the buddha Rasmi Samudgata Śrīku Rāja (’Od zer kun nas ’phag pa dpal brtsegs kyi rgyal po).

thugs bskyed smon lam dag pa'i mkha' la spangs dang rtogs pa'i ye shes 'od kyi cha shas yongs gang rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rgyu skar dbus/ / lnga bdor nag po'i dus kyi mtshan lhung 'gro kun la 'jug thugs rje'i zla ba bde gshegs gzhan las ches dkar nya ba mched brgyad gtso/ / drug cur grol ba'i dpal gyi mgur nas ma rig nad la sman gyi mdo sde brgyad brgya pa [*]dang sprul pa'i grong khyer yon tan gyi/ / lta na sdug tu lha dang drang srong phyi nang 'khor la bden don gso rig yan lag brgyad gsungs sman gyi bla mas shis par mdzod/ /[**]

Amid the stars of fully enlightened and perfect buddhas, the light of your exalted wisdom of insight and abandonment, which fill the skies of pure bodhi-mind prayers reaching all beings fallen into the night of the five dark degenerations, your full moon of compassion brighter than that of other tathāgatas, supreme among the eight medicine buddhas, from the glorious throat of Ṣaṣṭimukti you taught the medical sutras in eight hundred verses, medicine for the disease of ignorance, and in the manifested place of Sudarśana,[32] a city of qualities beautiful to behold, you taught the gods, rishis, insiders, and outsiders the truths of the eight branches of medical science. Guru of medicine, grant all auspiciousness.
[*] (sman bla dang ston pa nges don ltar gcig tu bsgrubs pa )
[**] (bya ba brjod pa dang ldan gzugs 'dres pa/)
[32] Lta na sdug. Sudarśana or Dṛśākāñkṣya.

gang gi sku yi gsang ba'i gnas lngar rnam par mi rtog dbyings las skyes pa'i ye shes lnga mtshon dag pa'i rang gdangs las/[1] / chu zla'i gzugs bzhin so sor shar ba'i don dam bden pa rig pa'i ye shes ngo bo mched bzhi gsung gi sprul pa'i sku/ / yid las skyes te sprul pa'i zol gyis rgyal ba'i 'phrin las ril bas lag brel [2]gzhan phan tshangs skud 'chang ba'i drang srong lngas/ / tshe ring chos nor bde ba 'dod pa'i yid can zhing kun gso dpyad rig pa bdud rtsi'i char gyis rtag tu rlan par mdzod/ /[*]

From the pure innate tones representing the five types of gnosis, which are born from the nonconceptual realm found at the five secret places of his body, the five rishis appear individually, like separate water reflections of the moon. Vidyājñāna, gnosis perceiving ultimate truth and in essence the four brothers; and Manasija, born from the mind, the manifestation of enlightened speech; by the illusion of manifestation you are companions carrying out the Conqueror’s deeds, of benefit to others, wearers of the brahman thread, you five great rishis,[33] drench all realms and all living beings who seek long life, Dharma, wealth, and happiness with the rains of the ambrosia of medical science.

[1] mdangs/ mtsho sngon deb dpar/ 'dir nga tshos ma dpe dang dpar ma bsdur zhib zhu yul ni mtsho sngon zhing chen bod kyi gso rig zhib 'jug khang nas phyogs bsgrigs mdzad pa'i bod kyi gso ba rig pa'i gna' dpe phyogs bsgrigs dpe tshogs pod phreng brgyad pa de yin la/ 'dir de'i bsdus ming du mtsho sngon deb dpar zhes bris yod/
[2] ri bo'i lag sbrel/ mtsho sngon deb dpar/
[*] (dpe gzugs nges bstan sogs kyi rab spel/)
[33] The five rishis are seen as manifestations of the five wisdoms of an enlightened being. See p. 86.

rgyal bas byin rlabs tshe yi rig pa mchog dran gdong bzhi skye dgu'i bdag dang tha skar bu sogs lha rnams dang / / mi na gnas shing ring por 'tsho dang na ba gso ba'i thabs kyi gzhung lugs rgyun shes bu sogs drang srong brgyad/ / 'jig rten kun bskyed mes po [*]tshangs sogs phyi rol pa dang cher snyigs 'gro la phan pa'i lam ston 'jam dpal dang / / spyan ras gzigs sogs nang pa'i 'khor bcas zhu gsol 'dus pas lus can shing rtar phan bde'i khur gyis lci ba stsol/ /[**]

Four-faced Caturmukha[34] blessed by the Buddha to recall the supreme Āyurveda, Prajāpati, Aśvinīputra, and other gods, the eight rishis,[35] Ātreya and so forth, of the scriptural traditions of methods of maintaining good health, of living long and of curing disease; outsiders such as Brahmā, patriarch and creator of all worlds, the insider entourage of Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and others, who show the path to sentient beings in these degenerate times, all present as requestors of the teachings; let the carriage of sentient beings be heavy with the load of happiness.
[*] (tshangs pa la rigs bzhi las )
[**] (yan lag gsum gzugs/)
[34] Epithet of Brahmā.
[35] The eight, or seven, rishis are well known in ancient Indian literature, where they are held to be the originators of the brahman caste. Their names vary according to tradition. See p. 103.

mi yi theg pa'i rtse mor mtho ba'i yon tan 'byor pas lus 'phags rigs las yul dbus ma ga d+ha'i/ / rgyal po dge ba'i gzugs can snying po'i zur khyim btsun mo'i sras 'khrungs sngon gyi skye bar sbyangs shugs kyis/ / bag chags sad pas tshe yi rig byed bslab par zhus te gso ba'i gnas kun mthar son phu bo yis/ / bu bzhin bskyed pas gzhon nus gsos zhes sman pa'i mchog gyur des kyang sa gsum dge ba'i shis pa stsol//[*]

Born into the Videhan race, named because of their lofty qualities found at the very pinnacle of the human race,[36] the son of the householder queen of Bimbisāra, king of Magadha. His instincts, by the power of training in former lives, brought him to seek out and study the Āyurveda, and perfect every branch of medical science. He was known as Kumāra Bhṛtya,[37] raised like a son by his elder brother to become the greatest of physicians. Grant us happiness and virtue in the three worlds.
[*] (rang bzhin brjod la chos dpes mdzes pa/)
[36] Videha (lus ’phags) literally means “superior body.”

[37] Literally, “raised by Kumāra”; Kumāra here refers to King Bimbisāra’s other son, Kumāra Abhaya, who raised his younger stepbrother, Jivaka, who is the object of homage here. The story is told later in the section on the life of this famous physician.

lho phyogs bai ta'i yul grur sku bltams mdo sngags gsar rnying don gyi rin chen 'byung gnas che/ / srid zhi'i gdung 'phrog rab zhi spros bral zag med bdud rtsi'i snying por yongs smin dam pa'i chos/ / spyi dang 'gro kun gso dpyad tshul la'ang baiDUR+ya'i 'od rgyal ba mchog bzhin bka' drin can/ /[*] sangs rgyas lung bstan zab mo'i lam brnyes klu sgrub zhabs kyis 'chi med tshe yi mchog byin zhig /[**]

Born in the southern region of Veta, a great and precious source for the understanding of sutras and tantras, old and new, his Dharma is peace, free of fabrication, destroying the torments of samsara and nirvana, ripening fully as uncontaminated ambrosia essence, and in his practice of medicine for all living beings, he is as kind as the supreme buddha of beryl light. Prophesied by the Buddha, master of the profound path, Nāgārjuna, grant us the great ambrosia of immortality.
[*] (lang gshegs dang 'jam dpal rtsa rgyud/)
[**] (chos dpe dang gzugs can lhan cig pa'i dpe gzugs/)

[*] nub phyogs tshangs spyod bram ze'i sman pa dge 'dun gsang ba'i sras 'khrungs dbang phyug gi / rten la sngon dad smon lam dus smin thog mar phyi rol gzhung smra grub pa'i mtha'/ / bden 'dzin lag lto 'phags pa lhas btul rgyal [**]gsung mthong bas las 'bras yid ches slar/ / nang par zhugs pa'i 'phags yul mkhas mchog dpa' bos tshe yi rig byed spobs pa stsol/ /[***]

Born in the west, son of the purely practicing brahman doctor Saṃghagupta, the ripening of previous faith and prayer at a shrine of Īśvara meant that he first became learned and practiced in outsider doctrine. Finally, his wrong views of true existence conquered by Āryadeva, he saw the words of the Buddha, found faith in cause and effect, and became a follower of the Buddha and a great scholar of India. Śūra, grant us confidence in Āyurveda.
[*] (shar dang lho sogs bzhed pa mang ste yang dag par/)
[**] (dran nye sogs )
[***] (rang bzhin brjod las mtshan nyid kyi sgo nas spyir bstan pa/)

gang gi rigs brgyud dag pa'i yang tsha 'gro la chags pa mngon dga'i sras/ / dam pa'i zla ba thugs bskyed yar ngor mngon dga'i bar du dpa' bo'i legs bshad skyes/ / gzhan don yan lag 'dab ma brgyad pa'i snying por 'dzum pa'i kun+da_'i mdzod/ / yang dag gsal byed zla zer la sogs gso rig rgyas mdzad rnams kyis skyongs/ /[*]

Great grandson[38] in the pure lineage of the above, son of Kāmānandana, in the sacred moon of his waxing mind of enlightenement, the gift of the well-written teachings of Śūra sent as far as Abhirati.[39] His moonlight perfectly illuminating the jasmine treasury, the smile at the very essence of the eight lotus-petal branch of working for the welfare of others. May we be nourished by these beings, who spread far and wide the science of medicine.
[*] (rigs rgyu/)
[38] Yang tsha. But see later section on Candranandana, where he is said to be Śūra’s grandson.

[39] The verse is homage to the physician Candranandana, whose name and most-renowned work is woven into the lines. Moon is “Candra,” and Abhirati, which possibly refers to Akṣobhya’s western buddha realm, can also be written as “Nandana.” His work is Moonlight: A Commentary on the Essence of Eight Branches.

snang mtha'i rang gzugs mchog gi pad+ma'i ze 'brur brdzus bltams shing / / 'gro srog 'tsho ba rdo rjer byed pa tshe rig tsam min par/ / 'phrin las chu bzhi'i rtsa lag sangs rgyas gnyis pa ma dros mtsho/ / bka' drin yangs pa'i gting mtha' mi mngon pad+ma ka ras srungs/ /[*]

Your own form that of Amitābha, born magically within a supreme lotus, making the lives and health of others as strong as vajras, not only through the medical science of Āyurveda but also with the source of the four rivers of enlightened deeds. Second Buddha, your Manasarovar lake of vast kindness is of a depth hard to fathom; watch over us Padmākara.
[*] (ldan pa'i cha shas gzugs can/)

rgyal kun yab rje zur phud lnga pa bsams bzhin du/ / 'gro kun rgyud la tshul khrims slob pa'i ngur smrig gar/ / mkhas btsun bzang por zlos pas rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi/ / bstan pa'i bdag po blo bzang grags pa spyi bos mchod/ /[*]

Master and father of every buddha, hair tied in five places, deliberately come to and perform the dance of the robed monk with wisdom, discipline, and goodness to plant the code of morality within the minds of all beings. Master of the doctrine of the perfect Buddha, Losang Drakpa, I bow to you with the crown of my head.
[*] (bsam pa rgya che ba'i rgyan/)
rnam par snang mdzad ye shes 'og min nas/ / sprul ba'i nyi ma srid na lo tsA bar/ / grags kyang gnas lnga'i don gzigs paN+Dita/ / thub bstan gsal mdzad bai ro tsa nar dad/ /[*]

Sun manifested from the gnosis of Vairocana in Akaniṣṭha, known in the world as a translator but in reality a pandit master of the five sciences, I bow to Vairocana, illuminator of the Buddha’s doctrine.
[*] (ldan pa'i yan lag gnyis gzugs/)
bde gshegs 'jig rten rnam 'dren rgyal ba'i tog / 'od zer kun 'phags dpa' brtsegs rgyal po nyid/ / bsams bzhin gangs can 'gro skyong rgyal po'i tshul/ / tshangs pa lha yi me tog phyag gi gnas/ /[*]

Sugata, guide of the world, crown of the conquerors, Rasmi Samudgata Śrīku Rāja in the form of a king, deliberately come to protect the people of Tibet, object of homage, flower of the god Brahmā.[40]
[*] (bsam pa rgya che ba'i rgyan/)

[40] “Flower of the god Brahmā” is an epithet of King Trisong Detsen, who is said to be an earlier incarnation of the Great Fifth Dalai Lama, who in turn is said to be a manifestation of the buddha Rasmi Samudgata Śrīku Rāja.
nges don bde gshegs dri med rgyal mtshan cher/ / gyur kyang drang don rgyal sras slob pa'i tshul/ / yongs bzung 'gro ba'i don mdzad pur rgyal rje/ / lhag bsam dge ba mu ne btsan por 'dud/ /[*]
In reality the sugata Vimaladhvaja, provisionally a bodhisattva on the path, working for the welfare of beings, lord of Purgyal, of an exceptional and virtuous mind, I bow to you, Muné Tsenpo.[41]
[*] (bsam pa rgya che ba'i rgyan/)
[41] Ninth-century son of King Trisong Detsen. Purgyal, the “the kingdom of Pu,” is an ancient name for Tibet.
zab gter chos dkar sbrang rtsir 'dzag pa'i ro/ / 'chi med bcud du ring ba'i pad+ma'i sgo/ / 'byed la mkhas khyod bai ro'i yang srid nyid/ / nges rnyed grwa mngon dbang phyug bstan 'gro'i gnyen/ /[*]

Skilled in opening the lotus gates to profound treasures that remained a long time in the ambrosia of immortality, their taste dripping into the honey of virtuous Dharma, you were the incarnation of Vairocana, discoverer of certainty, Drapa Ngönshé Wangchuk,[42] friend to the teachings and to living beings.
[*] (yan lag gsum gzugs/)
[42] Treasure revealer who unearthed Four Tantras; his biography appears later in the text.
gangs can yul dus dang 'tshams rgyud kyi bzhin/ / gsal ba'i zhu chen byi dor mdzad pa po/ / rigs 'dus sman pa'i rgyal po g.yu thog pa/ / yon tan mgon por gus pas cis mi 'dud/ /[*]

Great redactor who cleaned the face of the tantra according to the time and place in Tibet, king of physicians, Yuthok Yönten Gönpo, in whom all tathāgata lineages are gathered, I bow to you with reverence.
[*] (rdzas brjod par gsal/)
'jig rten dbang phyug 'gro na snying rje yis/ / gzhan dbang dag pa'i skye bar bzlos [3]pa'i gar/ / gsum ston [4]tshe dang ye shes mchog gi gzungs/ / grub pa'i dam pa de yang phyag gi yul/ /[*]

Lokeśvara, revealing three times a dance in a pure birth under the control of compassion, a holy being fully accomplished in the supreme meditative retention of life and gnosis, you too are a venerable object of homage.[43]
[3] zlos/ mtsho sngon deb dpar/
[4] sum ston/ mtsho sngon deb dpar/
[*] (bsam pa rgya che ba'i rgyan/)

[43] This homage to Sumtön Yeshé Sung, a disciple of Yuthok, includes a play on his name: Sumtön (“revealing three,” although Sum [sum] is a place name rather than the number three [gsum], and this phrase technically translates as “teacher from Sum”) Yeshé (“gnosis”) Sung (“meditative retention”).
chos rgyal me yi ag tshom can gyi gros/ / gsang tshig mdun na 'don pa'i blon po dang / / bla yi sman pa'i brgyud 'khrungs brang ti pa/ / dpal ldan 'tsho byed 'tsho ba'i bdag por 'dud/ /[*]

Of the lineage of a minister who recited secret words with Dharma king Aktsom Chen,[44] and from a family of royal physicians, Palden Tsojé of the Drangti line, master of healing, I prostrate before you.
[*] (rang bzhin brjod pa/)
[44] Refers to minister Drangti Gyalnyé Kharpuk, reputed to be royal physician and minister to Dharma king Tridé Tsukten Mé Aktsom, seventh-century father of Songtsen Gampo.
stong khun mi nyag brgyud 'khrungs shes bya'i gnas/ / spyi dang tshe rig 'gro kun phan bde'i srog / gso ba'i bka' drin sman pa'i rgyal po dngos/ / byang bdag rnam rgyal grags pa bzang por 'dud/ /[*]

Born into the Tongkhün[45] race from Minyak, who with his vast knowledge in general and of medicine in particular was of great kindness in restoring the welfare and happiness of all beings, truly a king of physicians, I bow to you, Jangdak Namgyal Drakpa Sangpo.[46]
[*] (phul byung gi rgyan/)
[45] The Tangut tribe; see note 583 about him below.
[46] Jangdak Namgyal Drakpa Sangpo (1395–1475) is the founder of the Tibetan Jang medical tradition.
bod yul dge ba chos kyi rgyal po'i rigs/ / skyabs gsum mchog 'dzin dge bsnyen sha dang chang / / dug bzhin yongs spangs gso rig 'dab brgya'i gnyen/ / byang pa 'tsho byed mi yi nyi mar 'dud/ /[*]

Of the lineage of the great Tibetan Dharma kings, Holding the three great refuges as supreme, a layman who avoided meat and alcohol like poison, sun-like friend to the hundred-petal lotus of medical science, Jangpa physician, Minyima, to you I bow.[47]
[*] (dpe gzugs/)
[47] Minyima Thongwa Dönden, a disciple of Jangdak Namgyal Drakpa Sangpo. Minyima (mi’i nyi ma) means “the sun of humanity.”
lha mi'i chos srid khri srong lde btsan gyis/ / gnya' bar bkur bas gnang rigs bla'i sman pa/ / chos bzang nas bzung rdo rje'i mtshan can bar/ / sman ngo lag len brgyud par cis mi dad/ /[*]

Trisong Detsen having taken upon his shoulders worldly affairs and the Dharma of men and gods, Chösang was a master physician by royal appointment. From this physician on down to the one named Dorjé: how could one not have faith in this lineage of practice and the discovery of medicines?[48]
[*] (baid r+b+ha'i mdzes pa gtam la sbyar ba/)

[48] This is homage to the Nya family lineage. Nya (gnya’) here means “shoulder,” hence the play on words. The first in the Nya family medical line was Nyapa Chösang, one of the nine wise physicians of Tibet, who are briefly identified later in the text. According to Trinlé (p. 68), the family name Nya was given to Chösang’s father by locals who said that because of his great love for others, he should be carried on the shoulders of all. The Dorjé is Lhünding Namgyal Dorjé, a seventeenth-century contemporary of the author.
yon tan mgon po zhal gzigs zur mkhar ba/ / bdag gzhan mnyam nyid tshe yi rdo rje nas/ / chos bum 'jo mdzad gter bdag gling pa'i bar/ / rgyab rten lung brgyud bla ma'i tshogs la'ang 'dud/ /[*]

Blessed with a vision of Yönten Gönpo, coming from the region of Surkar, holding self and others as equal, well possessed of the vajra of life,[49] I bow to the lamas of the support transmission up to Terdak Lingpa, who drank to satisfaction from the vase of Dharma.
[*] (bsam pa rgya che ba dang bsdus gzugs/)

[49] Surkhar Nyamnyi (“equal”) Dorjé (“vajra”) (1439–75) is the founder of the Sur medical tradition. Terdak Lingpa Gyurmé Dorjé (1646–1714) was a teacher and student of the Fifth Dalai Lama. A Nyingma treasure revealer, he founded Mindröling Monastery in 1670.
nyi ma'i gnyen dang pad+ma ka ra yis/ / rgyud kyi gnyer gtad zhang blon rdo rje'i mthus/ / bdud sde'i tshogs rnams rin chen ltar 'dul bas/ / mi 'jigs srog sbyin la sogs las bzhi sgrubs/ /[*]

By the power of protector Rājānaka Vajra Mārajit, who was entrusted with the tantra by Buddha and Padmākara, may the host of māras be crushed like jewels, and with feats such as the gift of removing fear, accomplish the four activities.[50]
[*] (chos srung la las bskul ba'i sgo dang po rdo rje pha lam gyis rin po che thams cad 'dul ba'i gtam sbyar ba'i dpe gzugs/)

[50] Rājānaka Vajra Mārajit is a wrathful yakṣa-like protector, whose tantric practice was discovered by treasure revealer Drapa Ngönshé in Samyé where he discovered the Four Tantras. The four activities usually refer to those of pacification, increase, subjugation, and wrath.
gter bdag yon tan ngo bo shing bya can/ / las byed dam nyams lug la bshan pa ltar/ / gtum pa'i ab se ce spyang gdong lag dgra'i/ / khrag dmar sogs kyis 'dod don thogs med sgrubs/ /[*]
[*] (chos dpe dang 'jigs rung gi nyams 'dres pa/)
[51] These are clearly three wrathful protectors. I cannot find much about them. However, see p. 164.
khyad par tshul 'di'i mthar thug mchog gi lam/ / zab mo snying gi thig le'i bka'i srung ma/ / rdo rje'i thog mtshungs dam can sde dgus kyang / / 'di phyir dge ba'i phun tshogs las sgrubs shig /[*]

In particular, doctrine protectors of the profound heartdrop, the supreme and final path of this tradition, the nine oath-bound guardians, too, protecting like a vajra canopy: in this and future lives ensure the accomplishment of a host of virtuous activities.
[*] (dngos po'i dpe/)
sdug bsngal brgyud mar 'babs pa'i 'khor ba las/ / thar dang thams cad mkhyen pa'i go 'phang mchog / thob phyir rig pa'i gnas la bslab dgos par/ / rgyal bas rgya cher chu gter bzhin gsungs nang / /[*]
To find freedom from samsara’s constant rain of suffering and reach the supreme level of omniscience, you need to study the sciences. And from among Buddha’s teachings, as vast as an ocean,
[*] (dngos po nges bstan dang po dngos dpe/)
gnas skabs dal 'byor rnyed dka'i mi yi lus/ / mi na gnas dang na ba'i sdug bsngal dag / gso zhing tshe ring los mang rgad po yang / / lang tsho can bzhin dar la 'jog pa dang / /[*]

the science that brings to this hard-to-find human form of opportunity and leisure — albeit only temporarily — good health, respite from the suffering of sickness, and long life, bringing even the vigor of youth to the elderly
[*] (chos dpe/)
mthar thug bla na med par byang chub pa'i/ / ye shes rgyal ba'i sa thob rig pa'i gnas/ / gzhan las dgos don gces pa'i mchog gyur pa/ / 'gro kun rjes 'dzin gso ba rig pa 'di'i/ /[*]

and ultimately the achievement of the gnosis of perfect enlightenment, the state of a buddha, is a great science more precious and essential than the others, this science of medicine that cares for all beings.
[*] (rdzas brjod mtha' gsal/)
chos kyi 'byung gnas rnams nas tshe'i gzhung lugs/ / ma nyams drang song spyod pa'i tshugs bzang po/ / ma nyams lung dang rigs pas zhib mo ru/ / brtag dpyad cho ga rdzogs pas ches gtsang ba/ /[*]

Drawing from various accounts of its history the uncorrupted literary traditions of the science of life, with the excellent credentials of rishi practices, made even purer with untainted scripture and the complete process of detailed reasoning,
[*] (dbus ma gnyis kyi 'gor brjod pa'i zung ldan/)
dpal ldan gso ba rig pa'i rgyud kyi khog / sman pa'i rgyal pos bzhin du 'bugs byed pa'i/ / legs bshad dri ma spangs pa baiDUR+ya'i/ / me long tshe rig drang srong dgyes pa'i bzhin/ /[*]

this good explanation that erects the structure of the glorious medical science tradition, as it was done by the king of medicine, a stainless mirror of beryl reflecting the faces of the delighted Āyurveda[52] rishis,
[*] (dpe gzugs mtshar ba/)

[52] The Tibetan translation of Āyurveda here is tshe yi rig byed, literally “science of life,” which is often used as a synonym of gso ba’i rig pa or sman dpyad rig pa, meaning the science of healing or medicine.

f.d: 'char byed dge mtshan dkyil 'khor can/ / tshe yi bdud rtsi'i mchod sbyin gyis/ / 'gro la ring po'i srog stsal ba'i/ / dpyid kyi dga' ston 'di na spel/ /[*] [8-9]

d.div: with their mandalas of manifest virtue; this great offering of the ambrosia of life, may it become a glorious spring feast, granting long life to all living beings here and now.[53]
[*] (bya ba mtha' gsal/)

[53] Here the title of the work is woven into the verses. This work belongs to a genre called khog ’bubs or khog ’bugs, which usually refers to the history of the development of medicine. Literally, it means “to erect a structure” or “create an enclosure” in the sense of erecting a tent, building the exterior of a house, or even opening an umbrella. Here the author has incorporated the two syllables of this term into the verse. Khog means “structure,” “interior,” “something hollow,” “the mind,” “stomach,” etc.; ’bubs means “to erect” or “to cover.”

f.d: gleng gzhi/
2. Medical Science

d.i: The importance of the five sciences

f.d:
zhes de bzhin gshegs pa dus mkhyen rgyal po yang tshigs su bcad pa'i dbyangs kyi bstod nas thugs bskyed par bshad pa dang bstan bcos gang yang bla ma dang lhag pa'i lha la shis pa brjod pas de'i thugs rjes blo gros bde blag tu stsol ba sogs dgos pa khyad par can yod pas daN+Dis/
shis brjod phyag bya dngos po ni/ / nges par bstan pa de yi sgo/[5] / zhes pa ltar bla ma dang sman rgyal brgyud pa'i tshogs la shis pa brjod cing chos bsrung la 'phrin las bskul ba dngos po nges par bstan pa dang bcas sh+lokr-i bsdus ba'i byings las bsgrubs pa'i sh+loka mkha' mes sgo yangs par phye nas rje btsun byams pa mgon po'i rgyud bla ma skabs lnga pa las/
de ltar yid ches lung dang rigs pa la/ / brten nas bdag nyid 'ba' zhig dag phyir dang / / gang dag mos dge phun sum tshogs ldan blo/ / de dag rjes su bzung phyir 'di bshad do/[6] / zhes pa ltar/ gleng bar bya ba ni/

It is said that even the Tathāgata Trikālajña offered praise in poetic verse before generating the bodhi mind. Also, for any kind of treatise, offering words of auspiciousness to the lamas and deities ensures that their compassionate blessings of wisdom are easily granted. Therefore, for these and other reasons Daṇḍin says:
Words of auspiciousness and homage and a synopsis of the text — this is the door.[54] With the words of auspiciousness to the lamas, medicine buddhas, and the lineages, the urging of the protectors to do their duties and a synopsis of the work, all found in the above thirty śloka (stanzas) — a word constructed from the root ślokṛ, meaning “to compile” — the door has been opened. In the fifth chapter of the Uttaratantra, the noble Maitreya says:
Relying upon trustworthy scripture and reasoning, I teach this solely to purify myself and to nourish those with faith and with minds possessed of great virtue.[55] With this verse in mind, I will begin.

f.d:
thabs mkhas pa chen po sangs rgyas drin lan bsab pa'i mdo nye bar bsnyen pa'i le'u dgu pa las/
gal te byang chub sems dpa' rig pa'i dngos po lnga sngar ma bslabs na/ nam du yang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes thob par mi nus so/ / de bas na bla na med pa'i byang chub thob pa'i phyir/ rig pa'i dngos po lnga bslab par bya'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' ni drin shes pa dang / drin bsab pa ni sems can la bshad pa'i dngos po bshad cing bstan par bya'o/ / ji ltar bshad ce na/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub thob par bya ba'i phyir/ rig pa lnga dang ldan par bshad par bya'o/[7] / zhes dang /

In the Sutra of Repaying the Kindness of the Skillful Buddha, it says in the ninth chapter, on devotion:
If a bodhisattva does not first train in the five sciences, he can never attain the gnosis of omniscience, the highest and perfect enlightenment. Therefore, in order to attain the highest enlightenment, train in the five sciences. For a bodhisattva, gratitude and repaying kindness are expressed by explaining to sentient beings the things to be explained and by teaching them. How should they teach? They should teach by possessing the five sciences in order to attain the highest and perfect enlightenment.[56]

d.div: [7] sde dge_353_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_drin lan bsab pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_190_na1

f.d:
theg pa chen po mdo sde'i rgyan yongs su tshol ba'i le'u bcu gnyis pa las/
rig pa'i gnas lnga dag la brtson par ma byas na/ / 'phags mchog gis kyang thams cad mkhyen nyid mi 'gyur te/ / de lta bas na gzhan dag tshar bcad rjes bzung dang / / bdag nyid kun shes bya phyir de la de brtson byed/[8] / ces dang /

Also Ornament to Mahayana Sutras says in the twelfth chapter, “Searching for the Mahayana”:
If efforts are not made in the five sciences, even great ārya beings will not attain omniscience. Therefore, to refute and to nourish, and to attain omniscience, make effort in the sciences.[57]

f.d:
'phags pa thogs med kyi bstan bcos sa sde lnga'i nang tshan rnal 'byor spyod pa'i sa'i sangs rgyas kyi bka' shes bya'i gnas gnyis pa las/
thos pa las byung ba'i sa gang zhe na/ de yang mdor bsdu na/ rig pa'i gnas lnga gang yin pa de dag ming dang / tshig dang / yi ge la blo sngon du btang ste nyan pa dang / 'dzin pa dang / 'chang ba dang / kha ton [9]byed pa dang / rjes su dran pa dang / ming gi tshogs dang / tshig gi tshogs dang / yi ge'i tshogs la brten pa'i don rtogs pa 'di ni thos pa las byung ba'i sa zhes bya'o/ / rig pa'i gnas lnga gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ nang gi rig pa dang / gso ba'i rig pa dang / gtan tshigs kyi rig pa dang / sgra'i rig pa dang / bzo'i las kyi gnas kyi rig pa'o/[10] / zhes dang /

Ārya Asaṅga states in Stages of the Yogacaryā, from his five treatises on the stages, in the second chapter on the words of the Buddha:
What level of knowledge is born from listening? In brief, it is as follows. Whichever of the five sciences is being studied, the mind is initially applied to the letters and words, and word forms, and one listens, keeps them in the mind, retains, recites, and recalls them. The understanding that arises from this gathering of letters, words, and word forms is the level of knowledge born from listening. What are the five sciences? They are inner science [i.e., Buddhism], medicine, logic, language, and arts and crafts.[58]

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i sa'i gzhi'i rnal 'byor gyi gnas stobs kyi rigs kyi le'u brgyad pa las/
de la byang chub sems dpa' chos tshol bas ci zhig tshol/ ji ltar tshol/ ci'i phyir tshol zhe na/ mdor bsdu na byang chub sems dpa' ni byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod tshol lo/ / nyan thos kyi sde snod dang / phyi rol gyi bstan bcos rnams dang / 'jig rten pa'i bzo dang las kyi gnas rnams tshol lo/ / de la gsung rab tu rtogs pa yan lag bcu gnyis las shin tu rgyas pa'i sde gang yin pa de ni byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod yin no/ / lhag ma ni nyan thos kyi sde snod yin par rig par bya'o/ / phyi rol gyi bstan bcos rnams ni mdor bsdu na rnam pa gsum ste/ gtan tshigs kyi bstan bcos dang / sgra'i bstan bcos dang / gso ba'i bstan bcos so/ / de la 'jig rten pa'i bzo dang las kyi gnas ni rnam pa du ma rnam pa sna tshogs mang po yod de/ gser mgar dang / lcags mgar dang / nor bu mkhan gyi las zhes pa la sogs te/ rig pa'i gnas kyi yongs su bsdus pa de dag thams cad ni rig pa'i gnas lnga po dag yin te/ nang gi rig pa dang / gtan tshigs kyi rig pa dang / sgra'i rig pa dang / nad gso ba'i rig pa dang / bzo dang las kyi gnas kyi rig pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpas btsal ba gang yin pa ni rig pa'i gnas lnga po 'di dag ste/ de ltar na rig pa'i gnas thams cad btsal ba yin no/[11] /

In the eighth chapter, “Types of Powers,” of Asaṅga’s Stages of the Bodhisattva from Stages of the Yogacaryā, it says:
The bodhisattva seeks out a Dharma. What does he seek out? How does he search? Why does he search? In brief, the bodhisattva seeks out the bodhisattva canon, the śrāvaka canon, the treatises of the outsiders, and the arts and crafts of the world. From the twelve branches of scripture[59] that comprise the teachings, the extensive canon is the bodhisattva canon. The remaining scriptures should be known as the śrāvaka canon. The treatises of the outsiders are of three types: those on logic, those on language, and those on medicine. The arts and crafts of the world are many and varied. They include, for example, the crafts of goldsmiths, blacksmiths, and jewelers. All this knowledge can be classified under the five sciences, which are inner science, logic, language, medicine, and arts and crafts. Whatever the bodhisattva seeks is contained within these five sciences. Therefore, he seeks out all sciences.[60]

d.div: [11] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 8_shog_51_ba7
[59] These are listed on p. 228.

f.d:
zhes dang /
de la ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' thos pa tshol zhe na/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' ni gus pa chen po nye bar bzhag nas/ legs par gsungs pa legs par bsnyad pa'i chos tshol te/ de ni mdor na 'di lta bu'i tshul gyis kyang legs par gsungs pa la gus pa nye bar gnas pa yin te/ byang chub sems dpa' de ni legs par gsungs pa gcig mnyan pa'i phyir yang gal te de ltar ma byas na legs par gsungs pa thos par mi 'gyur ba lta na lcags kyi sa gzhi tsha zhing 'bar ba la yang mchog tu dga' ba dang / gus pa'i mchog gis 'gro bar byed na legs par gsungs pa mang po'i phyir lta ci smos/[12]

Also:
How does the bodhisattva search? The bodhisattva adopts an attitude of great reverence and goes in search of well-taught, well-explained Dharma. In brief, he maintains his reverence for the teachings in the following ways. The bodhisattva in search of just one good teaching would happily walk over a searing hot surface with a mind of great reverence if not doing so meant that he would not receive that teaching. If that is true, need we mention it is the same for a bodhisattva seeking many teachings?[61]

d.div: [12] gong mtshungs/ shog_56_na4

f.d:
zhes dang /
de la byang chub sems dpa' ci'i phyir thos pa tshol bar byed ce na/ byang chub sems dpa' ni chos kyi rjes su mthun pa'i chos kyi nan tan gyis yang dag par sgrub par bya ba'i phyir dang / gzhan dag la yang rgya char yeng dag par bstan par bya ba'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi bka' yongs su tshol bar byed do/ / byang chub sems dpa' na gtin tshigs kyi rig pa tshol bar byed de/ /bstan bcos de nyid las nyes pa bshad pa dang / nyes par brjod pa yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir dang / phas kyi rgol ba tshar bcad pa'i phyir dang / bstan pa 'di la ma dad pa rnams dad par bya ba'i phyir dang / dad pa rnams kyang phyir zhing 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir ro/ / byang chub sems dpa' ni sgra'i rig pa tshol bar byed de/ tshig dang yi ge nges pa'i tshig bzang po spyod pas legs par sbyar te/ brjod pa la mos pa rnams bdag la yid ches pa bskyed pa'i phyir dang / don gcig la yang nges pa'i tshig rnam pa sna tshogs kyis rjes su tha snyad gdags pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir ro/ / byang chub sems dpa' ni gso ba'i bstan bcos tshol bar byed de/ sems can rnams kyi nad rnam pa sna tshogs rnams zhi bar bya ba'i phyir dang / skye bo'i tshogs chen po la phan gdags pa'i phyir ro/ / byang chub sems dpa' ni 'jig rten pa'i bzo dang las kyi gnas shes pa rnams tshol bar byed de/ sems can rnams kyi don du tshegs chung ngus longs spyod sgrub pa'i phyir dang / sems can rnams kyis gces par bya ba bskyed pa'i phyir dang / bzo dang las kyi gnas shes pa sbyin pa'i phan 'dogs pas bsdus pa'i phyir ro/ / byang chub sems dpas rig pa'i gnas lnga po 'di dag thams cad tshol ba yang / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi ye shes kyi tshogs chen po yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir te/ thams cad la de ltar ma bslabs na rim gyis thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes sgrib pa med pa thob par mi 'gyur ro/[13] / zhes dang /

Also:
Why does the bodhisattva seek out the study of the teachings? The bodhisattva seeks out the word of the Buddha so that he may truly practice with diligence in accord with the Dharma, and that he may teach others purely and extensively. The bodhisattva seeks out the science of logic in order to understand exactly the faults found in texts and in the spoken word, to defeat others in debate, to induce faith in those who have no faith in this doctrine, and to increase the faith of those who do. The bodhisattva seeks out teachings on language because with his excellent use of language that is definitive in it use of words and syllables, he will be able to compose his utterances well, and those who delight in speech will develop faith in him. Moreover, using various etymological analyses for a single meaning he will be able to make use of terminology. The bodhisattva seeks out the scriptures on medicine in order to cure living beings of their various illnesses and to benefit large communities. The bodhisattva seeks out knowledge of the arts and crafts of this world so that with little difficulty, he can create more pleasures for other beings. Also he will be valued greatly, and knowledge of arts and craft aids the practice of giving. Moreover, the bodhisattva seeks out all five sciences in order to complete the great gnosis accumulation for perfect enlightenment, because were he not to train in all of them, he would not attain the unobscured gnosis of omniscience.[62]

d.div: [13] gong mtshungs/ shog_57_na2

f.d:
sa'i gzhi'i rnal 'byor gyi gnas shes rab kyi le'u bzhi pa las/
de la byang chub sems dpa'i shes rab kyi ngo bo nyid gang zhe na/ shes bya thams cad la 'jug pa dang / shes bya thams cad la zhugs pa/ chos rnams rab tu rnam par 'byed pa gang yin pa rig pa'i gnas lnga po/ nang gi rig pa dang / gtan tshigs kyi rig pa dang / gso ba'i rig pa dang / sgra'i rig pa dang / bzo dang las kyi gnas kyi rig pa la dmigs nas 'jug pa 'di ni byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi shes rab kyi ngo bo nyid yin par rig par bya'o/ / de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi shes rab thams cad gang zhe na/ de ni rnam pa gnyis su blta bar bya ste/ 'jig rten pa'i sa dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa pa'o/[14] / zhes sogs dang /
de la byang chub sems dpa'i 'di dang gzhan du bde bar 'gyur pa'i shes rab gang zhe na/ de ni rnam pa dgur rig par bya ste/ nang gi rig pa la shin tu rnam par byang zhing rab tu gnas pa'i shes rab dang / gso ba'i rig pa dang / gtan tshigs kyi rig pa dang / sgra'i rig pa dang / 'jig rten pa'i bzo dang las kyi gnas kyi rig pa rnams la ni shin tu byang la/ rab tu gnas pa ma yin pa'i shes rab dang / rig pa lnga po shin tu rnam par byang ba de dag nyid la brten nas/ gdul bya rmongs pa rnams dang / bag med rnams dang / zhum pa rnams dang / yang dag par zhugs pa gzhan dag la go rim bzhin du yang dag par bstan pa dang / yang dag par 'dzin du gzhug pa dang / yang dag par gzengs bstod pa dang / yang dag par dga' bar bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa'i shes rab gang yin pa'o/[15] / zhes dang /

In chapter 14, the “Wisdom” chapter, of Stages of the Bodhisattva from Stages of the Yogacaryā, it says:
What is the wisdom of the bodhisattva? It is that which is engaging in all existing knowledge and that which is engaged in all existing knowledge.[63] It is the discernment of phenomena and focuses on and engages in the five sciences of inner science, logic, healing, language, and arts and crafts. This is the nature of the wisdom of the bodhisattva. What are the types of bodhisattva wisdom? They can be condensed into two types: those on the levels of mundane wisdom and transcendent wisdom.[64] Also:
What is the wisdom of the bodhisattva that brings happiness here and elsewhere? It should be known as being of nine kinds: the wisdom that is well trained in and abides in the inner science; the wisdom that is well trained in, but does not abide in, the science of healing, the science of logic, the science of language, and the science of worldly arts and crafts, and, in dependence on being well trained in these five sciences, the wisdom of the bodhisattva that brings the true teaching, true concentration, true encouragement, and true joy to, respectively, those disciples who are confused, heedless, discouraged, and engaged in the true path.[65]

d.div: [14] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 14_shog_113_na6
[15] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 14_shog_114_ba4

[63] According to the commentary to this text by Sāgaramegha (Toh 4047), wisdom that “engages” (’jug pa) is the wisdom of a bodhisattva who “practices by faith” and has not attained the first ārya level. The second, which is “engaged” (zhugs pa), is that of the ārya bodhisattva.
[64] Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 113a6.

f.d:
byang chub kyi phyogs kyi le'u bcu bdun pa las/
de la byang chub sems dpa'i bstan bcos shes pa gang zhe na/ 'di la byang chub sems dpas rig pa'i gnas lnga po dag las brtsams te/ ming gi tshogs dang / tshig gi tshogs dang / yi ge'i tshogs dang ldan pa'i chos gzhan las legs par bzung ste kha ton [16]legs par bya ba yin/ chos kyi don de nyid kyang gzhan las legs par thos pa yin/ yang na bdag nyid kyis legs par bsams shing legs par brtags pa yin te/ de ltar byang chub sems dpa' chos shes shing don shes pas chos dang / don de nyid mi brjed par bya ba'i phyir dang / chos dang / don gyi bye brag gsar pa gsar pa dag gong nas gong du shes par bya ba'i phyir sbyor ba mi gtong ba yin no/[17] / zhes dang /

Also in the seventeenth chapter, “Enlightenment”:
What does it mean to know the bodhisattva scriptures? From the five sciences, the bodhisattva receives the Dharma from others in the form of a collection of letters, words, and word forms that he retains and recites well. The meanings of the Dharma too he receives from others. Alternatively, he contemplates and analyzes their meanings himself. In this way the bodhisattva knows the Dharma and knows their meanings. In order not to forget the Dharma and its meanings and to learn new Dharma and new meanings, he perseveres in his endeavors.[66]

f.d:
'jam dbyangs sa skya paN+Di tas/
gangs ri'i khrod kyi blo gsal kun 'dus kyang/ / rig pa'i gnas lnga kun la blos mi lcogs/ / mkha' la rgyu skar bye ba'i 'od 'khrigs kyang / / tsha zer byed pa'i 'phrin las 'grub par dka'/[18] / zhes dang /

Jamyang Sakya Paṇḍita says:
All the bright minds in this snow mountain land would never outshine the five great sciences; even the light of a million stars combined would find it hard to outshine the sun.[67]

kun mkhyen thob par 'dod rnams kyis/ / rig pa'i gnas lnga shes bya ste/[19] / zhes dang /

Sasang Mati Paṇchen says:
Those who desire enlightenment should know the five sciences.[68]

d.div: [19] sa bzang ma ti paN chen/ sgra'i bstan bcos ka lA pa'i mdo'i rnam bshad legs sbyar rab gsal snang ba/ sa skya'i bka' 'bum pod brgyad pa/ shog_2_na3

f.d:
rin spungs sa spyod dbang pos/
sgra dang tshad ma'i rig pa gtum pos lta ngan ma lus shes bya'i dbyings su bsad/ / bzo dang gso ba rjes su 'dzin pa'i phan pa mngon sum nyid du yang dag rgyu/ / chos kyi dra ba sdom pa'i nang gi de nyid smra ba kun gyi rgyal po che/ / lnga rig mkhas dang grub pa'i 'khor lo dus gsum bsgyur ba rnams la dang bas bstod/[20] / ces dang /

Rinpung Sachö Wangpo says:
Slaying all wrong views in the arena of knowledge with the wrathful sciences of language and logic; flawlessly bringing the manifest benefits of the caring sciences of medicine and the arts; tying the net of Dharma, kings of the orators of inner reality, to you masters and practitioners of the five great sciences, universal sovereigns who turn your great wheels in the three times, I offer my joyful praise.[69]

d.div: [20] rin spungs sa spyod dbang pos/ sgra dang tshad ma'i rig pa gtum pos lta ngan ma lus shes bya'i dbyings su bsad/ /bzo dang gso ba rjes su 'dzin pa'i phan pa mngon sum nyid du yang dag rgyu/ /chos kyi dra ba sdom pa'i nang gi de nyid smra ba kun gyi rgyal po che/ /lnga rig mkhas dang grub pa'i 'khor lo dus gsum bsgyur ba rnams la dang bas bstod/ / ces pa 'di rin spungs pa'i gsung gang gi nang du yod ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[69] Citation untraced.

f.d:
bdag gi bla ma nges pa don gyi thams cad mkhyen pa lnga pa chen pos/
thub bstan zhing sa gshin par sgrub pa tshul khrims so so thar pa'i bstan/ / lung rtogs sdong bu lo 'dab rgyas byed sgra tshad bzo gso sde snod gsum/ / zung 'jug 'bras bu yongs su dud pa nges gsang rdo rje theg pa'i lam/ / tshul bzhin gnas lnga rig pa nyan 'di sngon bsags bsod nams shing rtas drangs/[21] / zhes rgyal pa'i bka' dang tshad ldan gyi bstan bcos rnams las lan cig ma yin par bsngags pa'i log smra tshar gcod pa sgra dang tshad ma/ gzhan rjes su 'dzin pa bzo dang gso ba/ rang nyid shes bya kun gyi de kho na nyid kyi gnas lugs shes par byed pa nang rig pa ste/ rig pa'i gnas chen lnga yan lag dang bcas pa'i bcu phrag gcig ni mkhas su 'dod pa thams cad kyis mi slob tu mi rung ba yin pas nges par slob dgos la/

My lama the Great Fifth, definitively an omniscient one, also said:
In the field of the doctrine of the Buddha, his soil made fertile by the doctrine of pratimokṣa ethics; the shoots, leaves, and flowers of transmission and insight grown by language, healing, logic, arts, and the three baskets, weighed down by harvest of method and wisdom union, on the definitively secret path of Vajrayana, this sun of the five sciences correctly applied, pulled by the horses of merit gathered in the past….[70] Therefore, the five great sciences, praised often in the teachings of the Buddha and in reputable treatises, are comprised of language and logic to defeat perverse teachers, medicine and arts to care for and nourish others, and the inner science to understand the ultimate reality of all phenomena. Together with their five secondary sciences[71] to make up the ten sciences, they are indispensable for all who wish to become wise. They should, therefore, be studied.

d.div: [21] rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ ka gsan yig glegs bam dang po/ shog_4_na6
[70] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Stream of the Ganges: An Account of Teachings Received, Collected Works, ka, 4a6.
[71] Grammar, poetic theory, prosody, drama, and lexicography.

f.d: gso ba rig pa'i khyad chos/

d.i: Features of the science of healing

f.d:
de'i nang tshan gso ba rig pa ni/ mdo drin lan bsab pa las/
byang chub sems dpa' ci'i phyir sman dpyad kyi rig pa'i bstan bcos slob ce na/ sems can rnams mi dge ba'i nad bzhi brgya rtsa bzhi dang dbral bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad la byams shing snying brtse ba'i phyir sems can rnams dad pa'i sems bskyed par bya ba dang / de ltar nad dang bral bas dga' ba'i sems bskyed par byed pa dang / de ltar dga' ba'i sems skyes pas rtag du sangs rgyas dran par 'gyur te/ snying rje chen pos sems can rnams pha rol tu phyin par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' sman dpyad kyi rig pa slob par byed do/[22] / zhes dang /

On the science of healing, the Sutra of Repaying the Kindness of the Skillful Buddha says:
Why do bodhisattvas study scriptures of the science of medicine? They do it to free living beings from the 404 diseases of nonvirtue.[72] They do it because they have great love and compassion for all living beings and want to generate faith in the minds of living beings. Freed of illness, the minds of living beings will be filled with joy, and they will constantly remember the Buddha. Then with great compassion, the bodhisattvas will bring living beings to the perfections. This is why they train in the science of medicine.[73]

d.div: [22] sde dge_353_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_drin lan bsab pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_189_ba4

[72] Mi dge ba. This probably refers to the fact that disease is a karmic fruit of nonvirtue, but the term also means “bad” or “unfortunate” and may just be referring to the general adversity of ill health.
[73] Chap. 4, Toh 343 Kangyur, mdo sde, ah, 189b4. Translated from the Chinese.

f.d:
rnal 'byor spyod pa'i sa'i thos pa las byung ba'i sar/
gso ba'i rig pa gang zhe na/ de ni rnam pa bzhir blta bar bya ste/ 'di lta ste/ nad la mkhas pa dang / nad ci las byung ba la mkhas pa dang / nad byung ba bsal ba la mkhas pa dang / nad bsal nas phyis mi 'byung bar bya ba la mkhas pa'o/ / mkhas pa 'di dag gi rnam par dbye ba ni mdo las ji skad 'byung ba kho na bzhin du rig par bya'o/[23] / zhes dang /

Also, in Stages of the Yogacaryā from the Stage of Wisdom from Hearing chapter:
What is the science of healing? It should be regarded as having four divisions: knowledge of diseases, knowledge of the origin of diseases, knowledge of how to eradicate the disease, knowledge of how to prevent the disease from reoccurring. The wise should learn these divisions exactly as they are taught in the sutras.[74]

d.div: [23] sde dge_4035_bstan/ sems tsam/ tshi_rnal 'byor spyod pa'i sa/ thos pa las byung ba'i sa'i le'u/ shog_187_na5
[74] Yogacaryābhūmi, Toh 4035 Tengyur, sems tsam, tshi, 187a5.

f.d:
le'u brgyad pa las/
gso ba'i bstan bcos ni rnam pa bzhis 'jug ste nad la mkhas pa'i rnam pa dang / ci las byung ba la mkhas pa ston pa'i rnam pa dang / nad byung ba bsal ba la mkhas par ston pa'i rnam pa dang / nad bsal nas phyi ma mi 'byung bar bya ba la mkhas pa ston pa'i rnam pa'o/[24] / zhes dang /

In the eighth chapter [of Asaṅga’s Stages of the Bodhisattva]:
The medical scriptures have four main aspects: imparting knowledge of disease; knowledge of the origins of disease; knowledge of the eradication of disease; and knowledge of the prevention of disease reoccurring.[75]

d.div: [24] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 8_shog_50_ba1
[75] Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 50b1.

f.d:
gso rig rtsa ba'i rgyud las/
mi na bar gnas par 'dod pa dang na ba gso bar 'dod pa'i gang zag gis gso ba rig pa'i man ngag la bslab par bya'o/ / tshe ring bar 'dod pa'i gang zag gis gso ba rig pa'i man ngag la bslab par bya'o/ / chos dang nor dang bde ba sgrub par 'dod pa'i gang zag gis gso ba rig pa'i man ngag la bslab par bya'o/ / 'gro ba gang zhig nad kyi sdug bsngal las thar bar 'dod pa dang / gzhan gyi spyi bos bkur bar 'dod pa'i gang zag gis gso ba rig pa'i man ngag la bslab par bya'o/[25] / zhes dang /

In the Root Tantra of the Four Tantras it says:
Those who wish to remain free of illness and to cure disease should study the teachings on the science of healing. Those who wish to live a long life should study the teachings on the science of healing. Those who wish for Dharma, wealth, and happiness should study the teachings on the science of healing. Those who wish to free living beings from the miseries of illness and who wish to be respected by others should study the teachings on the science of healing.[76]

d.div: [25] bdud rtsi snying po yan lag brgyad pa gsang ba man ngag gi rgyud las rtsa rgyud/ le'u gnyis pa/ shog grangs 4_phreng 7
[76] Four Tantras, Root Tantra, 2.4.7.

f.d:
bshad rgyud las/
'gro drug gtso bor gyur pa mi lus la/ / mi na gnas dang na ba gso ba dang / / tshe ring chos nor bde ba sgrub pa'i phyir/ / gso ba rig pa'i don rnams mdor bsdu na/[26] / zhes dang /

In the Explanatory Tantra of the Four Medical Tantras it says:
For those with human birth, chief among the six types of beings, to remain free of illness, to be cured of disease, for long life, Dharma, wealth, and happiness, the science of healing….[77]

d.div: [26] bdud rtsi snying po yan lag brgyad pa gsang ba man ngag gi rgyud las bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 1_shog_15_phreng 12
[77] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 1.15.12.

f.d:
phyi rgyud las/
'di ni sngags med pa yi srung skud yin/ / 'chi bdag bdud sde bzlog pa'i 'phrul 'khor yin/ / nad kyi dgra dpung 'joms pa'i dpa' bo yin/ / 'du ba 'phel zad snyoms pa'i spyi ba yin/ /
dus min 'chi zhags gcod pa'i ral gri yin/ / nad kyi zug gzer gcog pa'i tho ba yin/ / sdug bsngal 'dam nas 'dren pa'i lcags kyu yin/ / 'chi ba'i srog skyob mi 'jigs sbyin pa yin/[27] / zhes dang /

In the Final Tantra of the Four Medical Tantras it says:
This [medical science] is a protection cord without mantra, a magic charm to destroy the māras of the lord of death, the warrior who defeats the army of disease, the holder of the public purse who balances the excesses and deficiency in the constituents,[78]
a sword that cuts the noose of untimely death, a hammer that crushes the pain of illness, a hook that pulls us from the swamp of suffering. By giving us protection from death, it is the generosity that grants freedom from fear.[79]

d.div: [27] bdud rtsi snying po yan lag brgyad pa gsang ba man ngag gi rgyud las phyi ma'i rgyud/ le'u nyer bdun pa/shog_665_yig phreng 4
[78] ’Du ba. One of the names for the body’s three humors of wind, bile, and phlegm, whose excess, deficiency, and disturbance provoke illness.
[79] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 27.665.4. Generosity is often classified into three types: generosity with material things, generosity with Dharma, and generosity that grants freedom from fear.

f.d:
mkhas mchog bye ba'i gtsug rgyan dpal ldan pha khol gyis/
tshe ni ring bar 'dod pa yis/ / chos dang nor dang bde ba sgrub/ / tshe yi rig byed lung bshad pa/ / rab tu gus par bya ba gyis/[28] / zhes dang /

Pitṛceṭa, crown jewel of millions of scholars, states:
Those who wish for a long life, for Dharma, wealth, and happiness, should revere the teachings of the Āyurveda.[80]

d.div: [28] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u/ 1_shog_44_ba3
[80] Essence of Eight Branches (Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhita), chap. 1, Toh 4310 Tengyur, gso rig, he, 44b3. For more on the figure of Pitṛceṭa, see below, pp. 128–43.

f.d:
rje bla ma srid zhi'i gtsug rgyan lnga pa chen pos/
'dzad med bskal par gnas pa'i ring po'i tshe/ / sgrub pa'i srog 'tsho'i bcud len bdud rtsi'i gter/ / mi 'jigs sbyin pa'i sgo 'phar legs phye ba/ / ris med skye dgu'i bsod nams zong gis rnyed/[29] / ces dang /

My master lama, the Great Fifth, crown jewel of samsara and nirvana, said:
A treasure of ambrosia, the elixir of life bringing longevity lasting eons without end, opening the door to a gift of fearlessness, gained through the currency of merit, available to all living beings without exception….[81]

d.div: [29] rje bla ma srid zhi'i gtsug rgyan lnga pa chen pos/ 'dzad med bskal bar gnas pa'i ring po'i tshe/ /sgrub pa'i srog 'tsho'i bcud len bdud rtsi'i gter/ /mi 'jigs sbyin pa'i sgo 'phar legs phye ba/ /ris med skye dgu'i bsod nams zong gis rnyed/ /ces pa 'di rnyed son ma thub/
[81] Untraced.

f.d:
rin chen spungs pas/
mthar byed gdangs khar bcar ba'i zug rngu yis/ / lkog ma'i bar du srog rgyu shugs ring dbugs/ / lan mang brtsegs pa de kun gdung sel du/ / tshe yi rig byed dran dbang tshangs pa dang /[30] / zhes dang /

Rinchen Pungpa says:
The quickening rasping gasps of one’s life in one’s throat, wrought from the pain of being squeezed into the lord of death’s gaping mouth, all to be relieved by the science of life, recalled by Brahmā through his memory.[82]

d.div: [30] rin chen spungs pas/ mthar byed gdangs khar bcar ba'i zug rngu yis/ /lkog ma'i bar du srog rgyu shugs ring dbugs/ /lan mang brtsegs pa de kun gdung sel du/ /tshe yi rig byed dran dbang tshangs pa dang / /
[82] Untraced. As it says in the text below, Āyurveda emerged from the face of the god Brahmā.

f.d:
stag los/
'gro kun lus nad sna tshogs kyis gzir phyir/ / gso dpyad don du mi gnyer srid mtha' tsam/ / de phyir rig gnas gnyis pa 'di nyid ni/ / don gnyer rjes su 'dzin pa'i mchog tu grub/[31] / ces thog ma med pa nas nyon mongs pa dug lngas gzir zhing / nag po'i las ches cher brtsegs pa'i 'bras bu dang 'phral rkyen sna tshogs la brten nas 'du ba rnam bzhi 'khrugs pa'i nad ma bcos rang gar bzhag kyang 'tsho ba brgya rtsa gcig /gdon bcos pas 'tsho ba brgya rtsa gcig /bcos na 'tsho la ma bcos na mi 'tsho ba brgya rtsa gcig /bcos kyang mi 'tsho ba brgya rtsa gcig ste mu bzhir gsungs pa'i smad dpyad sogs kyis 'chi bdag gshin rje'i zhags pa las grol bar byed pa'i tshul skye dgu kun la mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa rlabs po ches gzhan phan gyi thabs rgyal ba'i sras kyi spyod pa'i yan lag tu nges par 'gyur ba shes ldan rnams kyis gcig tu gzhol pa'i gnas

Taktsang Lotsāwa says:
All beings are tormented by illness. To not seek out the science of healing, therefore, is to fall to the extreme of samsara; and to strive in this second science thus accomplishes the great good of caring.[83] Since time without beginning living beings have been tormented by the five poisonous mental afflictions and have thereby accumulated a great store of black karma. When the fruits of these actions come into contact with a variety of immediate conditions and circumstances, they bring about disturbances in the four constituents,[84] resulting in illness. These illnesses have been classified as fourfold: 101 ailments that disappear by themselves and need no treatment, 101 illnesses caused by spirits that are cured when treated, 101 illnesses that are cured if treated but not if left untreated, and 101 illnesses that even treatment cannot cure. The treatments for these illnesses free living beings from the noose of Yama, the lord of death, thereby bestowing on all beings the powerful gift of fearlessness. Therefore, it is definitely part of bodhisattva conduct and a field of endeavor for the wise.

d.div: [31] rig gnas kun shes dpe lag tu ma son/ 7rgyal ba lnga pa'i gsung 'bum/ tsa sku gsung thugs rten gsar bzhengs rin po che'i mchod rdzas khang bzang gi dkar chag dang tham phud deb khrims yig 'go rgyangs sde bzhi'i sgo 'phar phye ba'i skal bzang gi glegs bam gnyis pa/ shog_179_ba3
[83] Untraced in Taktsang Lotsāwa’s works, but cited in volume 2 of the Collected Works of the Great Fifth, tsa, 179b3.
[84] Again, ’du ba, here referring to the three humors of wind, bile, and phlegm with the addition of blood.

f.d: legs par sbyar ba'i skad du A yurbe daH_tshe dang srog don gcig ming gi rnam grangs yin/ 'tsho ba ni rnam shes kyi rten te/ 'dod pa dang gzugs kyi khams na drod dang rnam par shes pa'i rten gnyis ka byed pa gzugs med na rnam par shes pa'i rten kho na byed pa/ de rig par byed pa na tshe'i rig byed bi tsi kan+si taM zhes pa gso ba'i dpyad de yang khams sam 'du ba mi snyoms pa bsal nas snyoms par bya ba'i rnam dpyad yin pas gso dpyad ces bya dang tsi kit+sA bi d+yA ste gso ba rig pa zhes pa 'di yin la/

In Sanskrit this science is known as āyurveda. “Lifespan” (tshe, āyuṣ) and “life force” (srog, prāṇā) are synonyms. “Life” (’tsho ba, jīva) is the basis for consciousness. In the desire and form realms, it is the basis for warmth and consciousness, whereas in the formless realms it is only the basis for consciousness. Knowledge of this life is the science of life. The Sanskrit term cikitsitā means “expertise in healing.” It is the expertise in balancing the disordered elements or constituents of the body. It is also referred to as the “science of healing,” or cikitsā vidyā.
gso rig lha las dar tshul/
3. Origins of the Science of Healing in the Celestial Realms

de'ang lha las dar ba ni/ ji skad du/
snyan tshig mchod sbyin srid srungs dang / / nges brjod rig byed bzhi zhes bya/ / bslab dang brda sprod sdeb sbyor dang / / de bzhin skar rtsis thos pa dang / / rtog pa dang ni yan lag go / dran pa dang ni chos dang bcas/[32] /

A treatise states:
Sāmaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda, and Ṛgveda: these are the four Vedic sciences. Articulation, grammar, metrics, astronomy, etymology, and rites: these are the branches,[85] together with treatises on love and Dharma.[86]

d.div: [32] rig byed kyi skor gyi bshad pa rnams 'dir yongs su grags mod/ rig byed rang gzhung bod skad du ma bsgyur bas/ 'dir sde srid kyi gzhung rtog ge 'bar ba rtsa 'grel sogs mang por 'khod pa rnams las bkod par nges/ bshad pa 'di rnams zur mkhar blo gros rgyal po'i gsung du'ang drangs/ de'i gsung sman pa rnams kyis mi shes su mi rung ba'i shes bya spyi'i khog dbubs/ shog_159_phreng 16

[85] The six branches (rig byed kyi yan lag, vedānga) are articulation (bslab pa, śikṣā), grammar (vyākaraṇa, brda sprod), metrics (chandas, sdeb sbyor), etymology (nirukta, thos pa), astronomy (jyotiṣa skar rtsi), and rites and ceremonies (kalpa, rtog pa). The two subsidiary treatises are those on love (dran pa, smara) and Dharma (chos).

[86] Such citations from the Vedas are well known in Tibetan literature, but as the original texts were not translated into Tibetan, the citation cannot be sourced. However, this citation and the following two are quoted in Surkhar Lodrö Gyalpo’s General Compendium of Knowledge Indispensable to Physicians, pp. 159–60.

f.d:
zhes 'byung ba ltar yan lag drug /nye ba'i yan lag gnyis dang bcas pa kun kyang mes po'i zhal bzhi las byung ba'i rgyu mtshan/
gang phyir tshangs pa yi ni zhal/ / dbus ma nas ni tshe'i rig byed/ / snyan tshig nges brjod mchod sbyin rnams/ / zhal gzhan nas ni gsung bar mdzad/[33] / ces dang /
bram ze kha las skyes pa dang / / de bzhin dpung pa las rgyal rigs/ / brla las rje rigs yang dag byung/ / rkang pa las ni dmangs rigs so/[34] / zhes skye gnas kyi gtso bor bram ze rnams kyi chos lugs la rig byed ces bya la rig byed

f.d:
de'ang sus kyang ma byas pas rtag pa/ bya rtsol gyis ma slad pas rang byung / thams cad brjod du rung bas tshad ma yin pa zhig tu 'dod la/ mkhas mchog dpa' bos snying po bsdus par/ tshangs pas tshe yi rig byed dran/[35] / zhes gsungs pa'i dran tshul la/ khyad par 'phags bstod kyi 'grel pa slob dpon shes rab go chas mdzad pa las/
de yang 'di ltar lha rnams rgya mtsho bsrub pa'i phyir zhugs pa na/ de'i tshe nor bu ko tu ba dang / rta mgrin rings la sogs pa mang po zhig byung bar gyur pa dang / ji tsam na dug cig byung bar gyur nas de'i mthus khyab 'jug de'i gan na gnas pas pags pa'i mdog nag por gyur to/ / lha chen pos de blangs nas 'jigs pa med par mid par rtsom pa na ji tsam na mgrin par thogs te steng du yang ma byung 'og tu yang ma song bar de'i mgrin pa rma bya'i mgrin pa ltar snang bar gyur pa dang / lha rnams kyis smras pa/ 'di ni shin tu mdzes pas da ni deng nas de mgri+in pa nyid du bzhag par rigs so zhes smras par grag go/[36] / zhes dang /

It is said that because they were not created by anyone, the Vedas are permanent. Uncorrupted by effort and endeavor they are said to be self-arisen. Because they are able to speak of all things, they are said to be valid. In his Essence of Eight Branches, the master scholar Śūra said, “The Āyurveda was recalled by Brahmā.”[89] How he recalled it is taught in Commentary on Praise of the Exalted by Prajñāvarman:
In this way the gods came to churn the ocean. From the ocean arose many things, including the kaustubha jewel and Hayagrīva. After a while some poison also surfaced. Viṣṇu was standing nearby, and the poison turned his skin black. Mahādeva took the poison and swallowed it without fear. The poison stayed in his throat, moving neither up nor down. Because of this his throat glistened with the colors of the peacock. The gods exclaimed, “How beautiful this is! From now on, it is only fitting that his throat remain this way.”[90]

[90] Viśeṣastavaṭīkā, Toh 1110 Tengyur, bstod tshogs, ka, 10a1.

f.d: ji tsam na lha rnams kyis 'o ma can gyi rgya mtsho bsrubs pa na/ ji srid cig na bdud rtsi byung bar gyur pa dang / lha ma yin sgra gcan gyis 'phrogs nas spyod par rtsom pa na/ khyab 'jug gis bsams pa/ gal te 'dis bdud rtsi 'thungs par gyur na/ lha rnams kyis kyang mi thub par 'gyur ro snyam nas/ 'khor los mgo bcad pa dang / des de bor [37]ba na lha rnams kyis kyang blangs so/ / sgra gcan de'i lkog ma'i phyogs kyi bar bdud rtsi'i ches khyab par gyur pa dang/ des de'i 'og go cha'i lus shi bar gyur kyang gson la/ de yang lha dang mi rnams la gnod pa bya ba'i phyir rgyu'o/ / gnas skabs de nas brtsams te sa gsum snang bar byed pa'i nyi ma dang zla ba 'dzin par byed pa yin no/[38] / zhes dang /

Also:
The gods churned the mighty ocean of milk until ambrosia appeared. However, it was stolen by the asura Rāhu, who began to use it. Viṣṇu thought, “If he drinks it, even the gods will not be able to defeat him.” So with his mighty weapon wheel, he cut off Rāhu’s head, and the gods retrieved the nectar. However, some of the nectar had reached Rāhu’s throat, and although the body below his throat was dead, he was still alive, and he set off to wreak havoc among gods and men. From that time onward, he has eclipsed the sun and moon that light up the three worlds.[91]
