f.d: de nas rgya gar gyi paN chen tsan+d+ra b+hIr/ dpal ldan rgyud bzhi'i kha skong mu tig phreng ba dang dkar chag gsal sgron/ mkhas pa me dbang la ng+he skor phyi nang gsang gsum/ rgyud 'grel stong dang rtsa gcig /dmar 'ded brgya dngab co brgyad/ ro bkra 'phrul gye me long / byang khog gsang dbye mdzub btsugs/ thur dpyad gnad kyi lde mig /gnad kyi 'phrul 'khor/ gsang thig /phan byed gnod byed kyi man ngag phran tshegs bsam las 'das pa bcas gdams ngag gi dkor mdzod mang po zhus nas bod du phebs/ rgyal po shin tu mnyes par gyur/ slar yang rgya gar du byon/ paN chen tsan+d+ra b+hI dang mkhas pa me dbang la 'khrid yig brgya rtsa la sogs pa sman dpyad kyi gzhung dang gdams pa du ma thob/ rgyal po mi rtsa yo khur gyis bkrong par brtsams pa rdzu 'phrul sna tshogs kyis btul/ bod yul du phyag phab ste 'gro phan rlabs che ba mdzad/

In India he met the great pandit Candrabhīra,[430] who bestowed upon him the Pearl Garland Supplement to the Four Glorious Tantras with its Bright Beacon Table of Contents. From the scholar Agniśa he received the Outer, Inner, and Secret Stone-Removal Collection; One Thousand and One Commentaries on the Tantra; One Hundred and Eighteen Clear Instructions on Chasing Disease; Magic Mirror of Anatomy; Pointing Out Secret Divisions of the Torso; Essential Key to Surgery; Essential Charm Circle; Secret Measurements; and countless minor teachings on various eliminative and beneficial methods. With such a treasury of teachings he returned to Tibet to a delighted king. Again Yuthok returned to India, and from the pandits Candrabhīra and Agniśa he again received many medical texts and instructions, such as the Hundred Manuals. Using various magical powers he tamed King Mitsa Yokhur, who had wanted to kill him. He then returned to Tibet, where he worked extensively in the service of others.

d.div: [430] Referred to as Candradeva in Trinlé and in Darmo Menrampa.

f.d: yang rgya gar 'phags pa'i yul bgrod/ slob dpon pra wa ha sti la rdzogs chen/ mkha' 'gro seng gdong mar snyan brgyud/ mkhas pa me dbang la gso dpyad 'bum pa/ rgyud shel gyi me long / so ma rA dza kha skong dang bcas pa/ paN chen tsan+d+rA b+hI la drang srong snyan brgyud dang yan lag brgyad pa rnams zhus par rnam thar bka' rgya ma las bshad/

Once more he went to India. There he received teachings on Great Perfection from Ācārya Pravahasti; the whispered transmission from the ḍākinī Siṃavaktā; from Agniśa Collection on the Science of Healing, Crystal Mirror Tantra,[431] and the Somarāja with supplements. From the pandit Candrabhīra he received Whispered Transmission of the Rishis and Eight Branches. These are listed in his Sealed Manuscript Biography.[432]

d.div: [431] A text with the same was mentioned above as belonging to Tsenpashilaha.
[432] In other words, Darmo Menrampa’s Brilliant Jewel Treasury biography.

f.d: rgya gar rdo rje gdan du bud med me long lag tu thogs shing sman rkyal phrag par bkal ba gcig na re/ mkhas pa chen po g.yu thog pa khyed sman gyi grong khyer lta na sdug tu 'byon par bzhed na sman bla rig [207]'dzin brgyud pa dang bcas par gsol ba rtse gcig tu thob mdzod zer ba ltar btab pas/ zhing khams dang pho brang la sogs pa mtshan nyid thams cad rdzogs par sangs rgyas sman pa'i rgyal po/ 'tsho byed gzhon nu/ rang gi mes po rnams dngos su mjal/

In Vajrāsana in India a girl holding a mirror and carrying a medicine bag on her shoulder addressed him, “Great scholar Yuthok, if you wish to go to the medicine city of Sudarśana, single-pointedly pray to the medicine guru and the vidyādhara lineage.” He did this, and there in Sudarśana he saw the Buddha, the king of medicine, as well as the palace, the surrounding environment, all the features of the city of Sudarśana. There he met Jivaka Kumāra and his ancestors.

d.div: [207] ma dper rigs 'dzin zhes sa yang 'jug byung yang rig 'dzin zhes bcos/

f.d:
sman bla'i zhal nas/
sman gyi grong khyer phyi nang gsang ba gsum/ / phyi yi grong khyer lta na sdug ces 'di/ / rgya gar yul dang nub phyogs a+yon yul/ / 'og min gnas dang ri rab rtse la sogs/ / mchog sprul gnas der gang yang gsol btab na/ / skal ldan bu dang mjal bar nges pa yin/ /

The Medicine Buddha addressed him:
The medical city of Sudarśana has outer, inner, and secret locations. This outer Sudarśana is in the land of India, in the western land of Oḍḍiyāna, in Akaniṣṭha, on the summit of Meru, and elsewhere. It will be seen by the fortunate who pray to the supreme emanation dwelling there.

d.div: nang gi grong khyer lta na sdug ces bya/ / rang gnas gang yin rang nyid baiDUR+ya/ / gsang ba'i grong khyer lta na sdug ces bya/ / rang nyid lus gnas spyi bo bde chen 'khor/ / rang sems baiDUR+ya'i 'od du bsam/ / mgrin pa longs spyod ma la ya ru bsam/ / snying ga chos 'khor ri bo spos ngad ldan/ / lte ba sprul pa ri bo 'bigs byed de/ / gsang gnas bde skyong ri bo gangs can yin/ /

The inner Sudarśana is wherever one dwells, with oneself as the vaidūrya. Secret Sudarśana is found within one’s body. At the great-bliss cakra at the crown, see your mind as beryl light, see the enjoyment cakra at your throat as Malaya, see the dharma cakra at the heart as Gandhamārdana, see the emanation cakra at the navel as Vindhya, and see the nourishing-bliss cakra at the secret area as Himavat.

f.d: ri bo bzhi yi gnas su khyod song la/ / ri yi phan yon sman gyi skye gnas ltos/ / rgya gar yul nas gdams pa gnad ldan long / / bod yul dbus su gso dpyad sgron me spor/ / kha ba can ljongs 'gro mang skyob phyir du/ / mi lo brgya dang nyi shu rtsa lngar bzhugs/ / de nas sman gyi grong khyer lta sdug tu/ / dpa' bo rig 'dzin rnams kyi tshogs dpon la/ / the tshom yid gnyis mi dgos 'byon par nges/[208] / zhes sogs lung bstan dbugs dbyung gzengs bstod/

Go to these four mountains, see the qualities of these places of medicine, take the essence of the instructions from India, and light the lamp of medicine in the center of Tibet. So that you may care for many people of Tibet, you will live for 125 human years; then without doubt you will come to Sudarśana as lord of the ḍāka vidyādhara warriors.[433] This was followed by more prophecy, reassurance, and praise.

d.div: [208] sman bla'i zhal nas/ zhes sogs kyi lung bstan de phal cher sde srid kyis gong du smros pa'i g.yu thog gi rnam thar bka' rgya ma zhes pa de las drangs sam snyam mod rnam thar de'i dpe lag son ma gyur/
[433] Darmo Menrampa, Brilliant Jewel Treasury, p. 168.

f.d: ri bo bzhi sman rgyal gyi sprul pa dang bcas pa'ang zhib par mjal/ rgya gar bas mthar mo gling du tshud pa rdzu 'phrul gyis bar snang la 'phur/ mu stegs kyi ston pa smra ba zla med sgra tshad lung rigs kyi sgo nas btul ba sogs mdzad de gangs can ra ba dkar pos bres pa'i ljongs 'dir phebs/

Consequently, he went and saw in great detail the four medicine mountains and the emanations of Medicine Buddha that lived there. In a border land of India populated by women, he exhibited magical powers and flew into the sky.[434] Using language and logic, scripture and reasoning, he tamed the non-Buddhist teacher Advitīyavada. After these and other adventures, he returned to this land surrounded by its white ring of snowy mountains.

d.div: [434] He did this in order to escape, because they wanted to suck his blood and chop him to pieces.

f.d: klu'i rgyal po ma dros pa la btsun mo gsum yod pa'i rgan pa lta na sdug mthong dga' bro 'tshal ba la brten gdengs can gyi yul du gdan drangs pa ltar byon/ de dag mchod pa sna tshogs kyi las la brtson par ci byed gsungs pas/ klu ma rung pa rnams kyi kha gnon du sangs rgyas klu dbang gi rgyal po bzhugs pa la mchod pa byed zer/ de nas btsun mo nad las grol ba'i gsol ba btab pa bzhin/ g.yu thog pa nyid sman pa'i rgyal po'i skur bzhengs te nad pa gur kum gyi chus bkrus/ chab gtor dang klu gtor btang / klu gter bcug / bdud rtsi sman sgrub kyi dbang bskur / dngul chu rin chen sbyor ba khong du btang bas de ma thag nad las thar/ legs skyes su g.yu'i gdugs shig 'og tu rdo rje klu'i 'jim pa la sman gyi sku g.yu gdugs can du grags pa bzhengs nas phul/

Once he was invited to the land of the nāgas because Darśanīya, the eldest of the three queens of the nāga king Anavatapta, had fallen ill. While there he asked them why they were putting so much effort into making various offerings. They replied that they were making offerings to the buddha Nāgeśvara Rāja, who dwelt in their realm, in order to suppress the more unruly nāgas. In answer to the queen’s plea to him to cure her of the illness, Yuthok manifested as the king of medicine, washed the patient’s body with saffron water, offered a water torma and a nāga torma, performed a nāga treasure ritual, conferred the initiation for the achievement of ambrosia medicine, gave her the precious mercury compound, and she recovered at once. As a gift they presented him with a statue they had made from vajra nāga clay of Medicine Buddha under a turquoise parasol, which came to be known as the statue with the turquoise parasol.

phyi ltar lnga rig grub mchog sprul pa'i sku/ / nang du dug gsum nad sel sman pa'i rgyal/ / gsang ba kun 'dus grub pa kun tu bzang / / dbyer med gu Na khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ / zhes sogs bstod bsngags kyi me tog gtor/

Then they cast these flowers of praise:
Outwardly, an emanated form, supreme siddha of the five sciences, inwardly, the king of medicine, eliminating the three poisons inside: Samantrabhadra, all secrets gathered as one, these qualities indivisible, to you we bow.

khyad par du 'phags pa'i rten de g.yu thog pas bod yul du gdan drangs pa las rim pas rgyal khab chen po 'dir phebs/ rje bla ma srid zhi'i gtsug rgyan mchog 'gro ngor spyan mi gsal ba'i tshul bstan pa dbye ba'i dus 'di nyid gdan drangs te gsol ba 'debs pa gnang bas dpyad la cher ma bltos pa'i snyun las grol ba sogs thugs gtsigs nan tan che/ rin chen ril bu'i rab gnas kyang 'di nyid las legs par stsal ba sogs byin rlabs kyi gzi 'od dang ldan pas deng sang 'gro ba nad kyis mnar ba rnams kyi don 'chi gsos kyi bdud rtsi'i mdzod du bzhugs/ rje btsun g.yu thog pas rgya gar dang klu yul 'khor ba'i snyan grags kyis sa steng khyab/ byang chub rdo rje la sogs pa slob ma'ang mtha' yas pa byung / chos 'khor dpal gyi lha sar phebs/ jo bo shAkya mu ni dang rang byon lnga ldan la mu tig gis spras pa'i 'phan phul/ mi lnga stong tsam la chang tshul zla gcig btang /

This very special statue was brought by Yuthok to the land of Tibet and eventually came to this capital. Once my revered lama, crown jewel of samsara and nirvana, appeared, in the eyes of ordinary beings, to be suffering from poor sight. He called for this statue, made prayers to it, and without resorting to a great deal of medical treatment was cured of his ailment. Because of this and other incidents it is held in great esteem. It radiates blessings, such as granting the successful consecration of precious pills, and therefore remains to this day a repository of death-destroying ambrosia for living beings tormented by illness. After the noble Yuthok had been to India and to the land of the nāgas, his fame spread far and wide, and he amassed countless disciples, such as Jangchup Dorjé. When he came to the glorious Dharma wheel that is Lhasa, he ornamented Jowo Śākyamuni and the fivefold self-arisen statue with silk robes embroidered with pearls. He put on a month of festivities for about five thousand people.[435]

d.div: [435] Jowo Śākyamuni is the main statue of Buddha in the Jokhang temple in the heart of Lhasa. It was bridal gift to King Songtsen Gampo from his Chinese bride, Wen Cheng, in the seventh century. The fivefold self-arisen statue is a statue of eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara in a chapel of the Jokhang. It contains within a self-arisen sandalwood statue of the same deity. King Songtsen Gampo and his two brides also dissolved into the main statue, hence its name.

f.d: de nas yer par byon zla ba phug tu zhag lnga bzhugs/ sman gyi lha mo bdud rtsi ma byon nas g.yu thog gsar rnying gnyis kyi dbye ba yong tshul sogs 'byung 'gyur du ma gsungs/ bal po+o'i rgyal po ha d+ha ru grang ba thur babs kyis zin pa/ sman pa shrI sid+has lan tsha rus pa'i dug /chang sha'i dug /nyi ma pags pa'i dug /bud med lus zungs kyi dug ste bzhi spangs na tshe nyi zla dang mnyam par lung bstan pa bzhin byas pas phan bskyed ma byung / g.yu thog pas sngon bram ze skar mda' gdong bya bas gong gi dug bzhi spangs pa sha mig rus la thim/ pags pa rtsub cing rlung 'khrugs/ khu ba 'gags pas rde'ur song / lus kyi dgye sgu la rus pa chag nyams byed pa'i zug gzer yod pa gcig tu gyur ba/ sman gyi lha mos khyod kyis chang ma bsten pas sha skams grang rlung skya rbab kyis yan lag sbos/ nyi ma ma bsten pas rlung 'khrugs/ tshwa ma bsten pas rus pa 'grib/ bud med ma bsten pas khu ba 'gags pa yin zhes lung bstan nas nad las grol ba'i lo rgyus dang bcas bal rgyal gyi zug rngu sel bar mdzad/ sras 'bum seng la sogs pas dri ba zhus pa'i lan la/

Then he went to Yerpa where he stayed in Moon Cave for five days. The medicine goddess Amṛtā came to him and spoke of future events, such as the coming of a later Yuthok, how he would appear in the world, and so on. The Nepalese king Hadharu was ill with a disorder known as descending cold. His doctor, Śrī Siṃha, said that salt was poison to the bones, alcohol was poison to the flesh, the sun was poison to the skin, and women were poison to bodily tissue, and predicted that if the king abandoned these, his life would be as long as the sun and moon. The king had followed this advice, but it had not helped him at all. Yuthok told the king of the brahman Ulkāmukha, who had abandoned these four—his flesh and eyes had sunk into his bones, and his limbs were swollen, his skin was rough and troubled with wind disorders, his semen had solidified and had stopped flowing, and any physical movement gave him a pain, as though his bones were breaking. The medicine goddess told the brahman, “Because you have given up alcohol, you are emaciated, and the dropsy brought on by the cold and the wind element have made your limbs swell. Because you have given up sunlight, you are troubled by wind disorders. Because you no longer take salt, your bones are weak. Because you have given up women, your semen has stopped flowing.” The story continues with an account of how Yuthok cured the Nepalese king of his illness. In reply to questions put to him by his son Bumseng and others,

mkhas pa yon tan mgon po nga / / dang por skar ma dri ma med/ / bar du 'tsho byed gzhon nur grags/ / da lta g.yu thog yon tan mgon/ / 'di nas lta na sdug tu 'gro/ / drang srong rig 'dzin tshogs dpon byed/ / de nas rgya gar 'phags yul du/ / me lha phyag rdum zhes byar grags/ / de nas bod yul gangs can du/ / g.yu thog pa yi brgyud 'dzin sras/ / yon tan mgon por skye ba len/ / zhes sogs snga phyi'i skyes rabs gsungs/

Yuthok replied with details of his past and future lives:
I the wise Yönten Gönpo was Tāravimala early on; in between I was known as Kumāra Jivaka; and now I am Yuthok Yönten Gönpo. From here I will go to Sudarśana as head of the rishi vidyādharas. Again in India I will be Agnideva of amputated hand, and in Tibet, the land of snow, I will be Yuthok Gönpo, a son born of the Yuthok lineage.

sman blas lung bstan pa bzhin 'bum tsho'i sman chu ngos 'dzin dang rdo ring btsugs te dkar chag btab/ 'phags pa wa ti bzang po mjal bar byon/ zhal gser dang dkar me gya nom pa zhus/ cho 'phrul zla ba la sman bla drang song rig 'dzin sogs dpag tu med pa'i zhal gzigs/ drang srong chen po rA hu la dngos kyis gza' bcos zab khyad can phul/ lha sar jo bo rin po ches gsung byon/ ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma las khyi dug bcos pa la sogs pa'i gdams pa thob/ rgya nag ri bo rtse lngar phebs/ 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyis sbyor ba'i 'phreng ba dang byang khog don khrems sogs man ngag du ma gnang /

As prophesized by the medicine guru, he identified the medicinal spring of the seven hundred thousand qualities, and by the side of the spring he built a stone pillar inscribed with a list of the qualities. He went to Ārya Vati Sangpo, where he offered butter lamps and gold leaf to adorn the faces.[436] In the month of miracles[437] he had visions of countless medicine buddhas and rishi vidyādharas. The great rishi Rāhula came to him in person and offered him the profound treatment for planetary diseases. In Lhasa the Jowo Rinpoché statue gave him teachings. From a gnosis ḍākinī he received teachings on how to treat rabies, and so forth. He traveled to Mount Wutai in China, where the noble Mañjuśrī gave him many teachings, such as Garland of Medical Compunds and Exposition on the Abdomen.

d.div: [436] Ārya Vati Sangpo, in Mangyül near Tibet’s border with Nepal, is a pilgrimage site for viewing one of four statues of Avalokiteśvara constructed in Nepal from a single sandalwood tree.
[437] These days the “month of miracles” refers to the first Tibetan month.

f.d:
bya yul du bar snang 'ja' 'od 'khyil ba'i dbus nas sangs rgyas sman pa'i rgyal pos/
dang po'i dus na skar ma dri ma med/ / bar du gzhon nu 'jigs med grags pa yin/ / da lta g.yu thog yon tan mgon por grags/ / 'di nas sman gyi grong khyer lta sdug tu/ / drang srong rig 'dzin rnams kyi tshogs dpon mdzad/ / de nas snyigs ma lnga bdo'i dus babs la/ / nged kyi gsung sprul skyes bu dam pa khyod/ / g.yu thog gsar ma zhes byar rab grags pa/ / yon tan mgon po zhes bya 'byung zhing 'byon/ / sman phreng sman sgrub nyams len rgyas par byed/[209] / ces sogs gsung gi gnang ba mang du stsal/

In Jayül he saw Medicine Buddha amid a swirl of rainbow light in the sky granting him many gifts with his speech, such as:
In the beginning you were Tāravimala, then you became Kumāra Abhayakīrti, now you are known as Yuthok Yönten Gönpo. From here you will go to Sudarśana, as head of the rishi vidyādharas. Then in times of the five degenerations, great being and incarnation of my speech, you Yönten Gönpo will come again to be known as the new Yuthok and spread the Garland of Ambrosia Medicine and Ambrosia Medicine Practice.[438]

d.div: [209] g.yu thog gsar rnying gi rnam thar/ g.yu thog rnying ma'i rnam thar/ shog_248_phreng 11
[438] Darmo Menrampa, Brilliant Jewel Treasury, p. 256.

f.d: mkha' 'gro'i lung bstan ltar sras g.yu thog 'bum seng / dpal 'bum/ dga' dga' gsum bskrun/ dgung lo brgya dang nyi shu rtsa lnga'i bar 'gro ba'i don rlabs po cher mdzad pa'i mthar ye shes mkha' 'gros spyan drangs te sku lus ma spangs par sangs rgyas sman bla'i zhing du gshegs/

As the ḍākinīs prophesied, he had three sons, Bumseng, Palbum, and Gagang. He brought huge benefits to others, working tirelessly until he was one hundred and twenty-five years old. Finally, he was summoned by Yeshé Khadro[439] and, without leaving his bodily form, went to the pure land of Medicine Buddha.

d.div: [439] Consort of Padmasambhava.

f.d: [g.yu thog gsar ma ]

d.i: The contribution of the later Yuthok Yönten Gyatso

f.d: g.yu thog gsar ma ni/ 'dre rje la rgya rag ka ba 'phrang gi gdug 'dres bud med g.yu rgyan mchor ba'i ro las dngos grub byin pa sogs gtam rgyud snga ma ltar 'chad pa 'dug ste/ blun po zhig gi zhwa dpe lham 'gebs kyi legs par ma mngon/ stod lung skyid sna'i rigs las 'chad pa'i gdung rabs bcu gsum pa na gtsang nyang stod kyi sa'i cha sgo bzhi re thang du yab g.yu thog khyung po rdo rje dang yum pad+ma 'od ldan ma gnyis kyi sras su dge legs kyi mtshan ma bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang bcas 'khrungs/ drang srong rig 'dzin rnams kyis byin gyis rlabs shing sman gyi lha mos sku khrus gsol/ chung ngu nas las bzang po sad de sman gyi ngos 'dzin la sogs pa 'khrul med du mkhyen/

Those accounts of the coming of the later Yuthok that talk of the demon of Brass Pillar path granting Drejé Gyagar a siddhi using the corpse of a woman laden with turquoise, and so on—similar to accounts found in the biography of the earlier Yuthok—are words of the fool who uses a hat as a boot and are not correct. In the thirteenth generation of the Tölung Kyina family, in Goshi Rethang in the upper Nyang River region of Tsang, he was born to father Yuthok Khyungpo Dorjé and mother Pema Ödenma amid wondrous and unimaginable signs. He was blessed by the vidyādhara rishis and washed by the medicine goddesses. Virtuous karma awoke in him from an early age, and he was able to recognize various medicines and so on without mistake.

gsung las/
kho bo g.yu thog mgon po yi/ / lo brgyad lon nas sman dpyad bskyangs/[210] / zhes gsungs pa ltar dgung lo brgyad pa'i thog mgon po 'jam dpal dbyangs kyis rjes su bzung bas rig pa'i gnas spyi dang / khyad par gso ba rig pa la mkhas par gyur te 'gro phan gyi spyod yul bskyangs/ dgung lo bcu pa'i tshe grub pa'i lha mos da ste lo gnyis nas bdud rtsi snying po yan lag brgyad pa gsang ba man ngag gi rgyud dang mjal bar lung bstan pa bzhin/ mang mkhar tsha lung ba rog ston dkon cog skyabs sgo bzhi re thang du byon par/ rgyas pa 'bum dang rta sga srab bcas pa sogs 'bul ba gya nom pa phul te dpal ldan rgyud bzhi rdzogs par zhus/ re zhig chig brgyud kyi bka' rgya ma bkrol bar rang gi zab bzhes su mdzad/

As he himself said:
At the age of eight I, Yuthok Gönpo, nurtured the science of medicine.[440] From the age of eight onward, he was cared for by the noble guide Mañjuśrī and became wise in the sciences, especially in the science of medicine, and nurtured and developed an attitude of working for others. At the age of ten a longevity goddess prophesized that in two years he would meet the Essence of Ambrosia Secret Instruction Tantra on Eight Branches. Accordingly, Roktön Könchok Kyap from Mangkhar Tsalung came to Goshi Rethang. There Yuthok made him a grand offering of the Hundred Thousand Verse Perfection of Wisdom Sutra as well as smaller offerings, including a saddle and bridle, and in return he received Four Tantras in its entirety. For a while he did not release this work from its seal of being a one-to-one transmission and kept it for his own practice.

d.div: [210] g.yu thog snying thig gi chos skor/ g.yu thog snying thig las byin rlabs bla ma sgrub pa' cho+is skor sdug bsngal mun sel thugs rje'i nyi 'od ces pa'i thog mar lo rgyus dge ba'i lcags kyu/ shog_16_na5
[440] Darmo Menrampa, Biography of the Younger Yuthok Yönten Gönpo, p. 325.

f.d: dgung lo bco brgyad pa la rgya gar du phebs/ ku da'i zhing du ye shes mkha' 'gro'i gtso mo dpal ldan phreng ba la lcang lo nag po'i rgyud/ wa ra NA sir bdud rtsi snying po yan lag brgyad pa/ sau ma rA dza/ phan pa'i mdo/ rin chen spungs pa/ ku mu da/ reg pa rtsa mdo/ srog skyob ti ka / sing+ga la'i gling du zla zer dkar nag / bdud rtsi bum pa che 'bring chung gsum/ rgyal po'i khab tu dpa' bo'i bstan bcos yan lag brgyad pa/ 'khrungs dpe che chung / rdo sbyor gab pa/ gser gling du drang srong phyogs kyi go char rgyud bzhi/ nyi zla kha sbyor dang sha khrag 'tsho ba/ srog chags sgrol ba/ sgrol ma 'byung / gser sogs rin po che'i bzo/ gro kha'i 'debs ma/ 'jam dpal yab yum/ seng sgrom/ dpa' bo 'ching 'grol/ ro bkra/ bsil bu/ 'byung ba so so/ rtsa mdo chen po/ snying po bstan pa/ lus kyi rnam gzhag bdud rtsi them yig /rig pa rtsa dpyad/ rgya yig smra chung / gu Na sha gra rnams kyi rgyud/ bam bo sum brgya pa/

At the age of eighteen he went to India. In the land of Kuda he received the Tantra of the Black Lock of Hair from Śrīmālā, head of the gnosis ḍākinīs. In Vārāṇasī he received Essence of Ambrosia Eight Branches, the Somarāja, the Sutra of Help, the Heap of Jewels,[441] the Kumuda Flower, the Sutra on Pulse, and the Commentary on Protecting Life. In the country of Singhal[442] he received black and white editions of Candranandana’s Moonlight, the extensive, intermediate, and short exposition of the Ambrosia Vase. In Rājagṛha he received Śūra’s treatise on the eight branches, the extensive and short Illustrations of Medical Plants, and the Secret Preparations of Minerals. In Suvarṇadvīpa[443] from the rishi Kanakavarman he received Four Tantras and the following tantras: the Union of Sun and Moon, the Nourishing Flesh and Blood, the Liberation of Beings, the Arising of Tārā, the Craft of Precious Stones and Metals Such as Gold, the Leaves of the Birch Tree, the Mañjuśrī Mother and Father, the Hide Casket, the Ḍāka Liberation, the Chapter on Anatomy, the Fragment Transmission, the Individual Elements, the Great Treatise on the Pulse, the Teaching of the Essence, the Ambrosia Inscriptions on Presentation of the Body, the Examination of the Pulse, the Brief Indian Work, the Guṇaśāstra, and the Three Hundred Fasicles.

d.div: [441] There are multiple instances of a text of this name. Whether they all refer to the same work I cannot say. For sure, they do not refer to the Ratnakūṭa Sutra.
[442] Present-day Sri Lanka (Dungkar, p. 2040).
[443] Sometimes identified as Sumatra.

f.d: ka la'i tshal gyi nags gseb cig tu lha mo bdud rtsi ma dang mjal rjes su bzung nas zhus lan skor gsum dang rma rtsi 'chi med bcad sbyor gnang / slar yang be da'i gling du lha mo des mchog thun gyi dngos grub du ma dang gso dpyad sgron ma skor gsum stsal te lam gyi 'jigs pa rgyal po'i chad pa dang / dug sbrul/ glang chen/ stag zig /dom dred/ chom rkun sogs thams cad kyis skad cig kyang ma gnod par bod yul gyi shangs dpal skyes su phyag phebs/ bu dang slob ma 'du ba'i smon lam rgya cher btab/ sman dpyad gtso bor gyur ba'i 'gro phan skyong ba'i mur/ lha mo bdud rtsi mas rgya gar du byon zhig pa'i lung bstan pa ltar lam du zhugs/ rim pas paN grub drang srong du ma dang mjal/ mkha' 'gro'i gtso mo dpal ldan 'phreng bas yan lag brgyad pa bsil zer gyi gnad rgyud rigs drug cu rtsa lnga dang / zab pa las kyang ches zab pa rdo rje theg pa'i gsang ba'i lam gyi gdams pa mkha' 'gro'i snying khrag lta bu lung bstan dang bcas pa gnang /

In the middle of a forest called Kala he met goddess Amṛtā. She took care of him and gave him Three Collections of Question and Answer, and Ambrosia Preparation for Healing Wounds. Later, in the region of Vedha, he met the goddess again, and she bestowed upon him many ordinary and supreme siddhis and gave him the three collections on the Beacon Medical Texts, and on his journeys he was not harmed for a moment by the punishments of rulers, poisonous snakes, elephants, tigers, leopards, bears, robbers, and so forth. He arrived in the Shang Palkyé region of Tibet, and there he made many prayers for gathering disciples and bearing sons, working and caring for others mainly in the field of medicine. Then in accordance with the prophecy of the goddess Amṛta he again set off for India. Over time he met with many pandits and siddhas there. Śrīmālā, chief of the gnosis ḍākinīs, gave him the Sixty-Five Classes of Moonbeam Essential Tantras on the Eight Branches and teachings on the more-profound-than-profound secret Vajrayana path, such as Heart Blood of the Ḍākinī.

snga phyir 'phags yul du lan drug phebs par grags/ de dag tu rdzu 'phrul gyi bkod pa bstan pa bsam las 'das shing / khyad par mu stegs kyi ston pa lnga brgya sgra tshad rig pas tshar bcad de nang pa'i bstan par btsud/ lho phyogs dpal gyi rir byon pa'i lam du mi rgod kyi jag pas 'joms par nye ba lta stangs mdzad pa tsam gyis rengs/ a+yon gyi yul du sha za mkha' 'gro mas gnam lcags phab pa sdigs mdzub kyis rtser blangs te phyir 'phangs/ sing+ga la'i gling gi mtshor gru rdzings su zhugs pa'i tshe mu stegs kyi ngan sngags kyi mthus gru zhig pa na nam mkhar bya bzhin 'phur/ ka la'i tshal du dug sbrul gyi kha rlangs mun ltar gtibs pa snying rje chen po bsgoms pas zhi/ ri rab ri bran bcas par thogs med du 'byon/ brtan g.yo'i dngos po kun lag mthil skyu ru'i rnam pa bzhin gzigs/ bal yul du bon dang rdzu 'phrul 'gran par nyi phyed kyi ring nam mkhar bzhugs/ bka' rin po che 'gyur ro cog dang bstan 'gyur thugs thog nas 'chad/ rdo rje gdan du paN chen brgya phrag du ma'i tshogs dpon mdzad/ rgya gar dang bod yul gyi bar nyin gcig la chod pas a ru ra rlon pa lo ma dang bcas pa dang / me tog so ma skyes su bsnams nas 'byon pa sogs gsung las/

It is said that he traveled to India six times. On those journeys he gave indescribable displays of his magic powers. In particular he defeated five hundred non-Buddhist teachers using language and logic and converted them to the Buddhist path. In Śrīparvata, in the south of the country, he was accosted by a group of wild bandits on the road, but he gave them a wrathful stare that paralyzed them on the spot. In Oḍḍiyāna angry gandharva ḍākinīs hurled a thunderbolt at him, but with his fingers in the threatening gesture, he caught it and threw it back. Once when he was in a boat off the country of Singhal, a outsider black magician caused the boat to sink, but he flew up into the sky like a bird. When a snake in the forest of Kala caused the air to become thick and dense with its poisonous exhalations, he meditated on great compassion and immediately pacified the snake. He traveled unimpeded through Meru and the lesser mountains. He could see all animate and inanimate phenomena as clear as a berry in the palm of his hand. In Nepal, in a competition of magical powers with followers of Bön, he sat in the sky for half a day. He could recite from heart all the precious teachings of the Buddha and the commentaries, and he became supreme among the hundreds of pandits in Vajrāsana. He traveled from India to Tibet in one day and was able to bring as gifts fresh myrobalan with its leaves and soma flowers. In his own words:

nga mkha' la 'phur na bya ltar 'gro/ / chu la 'gro na nya ltar 'dzul/ / ri bo 'bigs na gnam lcags thog / me dpung dbus na me lha yin/ / dus snyigs ma'i sems can bsod nams chung / / nga mthong nga ming thos pa nyung / / mthong thos dran reg dad pa la/ / byang chub bla med myur du bskrun/ / bskal bar bsags pa'i sdig pa sbyong /[211] / zhes dang /
zhing khams brgya ru dus gcig bgrod/ / sangs rgyas brgya dang dus gcig mjal/ / sprul pa brgya yang dus gcig 'gyed/ / sems can brgya ni dus gcig 'dren/ / zad par zil gnon thams cad 'grub/[212] / ces zad par zil gyis gnon pa'i skye mched thob pas sprul bsgyur brjod las 'das/

Flying through the sky I am like a bird, moving through the water I am like a fish, penetrating mountains I am a thunderbolt, amid fire I am the fire god. In these degenerate times beings have little merit, few have seen me, few hear my name. Those who see, hear, remember, and touch me with faith will soon come to unsurpassed enlightenment and purify the unwholesome deeds of an eon.[444] Also:
I travel at one time to a hundred worlds, meet at one time a hundred buddhas, send out at one time a hundred emanations, bring in at one time a hundred sentient beings; I have attained every eclipsing samādhi.[445] Because he had achieved the bases of the totally eclipsing meditative concentrations,[446] his host of emanations were beyond description.

d.div: [211] g.yu thog gsar rnying gi rnam thar/ g.yu thog gsar ma'i rnam thar/ shog_332_phreng 21
[212] g.yu thog gsar rnying gi rnam thar/ g.yu thog gsar ma'i rnam thar/ shog_330_phreng 15
[444] Darmo Menrampa, Biography of the Younger Yuthok Yönten Gönpo, p. 332.

[446] Zad par zil gyid gnon pa’i skye mched. A group of samādhis, or meditative concentrations, focused on the elements, shapes, colors, and so on, in which the appearance of the object appears however one wishes and totally eclipses all other appearances.

f.d: sku tshe'i stod du yan lag brgyad pa kho na'i 'phrin las bskyangs/ de nas rtsa dpyad rig pa rang gsal sde tshan lnga pa/ lag len po ta chung / rgyud chung bdud rtsi snying po/ shog dril skor gsum/ lde mig skor drug sogs brtsams/

In the early part of his life he worked solely with the eight branches. Later he composed Naturally Illuminating Knowledge of Pulse Examination in five sections, Small Volume on Practice, the Ambrosia Essence Short Tantra, the Three Scroll Collections, the Six Key Collections, and many more.
rgyal ba'i bka'i rnam gzhag
11. The Word of the Buddha

dpal ldan rgyud bzhi 'di nyid gso dpyad kun gyi yang rtser gzigs nas phyi rabs kyi don du bka' rgya bkrol te lus can kun gyi spyi nor du spel/ 'gyur gsar du bcos shing yul dus gnas skabs dang bstun pa'i bsnan kha'ang gsham smos ltar mdzad/ bu'i don du gser mchan dang slob ma'i ngor zong mchan zhes pas mang nyung gnyis bkod/

Yuthok Yönten Gönpo realized that the glorious Four Tantras were the very pinnacle of medical science, and so for the sake of future generations, he released them from the seal of being purely a one-to-one transmission and propagated them as crown jewels to be venerated by all living beings. He revised the translation and, as I describe later, made additions to accord with time, place, and conditions. He also composed Golden Annotations for his sons, and Copper[447] Annotations for his disciples.

d.div: [447] Text has zong, but Prof. Losang Tenzin says it should be read as zangs.

f.d:
de la brten nas rgyud bzhi bka' yin min/ de las 'phros te bka' dang bstan bcos 'gal ba'i lugs dang mi 'gal ba'i lugs sna tshogs kyang rgyas bshad ni gzhan du smos la/ bka' 'am dam pa'i chos de yang / bla med pha rgyud rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi le'u dgu pa las/
chos kyi phung po brgyad khri dang / / bzhi stong gi ni grangs snyed kyi/ / mtshan gyi don ni 'di don du/ / yang dag 'dus par ngas bshad do/[213] / zhes dang / rnal 'byor rgyud kyi bshad rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba'i le'u dang po las/
dpal ldan 'dus par brda tsam gang / / rnal 'byor bla na med rgyud du/ / thub pa chen pos chos phung po/ / brgyad khri dang ni bzhi stong ngo /[214] / zhes dang / theg chen rnams bya ba'i rgyud du gtogs pa tshe dang ye shes dpag tu med pa'i mdor/
gang zhig mdo sde 'di yi ger 'bri'am/ 'brir 'jug na/ des chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong 'drir bcug par 'gyur ro/[215] / zhes dang /

These deeds have given rise to various positions on whether Four Tantras is the actual word of Buddha or not, and consequently on whether the actual teachings of the Buddha and the later commentaries are mutually exclusive or not. These points have been dealt with extensively elsewhere. However, on the subject of what constitutes the word of Buddha, or the sacred Dharma, the highest yoga father tantra Vajra Essence Ornament states in its ninth chapter:
The meanings of the 84,000 collections of Dharma I have condensed as this.[448] Also, in the first chapter of the Vajra Garland Tantra it says:
In brief, in the glorious Guhyasamāja, the 84,000 collections of Dharma of the Buddha in the form of the highest of yoga tantras. Also, in the Sutra of Limitless Life and Gnosis, which can be classified as either a Mahayana sutra or an action tantra:
By copying or encouraging someone to copy this sutra, one encourages the copying of the 84,000 collections of Dharma.[449]

d.div: [213] sde dge_451_bka'/ rgyud/ cha_dpal rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi rgyud/ le'u/ 9_shog_50_na7
[214] sde dge_445_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_bshad rgyud rdo rje phreng ba/ le'u/ 1_shog_210_ba4

[448] Vajrahṛdayālaṃkaratantra, chap. 9, Toh 451 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 50a7.
[449] Aparimitāyurjñāna, Toh 675 Kangyur, rgyud, ba, 218b1.

f.d:
gnyis med dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i 'grel chen dri med 'od kyi mdor bsdus gnyis pa las/
de'i phyir sems can gyi bsam pa'i dbang gis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad theg pa gsum ston par byed pa po dang chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong ston par byed pa po yin no/ /[216] zhes sogs spyir chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong spom bshad kyi rigs dang /

In the second summary of the nondual tantra, Stainless Light Great Commentary to the Kālacakra, it says:
Therefore, because of the dispositions of sentient beings, all tathāgatas teach the three vehicles and teach the 84,000 collections of Dharma.[450] These and other citations belong to the category of passages that talk of the Dharma in general terms as a collection of 84,000 categories or collections.

d.div: [216] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_dus 'khor rtsa rgyud/(rigs ldan pad+ma dkar po/ 'grel chen dri med 'od/) shog_16_na5
[450] Puṇḍarīka, Vimalaprabhā, Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 16a5.

f.d:
rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud don la 'jug pa slob dpon shrang+ng+hA ka ra wa rma'am dad byed go chas mdzad pa lo chen rin bzang gi 'gyur las/
de la bcom ldan 'das kyis chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong bka' stsal pa de dag kyang 'bras bu'i tshul gyis theg pa gcig tu 'dus te/ theg pa chen po'o/[217] / zhes dang /
theg pa chen po la'ang rnam pa gnyis te sa dang pha rol tu phyin pa'i theg pa dang / gsang sngags 'bras bu rdo rje'i theg pa'o/[218] / zhes byung bas theg pa ni yA na'i sgra las bzhon pa ste gdul bya'i blo'i theg tshad dang sbyar ba'i che chung gi rim pa yin la/ sde snod ni pi Ta ka'i sgras gong bu'am bsdus pa'i don/

In the Understanding Highest Yoga Tantras by Ācārya Śraddhakara Varman and translated by Lotsāwa Rinchen Sangpo it says:
The Bhagavān taught 84,000 collections of Dharma. These are also included in the one resultant vehicle. Thus it is the great vehicle.[451] Also:
The great vehicle is of two kinds: the vehicle of the levels and perfections, and the resultant secret-mantra vajra vehicle.[452] The term “vehicle” comes from the Sanskrit yāna meaning “mount,”[453] and that can be great or small when applied to the size of the vehicle of the minds of disciples. In this connection, the term “basket” is piṭaka in Sanskrit and means a “collection” or “compilation.”

d.div: [217] sde dge_3713_bstan/ rgyud 'grel / tsu_slob dpon shra d+d+hA ka ra wa rma/ rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud kyi don la 'jug pa bsdus pa/ shog_104_ba5
[218] sde dge_3713_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tsu_slob dpon shra d+d+hA ka ra wa rma/ rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud kyi don la 'jug pa bsdus pa/ shog_105_na7
[451] Yogānuttaratantārthāvatārasaṃgraha, Toh 3713 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tsu, 104b5.
[453] Gshon pa. As a verb this is the past and future of zhon pa, “to ride,” and as a noun it refers to that which is to be ridden—say a horse or a mule.

f.d:
theg chen la'ang sde snod gsum dang / theg chung la'ang nyan thos lta bu'i sde snod gsum du bshad pas ming 'dogs lugs tha dad kyang don mi 'gal bas gsang sngags kyang chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong la 'dus par song ba dang / yang de nyid las/
gsang sngags kyi theg pa sde snod gsum du 'dus par yang 'chad de/ gsung rab yan lag dgu ni theg pa chen po'i sde snod yin la/ gsang sngags kyi thog ma'i sde snod kyang gsung rab yan lag dgur 'dus shing / bslab pa gsum ston pa'i phyir sde snod gsum du bzhag go[219] / zhes gsang sngags kyang chos phung du gtogs pa ches gsal ba'i rigs dang /

The three baskets apply to the great vehicle as well as to the small vehicle, as in the three baskets of the śrāvakas for example. So, although they are different in terms of their names, in actuality “vehicle” and “basket” are not mutually exclusive. Therefore, secret mantra too is included in the 84,000 collections of Dharma. Furthermore, the same text says:
The secret mantra vehicle is explained as being included in the three baskets. This is because the nine categories of scripture are the basket of the great vehicle, and the basket of the secret-mantra vehicle is included in the nine categories of scripture. Secret mantra is also included in the three baskets because it teaches the three trainings.[454] The above citations belong to the category of passages that clearly teach secret mantra as being included in the collections of Dharma.

d.div: [219] sde dge_3713_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tsu_slob dpon shra d+d+hA ka ra wa rma/ rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud kyi don la 'jug pa bsdus pa/ shog_106_na4
[454] Yogānuttaratantārthāvatārasaṃgraha, Toh 3713 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tsu, 106a4.

f.d:
gsang sngags snga 'gyur du/ thang yig shel brag ma'i le'u nyer bdun par/
nyon mongs 'dod chags 'dul ba'i gnyen po ru: 'dul ba'i sde snod nyi khri chig stong gsungs: nyon mongs zhe sdang 'dul ba'i gnyen po ru: mdo sde'i sde snod nyi khri chig stong gsungs: nyon mongs gti mug 'dul ba'i gnyen po ru: mngon pa'i sde snod nyi khri chig stong gsungs: dug gsum cha mnyam 'dul ba'i gnyen po ru: gsang sngags sde snod nyi khri chig stong gsungs: chos kyi sgo mo brgyad khri bzhi stong de: bsdu na gsung rab yan lag bcu gnyis 'du: bsdus pas 'dul ba mdo sde mngon pa gsum:[220] zhes dang /

Concerning the early translations, the twenty-seventh verse of the Crystal Rock Lotus Chronicle states:
As an antidote to cure the affliction of desire he taught the 21,000 baskets of Vinaya. As an antidote to cure the affliction of anger he taught the 21,000 baskets of Sutra. As an antidote to cure the affliction of ignorance he taught the 21,000 baskets of Abhidharma. As an antidote to cure the three poisons equally, he taught 21,000 baskets of secret mantra. These are the 84,000 gateways to Dharma, compiled to form the twelve categories of scripture, condensed as Sutra, Abhidharma, and Vinaya.[455]

d.div: [220] pad+ma bka' thang / le'u nyer bdun pa/ shog_179_yig phreng 6
[455] Orgyen Lingpa, Lotus Chronicles, 27.179.6.

f.d:
rig pa rang shar gyi rgyud las/
theg pa'i dbye ba 'di lta ste/ / mdo dang rgyas pa chen po dang / / shin tu'ang rgyas pa chen po'o/ /

The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
The vehicle divisions are as follows: the sutras, the vast and great, and the even vaster and greater.

d.div: shin tu rgyas pa chen po ni/ / brgyad khri bzhi stong bsam mi khyab/ / rgya che grangs mang chen po ste/ / bsam gyis mi khyab gzhal du med/ / brjod med bsam 'das chen po'o/ /
The even vaster and greater is the 84,000 beyond conception, vast, numerous, and great, beyond conception, immeasurable, indescribable, and beyond thought.

rgyas pa chen po 'di lta ste/ / dbye ba rnam pa dgur 'dod do/ / nyan thos dang ni rang rgyal dang / / de bzhin byang chub sems dpa'o/ / kri ya dang ni u pa dang / / de bzhin yo ga'i theg par bshad/ / ma hA a nu yo ga dang / / de bzhin rdzogs chen a ti'o/ / de ltar rnam pa dgur bshad de/ / chos kyi bstan pa chen po yin/ /

The vast and great is divided into nine: those of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, the vehicles of kriya, upa, and yoga, mahāyoga, anuyoga, and Great Perfection ati. This is the great doctrine of Dharma explained in nine aspects.[456]
[456] Collected Tantras of the Nyingma, vol. 10, no. 153. Unable to locate citation within this text.

f.d:
zhes pa'i don klong chen pas theg mchog mdzod du bstan pa ni/
spyir sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi rnam grangs mtha' yas kyang / theg pa tsam du bsdu na/ theg pa mdor bstan pa che chung gnyis sam/ rgyu mtshan nyid kyi theg pa dang / 'bras bu rdo rje'i theg pa yin la/ rgyas par bshad na/ dbang po dman pa gsum la/ nyan thos rang rgyal byang chub sems dpa' gsum gyi theg pa dang / 'bring po gsum la/ kri ya u pa yo ga gsum dang / rnon po gsum la/ ma hA a nu a ti gsum gsungs te/ a ti bkod pa chen po las/
ngas bstan pa yi chos rnams ni/ / sems can blo yi rim pa las/ / che dang chung ba'i khyad par gyis/ / rim pa gnyis kyi tshul du bstan/ / rang rang lta dang sor bzhag go/ /

Longchenpa explains these verses in his Treasury of the Supreme Vehicle, where he says:
Generally speaking, the different Dharmas of the Buddha are beyond number. When they are compiled into vehicles, however, we can make an abridged classification into great and small vehicles, or causal vehicle and resultant vajra vehicle. To expand on these, the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva vehicles are the three types of beings with lesser faculties. The kriya, upa, and yoga vehicles are for those of middling faculties, while the mahā, anu, and ati are for those of the sharpest faculties. In the Great Presentation of Atiyoga it says:
The doctrine I have taught is of two levels, characterized as lesser or great according to levels of sentient beings’ minds, each possessing their own particular views.

d.div:
rang rang nyid ni rim pa gnyis/ / phyin ci log dang yang dag lta/ / log par rtogs pas 'khor la gnas/ / yang dag pa ni rim gsum ste/ / chung ba'i blo dang chen po dang / / de bzhin 'bring po'i blo can la/ / rim pa gsum gyi tshul du bstan/ /
chung ba'i rim pa rnam gsum ste/ / de yi blo dang mthun pa'i chos/ / rtog pas sbags la nyan thos so/ / 'du shes can la rang rgyal te/ / rtog 'dzud can la byang sems so/ /
'bring po gsum la bstan pa ni/ / rab tu dman la bya ba ste/ / dman pa rnams la spyod pa'o/ / rnam shes can la rnal 'byor nyid/ /
chen po rim ldan gsum dag la/ / sems yas pa la bskyed pa ste/ / sems bcud can la rdzogs pa'o/ / mchog gsang rab la rdzogs pa che/[221] / ces so//

div.div: Each is of two levels: of wrong views and of right. Those of wrong views dwell in samsara, those of right views are of three levels: those taught for lesser minds, those for middling minds, and those for great minds.

Those of lesser minds are three, and the doctrines taught according to their minds are that of the śrāvaka taught to those tainted by concepts, that of the pratyekabuddha taught to those with discernment, that of the bodhisattva taught to those who penetrate concepts.
Those of middling minds are also three, and the doctrines taught to them are kriya to the very low, carya to the low, and yoga to those of higher consciousness.
For those three of the sharpest minds, there is generation for those beyond mind, completion for those with the essence of mind, the Great Perfection for those of the supreme and most secret.[457]

d.div: [221] klong chen rabs 'byams pa'i gsung 'bum/ ga theg pa'i mchog rin po che'i mdzod ces bya ba/ shog_38_ba5
[457] Longchenpa, Treasury of the Supreme Vehicle, 38b5.

f.d: shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i theg pa ni/ bka' thams cad sde snod gsum la 'du la/ sngags rnams ni mngon pa chen po yin pas mdo sde dang / 'dul ba dang / mngon pa dang / de gsum cha mnyam ste bzhi so so la nyis khri chig stong res spyir chos kyi phung po brgyad khri dang bzhi stong ste/ de las kyang phye na sems can gyi rtog tshogs 'dul ba'i gnyen po re re la ltos nas rgya che la grangs mang zhing bsam gyis mi khyab brjod las 'das shing /[222] rdzogs chen sems sde/ klong sde/ man ngag gi sde gsum rang la'ang nang gses kyi grangs ni/

For the even vaster and greater vehicle, all the teachings of the Buddha are included in the three baskets, and mantra is in the basket of great Abhidharma. With 21,000 categories each in the baskets of Sutra, Vinaya, and Abhidharma and 21,000 more distributed among all three baskets equally, there are generally speaking 84,000 collections of Dharma. However, on the basis of individual antidotes for pacifying the hosts of conceptions found in sentient beings, these can be expanded even further to become “vast and numerous, inconceivable and indescribable.” The three divisions of the Great Perfection—namely the mind, sphere, and precept divisions—also have further divisions.

d.div: [222] klong chen rabs 'byams pa'i gsung 'bum/ ga theg pa'i mchog rin po che'i mdzod ces bya ba/ shog_38_ba5

f.d:
thal 'gyur las/
rang bzhin rdzogs pa chen po las/ / tshig gi bye brag rnam 'phros pa/ / sde gsum las ni klong dgur 'gyur/ / tshig sdud pa las sh+loka / 'bum phrag drug cu rtsa bzhi las/ / le'u stong phrag sum cu lnga/ / bam po nyi khri stong phrag gcig / brjod bya nam mkha'i mtha' dang mnyam/ / gdul bya'i sems can rtog pa gcod/ / 'di las brjod bya nyer bsdus pa/ / gzer bu brgya dang brgyad cu la/ / gegs ni stong phrag phyed dang gnyis/ / gnad chen 'dus pa stong phrag gsum/ / gol sgrib khri phrag bzhi bcu la/ / ming thogs rgyud ni khri phrag gnyis/ / tshig brjod rim pa gsal bkod do/ / zhes bshad pa de dag kyang sde snod kyi dbang du byas na mngon pa chen po'i sde snod du bsdu bas chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong la mdo sngags gnyis ka 'dus par snga 'gyur rdo rje theg pa'i lugs su'ang bshad/[223]

The Consequence says:
From the natural great perfection appear the specifics of words; from the three divisions come the nine spheres. From the compilation of words come verses numbering 6,400,000, in chapters numbering 35,000, in categories numbering 21,000, of content equal to the reaches of space, severing the conceptions of sentient beings. From these come the compilations of topics: in 180 rivets are 1,500 hindrances[458] and 3,000 essential points. On the 400,000 mistakes are 20,000 name-bearing tantras, word and content clearly arranged.[459] In terms of the three baskets, these passages place secret mantra in the basket of great Abhidharma. Therefore, even the early translations include both sutra and tantra in the 84,000 collections of Dharma.

d.div: [223] thal 'gyur las / rang bzhin rdzogs pa chen po las/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[458] Gegs, although other editions have gags. The Nyingma School of Tibetan Buddhism, p. 333, has ’gags, translated as “conclusion.”
[459] Untraced.

f.d:
gzhan yang mtshan brjod kyi 'grel pa rigs ldan pad ma dkar pos mdzad pa dri med 'od las/
theg pa gsum gyis nges 'byung la/ /zhes pa nyan thos rang rgyal byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa'o/ / theg pa gcig gis 'bras bur gnas/ /zhes pa dbyer mi phyed pa gsang sngags rdo rje'i theg par gsum po yang 'dus pa'o/[224] / zhes dang /

Furthermore, the Stainless Light Commentary on the Mañjuśrī Saṃgīti by Kalkī Puṇḍarīka says:
“Arising by way of three vehicles” refers to the vehicles of the pratyekabuddha, śrāvaka, and bodhisattva. “Dwelling in the one resultant vehicle” refers to the three vehicles included in the indivisible secret-mantra vajra vehicle.[460]

d.div: [224] sde dge_1398_bka'/ rgyud 'grel/ pha_rigs ldan pad+ma dkar po/ 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyi mtshan yang dag par brjod pa'i 'grel pa dri ma med pa'i 'od ces bya ba/ shog_225_ba3
[460] Mañjuśīnāmasaṃgīṭīkāvimalaprabhā, Toh 1398 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, pha, 225b3.

f.d:
mkhas mchog bu ston gyi rgyud sde spyi rnam du/
sde snod dag ni gsum mam gnyis kyang rung / /zhes theg pa dman pa'i sde snod dang / theg pa chen po'i sde snod gnyis su 'dus la/ theg pa chen po'i sde snod la yang rgyu mtshan nyid kyi theg pa dang / 'bras bu sngags kyi theg pa gnyis [225] zhes byung ba dang /

The great scholar Butön says in his General Presentation of the Tantras:
“The baskets of scripture number three or two” means that the baskets of scripture may be divided into the smaller-vehicle basket and the great-vehicle basket. The basket of the great vehicle in turn can be divided into the causal sutra vehicle and the resultant vajra vehicle.[461]

d.div: [225] bu ston rin chen grub kyi gsung 'bum/ brgyud sde spyi'i rnam par gzhag pa rgyud sde thams cad kyi gsang ba gsal bar byed pa zhes bya ba/ shog_2_ba5
[461] Collected Works, ba, 2b5.

f.d:
'jam mgon btsong kha pa chen po'i sngags rim du/
bla med kyi rgyud don la 'jug pa las/ rig 'dzin kyi theg pa sde snod gsum du mi gtogs pa'i sde snod bzhi bar 'dod pa dang / sde snod gsum du gtogs pa'i lugs gnyis bshad kyang / dpung bzang las/ gsang sngags mdo sde'i tshul du bshad kyis nyon/[226] / zhes pa dang / gzhan yang rgyud mang po las mdo dang mdo sder bshad pas/ shin+ti pas zab don bsdus te ston pas mdo sder bzhed pa ltar legs la/ de la yang nang gses kyis phye na sde snod gzhan gnyis kyi'ang don ston pas na a b+h+yas sde snod gsum gar gtogs par bzhed pa yang 'thad do/[227] / zhes dang /

The great Tsongkhapa, Mañjuśrī incarnate, says in his Stages of Mantra:
In Understanding Highest Yoga Tantras it says that there are two traditions: one of not including the vidyādhara vehicle in the three baskets of scripture but according it the status of a fourth basket, and another tradition that does include it in the three baskets. However, in the Questions of Subahu Tantra it says, “Listen I will explain secret mantra in the manner of the sutras.”[462] Also, many tantras are explained as being sutras and are mentioned in the categories of sutra. Therefore, Ratnakaraśānti’s assertion is correct that because these tantras explain the profound in an abridged form, they are classified as sutra. However, in terms of the internal divisions of scripture, they also teach topics from the other baskets, and so Abhayakara’s assertion that they belong in all three baskets is also correct.[463]

d.div: [226] sde dge_805_bka'/ rgyud/ wa_'phags pa dpung bzang gis zhus pa zhes bya ba'i rgyud/ le'u dang po/ shog_118_ba2_gsang sngags mdo sde'i tshul du ngas bshad do//
[227] rje tsong kha pa chen po'i gsung 'bum/ ga sngags rim chen mo/ shog_12_ba2
[462] Subahuparipṛcchā, chap. 1, Toh 805 Kangyur, rgyud, wa, 118b2.
[463] Collected Works, ga, 12b2.

f.d:
mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang po'i dus 'khor 'grel chen de nyid snang bar rje btsun btsong kha ba'i dgongs pa ltar bshad nas/
de mdo sde'i sde snod yin pa dang / de'i nang tshan gyi cha shas su gyur ba'i mngon pa dang 'dul ba'i sde snod kyang yod pa mi 'gal bar shes par bya'o/[228] / zhes sogs sde snod gsum gyi khongs su gsang sngags gtogs pa la chos phung gi kha gsal med pa'i rigs dang /

Khedrup Gelek Palsangpo in his extensive commentary on the Kālacakra, Illuminating Reality, explains this point in accord with Jetsün Tsongkhapa and states:
To include them in the basket of sutra, and to assert that in terms of their own internal divisions, parts can be included in the basket of Vinaya and parts in the basket of Abhidharma is not contradictory.[464] These and other passages talk of secret mantra being included in the three baskets of scripture without particular reference to the 84,000 collections of Dharma.

d.div: [228] mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang gi gsung 'bum/ kha dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i 'grel chen dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi rgya cher bshad pa de kho na nyid kyi snang bar byed pa/ shog_8_na2
[464] Collected Works, kha, 8a2.

f.d:
rgyud sde spyi rnam du/
rgyal ba'i gsung rab thams cad chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong du 'dus te/ gdul bya'i rgyud kyi 'dod chags la shas cher spyod pa nyi khri chig stong dang / zhe sdang la shas cher spyod pa dang / gti mug la shas cher spyod pa dang / de gsum cha mnyam la spyod pa nyi khri chig stong re ste/ nyon mongs pa brgyad khri bzhi stong gi gnyen por gsungs so/[229] / zhes thang yig dang dgongs pa mthun par gsungs/

In General Aspects of the Classes of Tantra it says:
All the teachings of the conquering Buddha are included in the 84,000 collections of Dharma. 21,000 are for disciples whose minds are predominantly affected by desire, 21,000 for those predominantly affected by anger, 21,000 for those predominantly affected by ignorance, and 21,000 for those affected by all three equally. These were taught, therefore, as antidotes for the 84,000 afflictions.[465] This passage follows the thinking of Lotus Chronicle cited earlier.

d.div: [229] mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang / gsung 'bum/ nya rgyud sde spyi'i rnam par bzhag pa rgyas par bshad pa/ shog_13_ba5
[465] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, nya, 13b4

f.d:
bo dong pa'i de nyid 'dus pa las/
'o na rgyud sde bzhi po sde snod gsum du 'du na sde snod du 'gyur zhing / ma 'dus na bka' ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na skyon med de/ phal cher byang chub sems dpa'i shin tu rgyas pa'i sde snod yin pa'i phyir dang / sde snod gsum char 'dus pa'i mdo sde khyad par can yin pa'i phyir/[230] zhes chos sgo brgyad khri bzhi stong kha ma gsal kyang gsang sngags sde snod gsum gyi nang du gtogs par bzhed pas don gyi dgongs pa snga 'gyur sogs gong ma rnams dang yang mi 'gal mod/

Bodong[466] in his Compendium of Reality says:
However, some might wonder, if the four classes of tantra are included in the three baskets, then they become part of that categorization. If they are not included, then they are no longer the word of Buddha. There is no problem here. They are mostly included in the basket known as the very vast scriptural basket of the bodhisattva and are special components of the sutra division of the three baskets.[467] Therefore, although there is no clear reference here to the 84,000 gateways of Dharma, he asserts that secret mantra is included in the three baskets and so actually is not in contradiction with the position of those mentioned previously—the early translation school, and so on.

d.div: [230] bo dong phyogs las rnam rgyal gyi gsung 'bum pod phreng 44_dang 56_96_119_bcas kyi nang yod nges 'tshol zhib byed kyang ma rnyed/
[466] Bodong Choklé Namgyal (1326/76–1451).
[467] Untraced in the works of Bodong Choklé Namgyal.

f.d:
'on kyang dkon cog ta la'i mdo bam po gsum pa las/
kun dga' bos gsol ba/ bcom ldan 'das bdag gis chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong de bzhin gshegs pa las mngon du thos na/ chos kyi rnam grangs 'di lta bu ni nam yang ma thos so/[231] / zhes byung ba/

However, in the third fascicle of the Jewel Lamp Dhāraṇī it says:
Ānanda said, “Bhagavān, I have heard the 84,000 collections of Dharma from the Tathāgata, but I have not heard such a Dharma before.”[468]

d.div: [231] sde dge_145_bka'/ mdo sde/ pa_dkon mchog ta la la'i gzung / bam po/ 3_shog_60_ba3
[468] Ratnolkānāmadhāraṇī, Toh 145 Kangyur, gzungs ’dus, pa, 60b3.

f.d: mdo 'di'i tshigs bcad rnams phal bo che bzang po'i dpal kyi le'u bcu bdun pa dang 'gyur khyad las don gcig pas phal po che'i le'u 'di yang gsung dus chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong bka' stsal zin pa lta bu dang / dkon cog ta la bya rgyud du bzhed pa mang ba ltar na yang sngags phyogs rnams de khongs mi 'dren pa sor bzhag sogs the tshom gyi gzhi che gshis/ sngon gyi mkhas pa rnams gyi zhal gsal mi gsungs mod/

Taking into account the vagaries of translation, the verses from this sutra are identical to those of chapter 17, the Śrībhadra chapter, of the Avataṃsaka Sutra. Therefore, when this chapter of the Avataṃsaka was being taught, the 84,000 categories had already been delivered. Also, even though there are many who assert the Jewel Lamp to be action tantra, scholars of tantra tend to leave this work unclassified. These and other points are the bases for doubt and query, and so the scholars of the past have not been clear on this.

'on kyang stag lo shes rab rin chen gyi rig kun tu/
dpal ldan gsang ba 'dus pas rtsa rgyud ni/ / mdo sde chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong gi+i/ / snod dang rgyud sde sum khri sum stong gi/ / rtsa bar gsungs pas snod dang rtsa ba'i khyad/ / phye phyir rig pa 'dzin pa'i sde snod ces/ / bzhi par rgya bod mkhas rnams bzhed par 'thad/[232] / ces rig pa 'dzin pa'i sde snod bsnan pa'i bzhi lta bu dang / snod dang rtsa ba'i khyad kyi dbye ba phye bar gsungs/

However, Taktsang Lotsāwa Sherap Rinchen in his Knowledge of All Sciences says:
The glorious Guhyasamāja root tantra is taught to be the scriptural basket holding 84,000 categories of sutra and the root of 33,000 categories of tantra. Basket and root are therefore differentiated, and so a fourth, called the vidyādhara category, is validly asserted by the scholars of India and Tibet.[469] Here, he is asserting the existence of a fourth category and also differentiating between “root” and “basket.”

d.div: [232] stag lo shes rab rin chen/ rig gnas kun shes/ shog_785_phreng 13
[469] Collected Works, vol. 1, 785.13.

f.d:
dus 'khor spyi don du/
des na mkhas rlom kha cig /bdag gis gsang sngags mdo sde'i tshul du bshad/ /ces pa dang / mdo sde 'di ni nyan byed na/ /zhes sogs dang / de nyid 'dus pa'i rtsa rgyud la theg pa chen po'i mdo zhes bshad pa dang / sgrub thabs mdo dang bsres pa zhes pa'i mdo sde gsang 'dus rtsa bshad kyi rgyud la gsungs pa sogs mang bas mdo rgyud mi 'gal zhes zer ba dang /[233] de bas kyang mkhas par rlom pa dag / 'gal yang sde snod gsum gyi nang nas mdo sde'i sde snod du sdud pa yin par lung de dag gis bstan to zhes zer ba ni/ 'o na ka lA pa'i mdo dang / tsan+d+ra pa'i mdo dang / tshad ma mdo dang / tsa ra ka'i mdo zhes sogs bshad pas de dag dang nang rig gi mdo mi 'gal ba'am 'gal ba yang mdo sde'i sde snod du bsdu dgos par 'gyur ro/ /zhes sogs rtog ge'i rigs pa nas bsgrubs pa'i snying po rje btsun btsong kha ba'i bzhed pa bkag par song 'dug kyang /

In his Ocean Overview of Kālacakra he says:
Therefore, some so-called scholars say that sutra and tantra are not mutually exclusive, because of passages such as “Listen I will explain secret mantra in the manner of the sutras” or “If you listen to this sutra” or because the Tatvasaṃgraha Root Tantra is described as a great-vehicle sutra, or that the category of sutra is taught in the root and explanatory Guhyasamāja in terms of sādhanas being mixed within sutras, and so on. Some even more pretentious scholars maintain that sutra and tantra may be mutually exclusive but that these citations teach that secret mantra is included in the basket of sutras from the three scriptural divisions. To them I say, in that case there are works called the Kalāpa Sutra, the Candravyākaraṇa Sutra, the Pramāṇa Sutra, the Caraka Sutra, and so on, and you would have to include them in the basket of sutra regardless of whether they contradict Buddhist sutras or not.[470] He is using overly intellectual reasoning here to establish his point, the essence of which is a refutation of Jé Tsongkhapa’s position.

d.div: [233] stag tshang ba'i dus 'khor spyi don de'i dpe lag tu ma son/
[470] Untraced in the text.

f.d:
sde snod gsum mdo sde chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong dang rgyud sde'i nang tshan sum khri sum stong po der ma 'dus pa'i shes byed dpal 'byor rgya mtshor/
mdo sde'i chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong rgyud sde nang tshan sum khri sum stong du ye shes rdo rje kun las btus las bshad/ ces byung ba/

The authority for his position on the three baskets of 84,000 categories of Dharma and his asssertion that the 33,000 categories of tantra are not included in them, is found in the Ocean of Wealth:
That the 33,000 categories of tantra are not included within the 84,000 categories of sutra is described in the Vajra Gnosis Compendium Tantra.[471]

d.div: [471] Untraced.

f.d:
ye shes rdo rje kun las btus pa'i rgyud kyi bde ba chen po'i rim par phye ba gnyis pa las/
bcom ldan 'das rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud dang / gnyis ka'i rgyud dang / spyod pa'i rgyud dang / bya ba'i rgyud dang / rtog pa'i rgyud rnams kyi tshad ji ltar lags/ bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal ba/ rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud kyi ming stong phrag bcu gnyis zhes bya ste/ rgyas par phye na grangs med do/ / gnyi ga'i rgyud stong phrag drug go/ / spyod pa'i rgyud stong phrag brgyad do/ / bya ba'i rgyud stong phrag bzhi'o/ / rtog pa'i rgyud stong phrag bzhi'o/ / de dag ni stong phrag sum cu rtsa bzhi ste/[234] zhes 'di dang phag mo mngon 'byung sogs la rgyud sde yang lngar bshad pa [235] sogs yod kyang mdo sde chos phung brgyad khri bzhi stong rgyud 'dir gtan med cing /

The actual text is from the second part of the tantra entitled Chapter on Great Bliss:
“Bhagavān, what are the numbers of great yoga tantras, dual tantras, conduct tantras, action tantras, and conceptual tantras?” The Bhagavān replied, “There are 12,000 with the name of great yoga tantras. Expanded further they would be beyond number. There are 6,000 dual tantras, 8,000 conduct tantras, 4,000 action tantras, and 4,000 conceptual tantras. This comes to 34,000 tantras.”[472] In this tantra, and in the Vajravarāhyabhibhava Tantra[473] and others, we find this division into five classes of tantra. However, this tantra makes no mention at all of the 84,000 categories of sutra.

d.div: [234] sde dge_447_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_ye shes rdo rje kun las btus pa/ rim par phye ba gnyis pa/ shog_284_ba7
[235] sde dge_378_bka'/ rgyud/ ga_'phags mo mngon byung / le'u/ 7_shog_65_ba6
[472] Vajrajñānasamuccaya, Toh 447 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, 284b7.
[473] Vajravārahī Tantra, chap. 7, Toh 378 Kangyur, ga, 65b6.

f.d: stong phrag sum cu rtsa bzhi zhes pa'ang spyan gyis ma gzigs pa'am gang ltar rdzun grog mo mgo rdum du song zhing / rig gnas kun shes kyi 'grel par yang gong gi tshigs bcad zur tsam las ma smos par sbam 'jog mdzad dgos byung 'dug

Also, maybe he has not noticed that this tantra talks of 34,000 tantras. Whatever the reason, it is as false as a headless ant.[474] Furthermore, in the commentary to Knowledge of All Sciences, the verses quoted above are not commented upon but have had to be left as they are.

d.div: [474] Grog mo mgo rdum; a saying that none of the Tibetan scholars I consulted have been able to recognize.

f.d:
bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen po'i gsan yig gang+gA'i chu rgyun du/
theg pa thams cad kyi yang rtser gyur pa rgyud 'bum ni/ dpung bzang gis zhus pa'i rgyud las/ gsang sngags mdo sde'i tshul gyi bshad kyi nyon/[236] / zhes rgyud rnams mdo sde'i sde snod kyi khongs su 'du bar gsungs pas sngags gsar rnying gi rgyud mtha' dag sngar smos pa'i sde snod gsum gyis khongs su bkod kyang mi rung ba ma yin la/[237]

My lama, the Great Fifth, in his Stream of the Ganges: An Account of Teachings Received, asserts that the tantras are included in the basket of sutras when he says:
Concerning the collection of tantras, the very pinnacle of all vehicles, the Questions of Subahu Tantra says, “Listen I will explain secret mantra in the manner of the sutras.”[475] Therefore, to include all the tantras of the old and new schools in the three baskets described earlier is not unacceptable.

d.div: [236] sde dge_805_bka'/ rgyud/ wa_'phags pa dpung bzang gis zhus pa/ le'u/ 1_shog_118_ba2_gsang sngags mdo sde'i tshul du ngas bshad do//
[237] rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ nga gsan yig_shog_195_na2
[475] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Collected Works, nga, 195a2.

f.d: 'on kyang gsan yig kha pa'i rgyab du snga 'gyur dgongs pa 'dus par 'gyur mi 'dra ba yod pa de yin par stsal zhing / bstan 'gyur gyi gras/ slob dpon dz+nyA na shrI'i mtha' gnyis sel bar gsang ba lung bstan pa'i mdo'i lung drangs par snang bas/ de dag rnams dang gdams ngag 'bogs pa gcig par dgongs pa'i lung /

However, in Stream of the Ganges, at the back of the kha volume, my lama, the Great Fifth, says there is a citation from the early-translation work Compilation of the Enlightened Mind, under a different translation, that is also quoted as being from the Sutra of Secret Prophecies in the Tengyur work Eliminating the Two Extremes by Jñānaśrī, and that is identical in thought to a citation from King of Teachings on the Sutras.

rgyu la mos pa rgyu'i chos kyi/ / 'khor lo rab tu bskor byas nas/ / 'bras bu'i theg pa nye lam zhig / ma 'ongs dus na 'byung bar 'gyur/[238] / zhes gsungs pas spyir rgyud sde rnams sangs rgyas kyis gsungs na'ang gdul bya thun mong pa'i snang ngor sde snod gsum gyi chos kyi 'khor lo bskor te mya ngan las 'das nas lo brgya dngab cu gnyas tsim nas 'bras bu'i theg pa dar bar gsungs pas sde snod gsum dang rgyud sde bzhi zhes so sor grags zhes stsal ba/

It runs:
Having turned the wheel of causal phenomena for those predisposed to the causal path, the result vehicle—a swifter path— will appear at a future time.[476] As a general truth, the tantras were taught by the Buddha. However, in the eyes of ordinary disciples, he first turned the Dharma wheel of the three baskets of scripture and then the result vehicle only began to appear about one hundred and twelve years after his passing. Therefore, says my lama, the three baskets and the four classes of tantra were said to be separate divisions of scripture.

d.div: [238] sde dge_3714_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tsu_slob dpon dz+nyAn shrI_rdo rje theg pa'i mtha' gnyis sel ba/ shog_115_ba2_rgyu la sbyor ba rgyu yi chos/ /'khor lo shin tu bskor byas nas/ /'bras bu'i theg pa nye lam zhig / ma 'ongs pa na 'byung bar 'gyur//
[476] Jñānaśrī, Eliminating the Two Extremes in Vajrayana, Vajrayānāntadvayāpoha, Toh 3714 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tsu, 115b2.

f.d:
rnam snang mngon byang ri rab kyi rtse dang / gshed skor rnams bdud 'dul skabs gsungs pa/ nA ro pas dus 'khor rtsa rgyud kyi lung dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel bar drangs par/
ston pas bya rgod phung po ru/ / shes rab pha rol phyin tshul bzhin/ / chos bstan dpal ldan 'bras spungs su/ / de bzhin gsang sngags tshul rab gsungs/[239] /

The Vairocana Enlightenment Tantra was taught on the summit of Mount Meru, and the Yamāri collection was taught while taming the māras. Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiation quotes a verse from the Kālacakra Root Tantra:
On Vulture’s Peak our Teacher gave the perfection of wisdom teachings, and likewise on Śrī Dhānyakaṭaka he taught the secret mantra.[477]

d.div: [239] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_nA ro pa/ dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad don dam pa bsdus pa/ shog_222_na7
[477] Sekoddeśaṭīkā, Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 222a7.

f.d:
zhes dang / a nu pa ma rak+Sha ta'i mtshan brjod 'grel bar/
dpal ldan 'bras spungs mchod rten du/ / zhes pa nas/
lha la sogs pa thams cad la/ / dbang bskur byin te rgyud sde bzhi/ / snying po'i rgyud dang lnga po dag / rdo rje 'chang gis rgyas par gsungs/[240] / zhes dus 'khor ba'i lugs la gsang sngags thams cad mya ngan las 'da' rgyu'i lo gsungs par bzhed pa dang /

Also in Anupamarakṣita’s commentary to the Saṃgīti:
In the shrine of Śrī Dhānyakaṭaka… up to:
The initiations were bestowed on all the gods and other beings, and the four classes of tantra, and, to make five, the essence tantras were extensively taught by Vajradhara.[478] Therefore, in the Kālacakra tradition all the tantras were taught in the year of Buddha’s passing.[479]

d.div: [240] sde dge_1396_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pha slob dpon a nu pa ma rak+Shi ta/ 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyi mtshan yang dag par brjod pa'i 'grel ba bdud rtsi'i thigs pa sgron ma gsal ba/ le'u/ 1_shog_96_ba3
[478] Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgītivṛtti, chap. 1, Toh 1396 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, pha, 96b3.
[479] According to some the Kālacakra was taught in the Buddha’s last year and therefore all tantras were also.

f.d:
mkha' 'gro rgya mtsho'i le'u nga gcig pa las/
shAkya seng ges gsungs pa'i rgyud/ / rnal 'byor pha rol son pa'o/[241] / zhes bde mchog skor dang / gsang 'dus kyang mya ngan las ma 'das gong du gsungs zin par 'dod pa sogs gsang sngags thun mong bar sna tshogs su gyur kyang

The fifty-first chapter of the Ḍākārṇava Tantra states:
Tantras spoken by the lion of the Śākya travel to the perfection of yoga.[480] This refers to the Saṃvara collection and also the Guhyasamāja being taught before the passing of the Buddha. These assertions make up the various common positions on tantra.

d.div: [241] sde dge_372_bka'/ rgyud/ kha_mkha' 'gro rgya mtsho/ le'u/ 51_shog_264_na4
[480] Toh 372 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 264a4.

f.d:
thun mong ma yin pa rnams/ mdo sde gdams ngag 'bogs pa'i rgyal po'am gsang ba lung bstan pa'i mdo las/
nga ni 'di nas mi snang nas/ / lo ni brgya dang bcu gnyis na/ / lha gnas gsum du grags pa yi/ / bstan pa'i snying po dam pa zhig / 'dzam gling shar kyi phyogs mtshams su/ / mi las bskal ldan dra ma che/ / rgyal po dza zhes bya ba la/ / sngon du ltas rnams 'byung 'gyur te/ / drag shul can zhes bya ba'i rtser/ / grogs kyi sems dpa' dman pa'i lus/ / lang+ka'i bdag po la sogs pa/ / lag na rdo rjes ston par 'gyur/[242] / zhes gsungs pa la dgongs pa yin nam snyam/

Other more exclusive positions, I think, are based on the prophecy made in the King of Teachings on the Sutras, also known as the Sutra of Secret Prophecies:
After I have gone from here in years numbering 112, the quintessential teachings renowned in the three celestial realms, augured by auspicious signs appearing to the king known as Ja in the eastern region of Jampudvīpa, and of a lineage of glorious human merit will be given by Vajrapāṇi in Ugra in the company of the king of Lanka and other great beings of a lower lineage.[481]

d.div: [242] zur mkhar blo gros rgyal po/ sman pa rnams kyis mi shes su mi rung ba'i shes bya spyi'i khog dbubs/ shog_117_phreng 16
[481] Cited in Lodrö Gyalpo’s General Compendium, 117.16.

f.d:
de ltar gsar ma'i rgyud grangs ni bde mchog sdom 'byung le'u nyer gnyis par/
rnal 'byor rgyud rnams kyi ni tshad/ / bye ba phrag ni drug nges te/ / de bzhin rnal 'byor ma rgyud grangs/ / bye ba phrag ni bcu drug grags/ / theg chen las gzhan mdo sde rnams/ / dung phyur phrag brgyad gsungs pa yin/ / de bzhin pha rol phyin pa'i tshul/ / sa ya dang ni dung 'phyur lnga/ / 'di dag thams cad thub dbang po/ / sku gsum bdag nyid can gyis gsungs/[243] / zhes dang /

Concerning the number of new translation tantras, the twenty-second chapter of the Cakrasaṃvara Tantra states:
The number of yoga tantras is ascertained at 60 million; Likewise, the number of yoginī tantras is said to be 160 million. Sutras other than those of the great vehicle number 800 million, while those of the perfection vehicle number 500 million times a million; all of them taught by the Munīndra, embodiment of the three bodies.[482]

d.div: [243] sde dge_373_bka'/ rgyud/ kha_bde mchog gi byung ba zhes bya ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po/ rim par phye ba/ 22_shog_291_na3
[482] Toh 373 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 291a3.

f.d:
sangs rgyas thod pa'i rgyud las/
rnal 'byor gyi rgyud la bye ba phrag drug nyid do/ / rnal 'byor ma'i rgyud la ni bye ba phrag bcu drug nyid do/ / mdo sde so so la ni bye ba phrag brgyad cu'o/ / de bzhin du pha rol tu phyin pa'i theg pa la ni bye ba la bsgres pa'i 'bum phrag lnga'o/ / 'di dag thams cad ni thub pa'i dbang pos gsungs so/[244] / zhes pa 'di dang gong gi sdom 'byung gnyis nas mdo sde'i tshad gsungs pa rnams sh+loka lta bu yin na ma gtogs brgyad khri bzhi stong las che brgal bas dang / ye shes rdo rje kun las btus kyi lung drangs ma thag par/ rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud kyi ming stong phrag bcu gnyis zhes pa yang gsang 'dus/ bde mchog ces rgyud kyi mtshan re re bgrangs pa lta bu yin pa dang /

Also, the Buddha Skull Tantra says:
There are 60 million yoga tantras and 160 million yoginī tantras. Individual sutras number 800 million. Likewise those of the perfection vehicle number 500,000 times 100 million. All of these were taught by the Munīndra.[483] Therefore, unless they are talking about the number of verses, the sutra count mentioned in this tantra and the Cakrasaṃvara is far greater than 84,000. With the line “There are 12,000 with the name of great yoga tantras” from the Vajra Gnosis Compendium Tantra citation quoted previously, it is as if it is counting the names of individual tantras such as Cakrasaṃvara and Guhyasamāja.

d.div: [244] sde dge_424_bka'/ rgyud/ nga sangs rgyas thod pa zhes bya ba rnal 'byar mo_'a rgyu+i_da kyi rgyal po/ le'u/ 1_shog_143_na6
[483] Buddhakapālatantra, chap. 1, Toh 424 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 143a6.

f.d:
rdo rje snying rgyan le'u bcu gcig pa las/
lha mo bstan bcos lnga brgya bdun/ / 'di rnams dgos pa'i bye brag gis/ / nga yi yang dag bstan par byas/[245] / zhes gsang 'dus gcig po'i phyogs gtogs la bstan bcos sam rgyud lnga brgya dang bdun yod pa dang /
de'i nang tshan rer yang / / khro zla thig le 'bum phrag lnga/[246] / zhes pa lta bu shin tu mang zhing /

Also the Vajra Essence Ornament Tantra says:
Goddess, these 507 treatises I have taught them perfectly for particular reasons.[484] Therefore, in the Guhyasamāja category of tantras alone, there are 507 treatises, or tantras, and each of these also contains related tantras. For example:
Of the Krodhacandratilaka, there are 500,000.[485] Therefore, this comes to an enormous amount.

d.div: [245] sde dge_451_bka'/ rgyud/ cha dpal rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi rgyud/ le'u/ 11_shog_51_ba1
[246] sde dge_451_bka'/ rgyud/ cha dpal rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi rgyud/ le'u/ 11_shog_51_na6
[484] Vajrahṛdayālaṃkaratantra, chap. 11, Toh 451 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 51b1.

f.d:
bya ba'i rgyud la'ang rang lugs su nang gses yod pa ni/ dpung bzang gis zhus pa'i le'u bcu pa las/
lha dang lha min mi la phan gdags phyir/ / gsang sngags rig sngags rnam pa sna tshogs dag / bye ba phrag gsum dang ni 'bum phrag lnga/ / rig 'dzin sde snod bshad par rgyal bas gsungs/ /

There are also many subcategories of action tantras. The tenth chapter of Tantra Requested by Subāhu says:[486]
For the benefit of gods, demigods, and humans, 30,500,00 different vidyā mantras—secret mantras[487]— were taught by the conquering Buddha to form the vidyādhara basket of scripture.

d.div: [486] These verses teach the lineages and tantras of action tantra. The line-break divisions between the verses indicate the sections on the three main lineages—tathāgata, vajra, and lotus—and the two worldly lineages, as explained in the three Indian commentaries on this tantra. There are various readings across the different editions of the tantra and its commentaries. The lineages and tantras are set out in more detail in Khedrup Jé’s General Presentation of the Tantras and in Tsongkhapa’s Stages of Mantra, the latter translated by Jeffrey Hopkins in Deity Yoga (Ithaca, NY: Snow Lion Publications, 1981).
[487] According to Notes Explaining the Text of the Questions of Subāhu Tantra (Toh 2672), these numbers refer to the verse count.

ngas ni gsung pa po rnams gzhom pa dang / / dbul ba'i sdug bsngal bsal bar bya ba'i phyir/ / dkyil 'khor bcas shing phyag rgyar ldan pa yi/ / gsang sngags bye ba phrag bdun rab tu bshad/ / pho nya bcu dang rig pa'i rgyal po bdun/ / de bzhin phyag brnyan drug bcu rtsa bzhi dang / / nga yi snying po dam pa brgyad rnams dang / /

To alleviate the sufferings of poverty and to destroy the secret ones,[488] I have taught 70 million tantras with mandalas and mudrās. To the ten messengers, the seven vidyā kings, likewise the sixty-four attendants, and eight supreme deities of my essence,

[488] Gsang ba pa. The “secret ones.” This is the reading of the Degé Kangyur and the three Indian commentaries to the Questions of Subāhu Tantra in the Tengyur. The second Indian commentary (Notes Explaining the Text of the Questions of Subāhu Tantra) explains this as “taming the yakṣa and others.” However, the Dharamsala and Lhasa editions of Beryl Mirror have gsung ba po (“speakers”).

khro bo drag po bdud rtsi thab sbyor dang / / rig pa mchog la sogs pa mthu bo che/ / rig pa'i bdag po gsang sngags rjes 'brang bcas/ / de snyed rdo rje'i rigs ni gang yin pa/ / der ni 'di dag nga yi rgya cher bshad/ /
Amṛtakuṇḍalī, and so forth, of the wrathful guardians, Vidyottama, and so forth, the powerful ones, the vidyā lords, and other followers of mantra: to these of the vajra lineage, I teach extensively.

spyan ras gzigs kyi gsang sngags bye ba phrag / gsum dang de bzhin 'bum phrag lnga rnams bshad/ / de yi rig sngags bdag po rta mgrin dang / / de'i ming can dkyil 'khor dam pa gsum/ / bcu gnyis phyag dang bcu drug pa dang ni/ / thor tshugs cod pan 'dod pa 'byor byed dang / / zhal bzhi don yod zhags par bdun bstan pa/ / sa steng gsang sngags nyi ma bdun ltar 'bar/ / de rnams rta mgrin dkyil 'khor gsang sngags te/ / mi la mchog sbyin 'jig rten gsum gyi 'dud/ /

I have taught 30,500,000 tantras of Avalokiteśvara; their vidyā lord is Hayagrīva. Mandalas bearing his name are those of the three supreme ones, the twelve-armed, the six-armed,[489] the Crown Protrusion Fulfilling Desires, and the four-faced Amoghapāśa— seven secret mantras shining above the earth like seven suns; these are the secret-mantra mandalas of Hayagrīva, granting the supreme to humans and worshipped in the three worlds.
[489] Phyag drug pa. This is the reading from Degé Kangyur. The Lhasa and Dharamsala editions have bcu drug pa (sixteen). This line is omitted from the commentaries.

sgrol ma dkar mo gso dkar can ma dang / / rnam gzigs ral pa gcig ma dkar sham dang / / grags ldan khro gnyer can dang 'di dag rnams/ / pad+ma'i rigs kyi rigs sngags rgyal mo mchog / de dag dkyil 'khor sna tshogs gzugs can dang / / phyag rgya rnam pa sna tshogs rnams dang ldan/ /
White Tārā, Pāṇḍarā, Vipaśyin, white Ekajaṭa, Yaśovatī, and Bhṛkuṭi, the great mantra queens of the lotus lineage. These have mandalas of different forms and mudrās of different designs.

rgyas pa'i gsang sngags rgyud du 'od dpag can/ / rig pa'i dbang phyug gsang sngags bdag por sgom/ / de yis gsang sngags mi la grub mchog ster/ / de la lnga rtsen yang ni mngon par dga'/ / gnod sbyin dbang phyug de dang rtag mthun pas/ / de yi dka' yis gsang sngags mchog rnams bshad/ / lngas rtsen gyis ni stong phrag nyi shu ste/ / de yi chung mas de yi phyed bshad do/ /

In the vast lineage, Mekhalāvat,[490] mistress of knowledge, queen of mantra, her mantra granting the supreme siddhi adored by Pañcaka, lord of the lineage, always in accord with the powerful lords of the yakṣa, with her words a host of tantras are taught. In the Pañcaka tantra, twenty thousand verses, and in that of his wife, half that number.
[490] Identified in Notes Explaining the Text of the Questions of Subāhu Tantra as Hari, wife of Pañcaka.

f.d: nor gyi bdag pos stong phrag sum cu ste/ / gang po'i pha yis kyang ni 'bum bshad do/ / lha dang lha min la sogs rgyal ba la/ / dad pa rnams kyis gsang sngags mtha' yas bshad/[247] / ces gsungs pas go bar nus la/
