He maintained his father’s dynastic seat and nurtured the uncle-nephew lineage[572] as senior physicians of the past had done. He passed on the texts, oral teachings, and practices to students all over the country and made an immense contribution to the welfare of living beings.

d.div: [572] According to Trinlé (p. 168), this refers to the Sakya family lineage.

f.d: de'i gcung gzhon nu nas rab tu byung bas dpal ldan 'tsho byed du grags/ des gcen dang phag ston shAkya mgon po yun ring du bsten nas rgyud bzhi cha lag 'grel tig phyag len dang bcas pa'i tshig don rdzogs par zhus/ thos lo tsam ma yin par thugs su chud cing / bstan bcos brgyad pa la g.yu thog pa'i Tik+ka/ byang mo khud pa'i 'grel pa/ yab dang che rje mi nyag gsum gyi bshad sgros/ mkhas pa sde snod 'dzin pa chen po gnas drug pa blo gros mtshungs med kyis mdzad pa'i mchan bu rnams la brten nas 'chad nyan lo du mar bskyangs/

Gyalwa Sangpo’s younger son became ordained at an early age and was known as Palden Tsojé. He studied for a long time under his elder brother as well as Phaktön Śākya Gönpo, where he received complete teachings on Four Tantras, its auxiliary texts, the commentaries, the essential commentaries, and the practices. This was not just superficial learning but a thorough understanding. For many years he propagated the teachings of the Treatise of Eight Branches using Yuthok’s commentary, Jangmo Khyüpa’s commentary, the teachings passed down from his father, Chejé, and Minyak,[573] and annotations made by the great scholar and great upholder of the baskets of scripture, Nedrukpa Lodrö Tsungmé.

d.div: [573] Possibly Chejé Śākya Pal and Minyak Dorjé Bum, who appear to be contemporary physicians.

f.d: khog 'bugs shes bya rab gsal/ rtsa rgyud kyi 'grel pa rgyud don rab gsal/ phyi rgyud 'grel pa tshul gsum snang ba/ rtsa mdo'i 'grel pa nyi ma'i 'od zer/ brgyad pa'i khog 'bugs/ drang srong gi rtogs brjod/ ma la ya'i dka' 'grel/ phyi rgyud sman sbyor dpe'u ris/ rtsa'i lha mo'i sgrub thabs/ chu mdo'i 'grel pa tshig don gsal byed yid bzhin nor bu/ thang phye'i 'grel pa/ byang khog gi thig 'grems gsal sgron/ gces bsdus/ mdo gnas le'u sum cu'i sa ma 'grel sogs bstan bcos che chung bco brgyad tsam mdzad de bstan pa dang 'gro ba'i don bsam gyis mi khyab pa byung /

Altogether he composed about eighteen works of various lengths, and his contribution to the welfare of others is inconceivable. His compositions include: • History of Medicine: Illumination of Knowledge • Commentary to the Root Tantra called Illumination of the Meaning of the Tantra • Commentary to the Final Tantra called Illumination of the Three Ways • Commentary to the pulse section of the Four Tantras called Rays of the Sun • Exposition of Eight Branches • Rishi Chronicles • Commentary on Difficult Points on the Malaya • Illustrations of Medicinal Preparations from the Final Tantra • Sādhana of the Pulse Goddess • Commentary to the urine section of the Four Tantras called Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Clarifying the Text • Commentary on Decoctions and Powder • Lamp Illuminating the Structure of the Torso • Compilation of Essentials • Thirty-Chapter Wooden-Board Commentary to the Compilations and Sections of the Tantra[574]

d.div: [574] Four Tantras in the later versions is categorized into four compilations (mdo), eleven main sections (gnas), and fifteen divisions (skabs).

f.d: 'di'i sku tsha brang ti dpal ldan rgyal mtshan gyis rtsa rgyud le'u dang po'i 'grel pa dang / yab mes gong ma na rim dang khyad par dpal ldan 'tsho byed kyi dgongs pa dang rang nyid la yi dam 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyis lung bstan pa dkar po drug sbyor sogs phyogs gcig tu bu rnam rgyal bzang pos don du bsdus te man ngag gser brer grags pa bsdebs/ gdung rabs mthar chags su bkod pa'i yig cha ma mthong rung / gser bre chung ba'i dmu chu'i gdams pa'i brgyud pa ltar na/ dpal ldan rgyal mtshan nas brang ti kun dga' bzang po/ de nas brang ti stag la dpal/ de nas brang ti rdo rje dpal bzang / 'dis bshad rgyud 'grel pa don gsal mdzad/ des brang ti dpal 'byor don grub la gzhung gdams man ngag dang bcas pa gnang / gser bre che ba las btus pa'i chung ba mdzad de sras la gnang / des man ngag dngul brer grags pa spel ba gser bre rnams las cung zad brjod bya zhel bar snang bas skya sman grong du yab mes kyi srol bzhin sman dpyad kyi bstan pa bskyangs/

Drangti Palden Gyaltsen was a nephew of Drangti Palden Tsojé. He produced a compilation consisting of the commentary to the first chapter of the Root Tantra, the thoughts of his paternal predecessors, and particularly those of Palden Tsojé, as well as the teachings given to him by his meditation deity Mañjuśrī, such as Compound of the Six White Ingredients. This compilation was given to his son, Namgyal Sangpo, and is known as Golden Measuring Dish of Instructions. I have not seen any documents setting out his family line, but according to the lineage of the instructions on treatment for dropsy from the Shorter Golden Measuring Dish of Instructions, the line passed from Palden Gyaltsen to Drangti Künga Sangpo, to Drangti Takla Pal, and then to Drangti Dorjé Palsang, who composed Illuminating Commentary to the Explanatory Tantra. He passed the texts, instructions, and oral teachings to Drangti Paljor Döndrup and composed the Shorter Golden Measuring Dish, compiling it from the longer version. This he passed to his son, who in turn propagated the Silver Measuring Dish of Instructions, which is shorter than the versions of Golden Measuring Dish and seems to be inferior in content. In the Sakya Mendrong medical tradition, he maintained the medical tradition as his fathers had done before him.[575]

d.div: [575] According to Trinlé (p. 171) and to the Sa skya sman grong pa’i man ngag dngul bre ma, the Drangti lineage eventually became the khu dbon bla sman tradition, popularly known as the Sakya Mendrong medical tradition.

f.d: brang ti'i zhal ngo dpal mgon rdo rje dang chos rgyal bkra shis zhes pa byung 'dug ste gong gi sras kyi mtshan yin min the tshom du gyur/ yan lag brgyad pa la brten pa shas che ba ma ra sgom chen gyis Ti ka'i gsal byed me long / g.yu thog bkra shis mgon gyis lung grangs kyi bsdus don/ 'phel zad/ ro sbyor/ ni ru ha'i las rim/ mtshan nyid nyi shu la sogs pa'i shog khra/ g.yu thog rgyal tshas stong thun chen mo/ lung grangs nyi ma'i snying po/ yang g.yu thog 'bum seng gi slob ma 'bal sman nyi ma dpal gyis gces bsdus yid bzhin nor bu brtsams nas g.yu thog 'jam dpal la bshad/ des brang ti dpal ldan bzang po la gnang / de nas rgyal ba bzang po dang / dpal ldan 'tsho byed la rim par brgyud cing / dpal ldan 'tsho byed kyis dpal ldan rgyal mtshan la gnang ba'i lung bshad kyi rgyun ma nyams par mchis/

There are two physicians called Palgön Dorjé and Chögyal Tashi, also prefixed with the title Drangti, but whether they are sons of the above is difficult to say. Other medical works of those times mostly based on the eight branches include the following: Revealing Mirror Commentary by Mara Gomchen, manuscripts such as Brief Work on the Number of Chapters, Increase and Diminution, Taste Preparations, Stages of Niruha Enema Therapy, and Twenty Characteristics, and so on, composed by Yuthok Tashi Gön; Scripture Count: Essence of the Sun and Great Compilation by Yuthok Gyaltsa. Balmen Nyima Pal, a disciple of Yuthok Bumseng, composed Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of Essentials and taught it to Yuthok Jampal. He in turn taught it to Palden Sangpo, who passed it on to Gyalwa Sangpo, who in turn passed it to his son Palden Tsojé. Palden Tsojé handed it down to Palden Gyaltsen, thereby forming an unbroken lineage of transmission and teaching.

gzhan yang che rje shAkya dpal gyis le'u dang po'i Tik+ka zla zer me tog /byang mo khud pa ye shes bzang pos don gsal nyi ma'i snying po/ mtha' bzhi shi la sam+b+has khog 'bugs bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun/ mi nyag rdo rje 'bum gyis zab 'grel/ sa bcad/ rdza jo zung gis spyi khog gsal ba/ shag rams pa nyi ma dpal gyis 'grel bshad nyi ma'i 'od zer/ dge bshes rog ston gyi tshig don gsal byed/ dpal chen 'od po'i brgyud chung nyi ma'i 'khor lo/ rje sa paN gyi brgyad pa'i don bsdus/ bcom ldan ral gri'i gso dpyad rgyan gyi me tog / stag lo'i khog 'bugs dang lag len gces bsdus/ stong sman 'tsho byed gzhon nu'i brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ dngul chu grub pa'i bstan bcos/ rje btsun grags rgyal gyi rgyal po'i dkor mdzod/ sman grong pa'i gser bre dngul bre sogs

Elsewhere, other works include: Moonlight Flower Commentary to the First Chapter by Chejé Śākya Pal; Clarifying Explanation: Essence of the Sun by Jangmo Khyüpa Yeshé Sangmo; Stream of Ambrosia Medical History by Thazhi Śīlasaṃgha; Profound Commentary and its outline by Minyak Dorjé Bum; Clear Overview by Dzajo Sung; Sunlight Commentary by Shakrampa Nyima Pal; Clarifying the Meaning of the Text by Geshé Roktön; Sun Circle Commentary on the Shorter Eight Branches by Palchen Öpo; Essence of Eight Branches by the great Sakya Paṇḍita; Flower Ornament Medical Text by Chomden Raldri; Exposition on the History of Medicine and Essence of Medical Practices by Taktsang Lotsāwa; Compilation of Essentials of the Eight Branches and Treatise on Mercury Preparation by Tongmen Tsojé Shönu; Treasury of the King by Jetsün Drakpa Gyaltsen; Golden Measuring Dish and Silver Measuring Dish from the Sakya medical tradition, and so on.[576]

d.div: [576] The works commencing from Revealing Mirror Commentary by Mara Gomchen is listed in Surkhar Lodrö Gyalpo’s General Compendium and are grouped there under those works that rely mainly on Eight Branches as opposed to Four Tantras.

f.d:
mdor na bod sman mkhas pas snga phyir mdzad pa'i bstan bcos kyi grangs snga rabs pa'i yig cha ltar na/
bdun pa bod kyi mkhas pa'i lugs/ de la gtso bo mkhas pa dgu/ stong dang gnya' dang mtha' bzhi gsum/ / mi nyag brang ti g.yu thog gsum/ / bi ji che rje 'ug pa'o/ /

In short, the works of Tibetan medical scholars are listed in an old manuscript:
Point seven: the tradition of Tibetan scholars, of which there are nine principal scholars: Tong, Nyah, and Thazhi, Minyak, Drangti, and Yuthok, Biji, Chejé, and Ukpo.

d.div: de la dang po stong sman ni/ / lo tsA dz+nyA na mi tra yis/ / dbus mtha' yi don rgyal ba sogs/ / d+harma pha las rig pa 'bum/ / kun dga' dbang phyug rtsa chu yi/ / stong thun 'phrul gyi me long brtsams/ /
rgyal mtshan 'byung gnas tsha ba yi/ / stong thun bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bkod/ / dza na d+ha ra zhes bya bas/ / dmu chu'i 'phrul tshags man ngag bstan/ /
Gyaltsen Jungné’s Stream of Ambrosia Compilation on Fevers; Magic Draining of Dropsy Instructions taught by Jñānadhara;

'tsho byed grub pas 'bras bcos dang / / shAka blos byang khog thig khrims byas/ / ye shes dbang phyug gag lhog gi/ / bcos skor bdud rtsi'i thigs pa sogs/ / dpal mgon shes rab ces bya ba'i/ / mo nad bcos skor bltas chog brtsams/ /
mgon po rdo rjes rten 'brel gyi/ / brtag pa sum cu pa zhes byas/ / mchog grub gag gzer bcos thabs dang / / kun shes mig gi man ngag bstan/ /
Thirty Chapters on Examination by Charms by Gönpo Dorjé that teaches the supreme attainment treatment of gakser and the oral transmission on all-knowing eye;

byang chub dpal gyi rde bcos sogs/ / bsam gtan shes rab dpyad dbyung ni/ / chu yi 'phrul 'khor zhes bya ba/ / 'od zer mgon pos bcud len dang / / stong la stag chung zhes bya bas/ / rtsa bshad phyi gsum 'grel pa dang / / man ngag rgyud la dka'am chan sogs/ / kun dga' snying pos bcud len rigs/ / dpal shes brgyad pa'i bsdus don sbyar/ /
don grub mgon gyis rims bcos dang / / legs ldan mgon pa'i dug bcos skor/ / 'jam dbyangs thor dpyad sna tshogs bsdus/ / shes rab 'od zer snying rgyud kyi/ / don 'grel gsang ba zhes bya brtsams/ /
lo tsA dz+nyA na shAka shrI yis/ / dbus mtha'i 'grel pa rnam 'byed sogs/ / gzhon nu dbang phyug ces bya bas/ / sau ma rA dza'i bsdus don brtsams/ /
Commentary on Differentiating the Middle Way and the Extremes and so on, translated by Jñāna Śākyaśrī;[577] Essence of Somarāja by Shönu Wangchuk;
[577] Above this work was stated as being translated by Jñānamitra, as the colophon of the Degé edition confirms.
'tsho byed grub pas mig dang ni/ / rde'u'i sgos bcos mde thung sbyar/ / dkon mchog rgyal mtshan zhes bya bas/ / brgyad pa'i le dang 'grel pa brtsams/ /
Arrowhead Treatment for Eyes and Urinary Stones by Tsojé Drupa; Chapters and Commentary to Eight Branches by Könchok Gyaltsen;
'tsho byed nam mkha' rgyal mtshan gyis/ / rtsa bshad phyi gsum 'grel pa dang / / brgyad pa'i don bsdus la sogs mdzad/
and commentaries on the Root, Explanatory, and Final Tantras, on Essence of Eight Branches, and on others by Tsojé Namkha Gyaltsen.
gnya' pa rnams kyis brtsams bcos ni/ / snying rgyud 'grel pa yang dag gsal/ / ja log don khrims sde drug brtsams/ / byang chub shes rab rtsod bzlog dang / / brtson seng dbus mtha'i don bsdus sogs/ /
mtha' bzhi rin chen zhes bya bas/ / skra shad 'dzings pa'i don bsdus dang / / dar seng mgon po'i bcos kha sogs/ / mi nyag rong rje 'ga' 'ga' yis/ / ri bo brtsegs pa'i 'grel pa sogs/ /
Thazhi Rinchen composed Matted-Hair Core Meaning, and Darseng Gönpo composed Treatments. Minyak Rongjé Gaga composed Mountain Stack Commentary and so forth.
brang ti spre'us khog 'bugs sogs/ / trig hus tshad pa'i skabs drug dang / / rgyal mnyes bdud rtsi gsang mdzod sogs/ /
g.yu thog mgon po zhes bya bas/ / rat+na gser gyi rgyud sogs las/ / mchan dang de'i lo rgyus bshad/ / g.yu thog mgon po grub pa yis/ / 'grel ba don gsal la sogs brtsams/ /
Yuthok Gönpo composed Annotations and Accounts from the Golden Jewel Tantra Golden Jewel Tantra; Yuthok Gönpo Drupa composed Commentary Clarifying the Meaning and others;

g.yu thog mgon po shes rab kyis/ / man ngag bdud rtsi bcud bsdus sogs/ / mgon po rin chen zhes bya bas/ / bu gdams le'u dgu bcu bzhi/ / g.yu thog mgon po rdo rje yis/ / rgyud kyi cha lag la sogs dang / / khyung pos brgyad pa'i 'grel pa dang / / mgon po gegs kyi lag len skor/ /

bi ji legs blo zhes bya bas/ / rig byed don bsdus la sogs brtsams/ / dpal chen rtsa ba don skor gsum/ / lhun nas mgo dpyad rgya mtsho'i 'phreng / / mar blos rma bya ne tso'i skor/ / shes rab blo gros klu bcos dang / / man ngag don bsdus la sogs byas/ /
chos rje rgyal bas rten 'brel dang / / rig byed don bsdus la sogs brtsams/ / lca ses bdud rtsis bcud bsdus dang / / mgon seng byang khog yig chung sbyar/ /
[578] Text with identical name attributed to Biji Leklo above.
stag la dga' zhes bya ba yis/ / brgyad pa'i lde mig don khrigs sogs/ / ti sang brgyad pa'i don bsdus dang / / dbu lang khog dbubs la sogs brtsams/ / zhig pos don khrigs bzhi skor sogs/ /

'ug pa chos seng zhes bya bas/ / dbyig shel don gyi 'grel pa sogs/ / dbang phyug dag rgyu'i tig ka dang / / rin chen rgyal pos skor chams bshad/ / chos ses kha 'thor rin chen spungs/ / de rnams mkhas pa mi dgus bshad/ /
gzhan yang mkhas pa sna tshogs kyis/ / legs bshad sna tshogs 'di lta ste/ / mkhas pa yid 'ong legs pa yis/ / bdud rtsi le brgyad ces pa brtsams/ /
Various works taught by other scholars include: • Eight Ambrosia Chapters by Yiwong Lekpa
gzi brjid 'bar gyis sgron gsal drug / zhang ston zhig pos bdud rtsi thigs/ / phan nas dri med gzi brjid dang / / grags pa rdo rjes phan gsal drug /
• Six Illuminating Lamps by Shangtön Siji Bar • Drop of Ambrosia by Chejé Shangtön Shikpo • Stainless Brilliance by Phenné • Six Beneficial Clarifications by Drakpa Dorjé

bkra shis rdo rjes rin chen 'phreng / / chig sman dga' bos sngo sbyor che/ / byams pa brtson seng dngul chu'i sbyor/ / bkras dar tshad pa'i tig chung dang / / dge bshes dmar pos 'bum chung ni/ / me yi 'khor lo zhes pa byas/ /

• Precious Garland by Tashi Dorjé • Extensive Work on Medical Plant Preparation by Chikmen Gawo • Mercury Preparation by Jampa Tsönseng • Short Essential Work on Fevers by Tashi Dar • Small collection by Geshé Marpo called Fire Circle
rdo rje 'bum gyis tshad pa'i skor/ / rgyal 'bum gyis ni mgo bo'i bcos/ / dga' sde man ngag rig pa'i sde/ / stag sgom mngon shes can gyi ni/ / thor dpyad snying gi don bsdus sbyar/ /
• Fever Collection by Dorjé Bum • Gyalbum’s Treatments for the Head • Gadè’s Teachings in the Field of Knowledge • Compilation of Essential Miscellaneous Treatments by Takgom Ngönshé Chen

smon lam rgyal mtshan sde ma'i skor/ / nyi ma dpal gyis me btsa' dang / / sbal sman dkar nag rde ma'i bcos/ / ye shes blo gros dug bcos dang / / zla 'od gzhon nu zhes bya bas/ / brgyad pa'i don bsdus rab tu bshad/ /

• Collection on Stone Removal by Mönlam Gyaltsen • Cauterization by Nyima Pal • Treatments for Stones by Balmen Karnak • Treatments for Poisoning by Yeshé Lodrö • Essence of Eight Branches by Dawa Shönu

blo gros kyis ni khog dbubs dang / / gra ba mngon shes can gyis ni/ / rgyud kyi bsdus don grub pa sogs/ / dar ma grags gyi rtsa chu'i skor/ / 'tsho byed dkon skyabs zhes bya bas/ / tsha grang gi ni stong thun byas/ /
• History of Medicine by Lodrö • Essence of the Tantra and so on by Drapa Ngönshé • Collection on Urine and Pulse by Darma Drak • Compilation on Hot and Cold Disorders by Tsojé Könchok Kyap

jo gzungs lo rgyus sku lnga dang / / rgyud kyi dbye ba cha lag sogs/ / dbon leb man ngag sna tshogs bsdus/ / a chos mgo sogs rma yi bcos/ / rog chung dmu chu 'chag skems 'grems/ / gter ston rgya zhang khrom zhes pas/ / zab gter bcud kyi don bsdus brtsams/ /

• Five Bodies Biography, Divisions of the Tantra Auxiliary, and others, by Josung • Compilation of Various Teachings by Bönlep • Treatment of Wounds of the Head and so forth by Achö • Draining and Drying Dropsy Procedure by Rokchung • Compilation of Essential Profound Treasures by Tertön Gyashang Trom
rag shag gter ston zhes bya bas/ / pad+ma lung 'chang bsdus pa bstan/ / khyung khris thugs kyi nying khu dang / / lha 'bar gter yig don 'phral bstan/ /
• Padma Transmission Holder Compendium taught by Rakshak Tertön • Essence of the Enlightened Mind by Khyung Tri • Commentary on Meanings of Treasure Writing unearthed by Lhabar
snye mo chos kyi dbang phyug gis/ / don bzhi gsal sgron la sogs so/ / dam pa rten 'brel brgyad cu dang / / ba ris rig pa 'bum chung sogs/ /
• Lamp Illuminating the Four Points and so on by Nyemo Chökyi Wangchuk • Eighty Charms by Dampa • Small Collection on Knowledge and so forth by Bari

rje btsun grags pa rgyal mtshan gyis/ / gso dpyad rgyal po'i dkor mdzod dang / / de bzhin dpal po che yis ni/ / brgyad chu'i nyi ma'i 'khor lo dang / / mkhas mchog sa skya paN chen gyis/ / yan lag brgyad pa'i don bsdus gsungs/ /
• Medical Treasury of the King by Jetsün Drakpa Gyaltsen • Sun Circle Short Commentary on Eight Branches by Palpoché • Essence of Eight Branches by the great Sakya Paṇḍita

f.d: o rgyan pa yi sman nag dang / / bcom ral gso dpyad rgyan me tog / byang mo khud dang me gling pa'i/ / mgo bo dras med zlum bcos dang / / blo gros mtshungs med brgyad pa'i mchan/ / 'di rnams rags pa cha tsam yin/[294] / zhes dang /

• Black Medicine Text by Orgyenpa • Flower Ornament Medical Text by Chomden Raldri • Head Compresses without Surgery by Jangmo Khyüpa and Melingpa • Annotations on Eight Branches by Lodrö Tsungmé This sections ends, “This has been just a rough listing.”

f.d: phyogs bzhi'i sman pa dang gnyug mar gnas pa bcas pas bcos lugs lnga bcu rtsa drug dar ba yang / de nyid las/
Physicians coming from other lands as well as resident physicians were responsible for the propagation of fifty-six medical traditions. The text continues:

d.div: shaN+ti gar+b+has mdze nad sman gso dar/ / ha shang ya nas me dang dbyug pa dar/ / tsan pa shi las tha dpyad zas spyod dar/ / gu gu sang mdos rta yi sman dpyad dar/ /
khyol ma ru rtses yan lag chag bcos dar/ / d+harma shI las dug gi sgos bcos dar/ / lo chen rin bzang brgyad pa'i bshad srol dar/ / skyes bu me lhas lag len rgyas bshad dar/ /
pu rangs nyang sman thur ma chad med dar/ / stod sman stag chung tshang ba'i sgos bcos dar/ / 'ug pa chos sang yan lag sgyogs bcos dar/ / bi ji g.yor bas ja log bcas tshul dar/ /
che rje na gus mo nad sgos bcos dar/ / brang ti sras khyung byang khog gsal 'byed dar/ / mi nyag zla grags stong thun rgyas bshad dar/ / mtha' bzhi shAka dar rde nad gces mthong dar/ /
gnyan nag dkon ston rtsa tshigs sgos bcos dar/ / sum sman bkra shis khong nad sgos bcos dar/ / che rje grags bsod mde'u dmar 'byin dar/ / thod dkar rgyal rin mig gi thur 'byed dar/ /
gyim ljang mgo dkar 'bras kyi gra bsreg dar/ / jo mo sna mos mde 'u'i ldum bcos dar/ / 'dar ston dge 'dun tsha grang gnad 'grel dar/ / grub chen o rgyan dngul chu'i sbyor ba dar/ /
rong ston chos bzang lag len sgang dril dar/ / rog ston shes dbang sngo sbyor chen mo dar/ / dge bshes rog chung dug bcos che chung dar/ / sba sman brtson dbang yan lag rus bcos dar/ /
li sman srid 'dzin mgo yi dras bcos dar/ / gong rje sman btsun me nyi brtag pa dar/ / khra tshang 'brug las rten 'brel nad gdon dar/ / gra ba mngon shes snga rtags gcer mthong dar/ /
zhang ston gzi brjid gtso bo bshad pa dar/ / dge bshes sug ston lag len dpe khyer dar/ / pu rangs ze sman mgo bo'i ldum bcos dar/ / sum sman jo bsod rgya nag 'khyug dpyad dar/ /
lce sman jo rdor yan lag rma bcos dar/ / sba sman jo thog tsha ba'i sgang dril dar/ / srog dgongs smad rin brgyad pa'i lag len dar/ / 'brom sman bkra shis mgo dang mig dpyad dar/ /
phyug mtshams dar bsod byang khong 'phrul bcos dar/ / rdog sman bsam gtan gag lhog sgog bcos dar/ / b+he nag me 'bar me chu go ldog dar/ / zhang grung blo gros man ngag me thur dar/ /
[579] Me chu go ldog, literally “Fire and water reverse,” in which the pulse of a close relative of the patient is taken when the patient himself is inaccessible.
lkugs pa mgo gtums man ngag mde thung dar/ / khyung po gyi nas dug bcos chen mo dar/ / rag shag gter ston thor bu'i sgos bcos dar/ / sba sman chen mos rnag gi 'dren skems dar/ /
rje sman zha lus byang khog chings khrems dar/ / stong sman seng grags rde skor bshad srol dar/ / chig sman dga' bos man ngag blun tshig dar/ / snubs sman jo bsod dug gi spyi bcos dar/ /

f.d: kha rag gtsang sman bstan bcos rgyas bshad dar/ / che rje khri 'od brgyad pa'i bka' 'grel dar/ / lha rje dge 'bum sman chos zung 'brel dar/[295] / zhes de ltar snga phyi bar gsum du pur rgyal gling dgu'i ljongs 'dir gso dpyad dar bar mdzad pa'i sman pa dge ba'i bshes gnyen dpag tu med pa zhig byon na'ang /

53. Kharak Tsangmen’s extensive teachings on the treatises; 54. Chejé Triö’s commentary on the eight branches; and 55. Lhajé Gebum’s union of Dharma and medicine.[580] Therefore, throughout the past, in this land of the nine regions of Purgyal,[581] countless spiritual-friend physicians transmitted and propagated the science of medicine.

d.div: [295] gong mtshungs/
[580] The list is only 55 lines, compared to the declared 56 traditions, but one line may include two traditions. The source text is untraced.
[581] Pur rgyal or spur rgyal, “the kingdom of Pur,” the old name for Tibet.

f.d: yongs su grags pa'i sman pa mang po'i mtshan/

thams cad la yongs su grags pa ni/ paN+Di ta ltar mkhas pa gcig /nam mkha' ltar khyab pa gcig /nyi zla ltar grags pa gnyis/ mnga' bdag gi sman pa gnang ba rjes sbyangs dgu / sprul pas 'gro don mdzad pa bcu/ sbyang stobs yon tan gyi che ba drug / yongs grags sman bla lta bu bcu/ sngon sbyangs las 'phro sad pa dgu/ dpyad 'go so sor thon pa bcu/ grags pa glo bur du thon pa drug grags pa hor gyis bton pa lnga/ dpyad la nang byan tshud pa gnyis/ rgyal po ltar grags pa gcig srog shing lta bu dgu / dar byed kun tu grags pa lnga bcu rtsa brgyad rnams yod pa las/

The most renowned Tibetan physicians are classified under fifteen categories: 1. One whose wisdom was that of a paṇḍita 2. One as pervasive as the sky 3. Two as renowned as the sun and moon 4. Nine trained and lineage physicians of the king 5. Ten who manifested to work for others 6. Six who developed great qualities through training 7. Ten renowned physicians like medicine buddhas 8. Nine whose qualities came from training in previous lives 9. Ten whose traditions arose individually 10. Six whose renown arose naturally 11. Five whose renown was promoted by the Mongolians 12. Two who specialized in surgery 13. One as famous as a king 14. Nine central pillars 15. Fifty-eight renowned propagators These are identified as follows:

dang po ni lo chen rin chen bzang po/ gnyis pa ni skyes bu me lha phyag rdum/ gsum pa ni nyang smad lo tsA dang stong sman stag chung gnyis/ bzhi pa ni/ stod kyi be ji che rje 'ug pa gsum/ bar gyi g.yu thog brang ti mi nyag gsum/ smad kyi gnya' dang stong dang mtha' bzhi gsum ste dgu /

1. Rinchen Sangpo 2. Puruṣa Agnideva 3. Nyangmen Lotsāwa and Tongmen Takchung 4. Biji, Chejé, and Ukpa from the upper regions; Yuthok, Drangti, and Minyak from the central regions; and Nyawa, Tongpa, and Thazhi from the lower regions

lnga pa ni/ lcang lung sbud tra'i grub thob o rgyan pa/ byang na sngon gyi dar ston dge 'dun/ khu lung go chen sman btsun/ tong ston chos bzang / khra tshang 'brug lha/ dbur stod sum sman jo bsod/ gra ba mngon shes/ yar mda'i zhang ston gzi brjid 'bar/ gnyal ba sbur stod/ khams kyi 'od chen sprul sku dang bcu/ drug pa ni/ mang mkhar che lung pa dkon mchog skyabs/ nyang stod rgya tsha phyag rdor/ ru mtshams rgya ston jo gzungs/ mkha' reg gtsang sman rdo rje/ sbo sman bya dpe/ stong sman seng grags dang drug /
