f.d: 20. Devotion to a Master

rang gzhan gyi don phun sum tshogs pa 'grub pa'i dgos pa yin la/ de ltar gso ba rig pa nyams su len pa po sman pa dang / gtso bo nang don rig pa'am mdo sngags dam pa'i chos nyams su len pa'i rigs sogs rig pa'i gnas gang la'ang thos pa dang nyams len byed pa po rnams dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang slob dpon 'tshol dgos te/

Therefore, the value of the science of medicine is that it accomplishes the welfare of self and others. Therefore, whether they wish to become doctors and practice the science of healing or practitioners of the sacred Dharma of sutra and tantra, the essential inner science, students and practitioners of all sciences should seek out both a teacher and a master.

sdong po bkod par/
rigs kyi bu khyod kyis dge ba rgya chen po bsgrubs pa'i phyir dge ba'i bshes gnyen btsal bas mi skyo bar bya'o/ / mthong bas mi ngoms par bya'o/ / dri bas chog mi shes par bya'o/ / de zin pa ni ngan song du mi ltung / / theg chen las mi ldog / bslab pa dang mi 'gal lo/ / des na yid la bya ba rgyun mi chad par de'i drung du 'gro bar bya'o/[341] / zhes dang /

The Array of Trunks Sutra says:
Son of the lineage, in order to accumulate great virtue, do not be discouraged in seeking out the spiritual friend, never tire of seeing him, and never be sated in questioning him. Held by him you will not fall to the lower realms, turn away from the Mahayana, or run contrary to its practices. Therefore, put him in your mind and remain constantly in his presence.[746]

d.div: [341] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a sdong po brgyan pa'i le'u/ bam po/ 17_shog_283_ba4
[746] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 283b4.

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las/
mdor na byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad thob cing yongs su rdzogs pa dang / de bzhin du pha rol tu phyin pa dang sa dang bzod pa dang ting 'dzin dang mngon par shes pa dang gzungs dang spobs pa dang bsngo ba dang smon lam dang sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad thob cing yongs su rdzogs pa ni bla ma la rag las/ bla ma rtsa bar rgyur/ bla ma las byung / bla ma las skye gnas dang skye mched du gyur/ bla mas bskyed/ bla mas spel/ bla ma la brten/ bla ma rgyur gyur ba dag go[342] / zhes dang /

The Bodhisattva Basket of Scripture says:
In short, acquiring and perfecting the activities of the bodhisattva, acquiring and perfecting the perfections, the levels, the forbearances, the meditative concentrations, clairvoyance, the dhāraṇī retentions, the types of confidence, the dedications, the prayers, and the phenomena of enlightenment all depend upon a guru. The guru is their root cause. From a guru they arise. From a guru they find their birth and their development. They are produced by a guru, increased by a guru. On a guru they rely. The guru is the cause.[747]

d.div: [342] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod/ 'di'i nang 'tshol zhib byed kyang rnyed son ma byung /
[747] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, citation untraced.

f.d:
sa 'tsho byin gyis/
mkhas pas nad la sman pa bzhin/ / thog mar dam pa bsten par bya/ / nad gsos bya phyir 'bad pa yis/ / sman ni sman pa la nyan ltar/ / dam pa'i chos ni nyan par bya/ / blo dang ldan pa'i skyes bu yis/ / sman de rnams ni thos nas su/ / gus pas bsten par byed pa ltar/ / de bzhin byas pas 'chi med 'grub/ / bdud rtsi de ni 'thungs pa yis/ / mchog ni thob par byed pa yin/[343] / zhes dge ba'i bshes gnyen nam bla ma dang slob dpon mtshan nyid dang ldan zhing bsti stang gi yul du gyur pa/ khyad par rig gnas gang la slob sbyangs nyams myong phul du phyin pa zhig la brten dgos te/ de ltar ma yin par rang bzos glegs bam sogs la 'jug pa ni chos kyi byin rlabs rgyun dang mi ldan zhing / sbas don/ shugs bstan/ gab 'khrugs sogs gzhung don dpyis phyin par mi nus te/

Gopadatta says:
As the sick depend upon the doctor, so the wise rely upon a guru from the start. To cure their illness the patient earnestly attends to the doctor regarding the taking of medicine. Likewise, attend to the Dharma of the gurus. As the intelligent patient diligently follows the treatment exactly as explained, the wise by doing likewise will gain deathlessness, and by drinking of this ambrosia will attain the supreme.[748] Therefore, the spiritual friend or guru and the fully qualified master of tantra are objects of great reverence. In particular, irrespective of which science you study, it is imperative you rely upon someone with experience and mastery of the subject. If this advice is not heeded, and you mix book study with your own made-up ideas, and so on, you will lack the continuum of the blessings of the Dharma, and you will not be able to comprehend fully the meanings of those texts with profound, implicit, and deliberately veiled meanings.

d.div: [343] sde dge_4172_bstan/ spring yig_nge sa 'tsho byin/ chos smra ba dang nyan pa la gus par bya ba'i gtam/ shog_4_na1
[748] Teachings of Respect for the Teacher of Dharma and for Listening to Dharma, Toh 4172 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 4a1.

f.d:
klu sgrub kyi lugs kyi bstan bcos shes rab sdong bu las/
rig pa glegs bam la slabs kyi/ / bla ma'i thad nas ma slabs pa/ / 'phyon ma'i bud med sbrum ma bzhin/ / tshogs pa'i nang du mi mdzes so/[344] / zhes dang /

In his Shoots of Wisdom Nāgārjuna states:
The study of great works of knowledge undertaken without the tutelage of teachers makes you repugnant in society, like a pregnant whore.[749]

d.div: [344] sde dge_4329_bstan/ lugs kyi bstan bcos/ ngo mgon po klu sgrub/ shes rab sdong bu/ shog_112_na4
[749] Nītiśāstraprajñādaṇḍa, Toh 4329 Tengyur, lugs kyi bstan bcos, ngo, 112a4.

f.d:
rgyal po in+d+ra b+ho ng+hi'i gsung las kyang /
skya ba 'dzin pa med par ni/ / gru yis pha rol phyin mi nus/ / yon tan thams cad rab ldan kyang / / bla ma med na srid thar min/[345] / zhes gsungs pa ltar yin la/

The teachings of King Indrabodhi also say:
Without the boatman you cannot cross the river. Without the guru, though you possess great qualities, there is no freedom from samsara.[750]

d.div: [345] sde dge_2219_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wa_in+d+ra b+hu ti/ ye shes grub pa zhes bya ba'i sgrub thabs/ le'u/ 14_shog_51_na2
[750] Indrabodhi, Gnosis Accomplishment Sādhana (Jñānasiddhināmasādhana), chap. 14, Toh 2219 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wi, 51a2.

f.d:
'o na bla ma'am slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid ji lta bu zhig dgos snyam na/ rab sangs 'phags byang sems gdul bya'i don du sku'i bkod pa sna tshogs bstan pa/ 'bring chos nyid kyi bden pa mthong ba rnams ma yin par tha ma so skye spyir btang la/ dus 'khor rtsa rgyud las/
brtan zhing dul la blo gros ldan/ / bzod ldan drang zhing g.yo rgyu med/ / sngags dang rgyud kyi+i sbyor ba shes/ / snying rjer ldan zhing bstan bcos mkhas/ / de nyid bcu ni yongs su shes/ / dkyil 'khor 'dri ba'i las la mkhas/ / gsang sngags 'chad byed slob dpon te/ / drang ba'i bdag nyid dbang po dul/[346] / zhes gsungs pa ltar dang zhes pa sems can thams cad la lhag pa'i bsam pas gnas pa la gsungs pas/ byang chub gyi sems kyis rgyud legs par sbyangs pa dgos kyi/ de med na rdo rje slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid gal che shos gcig mi tshang / sngags dang rgyud kyi sbyor ba shes zhes pa la sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i 'grel par gsang sngags rgyud kyi sbyor ba shes zhes bton nas sngags dang sman gyi sbyor bas bgegs bzlog nus pa la kun snying gis bshad cing /[347]

But what is the mark of a guru or master? The best gurus are the buddhas or bodhisattvas, who manifest in various forms for the benefit of disciples. The next best are those who have directly perceived the nature of reality. Otherwise, the minimum qualifications for an ordinary being is expressed in the Kālacakra Root Tantra:
Stable, disciplined, and intelligent, patient, honest, and free from deception, knows mantra and the yogas of tantra, is compassionate, wise in the treatises, knows well the ten activities, is wise in drawing mandalas, a master skilled in explaining tantra, of great faith with senses tamed.[751] “Honest” is explained[752] to mean “abiding with an exceptionally kind and honest attitude toward living beings.” The mind must be well trained by the discipline of bodhicitta. Without it one of the most important qualifications of a vajra master is missing. “Knows mantra and the yogas of tantra” is rendered in the Commentary on the Illusory Net Tantra as “knows the yogas of the secret mantra tantras,”[753] and is explained by the author, Ānandagarbha, as referring to the ability to thwart hindrances by the yogas of mantra and medicine.

d.div: [346] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_dus 'khor rtsa rgyud/ le'u/ 4_shog_262_na7
[347] sde dge_2513_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ i_kun dga' snying po/ sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i rgya cher bshad pa/ shog_196_ba7

[751] Found in Puṇḍarīka, Vimalaprabhā, chap. 4, Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 262a7. This passage is also found in Aśvaghoṣa’s Fifty Verses on the Guru (Gurupañcāśikā), Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu.
[752] Here and in the following explanations on these verses, the author is citing Jé Tsongkhpa’s commentary on Fifty Verses on the Guru, his Fulfilling All Hopes of the Disciples.
[753] Māyājālamahātantrarājaṭīkā, Toh 2513 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, i, 196b7.

f.d:
rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i 'grel par/
sngags ni rkang pa brgyad pa la sogs pa'o/ / rgyud ni sman rnams so/ / sbyor ba ni bya ba'o/ / shes pa ni mkhas pa'o/ / zhes sogs kyi sngags dang rdzas kyi sgo nas rang rang gi bya ba zhi rgyas dbang drag gi las rab 'byams pa'i tshul shes pa la bshad de/[348] 'di dag mi shes na lam gya go+i ba rags pa chags pa dang cho ga khrigs la mkhas pa sogs yod kyang da dung rdo rje slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid phyogs gcig mi tshang /

In the Commentary to the Vajraḍāka Tantra:
“Mantra” refers to the eight lines, and so forth. “Tantra” refers to medicine. “Yogas” refers to practices. “Knows” means skilled.[754] Therefore, by using mantras and substances, he knows how to accomplish a host of actions by way of the four feats of pacifying, increasing, controlling, and wrath. However, if these are not mastered, he may have developed general insights on the path and be skilled in the preparation of rituals and so forth, but he still lacks the particular quality of a vajra master.

d.div: [348] sde dge_1415_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshab+ha ba b+ha dra/ rdo rje mkha' 'gro ma'i rnam bshad/ le'u/ 49_shog_204_ba3
[754] Bhavabhadra, Vajraḍākatantravivṛtti, Toh 1415 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tsha, 204b3.

f.d: bstan bcos la mkhas pa ni rdo rje gur las/ rig pa'i gnas rnams kun la mkhas/[349] / zhes gsungs pa ltar nang rig pa sde snod gsum la sogs pa shes dgos pas sde snod gang yang mi shes par rdo rje slob dpon du rlom pa ni bong bu seng ger 'chos pa dang 'dra zhing /

The Vajrapañjara Tantra explains “wise in the treatises” as “wise in all the sciences,”[755] and therefore you have to know the inner science and with it the three baskets of scripture and so on. Therefore, holding yourself to be a vajra master yet not knowing any of the baskets of scripture is to be an ass posing as a lion.

d.div: [349] sde dge_419_bka'/ rgyud/ nga rdo rje gur zhes bya ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po'i brtag pa/ le'u/ 8_shog_48_ba6
[755] Vajrapañjaratantra, chap. 8, Toh 419 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 48b6.

f.d:
de nyid bcu ni/ rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi rgyud kyi le'u tha ma las/
phyir bzlog gnyis kyi cho ga dang / / gsang dang shes rab ye shes dang / / kha sbyor 'byed pa'i cho ga dang / / gtor ma rdo rje'i bzlas pa dang / / drag shul sgrub pa'i cho ga dang / / rab tu gnas dang dkyil 'khor bsgrub/ / gsang ba'i de nyid bcu yin no/ /
dkyil 'khor ting 'dzin phyag rgya dang / / stangs stabs 'dug stangs bzlas brjod dang / / sbyin sreg mchod pa las sbyor dang / / slar yang sdud pa'i rnam pa ni/ / phyi yi de nyid bcu yin no/[350] / zhes nang gi de nyid bcu dang phyi'i de nyid bcu gsungs shing de las rgyud sde 'og ma'i rdo rje slob dpon yin na phyi'i de nyid bcu dang / bla med kyi rdo rje slob dpon yin na nang gi de nyid bcu legs par shes dgos te/ 'di dag gi don rgyas par bshad pa ni 'dir yi ger mangs par 'gyur ba'i phyir ma bris kyi logs su rtogs par bya'o//

The “ten activities” are explained in the last chapter of the Ornament of Vajra Essence Tantra:
The two rituals for repelling, the secret and wisdom knowledge empowerments, the ritual of separating, the ritual food, vajra recitation, the ritual of wrathful expression, consecration, and mandala meditation: these are the ten secret activities.
Mandala, meditative concentration, mudrā, standing posture, seated posture, recitation, the fire ritual, offering, activity yoga, and concluding: these are the ten outer activities.[756] Therefore, ten inner and ten outer activities are taught. Vajra masters of the lower classes of tantra should know the ten outer activities. Vajra masters of the highest tantras should also know the ten inner activities. An explanation of these activities would be too much, and so their explanations should be sought elsewhere.

d.div: [350] sde dge_451_bka'/ rgyud/ cha_dpal rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi rgyud ces bya ba/ le'u tha ma/ shog_57_ba7
[756] Vajrahṛdayālaṃkāratantra, Toh 451, Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 57b7.

f.d:
yang rdo rje gur gyi le'u brgyad pa las kyang /
rdo rje slob dpon mtshan ldan nyid/ / de yis nye bar bstan pa'i sngags/ / sgrub pa po la 'grub po kye/ / brtan zhing zab mo'i chos ldan dang / / rig pa'i gnas rnams kun la mkhas/ / sbyin sreg dkyil 'khor sngags shes shing / / rab gnas gtor ma'i pha rol son/ / de nyid bcu po rnam par rig / nyan thos spyod pa skyong byed cing / / sngags kyi theg pa'i rim par gus/ / gzugs ldan mthong na dga' ba dang / / dkyil 'khor 'dri mkhas bzlas par ldan/ / rtsa ba'i ltung ba rab 'joms shing / / sngags dang rgyud kyi rab sbyor gyis/ / 'jig rten rnams la bde ster ba/ / de 'dra'i bla ma dngos byas nas/ / gang gis kyang ni smad mi bya/[351] / zhes gsungs te/

Also, in the eighth chapter of the Vajrapañjara Tantra it says:
Lo! Mantra taught by the qualified vajra master will grow within the practitioner. A guru who is stable, possessed of profound Dharmas, who is wise in all the sciences, knows the fire offerings, the mandalas, and the mantras, has perfected the art of consecration and the ritual food, possesses knowledge of the ten activities, guards with the conduct of the śrāvakas while revering the stages of the mantra vehicle, whose form is a joy to behold, who is skilled in the drawing of mandalas and has completed the mantra repetitions and vanquished all root downfalls, who brings happiness and welfare to the world through the great yogas of mantra and tantra: when such a guru has materialized let no one disparage him.[757]

d.div: [351] sde dge_419_bka'/ rgyud/ nga rdo rje gur zhes bya ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po'i brtag pa/ le'u/ 8_shog_48_ba5
[757] Vajrapañjaratantra, chap. 8, Toh 419 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 48b5.

f.d: khyad par du rdo rje slob dpon la rtsa ba'i ltung ba dang mi ldan pa dgos pa 'di dag sdom 'byung las gsungs pa ni med du mi rung pa'i yan lag gtso bo yin la/ nyan thos spyod pa skyong byed cing zhes pa ni bshad rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba las slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid kyi skabs su phyi ru so so thar pa spyod cing nang du gsang ba 'dus pa'i don la dga' bar [352] gsungs pa dang don gcig pas so so thar pa'i kun spyod 'dul ba dang mthun pa'i rnam par dag pa zhig dgos par bstan la/ phyi ru zhes pa ni lus la phyi dang sems la nang du byas pa yin gyi/ khang pa'i phyi nang ma yin no/ /

In particular, the requirement that the guru not possess any of the root downfalls, as pointed out above and expressed also in the Saṃvarodaya Tantra,[758] is indispensable. The line “guarding with the conduct of the śrāvakas” illustrates the same point made in the Vajra Garland Tantra,[759] in the section on the qualifications of the vajra master, where it states that outwardly one holds the conduct of the pratimokṣa while inwardly delighting in the Guhyasamāja. Therefore, pure pratimokṣa conduct in keeping with the Vinaya is essential. “Outwardly” refers to physical behavior while “inwardly” refers to the mind. These terms do not mean outside and inside one’s dwelling.

d.div: [352] sde dge_445_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_bshad rgyud rdo rje phreng ba/ le'u/ 65_shog_271_ba2
[758] Also called the Cakrasaṃvara Tantra.
[759] Vajramālābhidhānatantra, chap. 65, Toh 445 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, 271b2.

f.d: bzlas par ldan zhes pa ni sngon du bsnyen pa rdzogs par byas pa ste/ de yang bsnyen pa sngon du ma song bar dbang bskur dang rab gnas la sogs pa la 'jug pa ni rang gis rang la gnod pa byed pa yin par gsungs te/

“Completed the mantra repetitions” means having completed the re- quired deity-yoga meditation commitment.[760] Moreover, it is taught that he who gives empowerments, performs consecration rituals, and so on without having completed the required deity-yoga meditation commitment harms himself.

d.div: [760] Bsnyen pa.

f.d:
snying po mdor bsags las/
dkyil 'khor mchog gi slob dpon gyis/ / sngon du bsnyen pa la 'bad nas/ / de nas dkyil 'khor de nyid ni/ / shin tu dul bas brtag par bya/ / lha ni mnyes par ma byas na/ / bdag nyid rnam par sun 'byin yin/[353] / zhes dang /

In the Essentials of the Mandala Rite of the Four-Seat Tantra it says:
The vajra master of the supreme mandala has first completed the deity-yoga meditation and then, with mind completely trained, turns his attention to the mandala. If the deity has not been pleased, however, you will be rejected.[761]

d.div: [353] sde dge_1613_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ya_'phags pa lha/ snying po mdor bsags pa/ shog_114_ba3
[761] Āryadeva, Catuḥpīṭhatantra-maṇḍalavidhisārasamuccaya, Toh 1613, Tengyur, rgyud ’grel ya, 114b3.

f.d:
nag po spyod pa bas kyang / / sngon du bsnyen pas lha mnyes par ma byas na rang nyid sun 'byin par gsungs so/[354] / 'phreng ba las kyang
thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam shes pas/ / sngon du bsnyen pas tshogs gsog cing / / bgegs ni rnam par nyams byed bya/ / bsnyen pa med pas dngos grub med/ / de phyir rim gnyis de nyid rig / dben par yang dag gnas nas ni/ / lha yi 'khor lo sgom par bya/ skyo na de yi gsang sngags bzlas/ / 'khor lo'i gtso bo 'bum bzlas shing / / yang na rang gi lhag lha'i 'bum/ / dkyil 'khor ba yi khri yin te/ / 'di ni sngon du bsnyen par brjod/[355] / ces dang /

Kṛṣṇacarya also said that if the deity has not been pleased by your deity-yoga meditation, you will be rejected.[762] The Vajra Garland Mandala Rites states:
With a knowledge of the path to omniscience, first gather merit through deity-yoga meditation, weaken and destroy the hindrances. With no deity-yoga meditation there are no siddhis. Therefore, know well the two stages, live well in isolation, and meditate upon the deity assembly. When tired, repeat the deity’s secret mantras. Repeat a hundred thousand of the principal deity, or a hundred thousand of one’s own deity, and ten thousand of the mandala residents, This is prerequisite deity-yoga meditation.[763]

d.div: [354] sde dge_1446_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wa_slob dpon nag po spyod pa/ bde mchog 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga shog_277_na4_lha ni mnyes par ma byas na/ /bdag nyid rnam par sun 'byin yin//
[355] sde dge_3140_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ phu_slob dpon a b+h+ya kar/ dkyil chog rdo rje phreng ba/ shog_6_na6
[762] Kṛṣṇacarya, Cakrasaṃvarasādhana, Toh 1446 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wa, 277a4.
[763] Abhyākaragupta, Vajrāvalī, Toh 3140 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, phu, 6a6.

f.d:
phreng ba las/
de ltar sngon du bsnyen pa rgyas par byas pas skad cig gis dkyil 'khor gyi lha'i rnal 'byor rnam pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa spro ba dang bsdu ba mngon du bya bar nus pas 'khor lor gnas pa nyid kyi 'khor lo can gyis ma bkag pa'am/ tshogs bsags pa nyid kyis gnang bas kyang dkyil 'khor dang rab tu gnas pa dang slob ma bsdu ba la sogs pa bya'o/[356] / zhes dang /

The Vajra Garland Mandala Rites also says:
In this way, having comprehensively undertaken the prerequisite deity-yoga meditation, you will be able to instantaneously generate and withdraw the deity assembly of the mandala, complete in every aspect. Therefore, either because it has not been forbidden by the possessors of the mandala or because you have earned permission through your accumulation of merit, you can meditate on the mandala, perform consecration, gather disciples, and so on.[764]

d.div: [356] gong mtshungs/ shog_6_ba3

f.d: de bzhin du 'jam dpal rtsa rgyud/ kr-i ya sa muts+tsha/ rab gnas kyi rgyud/ rdo rje snying po rgyan/ bshad rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba/ sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i rim pa sogs rgyud sde phal cher 'dra zhing tshig mi gcig pa du ma gsungs/

On this point, the Mañjuśrī Root Tantra, [Jagaddarpaṇa’s] Kriyāsamuccaya, the Consecration Tantra, Ornament of Vajra Essence Tantra, Vajra Garland Tantra, Illusory Net Tantra, and other tantras are mostly in agreement, although the wording is often different.

gsang sngags snga 'gyur rdo rje theg par bsnyen pa rnam gsum du grags pa/ grangs dus gnyis kyi las bsnyen thongs shing / khyad par las gang rung ba'i sngon du nye bsnyen kha gso tshad dang ldan pa dgos par gsungs pas slob ma dbang bskur ba'i dkyil 'khor de nyid kyi lha'i rnal 'byor la legs par goms par bya zhing tha na'ang grangs kyi bsnyen pa tshul bzhin du sngon du song ba zhig rdo rje slob dpon gyi med du mi rung ba'i yan lag tu shes par bya zhing /

In early translation secret mantra, the Vajra Vehicle deity-yoga meditation is said to be of three kinds. These are the completion of “activity” deity yogas based on length of time and mantra count and, particularly, the requirement of a proper “close” deity yoga before undertaking any of the tantric activities.[765] Therefore, it can be understood that thorough familiarity with the yoga of the deity of the mandala you are initiating disciples into—having at minimum completed a deity-yoga retreat with the required number of mantra repetitions—is an essential requirement for being a qualified vajra master.

d.div: [765] Presumably “activity” refers to the duration of the meditation retreat determined by the activity of performing a required number of mantras or remaining for a requisite length of time. “Close” may mean remaining in the retreat until signs of becoming close to the deity have appeared. According to Je Tsongkhapa in his Stages of Mantra, the third of these deity-yoga meditations is based upon “signs.” “Tantric activities” refers to activities of pacification, control, increase, and wrathful expression.

f.d:
mdo phyogs su dpal mgon klus/
chog shes snying rje tshul khrims ldan/ / nyon mongs sel ba'i shes rab can/ / de dag la ni khyod bsten na/ / khyod kyis mkhyen gyis gus par mdzod/[357] / ces dang /

From the point of view of the Sutra Vehicle, the glorious Nāgārjuna has said:
Content, compassionate, moral, with the intelligence to dispel the afflictions— rely upon such beings; knowing this, honor and revere them.[766]

d.div: [357] sde dge_4158_bstan/ skyes rabs/ ge_klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka92_nas 93_shog_125_ba4
[766] Precious Garland of Advice for the King (Ratnāvalī), 5:92–93, Toh 4158 Tengyur, skyes rabs, ge, 125b4. The last two lines of this verse are a little different in Gyaltsap Jé’s commentary.

Candragomin says:
Take them from a guru who abides in his vows, is wise, and has great ability.[767]
