f.d: so thar gyi sdom pa len pa'i skal ba med cing bsrung mi nus pa du ma 'byung ba ltar dang / rang mi 'dod bzhin du pha rol pos 'dzin bcug pa'am gzhan dang 'gran pa'i phyir ma yin na so thar rigs bdun gang rung dang ldan pa nges par dgos pa ni ma yin no//

There have been many cases of there being no opportunity to take the pratimokṣa vows or instances where it has been impossible to keep them. Also, as long as you do not take them for competitive reasons and you have not been forced to take them against your will, it is not actually necessary for you to be endowed with the pratimokṣa vows in order to take the bodhisattva vows.
blangs pa mi nyams par bsrung ba'i tshul la/ gang srung bar byed pa'i tshul khrims dang / de nyid ji ltar srung ba'i tshul gnyis las/
dang po ni/

rgyal sras 'phags pa thogs med kyis/
byang chub sems dpa' khyim pa'i phyogs la brten pa dang / rab byung pa'i phyogs la brten pa'i tshul khrims/ de yang mdor bsdu na rnam pa gsum ste/ sdom pa'i tshul khrims dang / dge ba'i chos sdud pa'i tshul khrims dang / sems can la phan 'dogs pa'i tshul khrims so/[407] / zhes gsungs pa ltar dang / de yang byang sems kyi bya ba ni rang rgyud smin par byed pa dang / gzhan rgyud smin par byed pa gnyis su nges pa las/ dang por nyes spyod spong ba dang legs spyod bsdu ba gnyis su nges pa'i phyir/ tshul khrims rnam pa gsum du grangs nges pa'i rgyu mtshan/ nyan thos dang thun mong sdom pa'i tshul khrims ni tshul khrims phyi ma gnyis kyi gzhi rten du gyur la/ mdo las bdag ma grol bar gzhan mi dgrol bar gsungs pa bzhin rang rgyud la dge ba sdud pa dang por ma byas par sems can gyi don byed mi nus pas go rim de ltar 'thad cing /

The bodhisattva Ārya Asaṅga has said:
Bodhisattva ethics can be found in the householder and in one ordained. In brief, ethics are of three types: the ethics of having vows, the ethics of developing virtue, and the ethics of helping others.[829] The work of the bodhisattva is twofold: ripening your own mind and ripening the minds of others; and the first of these is twofold: freeing yourself from wrong behavior and developing good behavior. This is the reason ethics has a threefold division. Moreover, the ethics of holding vows in keeping with those of the śrāvakas becomes the foundation for the other two, because as a sutra states, “Without freeing yourself, you cannot free others.” Likewise, if you do not develop virtue in yourself first, you cannot truly fulfill the needs of others. The order of these three, therefore, is also appropriate.

d.div: [407] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 10_bam po/ 8_shog_74_ba6
[829] Stages of the Bodhisattva (Bodhisattvabhūmi), chap. 10, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 74b6.

f.d: de la byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa'i tshul khrims ni/ byang sems so thar gyi sdom ldan yin na de'i rgyud kyi theg pa chen po'i byang chub sems kyis yang dag par zin pa'i so thar gang rung gi sdom pa dang / so thar dngos kyi sdom ldan min na/ rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba spong ba'i tshul khrims chos nyid kyi thob pa'am blangs pa las byung ba gang rung ni sdom pa'i tshul khrims yin la/

Concerning the first of these, the ethics of holding vows found in the bodhisattva: if a bodhisattva holds pratimokṣa vows, this refers to those pratimokṣa vows firmly held by the Mahayana bodhi mind present in his mental continuum. If the bodhisattva does not actually possess pratimokṣa vows, it refers to an innate possession or deliberate development of the ethics of abandoning acts that are wrong by nature. This too is the ethics of having vows.[830]

d.div: [830] Therefore, the term “vow” (sdom pa) is being used in its more literal sense of “restraint” and not as some formal commitment.

f.d: dge ba chos sdud ni/ mdor na byang sems kyi sdom pa yang dag par blangs pa'i 'og tu de'i rgyud kyi theg pa chen po'i byang sems kyis yang dag par zin pa'i sgo nas pha rol tu phyin pa drug la sogs pa lus ngag yid gsum gyi dge ba bsags pa gang ci yang rung ba de dag thams cad do/ /

Briefly, the ethics of developing virtue refers to the following. Having taken the bodhisattva vows properly, and with your whole continuum grasped by the Mahayana bodhi mind, you engage as appropriate in acts of gathering virtue by physical, verbal, and mental means through the practices of the six perfections, and so on.

sems can don byed kyi tshul khrims ni/ byang sdom de yang dag par thob nas theg pa chen po'i byang sems kyis zin pa'i sgo nas grogs bya dgos pa dang / thabs la rmongs pa dang / phan 'dogs dang / 'ja_gis pas nyen pa dang / mya ngan gyis gzir ba dang / yo byad kyis phongs pa dang / gnas 'cha' bar 'dod pa dang / blo mthun par 'dod pa dang / yang dag par zhugs pa dang / log par zhugs pa dang / rdzu 'phrul gyis gdul bar bya ba ste rnam pa bcu gcig gi don ji ltar rigs par sgrub pa'o//

The ethics of helping others means the following. Having taken the bodhicitta vows and with your continuum grasped by the Mahayana bodhi mind, you work as appropriate for others in eleven ways. You help those in need of companionship, those confused in their way, those in need of help, those in danger, those tormented by grief, those bereft of possessions, those seeking a place to stay, those wishing for peace and harmony, those who have entered the correct paths, those who have gone astray, and finally you help by taming others with your supernatural powers.
ji ltar bsrung ba'i tshul yang /

d.i: The way to protect bodhisattva ethics

f.d:
rgyas sras zhi ba lhas bslab pa kun las btus su/
byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa ni/ / rgyas par theg pa che las 'byung /[408] / zhes dang /
dge ba'i bshes gnyen mi btang zhing / / mdo sde rnams la rtag blta bas/[409] / zhes thabs de dag gi sgo nas bsrung bar bshad pas na spyir theg chen gyi bslab pa'i gnas rnams la rang nyid goms pa lhur byed cing gdul bya gzhan dag kyang tshul de la sbyar ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen mi gtong bar gus pas bsten pa ni bsrung thabs kyi gtso bo yin la/ gzhan yang theg pa chen po'i mdo sde rin po che rnams dang / khyad par byang sa dang bslab btus la thos bsam legs par bya zhing / de tsam ma lcogs kyang tshul khrims le'u tsam la nges par sbyangs nas/ byang sems bslab pa'i gnas mtha' dag la sgro 'dogs chod cing mkhas par bya gal che ste/ de ltar ma yin na 'jug ldog bya ba'i gzhir gyur ba'i blang dor gyi gnas rnams la rmongs par 'gyur bas so//

The bodhisattva Śāntideva in his Compendium of Practice says:
The vows of the bodhisattva arise extensively within the Mahayana.[831] Also:
By never giving up the spiritual friend, by constant study of the sutras.[832] These verses state that these are the methods for protecting ethics. Therefore, you should familiarize yourself with the points of practices and devote yourself completely to the spiritual friend who brings those practices to other disciples. These are the main methods for keeping your ethics. You should also apply yourself well to the study and contemplation of the precious Mahayana sutras and especially to Stages of the Bodhisattva and Compendium of Practice. If that is not possible, it is important to at least study thoroughly the ethics chapter of Stages of the Bodhisattva and to become learned and be able to eliminate misconceptions about all points of bodhisattva practice. Without doing that, you will remain confused on what is to be developed and what is to be discarded, which is the foundation of the practices of engaging and rejecting.

d.div: [408] sde dge_3939_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ bslab pa kun las btus pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa/ shog_1_na3
[409] sde dge_3939_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon zhi ba lha/ bslab pa kun las btus pa' tshi+ig le'ur byas pa/ shog_2_na1
[831] Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3939 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 1a3.

f.d:
'o na byang sems las dang po pas mdo sde dag nas 'byung ba'i bslab bya rnams las ji tsam zhig la bslab ce na/ theg bsdus las/
byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa'i rab tu dbye ba tshad med de/[410] zhes dang / slob dpon byang chub bzang pos sdom pa nyi shu pa'i 'grel par/
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnams ni tshad med cing mthar thug pa med pa'i phyir ro/[411] / zhes rgyas par phye na byang sems kyi bslab pa'am spyod pa la grangs dang tshad med cing / 'on kyang grangs nye bar mtshon te gsungs pa ni/ sman bla'i mdo las/
byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa bslab pa'i gzhi bzhi brgya po dag 'dzin pa dang /[412] zhes bzhi brgyar bshad cing /

It might then be asked, to what extent should a novice bodhisattva engage in these practices taught in these sutras? The Compendium of the Mahayana says:
There are limitless divisions of bodhisattva practices.[833] Also, Ācārya Bodhibhadra in his Commentary on the Twenty Verses on the Bodhisattva Vows:
The practices of the bodhisattva are immeasurable and without limit.[834] Therefore, when divided extensively the practices or commitments of the bodhisattva are beyond number and measure. They can, however, be illustrated numerically. The Medicine Buddha Sutra mentions four hundred:
The bodhisattva vows hold four hundred commitments.[835]

d.div: [410] sde dge_4048_bstan/ sems tsam/ ri_'phags pa thogs med/ theg pa chen po bsdus pa/ bam po/ 3_shog_32_na5
[411] sde dge_4083_bstan/ sems tsam/ hi_slob dpon byang chub bzang po/ sdom pa nyi shu pa'i dka' 'grel/ shog_186_na7
[412] sde dge_504_bka'/ rgyud/ da 'phags pa bcom ldan 'das sman gyi bla baiDUR+ya'i 'od kyi sngon gyi smon lam gyi khyad par rgyas pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo/ shog_280_na3
[833] Asaṅga, Mahāyānasaṃgraha, fascicle 3, Toh 4048 Tengyur, sems tsam, ri, 32a5.
[834] Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśakapañjikā, Toh 4083 Tengyur, sems tsam, hi, 186a7.
[835] Bhaiṣajyagurusūtra, Toh 504 Kangyur, rgyud, da, 280a3.

f.d:
zhi ba 'tshos nyi shu pa'i 'grel par/
byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa'i gzhi stong phrag du ma/[413] zhes dang / rtog ge 'bar ba las/
byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa'i gnas bdun brgya la yang snang /[414] zhes dang /

Śāntarakṣita in his Commentary on the Twenty Verses on the Bodhisattva Vows says:
There are many thousands of bodhisattva commitments.[836] Blaze of Reasoning says:
There are seven hundred points of bodhisattva practice.[837]

The four hundred practices of the bodhisattva.[838] Buddha Vairocana’s Teachings on Bodhisattva Practice also talks of ten defeats and forty-eight downfalls.[839] Therefore, in these and other passages, various numbers are mentioned commensurate with the capacity of disciples’ minds. However,

f.d:
deng sang grags che ba 'jam mgon chos kyi rgyal po btsong kha pas byang chub gzhung lam du pham pa'i sde tshan dang nyes byas kyi sde tshan gnyis su phye ba'i dang po/ rtsa ltung ngam pham pa ni/ nam mkha'i snying po'i mdo las gsungs pa'i don zhi ba lhas bslab btus su len par mdzad pa'i tshigs bcad/
dkon cog gsum gyi dkor 'phrog pa/ / phas pham pa yi ltung bar 'dod/ / dam pa'i chos ni spong byed pa/ / gnyis par thub pas gsungs pa yin/ / tshul khrims 'chal pa'i dge slong la'ang / / ngur smrig 'phrog dang brdeg pa dang / / btson rar 'jug par byed pa dang / / rab tu byung las 'bebs pa dang / / mtshams med lnga po byed pa dang / / log par lta ba 'dzin pa dang / / grong la sogs pa 'jig pa dang / / rtsa ba'i ltung bar rgyal bas gsungs/ /

These days the most popular delineation of the commitments comes from the great Dharma king Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa in his Highway to Enlightenment, where they are divided into defeats and faults. The defeats or root downfalls have been taken from the Ākāśagarbha Sutra by Śāntideva and put into verse in his Compendium of Practice:
1. Stealing possessions of the Three Jewels is asserted as a downfall by defeat. 2. The second, the mighty Buddha has proclaimed, is to abandon the sacred Dharma. 3. Toward monks—even those of fallen ethics— stealing their robes, beating them, casting them into prison, causing them to leave their ordination, 4. committing any of the five heinous acts, 5. holding to wrong views, 6. and destroying towns and suchlike are said by the Buddha to be root downfalls.

blo sbyong ma byas sems can la/ / stong pa nyid ni brjod pa dang / / sangs rgyas nyid la zhugs pa dang / / rdzogs pa'i byang chub ldog pa dang / / so so thar pa yongs spangs te/ / theg pa che la sbyor ba dang / / slob pa'i theg pa chags la sogs/ / spong bar 'gyur ba min zhes 'dzin/ / pha rol dag kyang 'dzin 'jug dang / / tshigs bcad rgyu yis gzhan smod dang / / rang gi yon tan brjod pa dang / / rnyed pa dang ni bkur bsti dang / / bdag ni zab mo bzod pa'o zhes/ / log pa nyid ni smra ba dang / / dge sbyong chad pas spyod 'jug dang / / dkon cog gsum gyi sbyin byed dang / / sbyin pa len par byed pa dang / / zhi gnas 'dor bar byed pa dang / / yang dag 'jog gi longs spyod rnams/ / kha ton byed la sbyin pa rnams/ / de dag rtsa ba'i ltung ba ste/ / sems can dmyal ba chen po'i rgyu/[418] / zhes pa 'di la nam mkha'i snying po'i mdor rgyal rigs spyi bo nas dbang bskur ba zhes sogs/[419]

7. Talking of emptiness to those with minds untrained, 8. turning away from full enlightenment those dwelling in the way of the Buddha, 9. bringing others to the Mahayana by causing them to leave the pratimokṣa, 10. maintaining that the śrāvaka vehicle does not bring an end to desire and so forth, and causing others to hold that view, 11. talking of your own qualities for the sake of gain and reputation while abusing others in verse and other writings, 12. falsely proclaiming that you realize the profound, 13. punishing those intent on virtue by taking that given to the Three Jewels, 14. and abandoning śamatha, giving the possessions of those in meditation to those reciting scripture: These are the root downfalls, causes for the great hells.[841] On these the Ākāśagarbha Sutra it says, “Those of royal lineage empowered from the crown of their heads,”[842] and so on.

f.d: rgyal po'i rtsa ltung lnga blon po'i rtsa ltung lnga/ las dang po pa'i rtsa ltung brgyad de bco brgyad du ming 'dogs pa dang / 'jam dbyangs bla ma btsong kha pas rtsa ltung ngam pham pa dngos bcu bzhi dang / yan lag bzhi ste bco brgyad du mdzad pa don la khyad par med/ nyes byas kyi sde tshan la byang sa las rnam grangs bzhi bcu rtsa drug [420]gsungs pa mdor bsdu na/ dge ba'i chos sdud pha rol tu phyin pa drug gi mi mthun phyogs ser sna la sogs pa'i nyes pa dang / sems can don byed kyi mi mthun phyogs kyi nyes pa rnams spong dgos par gsungs so//

This means that five root downfalls are labeled as downfalls of the king, five are downfalls of the minister, and eight are called downfalls of beginners. Lama Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa’s categorization of fourteen root downfalls or defeats and four branch downfalls is essentially the same. Concerning the category of faults, Stages of the Bodhisattva lists forty-six faults to be abandoned. In brief, these are explained as being faults of miserliness and so forth—hindrances to the gathering of virtue as outlined by the practices of the six perfections—and faults that hinder working for the benefit of others.

f.d: sdom pa gtong ba'i rgyu ni/

smon sems btang ba dang / pham ba'i gnas lta bu'i chos de dang gang yang rung ba kun nas dkris pa chen pos spyad pa dang / sdom pa phul ba gsum gang yang rung bas gtong bar bshad/ de yang so so thar pa'i sdom pa ni bsrung ma nus pa na phul bas sdom pa'i rgyun rjes su 'jug pa'i bsod nams chad pa yin gyi/ sdom pa phul ba de nyid kyi cha nas sdig pa chen po mi bskyed la/ byang sdom phul na ni/ phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas sras bcas thams cad kyi spyan sngar sems can thams cad kyi phan bde sgrub par khas blangs te sdom pa bzung ba las 'das shing sangs rgyas dang sems can de dag thams cad bslus pas ngan 'gro mu mtha' med par 'khyam dgos te/ spyod 'jug las/
gal te de ltar dam bcas nas/ / las kyis sgrub pa ma byas na/ / sems can de dag kun bslus pas/ / bdag gi 'gro ba ji ltar 'gyur/[421] / zhes sogs mang du gsungs la rnam smin shin tu lci'o//

Three causes for losing the vows have been taught: giving up the aspiring bodhicitta; following any action that is similar to a “cause for defeat” and that is accompanied by the complete binding factors;[843] and thirdly, returning the vows. Any of these constitutes a cause for losing the vows. If you are unable to keep the pratimokṣa vows and return them, you cut the merit of continuing in the vows, but the actual handing back of the vows is not in itself a great wrong. However, to hand back the bodhisattva vows is to transgress those vows you made by promising in the presence of all the buddhas and bodhisattvas to work for and to bring about the welfare and happiness of all living beings. It is a betrayal of both the buddhas and sentient beings, and consequently you will have to wander endlessly in the lower realms. Engaging in the Practices of the Bodhisattva states:
If, when I have promised such, I do not accomplish it, I betray all those sentient beings; what kind of birth then shall I take?[844]

d.div: [421] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug /le'u/ 4_sh+loka4_shog_8_na4

[843] “Defeats” (pham pa) here refers to the defeats of the fully ordained monk. “Cause” (gnas) refers to the mental afflictions such as desire that bring about defeats. See Tatz, p. 51. To be a complete severing of the vow, there must be four binding factors (kun dkris chen po): habitually repeating of the fault, having no sense of shame, taking joy in the fault, not regarding it as a fault.
[844] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 4:4, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 8a4.

f.d: nyams pa phyir bcos pa ni/

Although striving not to be tainted by faults, if you should incur a fault by the four causes of downfall—ignorance, unawareness, a preponderance of mental affliction, and disrespect—you restore the vows in accord with the proper way.

d.div: [422] sde dge_4081_bstan/ sems tsam/ hi_slob dpon tsan+d+ra go mi/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa nyi shu pa/ shog_166_ba5

[845] Candragomin, Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśaka, Toh 4081 Tengyur, sems tsam, hi, 166b5. Śāntarakṣita’a commentary to the Twenty Verses explains this phrase as meaning that if there is no suitable person present, you should confess in front of your own mind, and then later if possible, you should confess again to another person. Sakya Drakpa Gyaltsen’s commentary explains it to mean that faults driven by afflictions should be confessed before another person and those not driven by affliction may be confessed internally (Tatz, p. 29).

f.d:
de ltar deng sang grags che ba so thar lta bu'i sdom pa gzugs can ma yin pa/ sa paN gyis/
byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa ni/ / sems las skye phyir gzugs can min/[423] / zhes sangs rgyas ma thob kyi bar yang mi gtong bar bshad la/ bye brag smra ba lugs kyi so thar gzugs can du 'dod pa ltar de gzugs can yin pas shi ma 'phos par mi gtong bar song na de lugs kyi bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pas ma nges shing / yang sdom pa gzugs can ma yin pas shi nas kyang mi gtong bar song na dbu ma rnams so thar shes pa'i ngo bor 'dod pas shi 'phos nas mi gtong bar song bas ji srid dang de nas de'i bar gyi khas blangs pa'i dus kyis phye ba las gzugs can yin min gyi dbye ba med pa bstan nam snyam/

A popular view these days is that the pratimokṣa and other vows do not possess form. Sakya Paṇḍita says:
The vows of the bodhisattva, being born from mind, have no form.[846] This is saying that they are not lost, even up to the attainment of enlightenment. If they did possess form, in the same way that the Vaibhāṣika school asserts the pratimokṣa to have form, and that meant that they remained until death destroyed them, this would render some uncertainty about the upavāsa vows found in their tradition that are taken for one day only. On the other hand, if vows had no form and this meant that they were not lost even after passing beyond death, then the Madhyamaka assertion that the pratimokṣa possess the nature of consciousness would mean that even after death they too would persist. Therefore, I am fairly sure that these divisions are created on the basis of time, in which you pledge to keep the vows until a certain event occurs or for a fixed length of time, and not on the basis of whether they are form.

d.div: [423] sa skya paN+Di ta kun dga' rgyal mtshan gyi gsung 'bum/ na sdom gsum rab dbye/ shog_2_ba2_sa skya'i bka' 'bum pod lnga pa/ na shog2_ba2

chos gsum dang ldan na sngags kyi spyod pa yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur te/ gsum po gang zhe na/ sems can thams cad yongs su mi gtong ba nyid dang / byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims kyi sdom pa bsrung ba dang / rang gi sngags yongs su mi gtong ba nyid do/[424] / zhes dang /

To enter the secret mantra Vajrayana, these bodhisattva vows are also indispensable. The Mañjuśrī Root Tantra, in the first chapter on the collection of rituals, states:
If three things are present, the practice of mantra will be complete. What are these three? Not to give up on all living beings, guarding the vows of the bodhisattva ethic, and never giving up one’s mantra.[847]

kye rdo rje'i bshad rgyud rdo rje gur gyi le'u bcu gnyis pa las/
byang chub sems su 'di bgyi ste/ / bdag dang gzhan don rab sgrub phyir/ / bdag gi byang chub sems mchog bskyed/ / e ma ho sems can kun mgron gnyer/ / byang chub spyod mchog mdzad bzhin spyad/ / 'gro la phan phyir sangs rgyas shog[426] / ces mad sngogs zung du 'jug pa'i lam po che 'di'i phan yon kyang / sdong pos brgyan pa'i mdo'i bam po brgya bcu gsum pa las/
rigs kyi bu 'di lta ste dper na/ me mar gcig cig khyim mam khang bu ji lta bur bcug kyang rung ste/ bcug ma thag tu lo stong du bsags bsags pa'i mun pa yang rnam par sel zhing snang bar byed do/ / de bzhin du byang chub kyi sems bskyed pa gcig kyang sems can gyi bsam pa'i khyim 'thibs po ma rig pa'i mun pa dang ldan pa ci yang rung ste/ de'i rgyud du phyin na de phyin ma thag tu bskal pa brgya stong brjod du med par bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang / mun pa thams cad rnam par sel zhing ye shes kyi snang ba yongs su bskyed do/[427] / zhes sems bskyed mtshan nyid pa de rgyud la skyes pa tsam gyis bskal pa du mar bsags pa'i sgrib pa thams cad skad cig gis 'joms nus pa dang /

The Hevajra explanatory tantra, the Vajrapañjara, states in the twelfth chapter:
This I will do for the bodhi mind: to accomplish the wishes of myself and others, I generate the supreme bodhi mind. Emaho! Inviting all living beings as guests, I will emulate the great deeds of the enlightened and become a buddha for the benefit of living beings.[849] On the benefits of following this great path of sutra and tantra combined, the Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra says:
Son of the family, it is like this. Just one shaft of light may enter a house or a room and all darkness therein present for thousands of years is immediately dispelled and replaced by light. Similarly, if just one generation of the bodhi mind enters the house of the mind of any sentient being, black with the dense darkness of ignorance, immediately the darkness and obstructions of karma and mental affliction accumulated over countless thousands of eons are dispelled, and the light of wisdom is born.[850] Therefore, a genuine bodhicitta, just by being generated in the mind, can remove in an instant the mental obstructions accumulated over many eons. Also

f.d:
byams pas 'jug pa'i mdo las/
rigs kyi bu 'di lta ste/ dper na rdo rje rin po che ni chag kyang gser gyi rgyan khyad par du 'phags pa thams cad zil gyis non cing rdo rje'i rin po che'i ming yang mi 'dor la dbul ba thams cad kyang rnam par bzlog go/ / rigs kyi bu de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen par sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje rin po che nan tan dang bral yang nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi yon tan gyi rgyan thams cad zil gyis non cing byang chub sems dpa'i ming yang mi 'dor la 'khor ba'i dbul ba thams cad kyang rnam par bzlog go[428] / zhes byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnams la ma bslabs kyang smon pa byang chub kyi sems de yod na byang chub sems dpar gsungs pa dang /

in the Maitreya Prasthāna Sutra:
Son of the family, it is like this. The precious diamond, even when broken, still outshines all wonderful golden ornaments, does not lose the name “diamond,” and will still dispel all poverty. Son of the family, similarly, the precious diamond of the mind generated toward omniscience, even when lax, still outshines all the ornaments of achievements of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and without losing the name of bodhisattva will dispel all the poverty of samsara.[851] Therefore, even when not engaged in the practices of the bodhisattva, if you have the aspiring bodhicitta, you are still a bodhisattva.

Atiśa in his Light on the Path:
The merit of the bodhi mind, were it to have form, would fill the realms of space and yet still be more.
Someone may fill with precious jewels Buddha realms as many as sand grains in the Ganges and offer them to the lord of the world, yet he who puts his palms together and bows his mind toward enlightenment makes the greater offering.[854] Thus, the benefits of the bodhi mind are extensively described in the precious sutras and cannot be adequately reproduced here.

khyim bdag 'di la byang chub sems dpa' khyim pa khyim na gnas pas sangs rgyas la skyabs su 'gro bar bya'o/ / chos la skyabs su 'gro bar bya'o/ / dge 'dun la skyabs su 'gro bar bya'o/ / de gsum la skyabs su song ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba de bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yongs su bsngo bar bya'o/[432] / zhes dang /
khyim bdag gzhan yang byang chub sems dpa' khyim pa ni bslab pa'i gzhi thams cad yongs su bzung ba yin te/ 'di lta ste bslab pa'i gzhi lnga yongs su bzung nas/ zhes yongs rdzogs dge bsnyen gyi sdom pas mtshon bslab pa'i gzhi mang du gsungs pa dang /[433]

Also, in the Sutra Requested by the Householder Ugra found in the nineteenth volume of the Heap of Jewels collection:
Householder, the bodhisattva householder living in a house should go for refuge to the Buddha, go for refuge to the Dharma, and go for refuge to the Sangha.[855] And:
Householder, furthermore, the bodhisattva householder holds completely the foundations of practice. It is like this: holding completely the five commitments of practice…[856] Thus much is taught on the commitments of practice using the vows of a complete upāsaka practitioner as an illustration.

d.div: [432] sde dge_63_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga khyim bdag drag shul can gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 1_shog_259_na2
[433] sde dge_63_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga khyim bdag drag shul can gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 1_shog_261_ba4
[855] Ugraparipṛcchā, fascicle 1, Toh 63 Kangyur, bkon brtsegs, nga, 259a2.

f.d:
'dus pa nyi shu rtsa bzhi ba 'dul ba rnam par gtan la dbab pa nye bar 'khor gyis zhus pa las/
nye bar 'khor de'i phyir khyod kyis nyan thos kyi theg pa pa rnams kyi bslab pa ni sbyor ba gzhan dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa gzhan gyis yongs su dag pa yin par smos shig /de ci'i phyir zhe na/ nye bar 'khor nyan thos kyi theg pa pa rnams kyi sbyor ba yang gzhan/ lhag pa'i bsam pa yang gzhan la/ theg pa chen po la yang dag par zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sbyor ba yang gzhan/ lhag pa'i bsam pa yang gzhan yin pa'i phyir ro/ / nye bar 'khor de la nyan thos kyi theg pa pa'i tshul khrims yongs su dag pa gang yin pa de ni theg pa chen po la yang dag par zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims yongs su ma dag pa nyid dang / shin tu 'chal pa'i tshul khrims nyid yin no/ / de ci'i phyir zhe na/ nye bar 'khor 'di la nyan thos kyi theg pa pa ni/ de'i skad cig tsam yang srid par skye ba len par mi byed do/ / de ni nyan thos kyi theg pa pa'i tshul khrims yongs su dag pa nyid yin la/ de ni theg pa chen po la yang dag par zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims yongs su ma dag pa nyid dang / shin tu 'chal ba'i tshul khrims yin pa'i phyir ro/[434] / zhes dang /

In the Sutra Requested by Upāli, from the twenty-fourth volume of the Heap of Jewels collection in the chapter “Determining the Vinaya,” it states:
Upāli, therefore, you should say that the practices of those of the śrāvaka vehicles are made pure by different actions and by different thoughts. Why is that? Upāli, the actions and the thoughts of those of the śrāvaka vehicles are one thing, and the actions and the thoughts of those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana are another. Upāli, whatever is pure ethics for those of the Śrāvakayāna is impure ethics, improper ethics, for those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana. Whatever is pure ethics for those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana is impure ethics, improper ethics for those of the Śrāvakayāna. Why is that? Upāli, those of the Śrāvakayāna do not seek, even for an instant, to take rebirth in samsara. That is pure ethics for those of the Śrāvakayāna. That is impure ethics, improper ethics for those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana.[857]

d.div: [434] sde dge_68_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca 'phags pa nye bar 'khor gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 2_shog_123_na7
[857] Vinayaviniścayaupāliparipṛcchā, fascicle 21, Toh 68 Kangyur, bkon brtsegs, ca, 23a7.

f.d: nye bar 'khor de lta bas na/ khyod kyis theg pa chen po la yang dag par zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bslab pa ni rjes su bsrung ba dang bcas pa yin par smos shig /nyan thos kyi theg pa pa rnams kyi bslab pa ni rjes su srung ba med pa yin par smros shig / theg pa chen po la yang dag par zhugs pa'i byung chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bslab pa ni bcos su yod pa yin par smros shig / nyan thos kyi theg pa pa rnams kyi bslab pa ni bcos su med pa yin par smos shig[435] / ces sogs dang /

Also:
Therefore, Upāli, you should say that the commitments of those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana are to be guarded. You should say that the commitments of those of the Śrāvakayāna should not be guarded. You should say that the commitments of those bodhisattvas who have truly entered the Mahayana are to be undertaken. You should say that the commitments of those of the Śrāvakayāna should not be undertaken.[858]

d.div: [435] sde dge_68_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca 'phags pa nye bar 'khor gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 2_shog_124_na1

f.d:
shA ri'i bu de la byang chub sems dpa'i nyes pa dang po'i lci ba ni tshogs bcu la drang por bshags par bya'o/ / bud med kyi lag pa nas 'dzin pa'i lag pa'i nyes pa lci ba ni tshogs lnga la bshags par bya'o/ / nyon mongs pa can gyi sems kyi mig gis bltas pa'i nyes pa ni gang zag gcig gam/ gnyis kyi mdun du bshags par bya'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' mtshams med pa lnga dang ldan pa'i nyes pa dang / bud med kyi nyes pa dang / khye'u'i nyes pa dang / lag pa'i nyes pa dang / mchod rten gyi nyes pa dang / dge 'dun gyi nyes pa dang / de las gzhan pa'i nyes pa lci ba rnams ni sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das sum cu rtsa lnga'i spyan sngar gcig pus nyin mtshan du bshags par bya'o// de la bshags pa ni 'di yin te/ bdag ming 'di zhes bgyi ba sangs rgyas la skyabs su mchi'o/ / nas/
yon tan bsngags pa mtha' yas rgya mtsho 'dra kun la/ / thal mo sbyar bar bgyis te skyabs su nye bar mchi/[436] / zhes pa'i bar deng sang ltung bshags su grags pa phung po gsum pa'i mdo gsungs nas/

Also:
Śāriputra, the first serious fault of the bodhisattva should be confessed in the presence of ten. The fault of taking a woman by the hand should be confessed in the presence of five. The fault of looking at her with a deluded mind should be confessed in the presence of one or two persons. The faults of the bodhisattva committing the five heinous acts, the faults concerning women, children, the hand, the shrine, the Sangha, and other serious faults should be confessed day and night solely in the presence of the thirty-five buddhas. The procedure of this confession is as follows: “I of such and such name go for refuge to the Buddha…” The passage continues up to:
To those who possess ocean-like achievements, exalted beyond number, I put my hands together and go for refuge.[859] This confession is the Sutra of the Three Heaps, known these days as the Confession of Downfalls recitation.

d.div: [436] sde dge_68_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca 'phags pa nye bar 'khor gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 2_shog_120_na3

[859] Vinayaviniścayaupāliparipṛcchā, fascicle 2, Toh 68 Kangyur, bkon brtsegs, ca, 120a3. The sutra excerpt beginning with the address to Śāriputra and containing the Sutra of the Three Heaps is quoted in full in Śāntideva’s Compendium of Practice, but in the Degé edition of the sutra, only the passages addressed to Upāli are found.

f.d: shA ri'i bu de ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das sum cu rtsa lnga po de dag la sogs pa de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad ldan pa'i yid la byed pa dag gis sdig pa thams cad rnam par dag par bya'o/ / zhes byang chub sems dpa'i bslab bya dang / ltung ba dang / de bshags pa/ so thar dang byang sdom gyi khyad par sogs snga rabs pa rnams nas gleng bar ma mdzad pa'i brda 'chad bag tsam 'dug pa kho bos 'dir sgo 'byed kyi tshul du mgo smos tsam bgyis pa yin la/ slad du byang sdom la rgyas bshad mdzad bzhed kyi rtogs dpyod mkhan yod na mdo der gzigs te smra ba'i ljags ring por rkyong bar 'tshal lo//

The text continues:
Śāriputa, in this way the bodhisattva with his mind concentrated on the thirty-five buddhas and all the tathāgatas should purify all wrong acts. These passages—on bodhisattva commitments, downfalls, confession procedures, and the differences between the pratimokṣa vows and the bodhisattva vows—which have not been elaborated on by commentators of the past, and on which there is little explanation, I have presented here only as an opener for further amplification. In the future, if any wise scholars wish to write extensively on the subject of bodhisattva vows, I would ask them to examine this sutra and flex their tongues.
gsang sngags kyi sdom pa/
23. Vidyādhara Tantric Vows

gsum pa rig 'dzin sngags kyi sdom pa ni/ sa skya paN+Ditas/
rdo rje theg pa'i lam zhugs te/ / myur du sangs rgyas thob 'dod na/ / smin sgrol gnyis la 'bad par bya/[437] / zhes dang /
smin par byed pa'i dbang bskur yang / / bla ma brgyud pa ma nyams shing / / cho ga 'khrugs par ma gyur pa/ / phyi nang rten 'brel bsgrig mkhyen cing / / sku bzhi'i sa bon thebs nus pa/ / sangs rgyas gsung bzhin mdzad pa yi/ / bla ma btsal la dbang bzhi blangs/ / de yis sdom pa gsum ldan 'gyur/[438] / zhes rdo rje slob dpon bla ma lnga bcu bar gsungs pa'i khro ba dang nga rgyal la sogs pa'i skyon dang bral zhing / snying rje dang de nyid bcu la sogs pa'i yon tan dang ldan pa/

Sakya Paṇḍita states:
Having entered the Vajrayana path, if you wish to attain buddhahood soon, strive in the stages of ripening and liberation. Also:
For the ripening of the empowerment, seek out a guru with lineage undiminished, who does not confuse the procedures, who is wise in organizing inner and outer rituals, who is capable of planting seeds of the four bodies,[860] and who acts in accord with the words of the Buddha. From him take the four empowerments; through him one becomes a holder of the three vows.[861] Therefore, the vajra master is one who is free from the faults of anger, pride, and so on, and who possesses the qualities of compassion and the achievements of the ten activities, as taught in [Aśvaghoṣa’s] Fifty Verses on the Guru.

d.div: [437] sa skya paN+Di ta kun dga' rgyal mtshan gyi gsung 'bum/ na sdom gsum rab dbye/ shog_18_na2
[438] sa skya paN+Di ta kun dga' rgyal mtshan gyi gsung 'bum/ na sdom gsum rab dbye/ shog_18_na2
[860] These are the four enlightened bodies or forms of a buddha.
[861] Treatise on the Classification of the Three Vows, Collected Works, na, 18a2.

f.d: kun tu bzang po'am rdo rje 'chang nas brgyud pa'i chu bo ma nub pa/ byin rlabs kyi ngad ma yal ba/ gdams ngag gi sarga [439]ma log pa/ mos gus kyi bsam pa tshim pa ste snyan brgyud bzhi tshang ba/ bla ma gong ma'i phyag len ji ltar mdzad pa'i bka' srol ma 'phyugs pa smar 'khrid kyi gsung rgyun khungs ma'i sgo nas cho ga rnams ma 'khrugs pa'i dmigs phyed pa/ sbyang gzhi dang sbyang bya dang / sbyong byed dang sbyang 'bras rnams thad kar ngo sprod shes pa zhig dgos la/ de lta bus slob ma la smin par byed pa dbang dang / grol bar byed pa'i khrid/ rgyab brten lung dang bcas pa de la brten nas bskyed rdzogs kyi rim pa nyams su bstar ba sogs rjes su 'dzin dgos pa las/

He should possess the four oral transmissions: a lineage beginning from Samantabhadra or Vajradhara whose river not dried up, whose aroma of blessing has not vanished, whose stream[862] remains uncorrupted, and whose water satisfies the devoted mind. He should be one who is focused on the unerring traditional explanations of the practices of past gurus and on the correct rituals by way of a soundly referenced lineage of explicit teaching. He should be one who is able to introduce directly the bases for purification, the phenomena to be purified or removed, the purification processes, and the fruits of purification. Such a person is necessary for nourishing the disciple by bestowing the ripening empowerment and the liberating explanatory teachings and providing the support of transmission, in dependence on which you practice the generation and completion stages and so on.

d.div: [439] ma dper se ka zhes byung yang sarga zhes bcos/

[862] Seka; corrected by the editor of the new Tibetan redaction to sarga, which according to the Great Tibetan-Chinese Dictionary means “outline” or “chapter” but according to Monier-Williams also means stream or emission. This is preferred because the four oral transmissions use the metaphor of a river and its water.

f.d:
dbang gi ngo bo ni/ thob bya'i 'bras bu khyad par can mngon du bskyed nus la/ nges tshig ni/ kye rdo rje'i rtsa rgyud las/
gtor dang blugs pa zhes bya 'dis/ / des na dbang zhes brjod par bya/[440] / zhes gsungs te dbang de yang shIkr-i 'khrud pa'am yang na blugs pa'i byings la shis byed loTa'i brta mA na pa ra sme pA da'i skyes bu dbus ma'i mang tshig ta byin r-i rjes 'brel apa bi ka ra Na byin pa yon tan gyi shekata zhes par yi ge rnam par 'gyur dang nyams dag gis zhes dang / lhag ma 'jig rten las grub pa sogs kyi she ser song bar nye bsgyur a b+hi bzhag /ku i la Sha ru byed de sa Shas sa Shar bsgyur ba'i a b+hi Sha ka ta zhes sam/

The nature of an empowerment is that which has the power to actually create the special result of your future achievement. On the etymology of the term the Hevajra Root Tantra states:
Meaning “to sprinkle” and “to pour,” it is therefore an “empowerment” (abhiṣekha).[863] The root “śīkṛ means to wash or pour.” To this root is added the particle ta, which is the middle-person plural of the parasmaipād vartamāna tense in the imperative (loṭ) mood in a benedictive sense. The ṛ is an anubandha indicatory letter and is omitted. The vikaraṇa in-between ap affix is added, causing i to become e by the guṇa process, and the resulting formulation is śekta. Because “letters change and weaken” and “the remainder can be known by worldly usage,” the śe becomes se and the prefix abhi is added. “From ku, i, la, sa becomes ṣa” (when gender endings of the consonants in the ka group, the eight vowels beginning with i, and the five consonants ha, ya, wa, ra, and la take a following sa, it becomes ṣa), and also “for sa, ṣa” means that the sa becomes ṣa. This results in abhiṣekta.

d.div: [440] sde dge_417_bka'/ rgyud/ nga kye rdo rje'i zhes bya ba rgyud kyi rgyal po/ le'u/ 3_shog_17_na3
[863] Hevajratantra, chap. 3, Toh 417 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 17a3.

f.d: yang na sitsa mthor ba'i byings la brta mA na pa ra sme pA da'i skyes bu dang po'i gcig tshig tipa byin byed pa po la apa 'o kyi apa bi ka ra Na byin pa rjes 'brel gyis phyis/ tsa a la drangs mu ts+ra la la sogs pa mu ma 'os mum byin/ byings las ma'i na 'os ma na satu'i sha tsu rnams la sha tsu 'os na nyar bsgyur drangs pas siny+tsa a b+hi sngon du bzhag / si gong ltar Shir bsgyur bas a b+hiShi ny+tsa zhes

Alternatively, the root “sic means to sprinkle.” To this is added tip, the first-person singular of the parasmaipād vartamāna present. The vikaraṇa ap affix is added because “For the agent, ap” (for expressing the agent from roots such as bhū, the in-between affix ap is added when followed by any of the eighteen affixes from tip to mahe). The p is elided as an anubandha. The c is brought to the vowel a. “From muc, etc., mum” (when roots such as muc meet vikaraṇa affixes such as ap, the āgama mum is added). Therefore, mum is added. “Sa and tu to śa and cu” (final consonants sa and those of the ta group brought to initial śa and those of the ca group become śa and those of the ca group). Therefore na becomes ña. The prefix abhi is added. As done previously the si becomes ṣi to form abhiṣiñca. (In the process, tip must also be elided, and the remainder of mum, being an agama, must also be elided.)

sngon ma gtor zhing blugs pa ste sa bon la chu lud kyis btab pa ltar lus gnas kyang spyi bo lce'am/ mgrin pa snying ga lte ba gsang gnas te dbang gi gnas rnams su rim pa bzhin gtor zhing blugs pa la brten nas dbang bzhi rang skal gyi dri ma 'khrud cing sku bzhi'i myu gu 'byung ba'i khyad par gyi skal ba 'jog nus pas dbang zhes sam/

Therefore, in keeping with “sprinkling” and “pouring,” as expressed in the first line of the verse above, just as water and fertilizer is added to a seed, the bodily sites of the empowerment—the crown, the tongue or throat, the heart, the navel, and the secret area—are progressively sprinkled and poured upon. Because of this the four empowerments will individually have the power to wash away the corresponding taints of these sites and develop the corresponding sprouts of the four bodies; hence the term “empowerment.”

phyi ma dbang bzhi bskur ba'i lam bzhi sgom pa dang 'bras bu sku bzhi thob pa la dbang bar byas pa'i dbang zhes sam/ yang na sna sgras 'khrud par byed pa ste dbang bzhi bskur bas sga gsu+om rlung sems dang bcas pa ngo bo nyid kyi sku bzhir gnas pa la gnas par ma shes pa'i dri ma 'khrud par byed pas na dbang ste/ 'jig med 'byung gnas sbas pas mdzad pa'i man snye chung ba las/
lus ngag yid las byung ba yi/ / dri ma dag phyir dbang du brjod/[441] / ces sogs gsungs pa'i dbang sbyangs gzhi ni/ thob bya rang gnas kyi gnyug ma'i rdo rje bzhi/ sbyang bya ni de nyid sgrib byed glo bur dri ma phra rags rnams/ sbyong byed ni slob bu'i blo'i theg tshad dang sbyar ba'i dbang bskur bas de dang rjes su mthun pa'i lam sgom rung dang 'bras bu thob rung du smin par byed pa yin/ sbyangs 'bras ni sku bzhi'i sa bon nam nus pa khyad par can gsos thebs pa sogs don sbyangs gzhi rdo rje bzhi/ sbyangs 'bras sku bzhi la thob pa'i dbang de bskur bas snod rung gi slob ma la 'bras bu sku bzhi'i sa bon thebs pas gsang sngags kyi rang bzhin du gnas pa'i rigs rgyas 'gyur gyi nus pa mthu can du grub pa'i tshul yang /

In keeping with the second line, receiving the four empowerments gives you power over the meditations on the four paths and power to attain the resultant four bodies, therefore it is called an “empowerment.” Alternatively, the particle ñca means “to wash,” and receiving the four empowerments will wash away the taints of not being aware that body, speech, and mind, together with mind and wind combined, dwell in the nature of the four bodies. Therefore it is an empowerment. Abhyākaragupta in his Lesser Stalks of Oral Instruction says:
Because it cleans away the defilements of body, speech, and mind, it is an empowerment.[864] The bases to be purified by the empowerment are the four primordial and naturally abiding vajras,[865] which form the goal of your practice. The phenomena to be purified or removed are the coarse and subtle temporal defilements that obscure these vajras. The purifying of these phenomena is by way of conferring an empowerment suitable to that disciple’s capacity, thereby ripening the disciple to meditate on the corresponding path and gain the result. The effect of purification is the nourishing of the special seeds or potentials of the four bodies. This means that by conferring empowerment, which will bring about the transformation of the bases-of-purification four vajras into the fruit-of-purification four bodies, the suitable-vessel disciple has been planted with the seeds of the four bodies, which is secret mantra’s way of activating the potential that is the naturally abiding lineage.[866]

d.div: [441] slob dpon 'jigs med 'byung gnas sbas pas mdzad pa'i man ngag snye ma chung ba zhes pa'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/

[864] Text untraced. Because early Tibetan translators decided to translate abhiṣeka, meaning to “wash” or “cleanse,” with the Tibetan word dbang, meaning “power,” then the etymological explanation of this verse does not quite follow. “Empowerment” is a direct translation of the Tibetan, but etymologically “initiation” might be better.

[865] Thob bya rang gnas kyi gnyug ma’i rdo rje bzhi. These are the vajras of body, speech, mind, and exalted wisdom. Their gradual purification results in the emergence of the four bodies of a buddha.
[866] Rang bzhin du gnas pa’i rigs; sometimes translated as “buddha nature.”

f.d:
phyag rgya chen po thig le rnal 'byor ma'i rgyud las/
dang po re zhig gang tshe slob/ / lan cig dbang rnams kyis ni bskur/ / de tshe gsang chen bshad pa yi/ / nges par snod du 'gyur pa'o/ / dbang med na ni dngos grub med/ / bye ma btsir la mar mad bzhi+en/ / gang zhig rgyud lung nga rgyal gyis/ / dbang bskur med par 'chad byed pa/ / slob dpon slob ma shi ma thag / dngos grub thob kyang dmyal bar 'gro/ / de bas 'bad pa thams cad kyis/ / bla ma las ni dbang don zhu/[442] / zhes dang /

The Mahāmudrā Drop Yoginī Tantra states:
When at the beginning the disciples are once conferred with empowerments, they become without doubt a suitable vessel for the explanation of the great secrets. No empowerment means no siddhi, as squeezing sand will produce no oil. Those who arrogantly give teachings on the tantras without the conferral of empowerment, master and disciples, even if they have gained siddhi will land in hell as soon as they die. Therefore, with all your effort, seek empowerment from a guru.[867]

d.div: [442] sde dge_420_bka'/ rgyud/ nga dpal phyag rgya chen po'i thig le zhes bya ba rnal 'byor ma chen mo'i rgyud kyi rgyal po'i mnga' bdag /le'u/ 2_shog_66_ba4
[867] Mahāmudrātilakayoginītantra, chap. 2, Toh 420 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 66b4.

f.d:
dpal rdo rje 'phreng ba rnal 'byor gyi rgyud las/
dbang skur ba ni gtso bo ste/ / dngos grub thams cad rtag tu gnas/ / nga yis ji bzhin don bshad kyis/ / de phyir thog mar yang dag nyon/ /
thog mar slob dpon gang gi tshe/ / blo ldan yang dag dbang bskur na/ / rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor la/ / de yi tshe na snod du 'gyur/ /
yang dag dbang bskur gyis dben na/ / sgrub pos rgyud kyi don shes kyang / / slob dpon slob ma mtshungs par ni/ / mi bzad dmyal ba chen por 'gro[443] / zhes te/

The Vajra Garland Tantra says:
Empowerment is prime, all siddhis will forever be present. I will explain accordingly; therefore, first of all, listen well.
Once the master confers perfect empowerment, the wise and intelligent disciple becomes a suitable vessel for the yogas of the completion stage.
When perfect empowerment is absent, even though the practitioner knows tantra, disciple and master alike will fall to unending hell.[868]

d.div: [443] sde dge_445_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud dpal rdo rje phreng ba mngon par brjod pa rgyud thams cad kyi snying po gsang ba rnam par phye ba/ le'u/ 2_shog_212_na2
[868] Vajramālābhidhāna, chap. 2, Toh 445 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, 212a2.

f.d:
dbang rnam dag ma thob par sgrub pa la zhugs pas ni/ rgyud don shes nas bsgrubs pas dngos grub phra mo thob kyang dpon slob mtshungs par dmyal bar 'gro zhes pa'o// dbang skur ba yang / dkyil 'khor du 'jug pa dang / dkyil 'khor mthong ba la rag las te/ sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam par sbyor ba'i rgyud las/
dkyil 'khor du ni ma zhugs dang / / dam tshig rnams ni spangs ba dang / / gsang ba'i de nyid mi shes pas/ / bsgrubs kyang ci yang mi 'grub bo/[444] / zhes dang /

If you enter the practices without receiving a proper empowerment, even though you know the tantra and through practice gain siddhi, the disciple will go to hell, as will the master. Receiving empowerment depends on entering the mandala and seeing the mandala. In the Yoga Equal to All Buddhas Later Tantra:
Not having entered the mandala, disregarding all pledges, ignorant of the reality of the secret mantra: one may practice but to no avail.[869]

d.div: [444] sde dge_366_bka'/ rgyud/ ka dpal sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam par sbyor ba mkha' 'gro ma sgyu ma bde ba'i mchog ces bya ba'i rgyud phyi ma/ le'u/ 37_shog_164_ba2
[869] Sarvabuddhasamāyogatantra, chap. 37, Toh 366 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 164b2.

f.d:
dpal sdom pa nyung ngu'i rgyud las/
sngags pas dkyil 'khor ma mthong bar/ / gang zhig rnal 'byor pa nyid 'dod/ / mkha' la khu tshur gyis brdeg dang / / smig rgyu'i chu ni 'thung dang mtshungs/[445] / zhes so/ /

The Little Saṃvara Tantra says:
The practitioner of mantra who has not seen the mandala and yet wishes to become a yogi is like one striking the air with his fist, like one drinking the water of a mirage.[870]

d.div: [445] sde dge_368_bka'/ rgyud/ ka rgyud kyi rgyal po dpal bde mchog nyung ngu / le'u/ 3_shog_216_na2
[870] Laghusaṃvaratantra, chap. 3, Toh 368, Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 216a2.

f.d:
des na thun mong ba'i dbang bdun la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor dang / mchog gi dbang gong ma dag la/
lus dang gsang ba'i dbang po sems/ / rtag tu dkyil 'khor rnam pa gsum/[446] / zhes bya ba las/ ci ltar rigs par mthong ba'i sgo nas dbang bskur bar byas zin nas/ 'jam mgon chos kyi rgyal po btsong kha pas/
rgyal ba'i gsung gi mchog gyur rdo rje'i theg / blo chen ldan la rmad byung dga' bskyed pa/ / der zhugs rnams kyi dngos grub 'grub pa'i gzhi/ / dpal ldan rdo rje sems dpa'i sdom pa ni/[447] / zhes gsungs pa bzhin sngags sdom mam dam tshig bshad par bya ba la/

For the seven common empowerments there are the powder mandalas, and for the higher exalted mandalas:
Body, secret organs, and the mind: these are always the three types of mandala.[871] By seeing the appropriate mandala one has received empowerment. Then, as the great Dharma king Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa says:
Vajrayana, supreme among the Conqueror’s teachings, brings joy to those of great intelligence. For those who enter it, the foundation of siddhi is the vows of the glorious Vajrasattva.[872] Therefore, this leads to an explanation of the tantric vows or pledges:[873]

d.div: [446] dpal sdom pa nyung ngu'i rgyud/ lus dang gsang ba'i dbang po sems/ /rtag tu dkyil 'khor rnam pa gsum//
[447] rje tsong kha pa chen po'i gsung 'bum/ ka gsang sngags kyi tshul khrims kyi rnam bshad dngos grub kyi snye ma/ shog_69_na5
[871] Untraced.
[872] Blossom Cluster of Siddhis: Teachings on Tantric Ethics, Collected Works, ka, 69a5.

[873] Vows (sdom pa, saṃvara) and pledges (dam tshig, samaya). Although Tsongkhapa in his Blossom Cluster of Siddhis cites a passage defining differences between the two, they are used interchangeably in the discussion here.

f.d: thog mar dam tshig dang sdom pa ji ltar khas blang ba'i tshul dang / khas blangs pa'i sdom pa dang 'gal ba'i ltung ba gtan la 'bebs pa'o/ /
1. The way to take the vows and pledges 2. Determining the downfalls that break the vows you have taken

d.i: The way to take the vows and pledges

f.d: dang po la gang khas blang rgyu'i sdom pa rnams slob mas shes pa'i phyir du go bar smras te len pa'i tshe tham thom ma yin par dmigs phyed par byas nas 'dzin dgos pas rdo rje rtse mo las bshad pa bzhin sdom pa bsgrag pa/ sdom bzung bshad pa/ sdom pa bzung ma bzung la dbang ji ltar bskur ba'i tshul dang gsum/

This is under three headlines: 1. In order that the disciples know the vows to be taken, they are recited for a clear understanding. This is because at the time they are taken they must be held with a clear and unconfused concentration. Therefore, the vows are declared as taught in the Vajraśekhara Tantra. 2. Taking the vows 3. Conferring or not conferring empowerment on those taking or not taking vows
sdom pa bsgrag pa
['di ]la rigs lnga so so'i dang / spyi'i dam tshig gnyis las/
1. The individual vows of the five families 2. Pledges in common with all five families
dang po[ rigs lnga so so'i dam tshig]/

d.i: The individual vows of the five families

f.d: sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun te/ / dkon cog gsum la skyabs su song / / 'di ni sangs rgyas rigs dag pa'i/ / dam tshig brtan par gyur ba'o/[448] / zhes dkon cog gsum la skyabs su 'gro bar bskul ba 'di 'dra ba ni rnam snang gi rigs kyi dam tshig yin la/ sangs rgyas rigs dag bzhes pa'ang mang du 'byung mod kyang / 'jam mgon btsong kha pa chen po dga' ba zhes par bzhed cing / brtan pa ni mi mthun phyogs kyi phyed par dka' pa'i don yin no/ /

Go for refuge to the Three Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha; this is the firm pledge of the pure buddha family.[874] Such an entreaty to go for refuge to the Three Jewels is the pledge of the Vairocana family. The lines, “this is the firm pledge of the pure buddha family” is as it appears in many texts. However, Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa has “joyful buddha family.”[875] “Firm” means that the pledges cannot easily be broken by destructive forces.

d.div: [448] sde dge_480_bka'/ rgyud/ nya gsang ba rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud rde rjo rtse mo/ shog_183_na7
[874] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 183a7.
[875] This refers to the verse as cited by Tsongkhapa in his Blossom Cluster of Siddhis. The words dag pa meaning “pure” and dga’ ba meaning “joyful” are close in spelling.

f.d: rdo rje dril bu phyag rgya yang / / blo chen gyis ni bzung bar gyis/ / byang chub sems gang de rdo rje/ / shes rab dril bu zhes bshad do/ / slob dpon dag kyang bzung bar bya/ / bla ma sangs rgyas kun dang mnyam/ / 'di ni rdo rje'i rigs dag pa'i/ / sdom pa dam tshig yin par gsungs/[449] / zhes rdo rje dang dril bu dang phyag rgya dag blo gros chen po can khyod kyis bzung bar gyis shig /de yang ji ltar snyam na byang chub sems gang de rdo rje zhes sogs dang / der ma zad slob dpon dag kyang gus pas bzung ba ste rdo rje mi bskyod pa'i dam tshig /

You of great intelligence: hold the vajra, bell, and mudrā. Bodhicitta is taught to be the vajra, wisdom is taught to be the bell. Hold also the vajra master, for the guru is equal to all buddhas. These are taught as the pledges of the pure vajra family.[876] This is urging that “you of great intelligence should hold the vajra, bell, and mudrā.” How this is to be done is explained by the lines, “Bodhicitta is taught to be the vajra” and so on. Moreover, the vajra master also should be held with reverence. These are the pledges of Akṣobhya.

d.div: [449] sde dge_480_bka'/ rgyud/ nya gsang ba rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud rdo rje rtse mo/ shog_183_ba1
[876] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 183b1.

f.d: rin chen rigs mchog chen po la/ / nyin dang mtshan mo lan gsum du/ / zang zing mi 'jigs chos dang byams/ / sbyin pa rnam bzhi rtag tu sbyin/[450] / zhes rin chen ni rin 'byung gi rigs yin la der nyin lan gsum dang mtshan lan gsum ste dus drug tu zang zing dang / mi 'jigs pa dang / chos dang byams pa bcas sbyin pa rnam bzhi rtag tu byin rin chen 'byung gnas kyi dam tshig

For the supreme jewel family, three times in the day and at night, practice constantly four kinds of giving: wealth, fearlessness, Dharma, and love.[877] “Jewel” refers to the family of Ratnasambhava. The verse is saying that three times in the day and three times in the night you should practice without fail the four kinds of giving: those of material wealth, gifts of fearlessness, Dharma, and love. These are the pledges of Ratnasambhava.

d.div: [450] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba2

f.d: phyi nang gsang ba theg pa gsum/ / dam chos khyod kyis bzung bar bya/ / 'di ni pad+ma'i rigs dag pa'i/ / dam tshig sdom pa yin par gsungs/[451] / zhes theg pa gsum la sogs pa'i dam chos thams cad mi spong bar 'dzin pa ni 'od dpag med kyi dam tshig /

You should hold the sacred Dharma of the outer, inner, and secret vehicles.[878] These are the pledges and vows of the pure lotus family.[879] Holding the whole Dharma without discarding any of the three vehicles and so on is the pledge of Amitābha.

d.div: [451] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba2

[878] Phyi nang gsang ba theg pa gsum. In this Vajraśekha line as cited by Tsongkhapa, the nang (inner) becomes dang (a conjunctive particle) and so reads phyi dang gsang ba theg pa gsum: “The outer and secret vehicles.” Tsongkhapa’s comments on this line are based on this reading.
[879] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 183b2.

f.d: las kyi rigs mchog chen po la/ / sdom pa thams cad ldan par ni/ / yang dag nyid du bzung bar gyis/ / mchod pa'i las kyang ci nus bya/[452] / zhes sdom pa thams cad yang dag par bzung ba dang mchod pa'i las kyang ci nus su bya ba don yod grub pa ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa/ rdo rje/ rin chen/ pad+ma/ las kyi rigs dang lnga'i lha spyi bye brag gi dam tshig dang /

For the supreme-activity family, hold well all vows taken and perform offerings as best you can.[880] Keeping all the vows you have taken and making offerings as best you can are the pledges of Amoghasiddhi. These have been the specific pledges of the deities belonging to the tathāgata, vajra, jewel, lotus, and activity families.

d.div: [452] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba3

f.d: de dag spyi bsdoms
Pledges held in common by all five families:
['di ]la/ rtsa ba dang / yan lag don bsdus gsum las/
1. Root pledges 2. Secondary pledges 3. Conclusion
dang po ni[ rtsa'i bdam tshig]/

de las gzhan pa bcu bzhi ni/ / phas pham par ni rab tu bshad/ / spang zhing dor bar mi bya ste/ / rtsa ba'i ltung ba zhes bshad do/ / nyin dang mtshan mo lan gsum du/ / nyin re bzhin ni bzla bar bya/ / gang tshe nyams gyur rnal 'byor pa/ / kha na ma tho sbom por 'gyur/[453] / zhes pa ltar rigs lnga so so'i dam tshig las gzhan pa thun mong gi dam tshig rnams kyang yid kyis spang zhing lus ngag gis dor bar mi bya la/ de dag gang zhe na/ thog mar rtsa ba'i dam tshig ston pa ni/ phas pham par rgyud sde rnams las bshad pa'i bcu bzhi rnams kyi bcas pa ste de rnams la ming gnyis pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba zhes grags shing / des sdom pa gcod pas gnyen po'i phyogs pham par byed la de yang pha rol mi mthun phyogs nas tshur la pham par byas pas pham mo/ / bcu bzhi zhes pa la kha cig /dang po la dkon cog gsum/ gnyis par rdor dril slob dpon gsum/ gsum par sbyin pa bzhi par chos gsum/ tha ma la mchod pa gcig pu ste bcu bzhi dang / la la srog chags bsad mi bya nas chang spong ba'i bar las ldog pa la lnga sogs bshad kyang / 'jam mgon btsong kha pa chen po 'og nas 'chad par 'gyur ba'i rtsa ltung bcu bzhi bar bzhed pa ltar ro//

Fourteen, other than these, are explained as other-inflicted defeats. Don’t abandon and discard them; they are explained as root downfalls. Three times in the day and at night, day after day, recite them. When they degenerate, the yogi has committed a gross fault.[881] There are common pledges other than the individual pledges of the families, and these too are not to be abandoned in the mind or discarded by verbal and physical acts. What are these pledges? First the root pledges are taught. These are proscriptive rules for the fourteen acts described in the tantras as other-inflicted defeats, whose alternative name is root downfalls. These actions break the vows and inflict defeat upon their disciplining powers. They are called other-inflicted defeats (phas pham pa, pārājika) because a destructive power from “over there” comes to inflict defeat “over here.” Concerning the identity of these fourteen, some say they refer to transgressing the pledges concerning the Three Jewels in the first buddha family; the vajra, bell, and vajra master in the second; the four types of giving in the third; the three Dharma pledges of the fourth; and just the offering pledge of the fifth family. These total fourteen. Others say they refer to the fourteen acts beginning with five contraventions, from non-killing of living creatures to abstaining from alcohol.[882] However, they should be understood as the fourteen root downfalls taught by the great Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa and which will be listed below.

d.div: [453] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba3

[881] Ibid., 183b3. “Gross” (sbom po, stüla) is a term normally used for the eight secondary downfalls. It means “thick,” “heavy,” “bulky,” and so on. “Fault” here is kha na ma tho ba (avadya) and is usually of two kinds: natural and proscribed.
[882] All fourteen are listed by Tsongkhapa in his Blossom Cluster of Siddhis.

f.d: yan lag gi dam tshig
['di ]la/ spong ba dang / bsten pa dang / gzhan bsten pa gsum las/
1. Pledges of abandonment 2. Pledges of reliance 3. Other pledges of reliance
dang po[ spong ba]/
Pledges of abandonment

khyod kyi srog chags bsad mi bya/ / ma byin par yang mi blang ngo / / 'dod pa log par mi spyad cig / brdzun du smra bar mi bya'o/ / phung khrol kun gyi rtsa ba yin/ / chang ni rnam par spang par bya/ / sems can 'dul phyir ma gtogs par/ / bya ba ma yin thams cad spang /[454] / zhes pa srog gcod pa nas brdzun gyi bar spong ba bzhi'i steng du chang 'thung ba spong ba'i bslab gzhi lnga ni dngos grub 'grub pa'i gzhi dang / gzhan yang sgo gsum gyi bya ba ma yin pa thams cad spang dgos la/ 'on kyang sngags sdom tshul bzhin bsrung ba'i rgyal sras 'ga' zhig la sems can gdul ba'i phyir du srog gcod pa sogs lus ngag gi bdun la gnang ba'i skabs yod pas de 'dra ba'i tshe ni ma gtogs so/ /

Do not kill living creatures, do not take what is not given, do not engage in perverse desire, do not tell lies, and do not take alcohol, the root of all ruin. Leave behind all improper activity not included in the taming of others.[883] The four acts of abandonment from not killing to not telling lies plus the abandoning of alcohol are the five practice foundations that act as foundations for the attainment of siddhi. Also, you should leave behind all improper activity of body, speech, and mind. However, for some sons of the Conqueror who properly guard their tantric vows, there are occasions when the seven physical and verbal activities, such as killing, are permitted when performed for the sake of taming others, and at those times such actions are not included in the above.

d.div: [454] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba4
[883] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 183b4.

f.d: bsten pa ni/
Pledges of reliance

dam pa nye bar bsten bya zhing / / rnal 'byor pa rnams bsnyen bkur bya/ / lus kyi las ni rnam gsum dang / / ngag gi rnam pa bzhi rnams dang / / yid kyi rnam pa gsum dang ni/ / ci nus bar ni rjes su skyongs/[455] / zhes dam pa'i bshes gnyen la bsten nas sngags kyi rig pa sgrub cing / rnal 'byor pa rnams la mi brnyas par bsnyen bkur ba/ dkar po'i las lam bcu po ci nus su bsten pa rnams dang /

Devote yourself to the holy beings, give respect and service to the yogis. The three activities of the body, the four of speech, and the three of mind— develop them as much as you can.[884] Devote yourself to the spiritual friend from which comes the development of mantra wisdom. Show respect to the yogis by not belittling them, and dedicate yourself to the ten white activities as much as possible.

d.div: [455] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba5

f.d: gsum pa dam tshig gzhan bstan pa la/
Other pledges of reliance

theg pa dman la 'dod mi bya/ / sems can don la rgyab phyogs min/ / 'khor ba dag kyang spang mi bya/ / rtag tu mya ngan 'das mi chags/[456] / zhes theg pa dman pa ni ched du bya ba gzhan don dang 'bras bu byang chub dman pa nyan rang gi lam yin pas des rang bgrod par 'dod par mi bya zhing / sems can grangs med pa'i don la sgyid lug pa sogs rgyab kyis mi phyogs pa/ 'khor ba ji srid bar sems can kyi don byed pa'i go cha gyon pa/ rtag tu srid pa'i 'ching ba las grol ba tsam gyi myang 'das la chags pa ste theg chen las ldog pa'i rgyu rnams spang ba dang /

Have no desire for the lesser vehicles, don’t turn your back on working for others, do not leave samsara behind, never develop a fondness for nirvana.[885] The lesser vehicles have a smaller intention of working for others and aim for a lesser enlightenment. These are the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and you should have no desire to travel down them. Do not turn your back on others by being lazy in your task of working for countless living beings and so on. For as long as samsara exists, wear the armor of working for others. Abandon desire for the nirvana that is the mere freedom from the bondage of existence. Abandon these causes of turning away from the Mahayana.

d.div: [456] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba6

f.d: lha dang lha min gsang ba pa/ / khyod kyis brnyas par mi bya zhing / / phyag rgya bzhon pa mtshon cha dang / / mtshan ma 'gom par mi bya'o/[457] / zhes 'jig rten las 'das ma 'das kyi lha dang lha ma yin rnams dang gsang ba pa gnod sbyin/ phyag rgya ni lha'i gzugs bris pa/ bzhon pa ni lha'i bzhon pa'i gzugs su byas pa dang bla ma'i bzhon pa/ mtshon cha ni lha'i phyag mtshan ral gri dang mdung sogs/ mtshan ma ni phyag mtshan 'khor lo dang rdo rje sogs la brnyas pa dang 'gom pa'i nyes pa rnams spong ba'o//

Do not despise gods, demigods, and guhyaka; do not walk upon mudrā, mounts, weapons, and implements.[886] “Gods” are both mundane and supramundane. The guhyaka are a type of yakṣa spirit. “Mudrā” refers to drawings of deities. “Mounts” are the representative forms of deity mounts and the modes of transport of the guru. “Weapons” are deity weapons such as swords and spears. “Implements” are deity implements such as wheels and vajras. Toward all of them, do not commit the faults of despising them or walking on them.

d.div: [457] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba7

f.d:
rigs lnga spyi'i dam tshig gi don bsdus pa ni/
'di dag dam tshig yin par bshad/ / khyod kyis rtag tu bsrung bar bya/[458] / zhes gsungs pa 'di ni sngar bshad pa'i thun mong gi dam tshig bsgrag pa man chad thams cad la sbyar bar bya ba yin la/

The conclusion of the common pledges of the five families:
These have been explained as pledges; guard them always.[887] This applies to all the pledges previously announced.

d.div: [458] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba7

f.d:
de nas/
rjes mthun sdom pa rgya cher ni/ / gsang ba'i rgyud las rab tu bshad/[459] / ces pa ni sngar bshad pa de dag dang 'dra ba'i sdom pa ste bslab pa'i gnas rgya cher ni rgyud kun las rab tu bshad do zhes dngos su smos pa de tsam du zad dam snyam pa spang ba'i phyir du'o//

The text continues:
Extensive teachings on related vows are to be found in the secret tantras.[888] Extensive teachings on vows or commitments of practice related to those already explained can be found in all the tantras. This has been said in order to dismiss any thought that the above explanations were exhaustive.

d.div: [459] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_ba7

f.d: sdom pa bzung ba
['di ]la gsol ba btab pa dang / sdom bzung gnyis las/
1. The request 2. Taking hold of the vows
dang po ni/

rdo rje rtse mo las/
gtso bo bdag la sdom pa stsol/ / thub pa nyi ma ma lus pa'i/ / sangs rgyas bdag la dgongs su gsol/[460] / zhes sogs kyis gsol ba 'debs pa'i slob ma la/ bla mas/
gsang ba chen po'i rigs dag pa'i/ / gsang ba yongs su 'dzin par ni/ / bdag nyid chen po khyod 'dod dam/[461] / zhes sdom pa len 'dod yod med legs par dris te snying thag pa nas len 'dod med na sdom pa mi skye bas spang zhing / don gnyer 'dug na/ 'dir ni slob dpon bdag la gson/ / zhes slob dpon la gsol nas sdom pa 'dzin pa yin la/

In the Vajraśekhara Tantra:
Master, grant me the vows. Sun of the Sage, every buddha, please hear this request.[889] To this request by the disciple the guru says:
Great being, do you wish to hold fully the secrets of the pure mahāguhya family?[890] The guru asks if the disciple wants to take the vows. If he does not want them from his heart, they will not grow and are therefore forfeited. If the disciple is truly seeking the vows, he requests the vajra master, “Master, please listen to me,”[891] and proceeds to takes the vows.

d.div: [460] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_na2
[461] gong mtshungs/ shog_183_na6

f.d: gnyis pa ni/
rtse mor/ gtso bos ji ltar bka' stsal pa/ / de bzhin du ni bgyid par 'tshal/[462] / zhes khas len pa 'di la/ sems bskyed pa/ sdom pa bzung ba dngos/ don bsdus te khas len pa dang gsum las/

The Vajraśekhara states, “Master, as you have repeated, so I will do.” This promise is dealt with under three headings: 1. Generating bodhicitta 2. Actually taking hold of the vows 3. Concluding promises

d.div: [462] gong mtshungs/ shog_184_na1

f.d: dang po ni/
Generating bodhicitta

ji ltar dus gsum mgon po rnams/ / byang chub tu ni nges mdzad pa'i/ / byang chub sems ni bla na med/ / dam pa bdag gis bskyed par bgyi/[463] / zhes bdag rdo rje sems par gyur nas sems can thams cad kyang de'i go 'phang la dgod par bya snyam pa'i smon sems dang / de'i lam sbyin sogs nyams su len pa'i rang bzhin 'jug pa ste smon 'jug de gnyis ni bla na med pa'i 'bras bu sgrub par byed pas bla na med pa dang dam pa'o//

Just as the guardian buddhas of the past, present, and future have single-pointedly developed their minds for enlightenment, I too generate this peerless and supreme mind.[892] This is the aspiring bodhicitta, thinking, “When I become Vajrasattva I will lead all beings also to this enlightened state,” as well as the engaged bodhicitta whose nature is the practices—giving and so forth—of this bodhicitta path. These two will produce the peerless result, and they are therefore “peerless and supreme.”

d.div: [463] gong mtshungs/ shog_184_na1

f.d: sdom pa bzung ba dngos ni/
Actually taking hold of the vows

sangs rgyas rnal 'byor sdom pa la/ / tshul khrims kyi ni bslab pa dang / / dge ba'i chos ni sdud pa dang / / sems can don byed tshul khrims gsum/ / bdag gis brtan por bzung par bgyi/ /
sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun de/ / bla na med pa'i dkon cog gsum/ / deng nas brtsams te bzung bar bgyi/ / zhes rnam snang dang /

The practice of ethics, the ethics of gathering virtue, and the ethics of working for living beings: this vow of the buddha family yoga I will hold firmly.
The Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the peerless Three Jewels: from now on I will firmly hold. This is the Vairocana vow.
rdo rje rigs mchog chen po la/ / rde rjo dril bu'i phyag rgya yang / / yang dag nyid du bzung bar bgyi/ / slob dpon dag kyang bzung bar bgyi/ / zhes mi bskyod pa/
For the supreme vajra family, the vajra, bell, and mudrā I will firmly hold. The master too I will hold. This is the Akṣobhya vow.
rin chen rigs mchog chen po yi/ / dam tshig yid du 'ong ba la/ / nyin re bzhin ni dus drug tu/ / sbyin pa rnam bzhi rab tu byin/ / zhes rin 'byung /
For the beautiful pledge of the supreme jewel family, six times a day I will perform the four acts of giving. This is the Ratnasambhava vow.
byang chub chen po las byung ba/ / pad+ma'i rigs chen dag pa la/ / phyi nang gsang ba theg pa gsum/ / dam pa'i chos ni bzung bar bgyi/ / zhes 'od dpag med/
For the great lotus family arising from the great enlightenment, I will hold the highest Dharma of the outer, inner, and secret vehicles.[893] This is the Amitābha vow.

d.div: [893] See previous note on the pledges of Amitābha.

f.d: las kyi rigs mchog chen po la/ / sdom pa thams cad ldan pa ni/ / yang dag nyid du bzung bar bgyi/ / mchod pa'i las kyang ci nus bgyi/[464] / zhes don grub dang lnga'i sdom pa so sor 'dzin pa dang /
For the supreme activity family I will hold well all vows taken, and perform offerings as best I can.[894] This is the Amoghasiddhi vow. These verses are for the taking of the individual vows.

d.div: [464] gong mtshungs/ shog_184_na2_nas na4
[894] In this section the verses from the Vajraśekhara Tantra run from 184a2–4.

f.d: Concluding promises

byang chub sems ni bla na med/ / dam pa bdag gis bskyed bgyis nas/ / sems can kun gyi don gyi phyir/ / bdag gis sdom pa ma lus bzung / / ma grol ba ni dgrol bar bgyi/ / ma brgal ba ni bsgral bar bgyi/ / dbugs ma phyin pa dbugs dbyung zhing / / sems can mya ngan 'das la 'god/[465] / ces rkang pa dang po gnyis smon 'jug dang / de nas gnyis ni sdom pa lnga'i don bsdu yin la/ gti mug sogs sgrib pa gnyis kyi 'ching bas bcings pa tshangs pa sogs ma grol ba dang / nyan rang shes sgrib las ma brgal ba/ dmyal ba sogs dbugs ma byin pa dbyung zhing sems can kun mi gnas ba'i mya ngan las 'das pa la 'god pa'o/ /

Having generated the bodhi mind, peerless and supreme, for the sake of all living beings, I will keep well all vows. Those not free I will free, those not delivered I will deliver, and those in torment I will comfort; I will bring living beings to nirvana.[895] The first two lines illustrate the aspiring and engaged bodhicitta. The next two lines encapsulate the five sets of vows. “Those not free” refers to Brahmā and others who are bound by the chains of the two obscurations—ignorance and so on. “Those not delivered” are the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who are not delivered from the obscurations to omniscience. “Those in torment” refers to hell beings and the like. “I will bring living beings to nirvana” refers to bringing all living beings to the nonabiding nirvana.[896]

d.div: [465] gong mtshungs/ shog_184_na5
[895] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 184a5.

[896] In the Mahayana, nonabiding nirvana (mi gnas pa’i mya ngan las ’das pa, apratiṣṭanirvāṇa) is the enlightenment of a buddha, who is free of both the turmoil of samsara and the quietism of an arhat’s nirvana. It signifies that while Mahayana enlightened beings remain active in the world, they are not stained by it.

f.d: sdom pa bzung ma bzung la dbang bskur mi bskur gyi tshul la/

d.i: Conferring or not conferring empowerment on those taking or not taking vows

f.d:
rdo rje 'byung ba las/
gang zhig sdom pa 'dzin par mi byed pa de la ni deng khyod ces bya ba la sogs pa rnams brjod par mi bya ste slob dpon du rjes su gnang ba dang / dbang bskur bar mi bya'o/[466] / zhes pa ltar sdom pa mi 'dzin pa la dbang mi bskur ba'i tshul dang de la rtsod pa spangs te dbang bskur bas sdom pa 'dzin tshul/

[Ānangagarbha’s] Sarvavajrodaya Vajradhātu Mandala Ritual says:
To those not taking the vows, do not say, “Now, today you…” and so forth. As master, do not confer permissions or empowerments.[897] This is a section on empowerment not being conferred on those who are not taking the vows, and a second section on refuting objections on this point and taking the vows through empowerment.[898]

d.div: [466] sde dge_2516_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ku slob dpon kun dga' snying po/ rdo rje dbyings kyi dkyil 'khor chen po'i cho ga rdo rje thams cad byung ba/ shog_44_na3
[897] Vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalavidhisarvavajrodaya, Toh 2516 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ku, 44a3.
[898] This abrupt style of commentary is the author quickly running through Tsongkhapa’s Blossom Cluster of Siddhis, which is followed closely in this topic.

f.d:
dkyil chog rdor 'phreng las/
phreng ba dang chu la sogs pa dbang drug po 'di rnams kyi ma rig pa'i gnyen po nus pa nyid du sgrub par byed pas rig pa'i dbang zhes brjod de/ dbang 'di rnams bskur ba'i slob ma bya ba dang spyod pa'i rgyud dag nyan pa dang bshad pa dang sngags sgrub pa rnams la dbang bar 'gyur ro/[467] / zhes dang /

The Vajrā Garland of Mandala Rituals says:
The six empowerments of garland, water, and so on grant power to activate the antidote to ignorance and are therefore called wisdom empowerments. Disciples who are conferred with these empowerments are empowered to hear, teach, and perform the mantra practice of the action and performance tantras.[899]

d.div: [467] sde dge_3140_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ phu.a b+ha yA ka ra gub+ta/ dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga rdo rje phreng ba/ shog_76_ba2
[899] Abhayākaragupta, Vajrāvalīmaṇḍalasādhana, Toh 3140 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, phu, 76b2.

f.d: a b+h+ya' bzhe+id pas rgyud sde gong ma gnyis ma gtogs pa'i 'byung 'dul la sogs pa rdo rje 'phreng bar gsungs pa rnams kyi dbang bskur ba na rigs lnga'i sdom bzung dor nas thun mong ba tsam bzung pas chog ste slob ma'i dbang tsam gyi bya spyod kyi rgyud 'chad nyan dang sgrub pa la dbang ba'i phyir dang slob dpon gyi dbang mi bskur ba la rdo rje slob dpon kyi sdom pa mi ster bar [468]gsungs pa sogs bya spyod kyi dbang bskur ba la sdom pa gang 'dzin bstan pa dang gsum yod cing /

Abhayākara is saying that, apart from the two higher classes of tantra, when conferring empowerments such as the Bhūtadamaka and other mandalas taught in his Vajra Garland of Mandala Rituals, it is acceptable to set aside the vows of the five families and to just confer the common vows. This is because they are just disciple empowerments for listening to, teaching, and practicing action and performance tantra, and that if the master empowerment is not conferred, the vajra-master vows are not given. This is the third section under this heading, dealing with which vows are conferred in action and performance tantra.

d.div: [468] gong mtshungs/ shog_76_ba4

f.d: de yang dam tshig bsdus par/ thun mong gi rtsa ltung bzhi/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i rtsa ltung bcu gnyis/ kr-i ya'i rgyud kyi rtsa ltung sum cu/ spyod rgyud kyi rtsa ltung bcu bzhir bshad pa sogs mchis la/

Pledges can be compiled under the headings of the four common root downfalls, the twelve pāramitā root downfalls, the thirty root downfalls of action tantra, the fourteen root downfalls of performance tantra, and so on.
rtsa ba'i sa bcad gnyis pa khas blangs pa'i sdom pa dang 'gal ba'i ltung ba gtan la dbab pa

d.i: Determining the downfalls that break the vows you have taken

f.d: ['di ]la/ gang gi rgyud la ltung ba bskyed pa'i rten ngos bzung ba/ rten de la bcas pa'i ltung ba'i rab tu dbye ba/ phye nas so so'i don bshad pa dang gsum gyi
Here there are three headings: 1. Identifying the person in whose mindstream the downfalls occur 2. Types of prescribed downfalls in that person 3. Explanations of each type
dang po ni/

d.i: Identifying the person in whose mindstream the downfalls occur

f.d: gsang sngags kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i sdom pa thob nas ma btang ba bsam pa rang bzhin du gnas pa ste khyad par gnyis dang ldan dgos la/ sdom pa dang mi ldan na de la rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba'i nyes spyod bskyed kyang bcas pa dang 'gal ba'i ltung ba mi bskyed pa'i phyir dang / smyo ba sogs kyi dran pa rnal du mi gnas na ltung med du gsung /

This person must possess two features. He must have received exclusive secret mantra vows and not given them up, and he must be in a normal state of mind. If you have no vows, you might commit natural faults but you would not incur a prescribed downfall. Secondly, if you go insane, for example, and your memory becomes deranged, it is said you cannot incur a downfall.
gnyis pa dbye ba ni/

d.i: Types of prescribed downfalls in that person

f.d: rdo rje 'phreng ba las/ rdo rje sems dpa'i sdom pa dang ldan pa 'di'i ltung ba ni ris rnam pa gnyis te rtsa ba'i ltung ba dang sbom po'i ltung ba'o/[469] / zhes ris gnyis su nges pa dang /
These are of two types. The Vajrāvalī of Mandala Rituals states: The downfalls of one who possesses the Vajrasattva vows are of two kinds: root (mūlā) downfalls and gross (sthūlā) downfalls.[900]

d.div: [469] gong mtshungs/ shog_85_ba7

f.d: gsum pa so so'i don bshad pa las/
rtsa ltung gis ma gos par bya ba dang / nyams na phyir bcos pa'i thabs dang gnyis las/
1. How not to be tainted with a root downfall 2. Restoring degenerated vows
dang por

d.i: How not to be tainted with a root downfall

f.d: rtsa ltung ngos bzung ba dang / des ma gos par bsrung ba'i 'dod pa bskyed pa/ ji ltar bsrung tshul dang gsum gyi/
1. Identifying the downfalls 2. Generating desire to guard the vows and not be tainted by downfalls 3. How to guard them
dang por
rtsa ltung so sor bshad pa dang / bsdus te bstan pa gnyis kyi dang po/
