gang phyir rdo rje 'dzin pa yi/ / dngos grub slob dpon rjes 'brang gsungs/ / de bas de la brnyas pa ni/ / rtsa ba'i ltung ba dang por bshad/[470] / ces gang lus can thams cad spang rtogs mthar phyin gyi zung 'jug sku bzhi'i go 'phang thob par bya ba'i phyir rgyal ba khyab bdag rdo rje 'dzin pa de yis bka' stsal pa rgyud sde rin po che rnams su 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub rnam pa gnyis 'grub pa ni bla ma'am slob dpon tshul bzhin bsten pa'i rjes su 'gro ba'am 'brang bar gsungs pa de lta bas na/ rang nyid la dbang bzhi rdzogs par stsol ba nas tha na tshigs bcad gcig tsam ston pa'i bar gyi slob dpon de'i sku gsung thugs mdzad pa 'phrin las la mi rang mi gus par brnyas thams bgyis pa ni/ dpa' bo bdag gis sngags kyi nyes byas phra rags mang du yod pa las gtso che ba bcu bzhir dbye ba'i nang nas kyang rtsa ba lta bu'i nyes ltung lci ba'i dang por gzhung chen po rnams las bshad pa bzhin bsdus zhes pa'o/ /

For this reason Vajradhara has said that siddhis follow from the master; to disparage him is the first root downfall.[901] For this reason of bringing all sentient beings to the attainment of the four bodies, which is the perfection of abandonment and insight, the all-pervading master and conqueror Vajradhara has said that the accomplishments of the two types of siddhis—the mundane and supramundane—taught in the precious tantras come from or follow from the practices of proper devotion to the guru, or master. Therefore, to disparage him with contempt and to disrespect the body, speech, mind, and deeds of any masters, from those who have conferred on us all four empowerments down to those who taught us just one verse, is the first heavy downfall and is the root of even the fourteen primary downfalls that I, Śūra,[902] have compiled from the many coarse and subtle faults in mantra that are explained in the great texts.

d.div: [470] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_na7
[901] Aśvaghoṣa [Śūra], Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls (Vajrayānamūlāpattisaṃgraha), Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179a7.

[902] Śūra is Aśvaghoṣa. Here and throughout this topic the author closely follows his Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, which in turn is quoted in Tsongkhapa’s commentary. The voice here is therefore primarily that of Aśvaghoṣa.

f.d: bde gshegs bka' las 'das pa ni/ / ltung ba gnyis pa yin par bshad/[471] / ces pa ni rnam 'grel las/ rgyu spangs yon tan gsum bde gshegs/[472] / zhes pa'i don ltar srid pa'i sdug bsngal gyi rten mi byed pas legs par gshegs pa dang bdag lta'i sa bon zad pas slar mi ldog par gshegs pa dang spang bya mtha' dag zad pas ma lus par gshegs pas na lam bde ba 'jug pa bde ba la legs par gshegs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi bka' rgya mtsho lta bu las/ sdom pa gsum gang rung dang khyad par sngags sdom gyi bcas pa gsungs pa la khyad du gsod 'dod kyi kun slong tshang bas 'das par byed pa ni/ gong bzhin rtsa ba'i ltung ba bcu bzhir phye ba'i gnyis pa yin par bshad ces pa'o/ /

Transgressing the words of the Sugata is said to be the second downfall.[903] Treatise of Valid Cognition says, “By his achievement of a threefold elimination of causes he is the Sugata.”[904] In other words, because there is no creation of a basis for the sufferings of samsara, he has “gone beautifully.” Because all seeds of the view of self have gone, he has “gone without return.” Because all phenomena to be eliminated have disappeared, he has “gone entirely.” Therefore, he dwells in the path of happiness, a buddha who has gone (gata) beautifully to happiness (su). To transgress any of the three sets of vows he has taught within the mighty ocean of his words, especially the prescriptions of the tantric vows, accompanied by the deliberate intention to ignore them, is said to be the second of the fourteen root downfalls.

d.div: [471] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_na7
[472] sde dge_4210_bstan/ tshad ma/ ce_chos graDa/ tshad ma rnam 'grel/ tshad ma grub pa'i le'u/ sh+loka142_shog_112_ba6
[903] Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179a7.
[904] Dharmakīrti, Pramāṇavārttika, 2:142, Toh 4210 Tengyur, tshad ma, ce, 112b6.

f.d: rdo rje spun la khros pa ni/ / nyes pa brjod pa gsum pa yin/[473] / zhes slob dpon dang dkyil 'khor dang rig pa'am rig ma rnams gcig las dam tshig thob pa ni khyad par gyi rdo rje spun dang / de rnams so sor thob pa ni bye brag rdo rje spun dang / theg pa chen po la zhugs pa rnams nye ba'i spun te/ rdo ba zhes sra ba dang mkhregs pa kun gyi rjer gyur bas gang gi'ang gzhig pa dang phyed par mi nus pa'i mtshon don du byas pa'i theg pa 'di'i dkyil 'khor gcig tu dbang bzhi rdzogs pa'am tha na tshigs bcad gcig mnyam du zhus pa'i mched lcam mam spun du gyur pa rnams la snying thag pa nas mi dga' bar khros pa ni/ sngags sdom gyi nyes par brjod pa'i rnam grangs gsum pa'o zhes so/ /

Anger toward a vajra brother or sister is spoken of as the third fault.[905] Those who have taken pledges from the same vajra master, the same mandala, or the same male or female consorts are special vajra brothers and sisters. Those who take pledges from different masters and so on are individual vajra brothers and sisters. All those who have entered the Mahayana are close brothers and sisters. To become angry from the depths of your heart at another brother or sister who has received all four empowerments within the same mandala of this vehicle of the vajra (rdo rje)—whose etymology is that, being the lord (rje) of all stones (rdo), so hard and solid, it cannot be broken or split by anything—or even with someone with whom one has received a single verse of tantra teaching, is spoken of as the third fault.

d.div: [473] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_na7

[905] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179a7. In this version of these two lines, the word “anger” is not in the instrumental case, and in the second line Sangyé Gyatso does not take it to mean that the anger that causes us to verbalize the faults of our vajra brothers and sisters. In the commentary in Blossom Cluster, Tsongkhapa reads the second line as a verbalizing of faults that is brought on by anger, and his text has the first line in the instrumental, which when translated would read, “Becoming angry at a vajra brother or sister/ and speaking of his or her faults is the third.” Both interpretations of this vow are discussed by Jé Tsongkhapa. Degé reads “Becoming angry and speaking of the faults of vajra brothers and sisters.”

f.d: sems can rnams la byams pa spong / / bzhi pa yin par rgyal bas gsungs/[474] / zhes rigs drug po gcig tu mi gnas par/ yang nas yang du 'khor zhing 'gro bas 'gro ba'am rnam par shes pa'i rten byin pa'i lus dang ldan pas lus can bem po ma yin par bde sdug la sogs pa shes pa'i sems dang ldan pa can gyi 'gro ba rnams las/ gang yang rung ba gcig 'di bde ba thams cad dang bral na snyam pa'i byams pa ring du 'dor ba ste spong bar byed na/ rtsa ba'i ltung ba bzhi pa yin par bdud sde bye ba phrag du ma'i g.yul las rnam par rgyal ba des legs par gsungs zhes pa'o//

Abandoning love for sentient beings the Conqueror has declared the fourth.[906] The six types of beings do not remain as one particular type but repeatedly circle and migrate in samsara and are therefore called “migrators.” Alternatively, by possessing a body that acts as the basis for consciousness, they are “embodied beings” who possess the nonmaterial sentience or mind that knows pleasure and pain, and so on. To wish that even one of these sentient beings has no happiness at all, thereby abandoning love in the sense of casting it far from your mind, the Conqueror, meaning he who has won the battle over millions of Māra hordes, has declared to be the fourth root downfall.

d.div: [474] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba1

f.d:
chos kyi rtsa ba byang chub sems/ / de spong ba ni lnga pa yin/[475] / zhes pa phal po che'i bam po brgya bcu gnyis par/
rigs kyi bu byang chub kyi sems ni sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad kyi sa bon lta bu'o/[476] / zhes bka' stsal pa ltar sangs rgyas chos thams cad kyi snying po'am rtsa ba lta bu ni yon tan ma lus pa byang zhing chub ste 'gro ba kun mi gnas pa'i myang 'das la 'god snyam pa'i sems bskyed pa kho na yin pas na/ bdag gis sems can mtha' yas pa'i don du byang chub de thob par mi nus bsams nas smon sems spong ba de ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba lnga pa yin zhes pa'o/ /

Bodhicitta is the root of Dharma, to abandon it is the fifth.[907] The 112th chapter of the Avataṃsaka Sutra says:
Son of the family, the bodhi mind is like the seed of all the Dharmas of the Buddha.[908] As this sutra says, the essence or the root of the Dharmas of the Buddha is exclusively the generation of the mind that thinks, “I will attain the enlightenment, the ultimate achievement of insight and abandonment, and bring all beings to the nonabiding nirvana.” Therefore, to think “I cannot attain that state of enlightenment for the sake of limitless sentient beings,” and thereby abandon the aspiring bodhicitta is the fifth root downfall.

d.div: [475] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba1
[476] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a sdong po bkod pa'i le'u/ bam po/ 9_shog_309_ba1
[908] Avataṃsakasūtra, chap. 9, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 309b1.

f.d: rang ngam gzhan gyi grub pa'i mtha'/ / chos la smod pa drug pa yin/[477] / zhes pa bka' 'grel du rang gi grub mtha' gsang sngags rdo rje theg pa dang gzhan gyi grub mtha' pha rol tu phyin pa'i theg par bzhed kyang nag po bas rang gi grub mtha' sangs rgyas kyi ring lugs dang gzhan mu stegs par mdzad pa 'thad dam snyam ste/

Deriding the doctrines of one’s own or others’ tenets is the sixth.[909] Although the commentary asserts one’s own tenets as referring to the secret mantra Vajrayana and the tenets of others as being the Perfection Vehicle, Nagpopa says that one’s own doctrine refers to Buddhism while “others” refers to non-Buddhist tīrthikas, and I wonder if this is not correct.

d.div: [477] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba1
[909] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b1.

f.d:
rgyud las/
mu stegs can la smad byas na/ / rnam par snang mdzad ring ba'i rgyu/[478] / zhes dang / theg pa gang la'ang med du mi rung ba'i skyabs 'gro'i bslab byar yang de dang cha mtshungs su bshad pas phyi nang ngam mdo sngags 'phags pa'i yul du grub mtha' smra ba chen po bzhi/ gangs can gyi ljongs su deng sang grags che ba sa dge/ kar 'brug / dgas shangs/ zhi byed sogs phyogs ris can gang la yang thog ma rang nyid der zhugs nas slar de bas gzhan la zhugs te thog ma'i rang nyid kyi grub mtha' de la smod par gyur pa'am/ gzhan pha rol gyi chos lugs grub pa'i mtha' ste gang la yang bsam pa thag pa nas sun 'byin cing smod pa rtsa ltung drug pa yin zhes pa'o//

A tantra says:
Deriding the non-Buddhists will send Vairocana far away.[910] Also, something similar can be found in the commitments of taking refuge, which is indispensable to all vehicles. Therefore, whether it refers to Buddhist and non-Buddhist, or to the four great tenets of the noble land of India, to sutra and tantra, and to the more well-known traditions these days in the snowy land of Tibet—the Sakya, Geluk, the Karma, Drukpa, Dakpo, and Shang traditions of the Kagyü, the Shijé tradition, and so on—if you initially belong to any such grouping, leave it for another, and then deride your own former tradition, or alternatively if you deride and wholeheartedly reject the traditions and tenets of others more generally, this is the sixth root downfall.

d.div: [478] sde dge_2488_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_'jam dpal grags pa/ rdo rje theg pa'i rtsa ba'i ltung ba rgya cher bshad pa/ shog_212_ba3_bye brag gi rgyud las zhes khungs mdzad do//
[910] Untraced.

f.d: yongs su ma smin sems can la/ / gsang ba sgrog pa bdun pa yin/[479] / zhes log lta can gsang sngags kyi chos yongs su ma rdzogs pas snod kyis ma smin pa log sred can/ log lta med kyang cho gas ma smin pa bum dbang ma thob pa/ rdzogs pas ma smin pa gsang ba shes rab ye shes ma thob pa/ nyams pas ma smin pa rtsa ltung phyir ma bcos pa/ zab mos 'jigs pas ma smin pa ste rnam pa lngas ma smin pa'i gang zag sems can ci yang rung ba la rim pa gnyis la sogs pa'i sngags kyi gsang ba'i de kho na nyid byung rgyal du sgrog pa ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba'i nang gi rnam grangs bdun pa yin zhes pa'o/ /

Proclaiming the secrets to beings completely unripe is the seventh.[911] Beings are unripe in five ways. Those said to have base desires are those with wrong views in whom the criteria necessary for secret mantra are incomplete and so are unripe in the sense of not being suitable vessels. Those who have not received the vase empowerment, even though they may be free of wrong views, have not been ripened by ritual. Those who have not received the knowledge-gnosis empowerment have not been ripened completely. Those who have not restored a broken root downfall are unripe by their degeneration. The fifth are those unripe because of their fear of the profound. Carelessly proclaiming to any of these types of beings the realities of the secrets of mantra, such as the two stages, is the seventh of the root downfalls.

d.div: [479] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba1
[911] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b1.

f.d: phung po sangs rgyas lnga bdag nyid/ / de la brnyas byed brgyad pa yin/[480] / zhes gzugs dang tshor ba dang 'du shes dang 'du byed dang rnam par shes pa'i phung po lnga rim pa ltar rnam snang / rin 'byung / 'od dpag med/ don grub/ mi bskyod pa ste rang bzhin rnam par dag pa'i sangs rgyas de bzhin gshegs pa lnga'i rang bzhin nam bdag nyid can yin pa de nang gi sbyin sreg gis mchod cing bde ba bsgrub par bya rgyu la/ theg chen sems bskyed kyis ma zin par rang nyid thar pa dang mtho ris thob pa'i rgyur blun rtags kyis 'gag pa dang g.yang sar mchongs pa dang dman pa'i yan lag cha tshang ba 'byung ba las yan lag nying lag mchod par 'bul ba gcod pa smyung bar gnas pa sogs rang lus la brnyas pa'am gdung ba rtsom par byed pa ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba brgyad pa yin zhes so/ /

d.div: [480] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba1

[913] The text here on the examples of despising the body appears to be corrupt. Therefore, as the author follows Tsongkhapa very closely in the whole of this topic, I have translated his sentence according to Tsongkhapa.

f.d: rang bzhin dag pa'i chos rnams la/ / som nyi za ba dgu pa yin/[481] / zhes rang bzhin med pa rnam par dag pa'i stong pa nyid spros pa dang bral ba dang / gzhan yang gong du brjod pa bzhin rang gzhan gyi grub pa'i mtha' phyogs ris med pa'i chos rnam par dag pa/ khyad par bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen pos tshad 'dzin nyams su bzhes pa'i chos zab mo rnams la bden rdzun som nyi'am the tshom za ba ni ltung ba dgu pa yin zhes pa'o/ /

The ninth is to doubt the natural purity of phenomena.[914] This refers to entertaining doubts of validity or uncertainty over phenomena’s lack of nature, the purity of emptiness free of fabrication, and also, as mentioned previously, toward the pure and nonsectarian Dharmas of one’s own and other traditions, and particularly to the profound and authentic Dharmas practiced by my guru, the Great Fifth.[915] Such doubts constitute the ninth downfall.

d.div: [481] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba2
[914] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b2.

[915] Probably a reference to the fact that the Fifth Dalai Lama practiced extensively in the Nyingma tradition as well as in the Geluk, and there may have been some who expressed doubts over the authenticity and purity of such practices.

f.d: gdug la rtag tu byams ldan par/ / byed pa 'di ni bcu par 'dod/[482] / ces dkon cog gsum dang bla ma smod pa dang bstan pa 'jig pa sogs kyi sems can zhing bcu tshang ba gdug pa can dag la'ang ngo bo brtse ba snying rje chen pos rjes su bzung ba'i rnam par shes pa gnas spar ba la sogs pa dgos mod kyang gnas skabs spyod pa de ltar du bskyangs kyang dus rtag pa dang yun ring po zhig tu snying rje'i sems kyis bsgral ba la sogs pa ma nus par byams pa dang ldan par skyong bar byed pa 'di lta bu ni rtsa ltung bcu par b+ha bi la bdag 'dod do zhes pa'o//

Constantly showing love to the wicked is asserted as being the tenth.[916] Even toward wicked sentient beings that possess the ten criteria for being an enemy of the doctrine, such as disparaging the Three Jewels and the guru, destroying the teachings, and so forth, you should of course maintain a level of consciousness that cares for them with great compassion. However, while it is acceptable to behave in this compassionate manner for a while, to nurture love for these beings constantly over a long period of time without being able to remove[917] them with a compassionate mind, is, as I Bhavila[918] assert, to commit the tenth root downfall.

d.div: [482] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba2
[916] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b2.

[917] Bsgral: to liberate, to kill legally, to banish. The sense here is to kill through the use of tantric powers, as Tsongkhapa cites passages here promoting the use of violent methods in such cases.
[918] Bhavila, or Bhabilha, is another name for Aśvaghoṣa, though it does not appear in the list of his twenty-one names listed previously.

f.d: ming sogs bral ba'i chos rnams la/ / der rtog pa ni bcu gcig pa/[483] / zhes don dam par ming dang tshig dang ngag gi brjod pa la sogs pa spros pa dang bral ba'i shes bya'i chos zab mo rnams la/ grub mtha'i dpyad pas ming sogs bden par 'dzin pa'i mtshan ma der rtog par byed na'am chos bdag med pa'i lta ba rnyed nas lta ba de rgyun du bsten dgos pa la de las ldog pa ni rtsa ltung bcu gcig pa'o/ /

To give concept toward phenomena that are devoid of names and so on is the eleventh.[919] The eleventh root downfall is using the philosophical analysis of tenet study to conceptualize with terminology and so forth marked by a grasping at true existence of those profound phenomena that ultimately are free of fabrication by name, words, verbalization, and the like. Alternatively, having found the perfect view of the no-self of phenomena, you then have to maintain it continuously; if instead you turn away from it, this is also the eleventh.

d.div: [483] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba2
[919] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b2.

f.d: sems can dad dang ldan pa yi/ / sems sun 'byin pa bcu gnyis pa/[484] / zhes sems can te skyes bu gang zhig gsang sngags rdo rje'i theg pa mchog gi lam la dad cing mos pa dang ldan pa'i gus pa lhag par che ba de yi sems kyi 'dun pa theg pa de la ma dad par ldog 'dod kyi bsam pas brnyas pa dang smad pa'i sgo nas sun yang nas yang du'am lan gcig tsam 'byin par byed pa ni rtsa ltung bcu gnyis pa'o/ /

Turning the minds of beings with faith is said to be the twelfth.[920] “Beings” refers to any living being possessed of a great devotion of faith and disposition for the path of the supreme secret mantra of Vajrayana. With the wish to reverse their faith in that vehicle, you use derision and disparagement to uproot their aspiration again and again or even just once. This is the twelfth root downfall.

d.div: [484] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba2

f.d: dam tshig ji bzhin rnyed pa dag / mi bsten pa de bcu gsum pa/[485] / zhes tshogs 'khor ram dpa' bo pho mo'i ston mo'i cho ga tshul bzhin du byed pa'i tshe dam tshig gi rdzas sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga sogs pa la ni rtog pas ma 'byongs bar ji lta ba bzhin du mi spyod la/ gzhan yang phyi dro'i kha zas sogs dam rdzas ji snyed cig mi 'dod pa'i bsam pas bsten par mi byed pa ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba bcu gsum yin zhes so/ /

Not using the pledges as they are found, this is the thirteenth.[921] This means that at properly conducted ceremonial feasts or hero and heroine festivities, not purifying though the power of thought the five meats, five nectars, and other pledge substances, and consequently not partaking of them as they are. It also means not using pledges in the sense of not wanting to partake of pledge substances in the form of evening meals and so forth. This constitutes the thirteenth root downfall.

d.div: [485] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba2

f.d: shes rab rang bzhin bud med la/ / smod par byed pa bcu bzhi pa/[486] / zhes pa shes rab ni bde ba chen po'i ye shes yin la rang bzhin ni 'dir 'byung ba'i don te rnal 'byor pa la de bskyed par byed pa po bskal pa dang po'i dus pho mo'i dbang po'i sgo dod par nye ba'i skabs lba ba lta bu'i dbyibs 'bur po re yod pa re zhig na la la ni skyes te pho mtshan du gyur bas skyes pa/ la la ni bud nas med pa'i bug pa can du gyur bas bud med du grags pa'i tshul 'dzin pa 'jig rten las 'das ba'i rigs dang bud med mtshan nyid pa gang yang rung ba la/ so thar chags bral la a 'thas pa'am gzhan yang skyon gdags 'dod kyi kun slong gi smod par byed pa ni rnal 'byor bla med kyis rjes su 'brangs ba'i rtsa ba'i ltung ba bcu bzhi pa'o zhes

Disparaging women, nature of wisdom, is the fourteenth.[922] With “wisdom” referring to the great-bliss gnosis, and “nature” meaning “arising here,” the agent that produces this wisdom in the yogi is woman, whose etymology is as follows. During the first eon close to the time of the development of male and female reproductive organs, a goiter-like protuberance appeared on the bodies of beings. In some beings it grew and became the sign of a male. Therefore, such a being was known as man (skyes pa, “growth”). In others it developed an opening and did not protrude. This was the sign of a female, and so she became known as woman (bud med, “with no protuberance”). “Woman” here can refer to those of supramundane qualities or any being that fulfills the criteria of being a woman. To disparage those women because of your stubborn attachment to the desire-free path of the pratimokṣa, or being motivated by a desire to find fault in them, is the fourteenth root downfall of those who follow highest yoga tantra.

d.div: [486] gong mtshungs/ shog_179_ba3

f.d: 'phags yul mkhas pa'i gtsug rgyan slob dpon dpa' bo'am b+ha bi las bsdu ba mdzad pa ltar/ pha rgyud rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi le'u bcu gnyis pa/ bshad rgyud rdo rje rtse mo/ dgra nag rgyud kyi rim par phye ba bcu bdun pa/ gshed dmar le'u bco brgyad pa rnams nas nang gses dang 'gyur khyad cung zad las rkang grangs bcu bzhi kho na dang / ma rgyud gur gyi rgyud le'u bco lnga bar rtsa ltung bcur gsungs pa yod kyang /[487] don gong du bshad ma thag pa'i bcu bzhir ma 'dus pa med cing /

These downfalls have been summarized by Ācārya Śūra or Bhavila, crown jewel of Indian scholars. Similarly, they are found in father tantras such as the twelfth chapter of the Vajra Essence Ornament Tantra, the explanatory tantra Vajraśekhara, the seventeenth section of the Black Yamāri Tantra, the eighteenth chapter of the Red Yamāri Tantra, where apart from few differences in internal divisions and in translation, they number fourteen. In the fifteenth chapter of the mother tantra Vajrapañjara, ten downfalls are listed,[923] but they contain nothing that is not included in the fourteen explained above.

d.div: [487] sde dge_419_bka'/ rgyud/ nga rdo rje gur zhes bya ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po'i brtag pa/ le'u/ 15_shog_64_ba3
[923] Vajrapañjaratantra, chap. 15, Toh 419 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 64b3.

f.d: de dag gi bsdu ba ni/ ltung ba 'di rnams gsungs pa kha na ma tho ba chen po rnams dgag pa'i phyir du bcas pa yin la/ gang la brten nas nyes pa rnams 'byung ba'i gtso bo ni/ 'di ltar rang la chos ston pa po dang / chos sgrub pa'i grogs dang / nyams su blang bya'i chos dang gsum gtso bo yin pa las/ dang po la dmigs pa'i kha na ma tho ba 'gog pa ni ltung ba dang po'i bcas pa/ grogs la gnyis te yang dag pa'i grogs dang phyin ci log gi grogs po/ dang po la log par sgrub pa 'gog pa ni ltung ba gsum pa dang bcu gnyis pa'i bcas pa/ gnyis pa la mdza' bar byed pa 'gog pa ni bcu pa'i bcas pa/ chos la lung dang sgrub pa gnyis las/ lung la khyad gsod kyis 'jug pa dang / bka' ma yin zhes skur ba 'debs pa dang / bstan par mi 'os pa ston pa 'gog pa ni ltung ba gnyis pa dang drug pa dang bdun pa'i bcas pa/ sgrub pa'i chos la/ lam gyi rten/ ngo bo/ yan lag dang gsum las/ rten la gang gi ched du sems bskyed pa'i sems can la log par sgrub pa dang / sems rang gi ngo bo 'dor ba 'gog pa ni bzhi pa dang lnga pa'i bcas pa/ ngo bor bskyed rdzogs gnyis kyi dang po gang ltar sgom pa'i gzhi phung po la brnyas pa 'gog pa ni brgyad pa'i bcas pa/ rdzogs rim la stong pa nyid dang po nas spang ba dang rtogs kyang yid la byed pa 'dor ba 'gag pa gnyi+os ni dgu pa dang bcu gcig pa'i bcas pa/ yan lag la lam gyi gzhi dam tshig dang grogs bud med gnyis las dam tshig mi brten pa dang bud med smod pa 'gog pa na ltu+ing ba bcu gsum pa dang bcu bzhi pa'i bcas pa'o//

The teachings on these downfalls are prescriptive rules for the prevention of serious faults. The principal objects through which these faults can occur are those who teach us the Dharma, our practitioner friends, and the Dharma to be practiced. Faults arising from focusing on the first of these are prevented by the prescription for the first downfall. Friends are of two kinds: true friends and false friends. The prescription of the third and twelfth vow stops us from acting wrongly to the first type of friend. The tenth prevents us from acquainting with the second type of friend. Dharma is of two types: scripture and practice. Practicing with disregard to the scriptures, slandering teachings by denying that they are the words of the Buddha, and teaching the unsuitable are prevented by the second, sixth, and seventh prescription. Dharma in terms of practice refers to the basis of the path, the nature of the path, and branches of the path. The basis of the path refers to the bodhi mind developed for sentient beings, and the fourth and fifth vows prevent us from acting wrongly to those sentient beings and from giving up the very nature of that mind. The nature of the path consists of the generation stage and completion stage. The eighth prescription prevents us from mistreating the aggregates, which are the bases of the deities we meditate on. The ninth and the eleventh vows prevent us from abandoning emptiness from the very outset of the completion stage and, even though it has been perceived, giving up mental engagement in it. There are two branches of the path: the pledges as the foundation of the path and women companions. The thirteenth and fourteenth prevent not partaking of the pledges and the disparagement of women.
bsrungs 'dod bskyed pa

d.i: Generating the desire to guard the vows and not be tainted by downfalls

f.d: ['di ]la bsrungs ba'i phan yon dang nyes dmigs bsam pa gnyis las/
1. Reflecting on the advantages of guarding the vows 2. Reflecting on the faults of not guarding the vows
dang po ni/
Reflecting on the advantages of guarding the vows

sngags pas 'di dag spangs na ni/ / dngos grub nges par thob par 'gyur/[488] / zhes dang / gsang ba'i mdzod las/
dbang bskur yang dag sbyin ldan na/ / skye dang skye bar dbang bskur 'gyur/ / de yis skye ba bdun la ni/ / ma bsgoms par yang dngos grub thob/[489] / ces sogs dang /

If mantra practitioners avoid these, they will without doubt gain siddhi.[924] The Treasury of Secrets says:
If given pure empowerment, they will be empowered life after life, and in seven lives even without meditation will gain siddhi.[925]

d.div: [488] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rja theg pa rtse ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba3
[489] gsang ba'i mdzod zhes pa'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[924] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b3.
[925] Tsongkhapa in his Blossom Cluster of Siddhis (p. 52a6) states this quote was cited by Saraha in his Commentary on the Buddhakapāla Tantra (Toh 1652 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel ra).

f.d:
dam tshig lnga pa las/
gal te ltung ba med gyur na/ / skye ba bcu drug dag na 'grub/[490] / ces dang / bi b+hu ti tsan+d+ra_sa kyang de bzhin du gsungs pas [491]rtsa ba dang yan lag gi nyes pas ma gos pa'am gos kyang phyir bcos tshul bzhin du byas nas dam tshig dang sdom pa tshul bzhin bsrungs na skye ba bcu drug tshun 'grub cing de ma thob kyi bar yang rgyal ba dang rgyal sras dpa' bo dang dpa' mo'i tshogs rnams kyis dgyes bzhin du srung bas yon tan gong nas gong du 'phel ba dang bdud rigs kyis glags mi rnyed pa sogs phan yon mtha' yas pas spro shugs che bar bya ba dang /

In Five Pledges it says:
If there are no downfalls, siddhi in sixteen lives.[926] Vibhūticandra says likewise.[927] Therefore, if you have not been tainted by the root and secondary faults—and even if you have been tainted, if you have properly restored them—thereby guarding the vows and pledges well, you will achieve siddhi within sixteen lives. Furthermore, until that time you will be happily protected by the conquerors, the bodhisattvas, and the great male and female warriors. Qualities will continue to grow, and the māras will find no opportunity to attack. These and many other bounteous benefits will follow. Therefore, develop great enthusiasm and inspiration in guarding the vows.

d.div: [490] sde dge_1224_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ nya_slob dpon pad+ma 'byung gnas/ dam tshig lnga pa/ shog_28_ba2
[491] sde dge_3727_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshu_slob dpon bi b+hU ta tsan+d+ri / sdom gsum 'od kyi phreng ba/ shog_56_ba6
[926] Padmasambhava, Samayapañca, Toh 1224 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, nya, 28b2.
[927] Garland of Light on the Three Vows (Trisaṃvaraprabhāmālā), Toh 3727 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 56b6.

f.d: gnyis pa nyes dmigs ni/
Reflecting on the faults of not guarding the vows

gzhan du dam tshig las nyams na/ / nyams pa bdud kyis bzung bar 'gyur/ / de nas sdug bsngal myong 'gyur zhing / / thur du bltas te dmyal bar 'gro[492] / zhes dang / sa ra has/
re zhig dam tshig nyams pa la/ / dngos grub thob pa lta zhog gi/ / mi yi skye ba'ang rnyed par dka'/[493] / zhes sogs mang du gsungs pa mdor bsdu tshe dam tshig dang bcas mtshams las 'das shing / nyams pa na tshe 'dir bdud dang log 'dren la sogs pas 'dzin pas bkra mi shis pa'i rnam pa sna tshogs byung nas lus dang sems la sdug bsngal mang ba dang / phyi ma rkang pa spyi bo tshugs su dmyal bar 'gro ba la sogs te khe nyen shin tu che bas spang blang ma 'dzol ba bya dgos/

Or, if they degenerate their pledges, such degenerates are seized by Māra. They will experience great suffering and, facing downward, go to hell.[928] Saraha says:
Conversely, if their pledges degenerate, forget the gaining of siddhi, even human birth will be difficult.[929] Many texts make the same point. In short, if you transgress the pledges and prescriptions and they degenerate, then in this life you will be seized by Māra and other wayward spirits and experience all manner of misfortune, thereby bringing much suffering to body and mind. In the next life you will be turned upside down and fall to hell. Therefore, the benefits and the corresponding disadvantages are huge, and consequently you should be very clear about what is to be developed and what is to be abandoned.

d.div: [492] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba3
[493] sde dge_1657_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ra/ sa ra ha/ sangs rgyas thad po'i dkyil 'khar gyi+o cho ga'i rim pa/ shog_243_na7
[928] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel zi, 179b3.
[929] Buddhakapāla Mandala Ritual, Toh 1657 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ra, 243a7.

f.d: ji ltar bsrung ba'i tshul ni/

de bas nga rgyal bcom nas ni/ / bdag nyid 'khrul pa shes byas la/[494] / zhes bsrung na phan yon shin tu che la ma bsrungs na nyes dmigs kyang de dang 'dra bas ltung bar 'gyur mi 'gyur gyi mtshams gang yin ma shes na mi shes pa ltung ba 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pas de'i gnyen por rtsa ba dang yan lag gi ltung ba rnams legs par shes pa dgos dang / shes kyang grogs dang bcas pa sogs la mi gus na ma gus pa ltung ba 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pas nga rgyal nges par bcom nas gus par bya la/ gus kyang bag yod dang dran pa dang shes bzhin ma bsten na bag med ltung ba 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pas bdag nyid ma 'khrul ba ste spyod lam kun tu bag yod sogs dang ldan dgos shing / gus la bag yod par spyod kyang nyon mongs shas che na nyon mongs mang ba ltung ba 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pas nga rgyal gyis mtshon nas nyon mongs gzhan gang shas che ba yang gnyen po bsten nas mthu chung du gtong /

Therefore, destroy your pride, do not deceive yourself, and be knowledgeable.[930] The benefits of guarding the vows are immense; the drawbacks of not guarding are likewise huge. Therefore, if you are not knowledgeable about the threshold between downfall and no downfall, then that lack of knowledge becomes a cause for downfall. Therefore, its remedy is to thoroughly know the root and branch downfalls. Even if you are knowledgeable, if you have no respect, even for practitioner friends and for the prescribed rules, then such disrespect becomes a cause for downfall. Therefore, destroy your pride and develop respect. Even with respect, if you do not cultivate mindfulness, awareness, and conscientiousness, such a lack of conscientiousness becomes a cause for downfall. Therefore, do not deceive yourself and arm yourself with conscientiousness and so on in all you do. Though you may behave conscientiously and with great respect, if you are troubled by much mental affliction, such a predominance of affliction will become a cause for downfall. Therefore, as illustrated above with pride, whatever other affliction predominates, apply yourself to its antidote and reduce it.

d.div: [494] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba' ltu+ing ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba4_lung 'di sde dge bstan 'gyur ltar bcos/
[930] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel zi, 179b4.

f.d:
de ltar yang rdo rje rtse mo las/
dam tshig nyid ni nyams gyur na/ / 'bras bu 'di ni thob mi 'gyur/ / 'di ni khyod kyi dmyal ba'i chu/ / dam tshig 'das na bsreg par byed/[495] / ces sogs mang du gsungs pa ltar ro//

The Vajraśekhara says:
If you degenerate the pledges, you will not gain these fruits. This will become your water of hell. Break your pledges and you will burn.[931]

d.div: [495] sde dge_480_bka'/ rgyud/ nya gsang ba rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud rdo rje rtse mo/ shog_211_na7
[931] Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 211a7.

f.d: nyams pa phyir bcos pa'i thabs ni/

mnyam par bzhag pas bla ma la/ / ci 'byor pa yis mchod byas la/ / gsum la skyabs 'gro nas brtsams te/ / byang chub sems sogs sdom pa ni/ / gal te bdag la phan 'dod na/ / sngags pas 'bad de bzung bar bya/[496] / zhes sngar bshad pa ltar gsungs kyang bag med pa la sogs pa'i dbang gis bla ma la smod pa sogs rtsa ltung gang rung byung na des thog ma nyid du mnyam par bzhag pas te yid rtse gcig tu byas nas tshogs 'khor sogs sngon du 'gro ba'i 'bul ba ci 'byor ba ste rang gi nus pa che chung dang 'tsham pas bla mar mchod pa byas la nyes pa de rnams bshags par bya zhing / gal te bdag la 'phral yun du bde zhing phan pa gcig 'dod na slar yang sdom pa bzung bar bya ba'o/ /

In meditation make offerings to the guru of whatever you have. Then beginning with refuge in the Three Jewels, if you want to benefit yourselves with the vows of bodhicitta and so on, you mantra practitioners should take them with great determination.[932] If you guard the vows as described above but still incur a root downfall, such as disparaging the guru through a lack of conscientiousness, straight away make preliminary offerings to the guru by sitting with the single-pointed mind of meditation and offering whatever you have—meaning according to your ability—to the visualized assembly. Then confess the transgressions. If you want to benefit yourself now and in the long term, retake the vows.

d.div: [496] sde dge_2478_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ rdo rje theg pa rtsa ba'i ltung ba bsdus pa/ shog_179_ba4
[932] Aśvaghoṣa, Compilation of Vajrayana Root Downfalls, Toh 2478 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 179b4.

f.d:
'jam mgon btsong kha pa chen pos/
mdo rgyud gzhan dang bshad srol mi 'dra ba'i/ / shing rta'i srol 'byed dus kyi 'khor lo'i rgyud/[497] / ces pa ltar gong bshad rnams dang cung mi mthun pa bzhed pa mang yang bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen po gnyis med du bzhed pa dus kyi 'khor lo'i skor/ dbang le las/ 'dod pa'i rdo rje la ni rdo rje dril bu phyag rgya bla ma dag kyang spyi bos bzung bar bgyi/[498] / zhes sogs sdom pa bzung tshul dang / dpal ldan bla ma'i thugs dkrugs pa las bu rnams kyi ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba ri bong 'dzin par 'gyur/[499] / zhes sogs rtsa ltung rkang grangs bcu bzhi la ngo bo mi 'dra ba'i khyad par dang /

Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa says:
The pioneering Kālacakra Tantra has a different tradition of explanation from other sutras and tantras.[933] In Kālacakra literature, which my guru the Great Fifth calls a nondual tantra, there are many slight variations on the topics explained above. For example, on the taking of the vows, it says in the Initiation chapter, “For the desire Vajra family, the vajra, bell, mudrā, and guru are venerated on the crown”[934] and so on. Also, on the lines teaching the fourteen root downfalls: “Disturbing the mind of the glorious guru is the first root downfall for the son,”[935] and so on. These indicate a difference in content.

d.div: [497] rje tsong kha pa chen po'i gsung 'bum/ kha gsung thor bu/ rtogs brjod mdun legs ma/ skabs/ 1_shog_53_ba5
[498] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas las phyung ba rgyud kyi rgyal po dpal dus kyi 'khor lo zhes bya ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka86_shog_66_na7
[499] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas las phyung ba rgyud kyi rgyal po dpal dus kyi 'khor lo zhes bya ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka102_shog_68_na1
[933] Song of Realization, chap. 1, Collected Works, kha, 53b5.
[934] Kālacakra Tantra, 3:86, Toh 362 Kangyur, ka, 66a7.
[935] Kālacakra Tantra, 3:102, Toh 362 Kangyur, ka, 68a1.

d.i: Vows in the early translation schools

f.d: 'phags yul du shin tu gsang bas chig brgyud du bzhugs shing / gangs can du 'gyur khyad kyis snga 'gyur du grags pa'i lugs rang bzhin spyir bstan pa la dam tshig gi ngo bo/ nges tshig / dbye ba/ rten/ phan yon/ nyes dmigs/ bskang thabs/ bsrung thabs dang brgyad las/

In India this tradition was so secret that it existed as a one-to-one oral tradition. In Tibet, as designated by the time of its translations, it became known as the “early translation” tradition. Generally, in this tradition this topic can be dealt with under eight headings: 1. Nature of the pledges 2. Etymology 3. Divisions 4. Bases of the pledges 5. Benefits of keeping the pledges 6. Disadvantages of breaking pledges 7. Repairing broken pledges 8. Guarding the pledges
dang po ngo bo ni/
Nature of the pledges

sngags kyi sdom pas rgyud bsdams pa'i gnyen po'i dpung dam bcas pa las mi 'da' bar byed pa ste/ dam tshig mchog gi rgyud las/
dam zhes bya ba bcings pa ste/ / rdo rje 'da' bka' gtan gyi gnyer/[500] / zhes so/ /

The power that is the mindstream bound by the tantric vows prevents the breaking of one’s oaths. The Supreme Pledges Tantra:
“Pledge” means bind: a vajra hard to break, a permanent guard.[936]

d.div: [500] dam tshig mchog gi+o rgyud las zhes pa'i rgyud kyi dpe lag son ma gyur/
[936] Untraced.

f.d: nges tshig ni/
Etymology

de nyid las/
spyir na dam tshig zhes bya ba/ / rang sems tshig pa med pa la/ / g.yo rgyu rnams dang bral ba'o/[501] / zhes dang /

The Supreme Pledges Tantra:
In general, “pledge” (dam tshig) means divorced of all pretense in a mind with no anger (tshig pa).[937]

d.div: [501] gong mtshungs dpe lag son ma gyur/
[937] Untraced. Tshig pa also means “burn,” and other commentators have glossed the term dam tshig to mean “bound and burn.”

f.d: dbye na
Divisions

sngags spyi'i lugs kyis rtsa ba dang yan lag gi dam tshig gnyis de yang rtsa ba sku gsung thugs gsum/ yan lag nyi shu rtsa lnga ste/ shes par bya ba/ dang du blang ba/ mi spang ba/ spyad par bya ba/ bsgrub par bya ba rnams la lnga lnga'o/ /

Generally, the tantra tradition talks of root and secondary pledges. The root pledges are divided into enlightened body, speech, and mind pledges. There are twenty-five secondary pledges—five headings each containing five: those to be known, those to be accepted, those not to be abandoned, those to be practiced, and those to be accomplished.

'dir bye brag gis dbye na/ lta ba/ spyod pa/ bsgrub pa/ thun mong ba/ khyad par sku gsung thugs/ yan lag / gal mdo nges pa'i dam tshig dang bdun te/ rang shar las/
'bum sder gsungs pa'i dam tshig rnams/ / mdor bstan legs par yid la bzung / / de yang mdor bstan 'di lta ste/ / rtogs byed lta ba'i dam tshig dang / / spyod pa rgyun gyi dam tshig dang / / bsgrub pa spyi yi dam tshig dang / / thun mong spyi yi dam tshig dang / / sku gsung thugs kyi dam tshig dang / / yan lag grangs kyi dam tshig dang / / gal mdo nges pa'i dam tshig go/ / de la sogs pa'i dam tshig rnams/ / mdo dang rgyas pa chen po'o/[502] / zhes pa ltar dang /

Specifically, in this tradition, there are seven divisions: those of view, practice, accomplishment, common pledges, specific pledges of enlightened body, speech, and mind, secondary pledges, and essential pledges. In the Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind it says:
A summary of the pledges taught in the great collections; hold them in your mind: pledges of the view bringing insight, pledges of continual practice, general pledges of accomplishment, the general common pledges, pledges of body, speech, and mind, pledges counted as secondary, and the essential definite pledges. These and other pledges are taught in brief and extensively.[938]

d.div: [502] rnying ma rgyud 'bum/ pod/ da rig pa rang shar chen po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 10_shog_176_ba7
[938] Collected Tantras of the Nyingma, vol. da, chap. 10, 176b7.

f.d: rten ni/
Bases of the pledges

slob dpon dang slob ma mched lcam ste/ de nyid las/
bsam gyis mi khyab dam tshig rnams/ / rnam pa gnyis su 'dus par gsungs/ / slob dpon dang ni slob ma gnyis/ / bsrung ba'i rgyu zhes kun du grags/ / bsrung ba'i rgyu ni slob dpon te/ / bsrung bar byed pa slob ma'o/[503] / zhes dang / mched lcam la bzhir nges pa yang /

This refers to the master and to the disciple brothers and sisters. The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
The pledges inconceivable to the mind are taught in brief as being two— those of the master and those of the disciple— and are known as foundations for the guarding of pledges. The cause for guarding pledges is the master, the guardian of pledges is the disciple.[939] Vajra brothers and sisters are determined as being of four types.

d.div: [503] rnying ma rgyud 'bum/ pod/ da rig pa rang shar chen po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 9_shog_175_na6

f.d:
de nyid las/
rdo rje'i spun la don bzhis bstan/ / spyi dang nye dang 'dres pa dang / / dkyil 'khor bum pa 'dres pa'o/[504] / zhes pa bstan par zhugs so cog dang khyad par gsang sngags la zhugs pa thams cad spyi'i mched dang / chos rigs gcig pa rnams nye ba'i mched/ bla ma gcig gis bsdus pa rnams 'dres pa'i mched/ dkyil 'khor gcig tu mar me gcig bum pa gcig gis dbang dus gcig la bskur ba rnams ni shin du 'dres pa'i mched do/ / 'di dag kyang yul bdun 'gyur gyis gnyan par shes par bya'o/ / slob dpon la'ang thams cad kyis slob dpon du bskur ba spyi'i slob dpon dang / rang nyid chos la sbyor ba 'dren pa'i slob dpon dang / dam tshig dang / sdom pa sbyin pa dbang gi slob dpon dang / gdams ngag 'bogs pa lung gi slob dpon te/

The same text says:
Vajra brothers are explained by four characteristics: common, close, joined, and joined by the mandala vase.[940] All those who have entered the teachings, and especially those who have entered tantra, are common vajra siblings. Those who follow the same Dharma are close siblings. Those brought together by the same guru are joined siblings. Those conferred empowerment at the same ceremony in the same mandala by the same lamp, the same vase, are all closely joined vajra siblings. You should know that all these are objects whose risk factor is multiplied seven times. Masters are also of four types. A commonly recognized master is one universally conferred with that title. A guiding master is he who brings one to Dharma. The empowering master confers pledges and vows. The scriptural master passes on oral instructions.

d.div: [504] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_177_ba7

f.d:
de nyid las/
slob dpon la yang don bzhi ste/ / spyi dang 'dres dang dam tshig dbang / / man ngag lung gi slob dpon no/[505] / zhes so/ /

The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
Master too are of four kinds: masters in general, guiding masters, the pledge empowerment master, the scriptural instruction master.[941]

d.div: [505] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_na1

f.d:
slob dpon dang / slob ma'i nges tshig kyang / de nyid las/
de yang nges tshig 'di lta ste/ / mi shes shes par 'grol phyir slob/ / rdzogs chen don la sbyor ba'i dpon/ / slob ma'i nges tshig 'di lta ste/ / ma yengs tshul gyis nyan pas slob/ / man ngag snod du gyur pas ma/ / de ltar don ldan dpon slob ni/ / yang dag sa la mnyam por gnas/ / dam tshig ldan na de bzhin no/[506] / zhes dang /

On the etymology of the terms master (lopön) and disciple (lopma), the text continues:
The etymology is as follows: Liberating from ignorance into knowledge, he is the teacher (slob). Bringing one to the great perfection, he is the powerful one (dpon). The etymology of disciple: Listening without distraction he is the student (slob). Becoming a vessel for instructions, he is the mother (ma).[942] In this way, such a master and disciple dwell equally in this perfect state. With the pledges it is thus.[943]

d.div: [506] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_na1

[942] These etymologies are for purposes of practice rather than scholastic precision. Another approach would be to say that slob dpon means “master of learning,” qualified by slob with its dual meaning of “to teach” and “to learn.” Also the ma of slob ma is more typically construed as a nominative ending rather than meaning “mother.”
[943] Collected Tantras of the Nyingma, vol. da, chap. 10, 178a1.

f.d: dam tshig bsrungs pa'i phan yon ni/
Benefits of keeping the pledges

de nyid las/
dam tshig sdom pa ji bzhin gnas/ / dam tshig la ni gang gnas pa/ / bsam pa thams cad mthar phyin 'gyur/[507] / zhes pa dang /
sgyu 'phrul las/ dam tshig mchog la gang gnas pa/ / dam pa mchog dang dam pa yis/ / sras dang spun dgongs byin gyis rlob/[508] / ces so/ /

The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
For those dwelling in the pledges, correctly bound to the pledges, all hopes will be fulfilled.[944] The Māyā Tantra says:
Those dwelling in the supreme pledges will be blessed and regarded as sons and brothers by the supremely great and the great.[945]

d.div: [507] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_177_ba3
[508] sgyu 'phrul las/ dam tshig mchog la gang gnas pa/ /dam pa mchog dang dam pa yis/ /sras dang spun dgongs byin gyis rlob/ /gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[945] Untraced.

f.d: dam tshig nyams pa'i nyes dmigs ni/
Disadvantages of breaking pledges

rang shar las/
nyams na gnyis ka 'tshig par 'gyur/ / sku yi dam tshig nyams gyur na/ / rdo rje dmyal ba chen por 'tshed/ / 'o dod 'bod pa'i gnas su skye/ /
gsung gi dam tshig nyams gyur na/ / snang ba 'gags par 'gyur ba dang / / mun rdul chen po'i gnas su skye/ / de nas thon par gyur nas kyang / / lkugs pa dag tu skye bar 'gyur/ /
thugs kyi dam tshig nyams gyur na/ / yid 'khrugs chen po'i gnas su skye/ / rtag du rtsod pa rgyun mi chad/ / 'thab dang sdug bsngal chen po dang / / yang na dran pa med par 'gyur/ / smyo 'bog nad kyi thebs par 'gyur/ / tha ma ngu 'bod gnas su skye/[509] / zhes pa dang /

The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
If broken, both guru and disciple will burn. If the body pledges are broken, they will boil in the vajra hell and be born in a place of great wailing.
If the speech pledges are broken, all light will disappear as you are born in a place of great darkness. Even when freed from there, you will be born dumb.
If the mind pledges are broken, you are born in places of mental turmoil, of constant quarrel, endless strife, fighting, and great suffering. Alternatively, you lose your mind, struck down with the illness of madness, to be born finally in the hell of wailing.[946]

d.div: [509] rnying ma rgyud 'bum/ pod/ da rig pa rang shar chen po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_na3
[946] Collected Tantras of the Nyingma, vol. da, chap. 10, 176b7.

f.d: dam tshig nyams pa'i snga ltas su/ / mi bde rnam pa sna tshogs 'byung / / yams dang 'tshe ba'i nad rnams dang / / rims nad sna tshogs 'byung bar 'gyur/ / gdon dang log 'dren rnams kyis kyang / / bsad nas sems can dmyal bar 'gro/ / mig gis gzugs mi mthong bar 'gyur/ / rna ba 'on cing las mi 'grub/ / mdze dang shu ba'i nad rnams 'byung / / chom rkun rgyal po'i chad pa 'byung / / gzhan la med pa'i rims nad 'byung / / bu dang chung ma 'chi bar ston/ / yul rnams thams cad dgrar ldang zhing / / byas pa don med chen por 'gyur/[510] / zhes pa ltar dang /

Also, further on:
Signs of broken pledges are: experiencing various misfortunes, plagues, and other infectious diseases, being murdered by demons and spirits and sent to hell, going blind, becoming deaf, never succeeding in whatever is attempted, your skin erupts in sores and leprosy, being punished by the king and robbed by bandits, getting infectious illnesses not caught by others, and seeing your wife and children die. Everyone becomes an enemy; all efforts are for naught.[947]

d.div: [510] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_ba4

f.d: nyams na bskang thabs
Repairing broken pledges

['di ]la gsum las/ dang po'i sku'i nyams na bskang ba'i thabs ni/ yang de nyid las/
gsung rab rgya chen bklag pa dang / / tshogs kyi 'khor lo rgya chen bskor/ / 'khor gsum yongs dag bya bar gsungs/[511] / zhes dang / gsung yang de las/
de yang sbyangs thabs 'di lta ste/ / mar me brgya rtsa cho ga dang / / spang bskong brgya rtsa gdon pa dang / / bshags pa rnam pa sna tshogs bya/ / des ni byang ba'i yon tan mthong /[512] / zhes pa'i spang bskong ni na rag rgyun bshags so/ /

This is under three outlines. On repairing broken pledges of the enlightened body, the Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
Recitation of the vast scriptures, extensive gaṇacakra offering ceremonies, and meditation on the three-circle purity.[948] For repairing broken pledges of the enlightened speech:
Perform the ceremony of the hundred lamps, recite the Hundred Abandonment Reparations and undertake various confession practices and you will see the achievement of purification.[949] Abandonment Reparations[950] refers to the naraka confession ritual.[951]

d.div: [511] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_na5
[512] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_na7
[948] Ibid., 178a5. “Three-circle purity” refers to the fact that for any act, the object, action, and agent all lack true existence.

[950] Hundred Prostration Abandonment Reparations, Toh 267, mdo sde, ya. One of the texts that fell from the sky during the reign of the early Tibetan king Lha Thothori Nyenshal as a sign that the Dharma would spread to Tibet. It was eventually translated into Tibetan by Thönmi Sambhota but has no Sanskrit title.
[951] Naraka (“hell”) here refers to the fruits of breaking pledges.

f.d:
thugs kyang de nyid las/
de yang sbyang thabs 'di lta ste/ / slob dpon mnyes pa'i rdzas kyis mchod/ / 'byor tshogs ci yod 'phags pa mchod/ / de ltar bshags pa byas gyur na/ / bsams pa thams cad 'grub par 'gyur/ / 'dod pa thams cad bskongs par 'gyur/ / bya ba thams cad rdzogs par 'gyur/[513] / zhes dang /

For repairing broken pledges of the enlightened mind:
Make offerings to please the guru, exalted offerings of whatever you have. If you perform confessions in this way, all thoughts will be realized, all wishes will be fulfilled, and all works will be accomplished.[952]

d.div: [513] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_178_ba3
[952] Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind, Collected Tantras of the Nyingma, vol. da, chap. 10, 178b3.

f.d: bsrung thabs ni/
Guarding the pledges

skyon yon mthong nas dran pa dang shes bzhin dag pas rgyud sdom pa ste/ de nyid las/
dam tshig la ni ji bzhin gnas/ / bskal ba zhig kyang mi gtong ba/ / dam tshig chen po'i bsrung thabs so/[514] / zhes pa bzhin dang / de'ang slob dpon gyis rgyud dang dam tshig gi rim pa shes pas shes pa bcus bsrung la/ slob mas mi shes pas slob dpon gyi bka' bzhin bsrungs pa'o// shes pa bcu ni/ tshig don gyi gnas shes pa dang / dris pa'i lan ldon par shes pa dang / dbang dang man ngag gi skabs shes pa dang / lta ba yangs par shes pa dang / bsgom pa'i dad che bar shes pa dang / chos nyid zab par shes pa dang / 'khor ba dang ma 'dres par shes pa dang / 'das pa'i sa la gnas par shes pa dang / rang dang spyi'i chos dang chos can gyis mtshan nyid shes pa'o/ /

Seeing the advantages and disadvantages, bind the mind with mindfulness and pure awareness. The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
Dwelling perfectly in the pledges, not forsaking them even at the eon’s destruction, is the way to guard the great pledges.[953] The master possesses knowledge of the tantra and the levels of the pledges and guards those pledges by the tenfold knowledge. The disciple does not possess this knowledge and guards the pledges by following the instructions of the master. These ten are: knowledge of the meanings of text, knowing how to answer questions, knowing the right time and occasion for empowerment and instruction, knowledge of the wide view, knowledge of the great desire of meditation, knowledge of profound reality, knowledge of being unmixed with samsara, knowledge of dwelling at a supramundane level, and knowledge of the defining characteristics of general and specific phenomena and the features of phenomena.

d.div: [514] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_177_ba3

f.d:
yang de nyid las/
de yang bsrung thabs 'di lta ste/ / shes pa gcig gi khyad par gyis/ / khyad par bcu yi bsrung thabs 'phags/ / gcig la de bas nyung ba'o/ / dam tshig rgyal po de bzhin spyod/[515] / ces dang / gzhan sku gsung thugs kyi dam tshig bye brag bshad pa dang / bla na med pa'i dam tshig mchog tu bstan pa'i rgyas bshad yod kyang 'dir de tsam mo//

The Tantra of the Self-Appearing Mind says:
As a method of protecting the pledges, the ten features within a single consciousness is exalted. In one with fewer than that, conduct yourself according to the master of pledges.[954] There is much explanation to be given on the specific pledges of the enlightened body, speech, and mind and on the supremacy of the peerless pledges, but this will suffice.

d.div: [515] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 10_shog_177_ba4

f.d: gzhan yang dpal mgon 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi bstan bcos las sbom po'i ltung ba brgyad bshad pa'i dang po/ shes rab stobs kyis len pa dang /[516] /zhes rig ma yongs su ma sbyangs par rang gi mthu'am stobs kyi dbang med du len pa/ gnyis pa/ de yi bdud rtsi stobs kyis len/ /zhes gong bshad rig ma'i bdud rtsi stobs kyis len pa/ gsum pa/ snod min la ni mi gsang dang / /zhes dbang ma thob pa dang / dad pa med pa'i snod min la bris sku glegs bam rgyan drug sogs gsang rdzas rnams ston pa/ bzhi pa/ tshogs kyi nang du rtsod pa dang / /zhes tshogs 'khor ram dpa' bo pho mo'i dga' ston gyi dus rtsod pa/ lnga pa/ dad ldan la gzhan chos ston dang / /zhes dper na don dam pa'i mtshan nyid 'dri ba la kun rdzob kyi mtshan nyid ston pa lta bu/ drug pa/ nyan thos nang du zhag bdun gnas/ /zhes gsang sngags sun 'byin byed pa'i nyan thos kyi nang du zhag bdun phan chad gnas pa/ bdun pa/ brdzun gyis rnal 'byor nga rgyal byed/ /ces lha'i sgrub thabs tsam zhig la brten nas de kho na nyid shes par nga rgyal gyis gnas shing ston pa/ brgyad pa/ dad pa med la chos ston pa/ /zhes dbang gis ma smin pa'i sngags la mi dad pa la dbang bskur ba'am phyi'i chos la mos par sngags kyi gsang ba ston pa rnams sbom po'i ltung ba yin la/

These are taught in the works of the glorious guide, Ācārya Nāgārjuna.[955] 1. “Taking wisdom by force” is to take by force a consort not fully trained. 2. “Taking her ambrosia by force” is to take the ambrosia of the above by force. 3. “Not keeping the secrets from unsuitable vessels” is to show paintings, statues, texts, the six types of tantric ornaments, and so on to unsuitable vessels, such as those who have not received the empowerment and those who have no faith. 4. “Fighting during the ceremonial feast” is to quarrel or fight during the gaṇacakra feast or festivities of heroes and heroines. 5. “Showing another Dharma to those with faith” means, for example, teaching conventional truths to those who ask about the meaning of the ultimate truth. 6. “Staying seven days with a śrāvaka” means staying for seven days or more in the house of a śrāvaka who rejects and has contempt for secret mantra. 7. “Falsely having the pride of being a yogi” means to have and to teach with great conceit knowledge of reality merely by relying on a deity sādhana. 8. “Teaching Dharma to those with no faith” means giving empowerment to those who are not ripened by empowerment and lack faith in mantra, or to teach the secrets of mantra to those attracted to non-Buddhist Dharma. These are the eight serious downfalls.

d.div: [516] sde dge_2482_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ zi_mgon po klu sgrub/ rdo rje theg pa'i sbom po'i ltung ba/ shog_180_ba1
[955] Gross Downfalls in the Vajrayana (Vajrayānasthūlāpatti), Toh 2482 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, zi, 180b1.

f.d: nyams par gyur na bshags par bya/[517] /zhes gsungs pa mi shes pa sogs kyi dbang gi nyams na cho ga bzhin du bshags par bya'o// de ltar dam tshig dang sdom pa la tshul bzhin gnas pas rab tshe 'di/ 'bring bar do/ / tha ma skye ba bdun nam/ bcu drug tshun la sangs rgya bas na/

“If they degenerate, undertake confession.”[956] Therefore, if these vows are broken through ignorance and so on, undertake the confession practices according to the procedures. Dwelling purely in the vows and pledges means that at best you will become a buddha in this life; if not, then in the intermediate state; and at the very least within seven lives or sixteen lives.

d.div: [517] gong mtshungs/ shog_180_ba1

f.d:
'jam mgon chos kyi rgyal po btsong kha pas/
shin du phrad dka' gong na med pa'i lam/ / 'di 'dra yal bar 'dor ba kye ma'o mtshar/ / de nyid phyir na rgyal ba'i theg pa mchog / sangs rgyas las kyang dkon pa'i rdo rje theg / dngos grub gnyis kyi gter gyur zab mo der/ / zhugs nas 'bad pa chen pos ring du sbyangs/[518] / zhes dang /
thub pa'i legs bshad kun gyi mthar thug pa/ / dpal ldan rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud/[519] / ces sogs rgya cher bsngags pa dang / rgyu mtshan nyid kyi theg pa las 'bras bu sngags kyi theg pa khyad par 'phags tshul rgyud sde rin po che du ma dang rgya gar gyi paN grub du mas gsungs pa gzhan du rgya cher bshad pa ltar yin la/ phal skad khe che sar nyen gyi dpe bzhin sdom pa gsum gyi nang nas bsrung sdom kyang sngags kho na ches dka' ba ni/

The Vajrayana has been extensively praised. Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa says, for example:
So hard to find, this peerless path; to discard it, how extraordinary! Therefore, enter this profound path, the Conqueror’s supreme vehicle, the Vajrayana, rarer than the Buddha himself, a treasure source of the two siddhis, and practice with determination for a long time.[957] Also:
Ultimate teaching of the mighty[958] Buddha, the glorious highest yoga tantra. The manner in which the resultant mantra vehicle is superior to the causal vehicle is taught in several precious tantras and propounded by many Indian scholar practitioners, and has been extensively dealt with elsewhere. Nevertheless, as the saying goes, where there is great profit there is great danger, and of the three vows, those of mantra are the hardest to guard and keep.

d.div: [518] rje tsong kha pa chen po'i gsung 'bum/ kha gsung thor bu/ rtogs brjod mdun legs ma/ skabs/ 1_shog_53_ba1
[519] rje tsong kha pa chen po'i gsung 'bum/ kha gsung thor bu/ rtogs brjod mdun legs ma/ skabs dang po/ shog_54_ba4
[957] Song of Realization, chap. 1, Collected Works, kha, 53b1.

f.d:
bdag nyid chen po dI pAM ka ras pha chos thor bur/
so so thar ba'i sdom pa la nyes pas gtan nas ma gos pa byar rung / byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa nyes pa co le tsam gyis gos/ gsang sngags kyi dam tshig la nyes pa ca re nya re brgyab ste nyes pa dang zhag tu 'grogs ma myong /[520] zhes gsungs pas go nus pa bzhin 'di la gzab par bya'o//

The great being [Atiśa] Dīpaṃkara said in the miscellaneous section of the Book of Kadam: Father Teachings:
I am never tainted by faults in my pratimokṣa vows. However, I have been tainted by one or two small faults in my bodhisattva commitments. In my tantric vows, faults occur constantly, but these faults have never accompanied me for more than a day.[959] Therefore, as can be clearly understood, we should be very careful.

d.div: [520] bka' gdams pha chos/ jo bo rje dpal ldan a ti sha'i rnam thar rgyas pa yongs grags/ shog_92_phreng 5
[959] Book of Kadam: Father Teachings (in “Extensive Biography of Glorious Atiśa”), 92.5.

f.d: sdom gsum gnas 'gyur yin min gyi khyad par/
24. Changes in Vow Status and the Preceptor Question

d.i: Changes in the status of the three vows

f.d:
de lta bu'i sdom pa gsum po de gsum ldan rdo rje 'dzin par 'gyur mi 'gyur rang gi gnas 'gyur mi 'gyur sogs la bshad khungs mang du yod pa'i thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa gnyis las/ thun mong ba'i lugs su/ sa bzang ma ti paN chen gyis/
mngon pa mdzod las/ tha dad de dag 'gal ba med/[521] /ces gsungs pa ltar sdom pa gsum po de dag na gang zig gcig gi rgyud la yod pa'i tshe na'ang tha dad kho nar yod de/ gzhan du na dge slong gi sdom pa btang bas gsum char gtong bar 'gyur ba las/ dge slong btang nas dge tshul dang de'ang btang nas dge bsnyen du 'gyur bar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang de dag 'gal ba med pas bstan pa la rim gyis zhugs pa'i dge slong gi rgyud la de gsum gyi rig byed ma yin pa rnams ni so sor yod ces so/[522] / zhes sogs dang /

There are many scriptural references on whether the three vows change their individual status[960] in the mindstream of vajra-holding tantric practitioner who possesses all three vows. These can be rendered into common and exclusive assertions. On the first Sasang Mati Paṇchen says:
The Abhidharmakośa says, “Separate, they are not mutually exclusive.” Therefore, even when they exist in the mindstream of a single person, these three vows are quite separate. Were it otherwise, when the vows of a fully ordained monk are given up, all three would be given up. However, it is taught that when the vows of a fully ordained monk are given up, one reverts to being a novice monk, and when these are given up, one possesses the vows of a lay upāsaka. Because they are not mutually exclusive, their nonrevelatory[961] aspects can exist individually in the mindstream of a fully ordained monk who has entered the doctrine in successive stages.[962]

d.div: [521] sde dge_4089_bstan/ mngon pa/ ku dbyig gnyen/ chos mngon pa mdzod/ gnas/ 4_sh+loka14_shog_11_na7
[522] sa bzang ma ti paN chen gyi gsung 'di gang las drangs ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[960] Gnas ’gyur ba.
[961] Rnam par rig byed ma yin pa. The pratimokṣa vows are nonrevelatory because they are conceptualized forms known only by the mental consciousness that conceptualizes them.
[962] Untraced.

f.d:
mkhas mchog bu ston rin po che/
'o na gang zag gis sdom pa rim can du blangs pa na/ spong ba'i 'phel ba dang ldan par dge bsnyen gyi lnga'i steng du dge tshul gyi lhag po lnga bsnan pas bcur song ba lta bu yin/ 'o na thams cad tha dad ce na/ dong tse brtsegs pa ltar rdzas tha dad ma 'dres par yod de/ srog gcod spong ba gsum nas chang spong ba gsum gyi bar mtshan nyid tha dad pa skye ste/ lhag ma gar sogs spong ba'ang de dang 'dra'o/ / 'o na khyad par ci yod ce na/ gzhi'i khyad par las khyad yod de/ bslab pa'i gzhi chos mang po dag len par 'dod pa ste de ltar rgyags pa dang bag med pa'i gnas chen po mang po las log pa dang / srog gcod pa la sogs pa'i gzhi dus ma yin pa'i kha zas la sogs pa las log par 'gyur ba dang / spong ba'i gzhi rnams la yang 'jug par 'gyur pa'i khyad yod do/[523] / zhes sogs dang /

The great scholar Butön Rinpoché says:
However, when a person takes the vows in successive stages, he increases his renunciation by adding, for example, the five remaining vows of a novice monk to the five lay upāsaka vows to make ten. Are they all separate? Like stacking coins on top of each other, they are substantially different and distinct from each other—the three vows of renouncing killing up to the three vows of renouncing alcohol are produced with distinct characteristics, and it is the same with renouncing singing and dancing and so on. So what are these differences? Differences exist because the bases are different. The wish to take on many different bases of commitment involves turning away from many different areas of pride and negligence. Also the basis of, say, killing is different from the basis of, say, eating at the wrong times. There are also differences in the way you engage in the various foundations of restraint.[963]

d.div: [523] bu ston rin chen grub kyi gsung 'bum/ zha 'dul ba mdo'i rnam par 'byed pa 'dul ba rgya mtsho'i snying po rab tu gsal bar byed pa/ shog_7_na7
[963] Analysis of the Vinaya Sutra: Elucidation of the Essence of the Ocean of Vinaya, Collected Works, zha, 7a7.

f.d:
mngon pa'i 'grel pa rgyan las/
dge bsnyen la sogs pa'i sdom pa de dag tha dad pa yin gyi snga ma snga ma gnas 'gyur ba phyi ma phyi ma'am gcig tu yod pa ni ma yin te/[524] zhes sogs dang /

[Chim Jampaiyang’s] Ornament to Commentary on Abhidharmakośa says:
The vows of the upāsaka and so forth all remain separate. The former do not transform into the latter, nor do they all become one.[964]

d.div: [524] mchims 'jam pa'i dbyangs/ chos mngon pa mdzod kyi 'grel ba mngon pa'i rgyan/ gnas/ 4_shog_195_ba4
[964] Chim Jampaiyang, Ornament to Commentary on Abhidharmakośa, chap. 4, 195b4.

f.d:
mkhas grub rin po che dge legs dpal ba'i sdom gsum rnam gzhag thub bstan byi dor las/
gzhan lugs rnams bkag nas/ 'thad pa'i phyogs ni 'di yin te/ sdom pa gsum ldan gyi gang zag gcig gi rgyud kyi sdom gsum rang rang gi thog ma'i rgyu tshogs/ tshogs pa ris mi mthun gyi cho ga rigs tha dad las skyes pa'i thob tshul so sor nges shing / de'i dbang gis mthar gtong ba'i rgyu yang so sor nges pa yin/ 'on kyang gnas skabs su sdom pa 'og ma bsrung ba yang gong ma'i kun slong khyad par can gyi zin pa'i rkyen gyi gnas skabs kyi rkyen de dang ma bral gyi ring la 'og ma yang gong ma'i yan lag tu 'gyur ba yin gyi/ grub sde dbyer med dang rigs rgyun phan tshun gcig bkag na cig shos khegs pa'i yan lag tu 'gyur ba ma yin te/ dper na snod shin tu dwangs shing dri ma med par chu shin tu dwangs pa'i nang du rin po che mar gad la sogs pa bcug na de srid du chu'i mdog kyang rin po che'i kha dog gis yan lag tu 'gyur mod kyi/ chu dang rin po che de dag phan tshun gcig bkag kyang cig shos mi khegs pa bzhin no/[525] / zhes sogs gsungs pa

In his Broom of the Buddha’s Precious Doctrine: A Brief Presentation on the Three Sets of Vows, Khedrup Rinpoché Gelek Palsangpo, having refuted the views of others, says:
The correct view is as follows. The development of the three vows in the mindstream of one person requires three separate processes, constituting the initial collections of causes in the form of three distinct ceremonies. Because of this, the causes for giving up these sets of vows must also be individual. However, in between these times, guarding a lower vow becomes a causal condition for the higher vows to be held by a special motivating force, and for as long as that condition is present, the lower vows are a branch of the higher vows. However, this is not a case of these two being substantially the same or of sharing a mutual type or mutual continuum, in which one would disappear if the other were taken away. For example, if a jewel such as an emerald were placed in clear water in a clear and clean receptacle, the color of the water becomes part of the color of the jewel, but removal of either the jewel or the water would not remove the other.[965]

d.div: [525] mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang gi gsung 'bum/ nya sdom gsum rnam gzhag thub bstan byi dor/ shog_121_na1
[965] Collected Works, nya, 121a1.

f.d: 'og ma gnyis med na gong ma'i yan lag mi tshang ba'i skyon dang / gong ma'i thob byed kyi cho ga las 'og ma gnyis kyang thob dgos pa 'dra zhig 'dug ste/ thugs rig gi dgongs pa khyad par can yod pa gzhir bcas/ gzhan yang so thar dge slong gi dngos po bsgrub zin zhig la ma gtogs byang sdom mtshan nyid ldan pa mi tshang ba lta bu dang /

This means that, without the two lower vows, the higher vows suffer the fault of not having all parts complete. There are also statements that seem to say that the two lower sets of vows are necessarily taken within the ceremony creating the higher vows. These statements are made on the basis of a special intention of the author. Furthermore, there are assertions that state, for example, that the true bodhisattva vows are only made complete on the basis of already being a fully ordained pratimokṣa monk.

dus kyi 'khor lo rtsa rgyud las/
sa thob ma gtogs khyim pas ni/ / rgyal po'i bla ma mi bya ste/ / de las thos pa yongs shes pas/ / gang zhig rtags can bya ba nyid/[526] / ces sogs la brten/ so thar dge slong dang mi ldan pa'i bshes gnyen la slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid mi tshang ba'i shes byed mang du byung kyang /

Many scriptural sources also state that the qualification of a true vajra master is incomplete within a spiritual friend without the pratimokṣa of a fully ordained monk. For example, the Kālacakra Root Tantra states:
Except for those on ārya levels, householders should not be gurus of kings. Of those whose learning is complete, who possess the signs…[966]

d.div: [526] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_dus 'khor rtsa rgyud/(pad+ma dkar po/ 'grel chen dri med 'od/) le'u/ 4_shog_262_na4
[966] Puṇḍarīka, Stainless Light Great Commentary (Vimalaprabhā), chap. 4, Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 262a4.

f.d:
bdag gi bla ma nges pa don gyi thams cad mkhyen pa ngag dbang blo bzang rgya mtsho'i las chog rnam rgyal gser mdog tu/
mkhas pa rnams kyi grub mtha'i 'jog mtshams la blo dman rnams kyi mtha' gcig tu nges bzung dka' na'ang / gnya' nang brag phug gi rgyus mi la ras pa'i dpe bzhin nyan thos lugs ltar so thar blangs pa'i gdul bya so skye las dang po pa rnams kyi skal ba dang 'tsham pa ni/ lugs srol 'di la kha che'i bsod snyoms pa chen po brgyud par bcas pa mkhas pas/ paN chen shAkya shrI dang bi b+hu ti tsan+d+ras sdom gsum rdzas tha dad du bzhed cing / bi b+hu ti tsan+d+ras/
mkhyen brtse dung 'phyur dang ldan zhing / / paN chen blo yi rgya mtsho mtsho las/ / sdom gsum nor bu'i 'phreng ba blangs/[527] / zhes paN chen gyi dgongs pa ltar sdom gsum rdzas tha dad du ston pa'i 'od 'phreng mdzad cing der/
des na rig 'dzin gcig pu la/ / gsum ldan sbyor ba 'thad ma yin/ / gal te 'thad na 'og ma gnyis/ / cho ga mi dgos skye bar 'gyur/ /
sdom gsum cho ga thun mong du/ / thub pa chen pos gsungs pa med/ / rig 'dzin sdom pa kho na bas/ / gsum ldan bsngags pa'i dgongs pa ni/ / 'bras bu'i sgo nas ma yin te/ / yin na kun mkhyen mchog dman 'gyur/[528] /zhes sogs gsungs pa'i don/

However, my guru the Great Fifth, in reality the omniscient one, states in his Golden Victorious Myrobalan Vinaya Ceremonies:
For those of lesser minds, the boundaries of the tenets of the great scholars are hard to ascertain. Nevertheless, like Milarepa knowing his own cave in Nyanang, in keeping with the merit of beginner disciples who take pratimokṣa according to the śrāvaka tradition, Paṇchen Śākyaśrī and Vibhūticandra, who are learned in this tradition and belong to the lineage of the great alms-seekers of Kashmir, maintain that the three vows are separate in terms of substance.[967] Vibhūticandra says:
From the ocean of the Paṇchen’s mind, with its vast wisdom and compassion, I have taken this garland of jewels on the three vows.[968] Therefore, Vibhūticandra composed Garland of Light on the Three Vows, in which the three vows are taught as being separate in substance, in accordance with the thinking of Paṇchen. In it he says:
Therefore, to say the union of all three exists in the vidyādhara vows alone is not correct. If it were, the lower two would be produced without need of the ceremony.
A common ceremony for all three vows the mighty Buddha did not teach. The thought behind the praise that by vidyādhara vows alone, one comes to possesses all three, is not from the resultant point of view. If it were, omniscience would be of supreme and inferior types.[969]

d.div: [527] sde dge_3727_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshu slob dpon bi b+hU ti tsan+d+ra/ sdom gsum 'od kyi phreng ba/ shog_56_ba6

[528] sde dge_3727_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshu slob dpon bi b+hU ti tsan+d+ra/ sdom gsum 'od kyi phreng ba/ shog_56_na4_de bzhin du rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ pha bstan pa'i rtsa ba rab byung dang khyim pa la phan gdags pa'i las kyi cho ga mtha' dpyod dang bcas pa 'khrul spong rnam rgyal gser mdog_shog_82_ba4
[967] Rdzas tha dad.
[968] Garland of Light on the Three Vows (Trisaṃvaraprabhāmālā), Toh 3727 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 56b6.
[969] Ibid., 56a4. Quotes together with the commentary found in Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Golden Victorious Myrobalan Vinaya Ceremonies, Collected Works, pha, 82b4.

f.d: so skye gcig gi rgyud kyi sdom gsum rdzas tha dad de/ sdom gsum phyi ma skye ba snga ma snga ma skyes zin rten du dgos pas skye ba'i dus tha dad/ so thar ji srid 'tsho'i bar dang gzhan gnyis sangs rgyas ma thob bar yin pas gnas dus tha dad/ so thar tshe 'phos pas gtong zhing phyis ma gnyis mi gtong bas rgyu tha dad cing sangs rgyas kyi dkor kun dkris chen pos phrogs na byang sems kyi sdom pa 'jig kyang so thar la de ltar ma yin pa dang / kun nas 'khrugs pas bud med la smad na sngags sdom 'jig kyang so thar la pham par mi 'gyur/ sha chang bdud rtsi lnga sogs dam tshig gi rdzas zhe nas spong na sngags kyi rtsa ltung bcu gsum par 'gyur kyang / so thar gyi de spang bya yin pa sogs kyi phyir sdom gsum rdzas tha dad pa dang / nam mkha' la nyi zla skar gsum dus gcig tu shar tshe gzhan gnyis med pa min kyang nyi ma'i 'od kyis zil gyis mnan nas bag la zha ba bzhin du sngags sdom gyis byang sems so thar zil gyis gnon pa dang / de'i shugs la so thar gyi tshigs gsum gang zag gcig gi rgyud la so sor yod kyang bsnyen rdzogs kyi sdom pa gtso che bas gzhan gnyis dngos su mi mngon kyang / snod gcig tu chu chang 'o ma gsum rim gyis bsres tshe chang gi dri dang 'o ma'i mdog sogs mngon che rung de la chu med par sgrub mi nus pa lta bu nas/

The three vows in the mindstream of an ordinary being are substantially different from each other. The creation of the higher vows requires the previously created foundation of the lower vows, and therefore the three vows have different times of creation. The pratimokṣa vows dissolve at death while the other two are not lost, therefore they possess different causes for their dissolution. If you steal the possessions of the Three Jewels and your action is accompanied by the complete binding factors, your bodhisattva vows are destroyed, but that is not true of your pratimokṣa vows. Despising women out of great affliction breaks a tantric vow, but it does not incur a defeat in pratimokṣa. Feeling repulsion for and refusing pledge substances such as meat, alcohol, and the five nectars is to incur the thirteenth root downfall of the tantric vows, but such acts are to be abandoned in pratimokṣa. Therefore, the three vows are different in terms of substance. When the sun, moon, and stars are all present in the sky, the latter two are outshone by the sun and remain unseen, even though they are not nonexistent. In a similar way the pratimokṣa and bodhisattva vows are outshone by the tantric vows. From this it can be inferred that the three parts of the pratimokṣa existing in one person are separate but that the full monastic vows predominate with the other two remaining not evident. They are not nonexistent, just as when water, alcohol, and milk are poured one after the other into a single bowl; the smell of the alcohol and the color of the milk predominate, but this does not prove the absence of water. Similarly,

'od 'phreng las/
dang po de ni kun gzhi la/ / bag la nyal ba'i tshul du gnas/ / rig 'dzin sdom pa thob pa na/ / 'og ma gnyis ka bag la nyal/ / dper na mkha' la skar ma shar/ / cung zad snang bar byas 'gyur mod/ / zla ba'i dkyil 'khor shar ba'i tshe/ / skar 'od nyams mdo 'jig rten gsal/ / rta bdun tsha zer byung ba na/ / zla ba'i 'od nyams 'jig rten gsal/[529] / zhes snga ma snga ma phra zhing phyi ma rags par gsungs pa'i don ltar rje bla ma'ang bzhed/

the Garland of Light on the Three Vows says:
When one endowed with the pratimokṣa takes those of the bodhisattva,[970] the first remains unseen in the foundation consciousness. Having taken the vows of the vidyādhara, the lower two remain unseen. For example when the stars appear in the sky they shine with a little light, but when the face of the moon rises, the world is lit and the stars’ light fades. In turn, when the seven horses of the blazing sun appear, the world is bright and the moon’s light dims.[971] Therefore, the lower the vow the fainter it becomes. The higher the vow the stronger it is. This is also the position of my great guru.

d.div: [529] sde dge_3727_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshu_slob dpon bi b+hU ti tsin+d+ra/ sdom gsum 'od kyi phreng ba/ shog_55_ba4
[970] I have added the two previous lines as found in the Degé Tengyur edition here to give reference to the next line beginning, “the first….”
[971] Vibhūticandra, Trisaṃvaraprabhāmālā, Toh 3727 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 55b4.

f.d:
gsang sngags snga 'gyur las kyang rtsa rgyud gsang ba snying po las/
bla med mchog gi dam tshig tu/ / 'dul ba'i dbang gis tshul khrims dang / / ji snyed sdom pa bsam yas pa/ / ma lus kun 'dus rnam par dag[530] / ces pa'i gsum ldan rdo rje 'dzin pa'i rgyud kyi sdom pa gsum ngo bo tshang zhing gnas 'gyur ba ste so thar byang sdom de gnyis sngags sdom du gnas 'gyur ba'i phyir/

In the Essence of Secrets Tantra the early translation school also says:
The ethics of the might of the Vinaya and its inconceivable vows are all complete and pure in the pledges of the supreme and peerless.[972] Therefore, in the mindstream of a three-vow vajra-holding tantric practitioner the three vows are complete and yet have changed their status. This is because the pratimokṣa and bodhisattva vows have transformed into tantric vows.

d.div: [530] sde dge_832_bka'/ rnying rgyud/ kha dpal gsang ba'i snying po de kho na nyid rnam par nges pa/ le'u/ 19_shog_129_ba6
[972] Guhyagarbhatantra, chap. 19, Toh 832 Kangyur, rnying rgyud, kha, 129b6.

f.d: 'gyur tshul ni/ so thar dang byang sdom gnyis la mnyam pa chen po'i thabs kyis ma zin pa'i snang zhen gyi ldog cha re yod pa de rtsa ba nas btang nas so thar gzhan gnod zhi bcas kyi cha dang / byang sdom gyi gzhan la phan zhugs pa'i ldog cha gnyis po de sngags sdom mnyam pa chen po'i ngang nas gzhan don 'bad rtsol med pa byed pa'i thabs mkhas kyi nang du tshang zhing / rdzas gong 'phel gyi tshul gyi sngags sdom rdzas su gnas 'gyur bar bshad/

They way they change is as follows. The clinging to appearances aspect of the pratimokṣa and bodhisattva vows, which is not held in the approach of the great equalizing wisdom, is completely given up.
