de la dang po blo dang ldan pa ni/ / blo che blo brtan blo gzeg gsum ldan pas/ / gso dpyad mdo rgyas ma lus khong du chud/ / lag len kun la thogs brdugs nyam nga med/ / rig pas dpyod shes mngon shes phra mo 'char/ / de nyid rgyu yi nang nas mchog ces bya/[575] / zhes sman pa mkhas pa'i rgyu drug po de las dang po blo dang ldan pa zhes pa ni/ spyir blo zhes chos rab tu rnam par 'byed pa'i shes rab la bya'i blo gros zhes kyang yongs su grags pas gtsug lag mtha' dag gi don khong du chud nus pa'i blo che ba dang / rkyen gang gis kyang bskyod mi nus pa'i blo brtan pa dang / gang la'ang brtag dpyad sngon du gtong ba'i blo gzeg pa ste 'di gsum dang yang dag par ldan pa'i sgo nas nad gso bar byed pa'i dpyad gtso bor gyur pa'i gzhung lugs mdor bsdus dang rgyas bshad kyi don ma lus pa khong du chud pa la brten nas nyams su blang bar 'os pa'i lag tu len 'os kun la mi shes pas thogs pa dang rdugs pa mi nus pa'i nyam nga bag tsha la sogs pa med par bde blag tu 'jug pa dang / gzhung nas ma bshad pa'i don rnams la'ang rig pa dri ma med pas dpyod shes pa'i mngon par shes pa lta bu phra mo gang la gang 'tsham par 'char ba de nyid ni rgyu drug po rnams kyi nang nas mchog dam pa yin la/

Now the extensive explanation:
Possessed of great intellect, stable, and careful, he comprehends all healing practices, extensive and brief; in all procedures he fears no hindrance, and with his wisdom a subtle clairvoyant discernment arises. This is the most important of the causes.[1029] The first of the six causes is intelligence. Generally the term “intellect” (blo) refers to a wisdom capable of great discernment and analysis, though the term “intelligence” (blo gros) is more widely used. Therefore, a doctor has a great intellect capable of comprehending all the scriptures. It is not distracted by extraneous circumstances and is therefore a stable intellect. It is careful because it proceeds in all matters by way of prior examination. With genuine possession of these three qualities, a doctor comprehends the meanings of all the short and extensive texts that primarily explain practices for healing. With this learning he does not have the fear and apprehension of being hindered or obstructed by a lack of knowledge, and he undertakes with ease every medical practice the occasion calls for. Even with those practices not taught in the scriptures, because of his untainted wisdom, he has a subtle clairvoyance-like discernment that arises appropriately for the occasion. Of all the six causes, this intelligence is the most important.

d.div: [575] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_96_yig phreng 2

f.d: bsam pa dkar ba byang chub sems ldan pa/ / sbyor ba dngos gzhi mjug las dang po ni/ / sdug bsngal mthong dang phan 'dogs dad pa dang / / bzang ngan byams sdang zhe nas snyoms pa yis/ / snying rje byams pa dga' ba btang snyoms bzhi/ / smon pa byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed de/ / dngos gzhi 'jug pa tshad med nyams su blang / / 'jug pa bsngags par blta zhing khon 'dzin med/ / de ldan gso sla 'tsho mang grogs su 'gyur/[576] / zhes pa ni 'gro ba sems can mtha' dag la pha mar 'du shes pa'i byang chub kyi sems dang ldan pa zhig ste/

A virtuous mind means possessing bodhicitta— its preparatory, actual, and subsequent practices. The first is seeing the suffering, wanting to help, developing faith, having firm equanimity toward the good and bad, the loved and the hated, with compassion, love, joy, and equanimity, and generating the yearning bodhicitta. To engage in actual practice is to practice without limits. Subsequent practice is to hold in esteem without resentment, which makes your curing easier, allowing you to become a support to the lives of many.[1030] The second cause is to be endowed with the bodhicitta that recognizes all living beings as your parents.

d.div: [576] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_96_yig phreng 4

f.d: don 'di la sbyor ba dngos gzhi dang mjug gsum las/ dang po bsam sbyor ni khams gsum po 'di sdug bsngal gyi rang bzhin 'ba' zhig tu mthong ba dang / pha mar ma gyur ba med pa'i sems can thams cad la phan 'dogs 'dod kyi blo rgyun chags pa dang / dkon cog gsum po la mi bslu ba'i skyabs kyi dad pa dang / gser dang bong ba la bzang ngan dang dgra gnyen byams sdang sogs zhe thag pa nas mnyam pa'i sgo nas ngan 'gro'i sdug bsngal mi bzod pa'i snying rje dang 'gro ba la bu gcig pa'i ma ltar brtse ba'i byams pa dang / gang dag sdug bsngal dang bral ba la dga' ba dang / nye ring chags sdang thams cad dang bral ba'i btang snyoms la gnas pa ste tshangs pa'i gnas bzhi la gnas par byas nas/ sems can thams cad kyi don du rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par smon pa byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed de/ de nas dngos gzhi gzhan phan 'ba' zhig la 'jug pa dus dang grangs 'di dang 'di rnams tshad dang ris med par nyams su blang bar bya zhing / de ltar byed pa'i mjug tu yang ni gso dpyad kyi don la bsngags par blta zhing nad pa sogs su la'ang 'khon 'dzin med pa'i lhag bsam de lta bu dang ldan na gang lta ba'i nad pa rnams gso sla zhing 'tsho ba shin tu mang po 'byung ba'i grogs su 'gyur ba zhig dgos pa yin la/

As a topic it is divided into preparatory, actual, and subsequent practices. The preparatory practices of attitude are seeing these three realms as nothing but suffering, developing a sustained state of mind that wishes to help all living creatures—none of which have not been your parents—having a faith in the Three Jewels as the unfailing refuges, and from the depths of your being having a mind of equanimity toward the good and the bad such as gold and clods of earth, toward the loved and the hated such as friends and enemies, and so on. From this attitude you abide in the compassion that cannot bear the suffering of the lower realms, the love that regards living beings as a mother would regard her only child, the joy of seeing any being freed from suffering, and the equanimity of being divorced from all attachment and aversion. These four are known as dwelling in the four realms of Brahmā. Then comes the generation of the mind of supreme enlightenment that yearns to attain the state of a buddha for the sake of all sentient beings. The actual practice is to work solely for the benefit of others and, in terms of time and number, to practice without limits and without partiality. Subsequently, if you hold the practice of medicine in high esteem and treat the sick with an exceptional state of mind that carries no resentment for any patient whatsoever, your patients become easier to cure, and you become a support for many lives.
dam tshig ni/

d.div: dam tshig ldan pa blo bzhag rnam pa drug / gzung bya gnyis dang shes bya gsum du bshad/ /

dang po slob dpon gsung dang gso dpyad dang / / mched dang nad pa rnag khrag rnam drug la/ / sangs rgyas drang srong gsung dang bka' brgyud dang / / grogs spun bu tsha khyi phag lta bur ni/ / blo bzhag pa yi dam tshig drug bsrung bya/ /
gnyis pa sman gyi rig 'dzin cha byad rnams/ / bka' srung phyag cha lta bur bzung zhing bsrung / /
gsum pa sman rnams nor bu bdud rtsi dang / / mchod rdzas shes par bya ba gsum yin te/ / dgos 'dod 'byung ba'i nor bur shes par bya/[577] /
Of the pledges, six to keep in the mind, two to hold, and three to know.

In the first are those of the master, speech, medical literature, your brothers, patients, and pus and blood. These are like the Buddha, the rishis’ speech, the transmission of enlightened speech, friends and brothers, children, and dogs and pigs, these six pledges of the mind to be guarded.
For the second, the medicine vidyādharas and their instruments, hold them as oath-bearing protectors and their implements.

Medicines like gems, ambrosia, and offering substances— these are the three recognitions; they are gems fulfilling needs and desires, ambrosia curing all disease, and the ritual food offerings for the vidyādhara.[1031]
[577] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_96_yig phreng 9
[1031] Ibid., 31.96.9. These last two lines are omitted in both editions of the text, but because they are commented on later, I have inserted them as found in Four Tantras.

f.d: zhes dam tshig dang ldan pa ni blo bzhag rnam pa drug dang gzung bya gnyis dang shes par bya ba gsum du bshad de/ dam tshig gsum gyi dang po ni rang gi slob dpon dang de'i gsung dang gso dpyad kyi gzhung dang rang gi grogs mched dang nad pa dang nad pa'i rnag khrag ste rnam pa drug la rim pa bzhin du sangs rgyas dngos dang drang srong gi gsung dang rgyal ba'i bka' dngos kyi rgyud dang / rdo rje'i spun grogs dang bu tsha dang khyi phag gi spyod pa lta bur ni blo bzhag pa'i dam tshig drug bsrung zhing / gzung bya gnyis pa ni sman gyi rig pa 'dzin pa'i drang srong rnams dang btsag bu la sogs pa'i cha byad rnams la rim pa ltar sman gyi bka' srung dang de'i phyag cha lta bur bzung zhing bsrung /

“Keeping the pledges” refers to six to be kept in the mind, two to be held, and three to be known. Concerning the first of these three sets, the six refer to your master, his words, medical literature, your brother-like companions, patients, and the blood and pus of patients. These six are to be kept in the mind and guarded as being, respectively, the actual Buddha, the speech of the rishis, the actual tantra as the speech of the Conqueror, your vajra brothers, children, and as objects that engender the behavior of dogs and pigs.[1032] The two pledges to be held concern the vidyādhara medicine rishis and their instruments—the bloodletting funnel, and so on. These should be regarded as pledged protectors of medical science and their implements, respectively.

d.div: [1032] The doctor should not be squeamish or repulsed by blood and pus but regard them as dogs and pigs would.

f.d: dam tshig gsum pa ni sman thams cad nor bu dang bdud rtsi dang mchod pa'i rdzas su shes par bya ba dang rnam pa gsum yin te/ de yang sman la brten nas dgos 'dod thams cad shugs la 'byung bas yid bzhin gyi nor bur shes par bya ba dang / des nad rnams bde blag tu sel bar byed pas 'chi med kyis bdud rtsir shes par bya ba dang / sman de legs par sbyar ba'i phud kyis rig pa 'dzin pa'i drang srong rnams mchod pas mchod rdzas su shes par bya ba rnams yin la/ de dag rgyas bshad kyi lhar bsgom pa/ bstod pa bya ba/ shis brjod/ sngags bzla ba rnams gzhan du bshad pa ltar dang /

The third set of pledges is that all medicines should be recognized as gems, ambrosia, and offering substances. Indirectly, relying on medicine fulfills all your needs and desires, therefore, medicines should be regarded as wish-fulfilling jewels. Because they quickly and easily cure patients of their illnesses, they should be regarded as ambrosia. Medicines in the form of ritual food offerings[1033] please the vidyādhara rishis and are to be regarded as offering substances. The extensive explanation of this topic involving deity meditation, eulogies, prayers for auspiciousness, and mantra recitation has been dealt with elsewhere.

d.div: [1033] Phud. A term usually referring to a portion of food and drink separated out as an offering at the beginnings of meals, festivities, etc.

f.d: rnam pa bzo ba lus ngag yid dang gsum/ / lag pa bzo bas sman dpyad bzo la mkhas/ / ngag tshig snyan pas nad pa spro bskyed nus/ / rig pa bkra bas yid la ma rmongs gsal/ / de shes bzo rnams kun gyi dpon du 'gyur/[578] / zhes sman pa'i rgyu rnams kyi nang nas rnam pa bzo ba zhes pa la'ang lus bzo ba dang ngag bzo ba dang yid bzo ba dang gsum/ de la dang po lus kyi cha shas lag pa bzo bas sman dang dpyad kyi skabs su gce'u dang btsag cha dang 'gyogs khri bye tshe la sogs pa'i bzo la mkhas pa dang / ngag gi bzo tshig snyan zhing bzlos par mkhas pas nad pa spro ba bskyed nus pa dang / yid kyi bzo rig pa shin tu bkra bas na rtags dang sman dpyad sogs so sor yid la ma rmongs par gsal ba ste/ de rnams shes pa ni bzo rnams shes pa kun gyi dpon po ste mchog tu 'gyur ba yin la/

d.div: [578] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_97_yig phreng 14
[1034] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.97.14.

f.d: bya ba la brtson bdag dang gzhan gnyis te/ / bdag nyid bya ba brtson pa rgyu la bslab/ / rkyen bsten grogs la brtson bya goms mthar dbyung / / rgyu ni 'dri klog mtha' ru phyin par bslab/ / chod dang mi chod de la brten par snang /[579] / zhes sman pa'i rgyu bya ba la brtson pa zhes bya ba la'ang bdag gi bya ba la brtson pa dang / gzhan gyi bya ba la brtson pa gnyis te/

Effort in activities concerns yourself and others. For yourself this means training in the causes, devoting yourself to causal conditions, making effort with regard to your companions, and endeavoring to complete your development.[1035] Exerting yourself in work as a cause for becoming a doctor therefore involves: 1. Endeavor for yourself 2. Endeavor for others

d.div: [579] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_97_yig phreng 17

f.d: de la dang po bdag nyid kyi bya ba
['di ]la brtson pa la yang rgyu la bslab pa dang rkyen bsten pa dang grogs la brtson par bya ba dang goms pa mthar dbyung ba dang bzhis mdor bstan nas/

1. Training yourself in the basic causes 2. Devoting yourself to acquiring the necessary conditions 3. Endeavor with regard to your companions 4. Completing your development These four are presented in the verse in outline.

d.i: Training yourself in the basic causes

f.d:
shes par bya ba'i yon tan thams cad kyi rgyu ni yi ge 'bri ba dang klog pa rnam dag shes pa de nyid yin pas thog ma nyid du de dag mtha' ru phyin nges shes par slob dgos te/ de ci'i phyir na yon tan rgya che zhing 'chad rtsod rtsom pa la mkhas pa chod pa dang mi chod pa yi ge 'dri klog la gtso bor bsten zhing rag lus par snang ba'i phyir/ sum cu pa las/
bslab pa kun gyi gzhi 'dzin zhing / / rig byed smra ba rnams kyi rgyu/ / ming tshig brjod pa kun gyi gzhi/ / yi ge'i sbyor ba bshad par bya/[580] / zhes dang /
bslab pa'i rim pa 'di yis ni/ / gang zhing 'bad pa chung ngus kyang / / shes rab myur du grol bar 'gyur/ / de phyir dang por 'di nyid bslab/[581] / ces gsungs pa ltar dang /

The basic cause for all achievements in the field of knowledge is a good comprehension of writing and reading. Therefore, from the beginning you must complete and master these skills. Why? Because the line between having and not having great qualities, and being skilled and not skilled in teaching, composition, and debate, is determined primarily by ability in reading and writing. The Thirty Verses says:
The foundations of all training, the cause of the wise orator, the foundation for the expression of words, is explained as the construction of letters.[1036] Also:
With this order of study, even those of little effort will soon find wisdom; therefore begin your studies here.[1037]

d.div: [580] sde dge_4348_bstan/ sna tshogs/ co_slob dpon a nu/ lung ston pa'i rtsa ba sum cu pa zhes bya ba/ shog_160_ba2
[581] sde dge_4348_bstan/ sna tshogs/ co_slob dpon a nu/ lung ston pa'i rtsa ba sum cu pa zhes bya ba/ shog_161_ba2
[1036] Thönmi Sambhota, Vyākaraṇaliṅgāvataraṇa, Toh 4348 Tengyur, sna tshogs, co, 160b2.

f.d:
der ma zad bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen pos/
sgra tshad bzo gso nang rig snyan ngag dang / / mngon brjod sdeb sbyor zlos gar skar rtsis sogs/ / bslab byar 'os min 'ga' yang ma mchis pas/ / ngoms med thos pa'i sgro 'dogs chod par mdzod/[582] / ces bka' stsal pa ltar mkhas pa rnams 'jug pa'i sgo'i gtso bo'am thos bsam bya ba'i yul rig pa'i gnas chen lnga yan lag dang bcas pa'i bcu phrag gcig la sgro 'dogs chod pa zhig dgos la/

My own guru the Great Fifth also said:
Grammar, logic, crafts, medicine, Buddhism, poetry, lexicography, metrical composition, drama, astronomy— nothing is not worth studying. So without ever being satiated cut wrong notions about learning.[1038] It is important to sever all mistaken notions about the five major and five secondary fields of knowledge. For scholars these are the main gateways, or subjects of study and contemplation.

d.div: [582] rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ dza rgya bod hor sog gi mchog dman bar ma rnams la 'phrin yig snyan ngag tu bkod pa rab snyan rgyud mang / shog_26_na3
[1038] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Letters Arranged in Verse to Various Persons in China, Tibet, and Mongolia Containing Many Oral Transmissions, Collected Works, dza, 26a3.

f.d:
de yang mdo sde drin lan bsab pa las/
byang chub sems dpa' ci'i phyir sgra rig pa'i bstan bcos la slob ce na/ sgra'i tshig yongs su dag pas brgyan pa dang / yongs su ma dag pa'i tshig gis don gsal bar ston mi nus pa dang / don thams cad shes shing khong du chud par bya ba sogs pa'i phyir sgra'i bstan bcos la slob/[583] ces gsungs pa ltar/ gtso bo don thams cad shes shing khong du chud pa dang / rang dang gzhan gyi tshig dang don la 'khrul pa zhugs pa'i nyes pa thams cad drungs nas 'byin pa'i sgra rig pa ma shes na/ sman gyi sgra sbyor dang nges tshig la sogs pa ji bzhin mi rtogs shing / mkhas pa'i yan lag mi tshang /

The Sutra of Repaying the Kindness of the Skillful Buddha says:
Why should bodhisattvas study the great treatises on grammar? They will be adorned with accurate language, whereas with inaccurate language they will not be able to explain the meanings. Moreover, they will come to know and comprehend all topics. For these and other reasons they should study the treatises on grammar.[1039] Therefore, study of the science of grammar primarily brings knowledge and comprehension of all topics. It eradicates all errors of language and meaning that oneself and others fall into. If you do not know this science, you will similarly not understand the grammatical formations, etymologies, and so on found in medical literature, and you will be incomplete as a scholar.

d.div: [583] sde dge_353_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_sangs rgyas drin lan bsab pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_189_ba2
[1039] Chap. 9, Toh 353 Kangyur, mdo sde, ah, 189b2. Translated from the Chinese.

f.d:
mdo sde drin lan bsab pa las/
nyes pa'i skyon thams cad shes par bya ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung rab kyi don dang 'jig rten pa'i tshig gi don rnam par 'byed pa'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rgyu rig pa'i bstan bcos slob par byed de/[584] zhes dang /

The Sutra of Repaying the Kindness of the Skillful Buddha says:
Because one will come to know of all errors, and because one will be able to distinguish the words of the Tathāgata from the words of the worldly, the bodhisattva should study the treatises on reasoning.[1040]

d.div: [584] sde dge_353_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_sangs rgyas drin lan bsab pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_189_na7

f.d:
'jam mgon btsong kha pa chen pos/
log smra tshar gcod phyogs glang grags pa las/ / legs par 'ongs pa'i rigs lam bdud rtsi'i chus/ / blo mig dri ma yang yang ma bkrus na/ / shin tu zab gnas mthong ba smos ci dgos/ / rigs pa'i lung don la yang dpyod pa na/ / phal cher log par rtog pa 'phel 'gyur zhing / / gal te yang dag dam bca' tsam zhig gis/ / nges pa rnyed kyang sgrub dang sun 'byin gyi/ / tshad ma'i stobs kyis the tshom ma chod phyir/ / 'dam la btab pa'i phur pa bzhin 'gyur bas/ / yang dag bag chags brtan po 'jog mi nus/[585] / zhes gsungs pa ltar/

The great Mañjuśrī Tsongkhapa said:
If you do not wash the eyes of your mind again and again with the ambrosia waters of reasoning flowing from the great Dignāga, defeater of false orators, let alone not seeing the supremely profound, your misconceptions are likely to proliferate even when examining the meaning of lesser texts. Though you find conviction merely through correct affirmation, you will not be able to eliminate doubts through the power of valid perception that establishes and refutes.[1041] You become like a stake driven into mud— unable to secure any stable and valid imprints.[1042]

d.div: [585] rje tsong kha pa'i gsung 'bum/ kha gsung thor bu/ rin po che gsum gyi gtam gyi sbyor ba/ shog_58_na6
[1041] In other words, merely asserting and firmly believing that which is true is not enough to cut deep-seated doubts.
[1042] Words Composed on the Three Jewels, Collected Works, kha, 58a6.

f.d: don gyi cha la 'khrul pa zhugs pa mtha' dag tshar gcod cing lta ba ngan pa ma lus pa 'joms par byed pa rgyu rig pa'am tshad ma la mkhas par ma byas na bka' dang bstan bcos kyi don zab mo lta ci rigs pa'i lung don tsam la'ang yang dag pa'i bag chags brtan po 'jog mi nus shing log par rtog pa 'phel bar 'gyur ba dang /

If you do not become learned in the science of reasoning or valid perception, defeater of all those dwelling in errors of meaning and destroyer of all wrong views, then let alone not understanding the profound meanings of the teachings of the Buddha and the treatises, you will not even be able to develop any stable and valid imprints concerning the meanings of coarser scriptures, and meanwhile your misunderstandings will increase.

lnga pa chen pos/
sbyor sde'i 'khor lo tsha bsil snyoms pa'i rtsibs/ / stong phrag rig pa'i 'phrul gyi rno ba'i dpal/ / nad kyi dra ba gcod pa'i gso rig gzhung / / lus can kun gyi nyer 'tsho 'di rmad byung /[586] / zhes gsungs pa bzhi brgya rtsa bzhi'i nad do cog gi gnyen po rgas med ring por 'tsho ba'i bdud rtsi 'chi gsos kyi rig pa ni gzhung 'di'i brjod bya dang bslab par bya ba'i gtso bo yin pas smos ma dgos la/

The Great Fifth said:
This great wheel of the compounding of medicine, with its spokes of heat and cold finely balanced, glorious magical blades of a thousandfold knowledge, cutting through the nets of disease for the health of all living creatures— how amazing![1043] This death-destroying, ambrosia-like science that grants longevity without old age, and is the antidote to all 404 types of disease, is the main topic and practice of this work. Therefore, there is no need to dwell on it here. Also:

d.div: [586] rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ dza rgya bod hor sog gi mchog dman bar ma rnams la 'phrin yig snyan ngag tu bkod pa rab snyan rgyud mang / shog_58_na2
[1043] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Letters Arranged in Verse, Collected Works, dza, 58a2.

f.d: lus ngag yid kyi sgyu rtsal chu gter che/ / nam yang zad mi shes pa'i pha mtha'i tshad/ / 'jal byed sbyangs pa'i rtags gsum gyis thob pa/ / bzo rig nor bu'i dpyad de mchog tu gshin/[587] / zhes lus bzo ngag bzo yid bzo gsum gyi khongs su ma chud pa'i rig gnas dang sgyu rtsal la sogs pa 'ga' yang ma mchis pas bzo rig pa'i gnas 'di gtso bo yin zhing sman pa la'ang rnam pa bzo ba gong du bshad ma thag pa ltar med du mi rung ba'i yan lag tu go /

Supreme jewel wealth of the science of crafts: great ocean that knows no end, the arts and crafts of body, speech, and mind, the measure of the distance to its farther shore gained by the three signs that training is complete.[1044] There is no art and no science that cannot be included in physical, verbal, or mental skills. Therefore, the science of crafts and skills is the most important and is indispensable knowledge for a physician, as taught above in the section on being well skilled.

d.div: [587] lus ngag yid kyi sgyu rtsal chu gter che/ /nam yang zad mi shes pa'i pha mtha'i tshad/ /'jal byed sbyangs pa'i rtags gsum gyis thob pa/ /bzo rig nor bu'i dpyad de mchog tu gshin/ /zhes pa gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1044] Untraced.

f.d: nang rig nges 'byung mchog dang byang chub sems/ / rnam grol gsum gyi lam mchog ston pa ste/[588] / zhes pa'i nang rig pa chos phung stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'am gsung rab yan lag bcu gnyis sde snod gsum rgyud sde bzhis bsdus pa'i brjod bya mdo dang sngags gsar rnying gi lam la tshul bzhin du zhugs na bdag gzhan gyi don rlabs po che 'grub pa'i dgos pa bsam gyis mi khyab cing / rig lam 'dir yang sman gyi rab gnas sogs gang du'ang khyad par che bas tha na yang rdo rje khrab ring ngam yi dam gang rung gi las bsnyen sogs bskyed rdzogs 'phrin las kyi rim pa la mnga' 'byor ba dang / gzhan yang gnas skabs su yang mdo sngags gsar rnying / rgyud sde bzhi/ theg pa mtho dman sogs kyi rnam par dbye ba tsam 'chad ma shes na 'chad rtsod rtsom gyi bya ba thams cad mun nag gi mda' kho nar 'gro bas brtson bya'i gnas gal che shos dang /

The inner science, revealing the supreme path of great renunciation, bodhi mind, and liberation.[1045] The inner science of the 84,000 Dharma collections or the twelve branches of scripture are gathered into the three baskets of scripture and the four classes of tantra and contain a subject matter of sutra and the new and old-school secret mantra; he who has correctly entered their paths will accomplish great waves of benefit for himself and others. Its need and importance, therefore, is unimaginable. In medicine also, the inner science is of great significance, such as in the practices for consecrating medicine. Therefore, you should have mastered the stages of generation and completion and the invocation of enlightened activity, having completed at the very least the stipulated deity-yoga meditations of Dorjé Trapring[1046] or other meditation deities. Furthermore, knowledge of this science is necessary on occasions, because if you cannot even explain the divisions of the sutras, old and new tantra, the four classes of tantra, the great and the two lesser vehicles, and so on, then any attempts at teaching, composing, and debating will be like arrows fired in the dark. This science then is the most important area to persevere in.

d.div: [588] nang rig nges 'byung mchog dang byang chub sems/ /rnam grol gsum gyi lam mchog ston pa ste/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1045] Untraced.
[1046] A garuḍa-faced protector often invoked in medical practices, such as those found in Yuthok’s Heartdrop.

f.d:
de dag gi rjes/
rgyal po lang tshos dregs gyur kyang / / rgyan med pa na skye bos gleng / / de bzhin snyan ngag mi ldan pa'i/ / bstan bcos mkhas la rtsis su med/[589] / ces bshad pa ltar don bzang por rloms kyang tshig gi rgyan dang mi ldan pa ni lang tsho dang ldan pa'i mi gcer bur rgyu ba bzhin mi mdzes pas nyams dang 'gyur ba stong gis sgeg pa'i tshig rgyan snyan ngag gi bstan bcos rnams su'ang bslab par bya zhing /

Also:
A king proud of his youth but unadorned is a target of gossip. Similarly a work shorn of poetics is not ranked as a work of the wise.[1047] You may be proud of the excellence of a composition, but if it lacks the devices of poetics, then like a man in the prime of youth wandering around unclothed, it is not a thing of beauty. Therefore, with their beautifying verbal adornments of a thousand moods and expressions,[1048] you should pursue a study of the treatises on the art of poetry.

d.div: [589] zur mkhar blo gros rgyal po'i gsung / rgyal po lang tshos dregs gyur kyang / /rgyan med pa na skye bos gleng / /de bzhin snyan ngag mi ldan pa'i/ /bstan bcos mkhas la rtsis su med/ /zhes pa'i dpe lag son ma gyur/
[1047] Untraced.
[1048] Moods (’gyur) are internal and made external through expression (nyams) by way of the many verbal adornments (tshig rgyan) taught in the treatises on poetics (snyan ngag, kāvya).

f.d: rtog pa'i byed pos brda yi tshon pir gyis/ / yid kyi ka shi gsar pa'i ngos yangs por/ / sna tshogs ming gi ri mo rab bkra ba/ / mngon brjod gzigs mor byed la tshar du dngar/[590] / zhes pa'i mngon brjod kyi bstan bcos rnams kyang 'chad rtsom la nye bar mkho ba ma zad/ gso ba rig pa'i bka' bstan dag tu'ang mngon brjod kyis bcing pa shin tu mang bas tshig don bde blag tu 'khrol phyir 'chi med mdzod dang sna tshogs gsal ba la sogs par kyang mkhas par bya/

The lexicographer with his brush of communication paints a variety of beautiful word pictures on the broad new silks of the mind; arranged in series, a show of lexicography.[1049] The treatises on lexicography[1050] are not only essential for teaching and composing, but in the medical sutras and treatises also, much depends on lexicography. Therefore, you should study Treasury of Immortality,[1051] Various Clarifications,[1052] and other works.

d.div: [590] rgyal ba lnga pa blo bzang rgya mtsho'i gsung 'bum/ dza rgya bod hor sog gi mchog dman bar ma rnams la 'phrin yig snyan ngag tu bkod pa rab snyan rgyud mang / shog_57_ba4
[1049] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Letters Arranged in Verse, Collected Works, dza, 57b4.
[1050] Mngon brjod, abhidhāna. This term is often used to mean a thesaurus.
[1051] By the Indian lexicographer Amarasiṃha, Amarakośa, Toh 4299 Tengyur, sgra mdo, se.

[1052] Śrīdhara, Various Clarifications: A Work on Lexicography, Abhidhānaśāstraviśvalocana(ityaparābhidhānamuktāvalī). Mngon brjod kyi bstan bcos sna tshogs gsal ba, Toh 4453 Tengyur, sna tshogs, po.

f.d:
br-i t+ta dzA ti'i rnam bkra za 'og thags/ / lci dang yang ba'i sna tshogs ri mo can/ / legs sbyar skad kyi gos su legs grub pa/ / gyon mkhas gangs ri'i ljongs su mang zhig rgyu/[591] / zhes gsungs pa'i tshigs rkang gcod mtshams phyed pa'i phyir sdeb sbyor rin chen 'byung gnas sogs de'i bstan bcos kyang nyams su blang bya kho na dang /
tha snyad rig pa'i sin+d+hu wa ra'i tshal/ / bcad lhug spel ba'i lus phra'i kha tshang gi/ / 'dzum gyis legs bshad mgron kun bsu mkhas pa'i/ / zlos gar ke sa ra yi mgo cog ldem/[592] / zhes pa'i zlos gar kyang skad rigs la mi rmongs pa sogs dgos pa khyad par can du ma yod pas dang /

The beautifully woven brocade of vṛtta and jāti meters adorned with the patterns of light and heavy sounds, well made into the clothing of well-constructed Sanskrit, is worn by many a scholar in the land of snow.[1053] To learn how to construct a line of verse, study thoroughly the treatises on metrical composition, such as Jewel Source Treatise of Metrics by Ratnākara.
In the Sindhuvari grove of worldly knowledge, their slender bodies blend prose and poetry, their smiles skillfully welcome the guests of well-told tales; the saffron heads of drama sway to and fro.[1054] There are many special reasons for studying the art of drama, such as to curb ignorance of different languages and dialects.

d.div: [591] gong mtshungs/ shog_63_ba4
[592] gong mtshungs/ shog_57_ba5
[1053] Ngawang Losang Gyatso, Letters Arranged in Verse to Various Persons in China, Tibet and Mongolia containing Many Oral Transmissions. Collected Works, dza, 63b4.
[1054] Ibid., 57b5. The last line is clearly a tease.

f.d:
khyad par/
phra zhib rtogs dka' shes bya'i snang brnyan kun/ / mngon sum 'char byed g.yul las rnam rgyal ba'i/ / skar nag rtsis kyi sngon med me long gis/ / kun mkhyen ye shes khengs pa phrogs kyi dogs/[593] / zhes gsungs pa'i g.yul rgyal lam dbyangs 'char de la sman dpyad 'khor lo dang / bdud rtsi'i thun/ zla snyigs la sogs la brten te sman dpyad mtha' dag bdud rtsir 'gyur ba'i dus nges pa shes pa dang / rigs ldan phyi nang gsang gsum ma shes na sman dpyad gang yang dug tu 'gyur ba sogs kyi nyes dmigs che zhing / rlung dang tshe'i rtsis sogs kyi gso dpyad kho na gcig po'i ma yin pa'i 'tsho 'chi'i kha smar sogs gso ba rig pa la mkho ba'i yan lag mang zhing /

Of particular importance:
A never-before-seen mirror of elemental and astrological calculation, the Victory in Battle Tantra clearly revealing images of phenomena subtle and hard to perceive— does it steal the pride of the omniscient mind?[1055] The Victory in Battle Tantra, or Arising Letters (Svarodaya Tantra) contains many practices essential for the science of medicine, such as divination diagrams for medical practices, the auspicious ambrosia times, lunar remainders[1056] calculation, and so on through which the doctor is able to ascertain when medicine and medical practice becomes ambrosia-like in its benefits; the outer, inner, and secret inauspicious kulika times, which if not known can mean the medicine becoming poison and so forth; fortune and life divinations for life-and-death prognoses—not always used for medical purposes; and so on.

d.div: [593] gong mtshungs/ shog_57_ba6
[1056] Zla snyigs, a subdivision of the zodiac sign occupied by the moon. My thanks to Edward Henning for this information.

f.d: skar ma'i dpyad gtso bor bshad pas skar rtsis kyis gza' skar 'phrod sbyor sogs kyis sman gang yang 'thu ba/ sbyor ba/ gtong ba la sogs pa'i dus phyogs tshes grangs kyi dge zhing nus pa'i stobs can du 'gyur ba dang / de dag ma rtogs pa'i ngan pa dang thug na mi shis pa sogs kyi khyad par che zhing /

Astrology,[1057] so called because it primarily teaches the examination of constellations, calculates planetary and stellar combinations,[1058] and so on. Using it one calculates the times, directions, and dates when the collecting, preparation, and taking of medicines becomes effective and auspicious. There is a great difference between these benefits and the disastrous consequences that come from not knowing this astrology.

d.div: [1057] Astrology is skar rtsis, which I have elsewhere translated as “astronomy,” and in its function of calculating the calendar, phases of the moon, eclipses, and so on, “astronomy” would be a preferable translation. After all, the term does mean “calculations from the stars.” However, in this context, its function is more divinatory, in the sense of predicting outcomes and auspicious times.

[1058] “Planetary and stellar combinations” (skar rtsis ’phrod sbyor) refers to the correspondence of element combinations with the planets and constellations. Each correspondence portends a particular outcome.

f.d: rgya nag po'i yul nas dar bas nag rtsis su grags pas rtsa'i sgo nas ma bu dgra grogs/ chu'i sgo nas rus sbal la brten pa sogs gzhung 'di nyid kho na gtso che bar ma zad/ las rtsis la sogs pa nas tshe tshad 'tsho 'chi kyang gso ba rig par ma bltos pa dang / lo zla zhag dus kyis dpyad la sogs pa rung min/ sman sbyor ba nyams su len pa sogs kyi dus dang phyogs sa bdag la brten nas dge min rtogs pa/ khyad par nad rtsis dang dus rtsis kho nas 'tsho 'chi dang gdon gang gnod rim gro 'bogs pa sogs 'ol tshod dang mo phya lha 'dre sogs la ma ltos par shes pa sogs gso rig 'di dang shin tu 'brel che ba dang bcas

Black [or, elemental] calculation is so called because it spread from the country of black clothes.[1059] It describes pulse evaluation—calculating mother, son, enemy, and friend pulses—and urine analysis in conjunction with turtle diagrams and so on, topics that are of prime interest for medical literature. It also covers subjects such as karma calculation, which can predict lifespans and foretell whether one will survive an illness without medical intervention. It deals with the examination of the year, month, day, and hour to divine whether various therapies are appropriate and to calculate the auspicious and inauspicious times for compounding medicines, for performing various medical practices, and so on. It also covers the consulting of land guardians[1060] to divine auspicious and inauspicious directions. In particular, using only illness divination and time divination, you can make prognoses and learn which demon is causing the illness and what rituals are to be performed, all without resorting to guesswork or relying on other forms of divination, oracles, and the like. In this way elemental calculation has a very strong connection with medical science.

d.div: [1059] Nag rtsis. It is also known as elemental calculation (’byung rtsis). The country of black clothes is China (rgya nag), often juxtaposed with India (rgya dkar), the land of white clothes.
[1060] Sa bdag. Spirits, usually nāgas, that have domain over land and are especially linked to astrological influences.

f.d: rtsis skar nag dbyangs 'char dang bcas pa rnams shes bya spyi la khyab che zhing / bla gnas sogs gang ci nas med thabs med pa lta bu/

Astrology, elemental calculation, and Arising Letters divination generally can be applied to all phenomena, and together with the location of the life force[1061] and so on, they are in all respects indispensable tools.

d.div: [1061] The life force (bla) travels about the body, and its position can be mapped out by recourse to astrology.

f.d: rkyen bsten pa ni/

d.i: Devoting yourself to acquiring the necessary conditions

f.d:
de rkyen slob dpon bsten te mtshan nyid dang / / bsten pa'i thabs dang bsten pa'i dgos pa gsum/ / mtshan nyid rgya che mkhas dang man ngag ldan/ / ngang ring gsog chung brtse la bkur 'os bsten/ /
bsten thabs dogs pa med par blo btad la/ / ngo lkog med par bya ba sgrub par bya/ / spyod pa thams cad de yi yul dang bstun/ / drin du tshor bas rgyun du bsring bar bya/ / dgos pa myur bar lobs dang mkhas par 'gyur/[594] / zhes de ltar yi ge 'dri klog gis mtshon pa'i rig pa mtha' dag la byang bar gyur nas sman dpyad la mkhas par byed pa de'i rkyen du slob dpon rnam dag bsten dgos te/ de la'ang slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid dang / bsten pa'i thabs dang / bsten pa'i dgos pa gsum las/ dang po mtshan nyid ni/ rang gzhan gyi gzhung lugs rgya che bar mthong zhing de'i tshig don la mkhas pa dang / sna gcig ma yin pa'i man ngag gang mang du ldan zhing ser sna med pa dang / ngang rgyud ring zhing gsog dang gsob ste g.yo sgyu dang zol zog chung ba / nad pa dang slob ma la brtse zhing rigs mtho ba kun gyis gong du bkur 'os pa nyid bsten par bya ba dang /

The necessary condition is devotion to the master, dealt with under three headings: definition, manner of devotion, and reason. The definition of a master is one extensively learned, in possession of the oral tradition, patient, of little guile, compassionate, and worthy of reverence.
Devotion should be one of trusting without doubt, of carrying out tasks without duplicity, of behaving always in harmony with his thoughts, and of making effort in constant thought of his kindness. The reason for such devotion is that you learn quickly and become wise.[1062] Therefore, having trained yourself in all forms of knowledge, as illustrated by the previous topic of reading and writing, you devote yourself to the causal condition for becoming learned in medicine. This is the master, and this topic is under the three headings of definition of a master, the way to devote oneself, and the reason for such devotion. The definition of a master is someone who has extensively examined his own and others’ medical traditions and become wise and learned in their words and meanings. He possesses not just one but as many oral traditions as possible, and he is not miserly with them. He is calm and patient. “Of little falsehood” means with little guile and deceit.[1063] He has compassion for the sick and for his students, and is deemed worthy of reverence by those of noble status. The student should devote himself to such a person.

d.div: [594] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 2
[1062] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.98.2.

[1063] The verse has gsog cung, which could mean “of simple means” as Clarke has translated it, because the verb gsog pa means “to accumulate,” and cung means “few,” but here the author understands it as gsog po, meaning “hollow,” “without essence,” and “false.” He has also paired it with gsob pa, which has the same meaning.

f.d: mtshan nyid de dang ldan pa'i slob dpon rnyed nas bsten pa'i thabs ni/ 'dis dpyis phyin pa slob bam mi slob ces pa la sogs pa'i dogs pa ye med par blo rtse gcig tu gtad/ slob dpon gyi ngos lkog khyad med pa'i bya ba de'i gsung bzhin du bsgrub pa dang / spyod pa rnam thar thams cad kyang de'i dgongs pa'i yul dang bstun zhing / blo bskyed cud zad re las ma byung kyang de'i drin kho nar tshor bar byas nas dus rgyun du ngang bsring bar bya dgos la/ de ltar byas pa'i dgos pa sman dpyad kyi gzhung lugs myur du lobs shing mkhas par 'gyur ba yin no/ /

Having found a master with such qualities, the way of devotion is with single-minded trust devoid of the doubt that asks, “Through him will I master my studies? Should I study with him or not?” You follow his instructions exactly, whether in his presence or not. All your behaviour should be in harmony with his thoughts. Even if you have made only meager development, think of it as being the result of his kindness, and steadily persevere. The reason for such devotion is that it allows you to quickly master the medical texts and become learned.

d.i: Endeavor with regard to your companions

f.d: grogs la brtson bya zhu dang dri ba dang / / bzung dang bsam pa le lo bya ba min/ / ci yi phyir na de nyid bar gcod dgra/[595] / zhes slob dpon bsten pa tsam du ma zad grogs mched rnams la'ang brtson 'grus dang ldan pa'i sgo nas 'di ltar bya ste/ 'ga' zhig la gzhung 'di'i skabs su ci zhes zhu ba dang / la la la 'di dang 'di ci zhes 'dri ba dang / dpe dang slob dpon sogs kyi ngag las bzung ba dang / de rnams kyi don la bsam pa rnams la le lo bya ba ma yin te/ ci'i phyir na/ le lo de nyid bsam pa la bar du gcod pa'i dgra yin pas rnam pa kun tu brtson 'grus brtsams par bya/

Endeavor with regard to your companions is to ask and make enquiries of them, and to memorize and contemplate without laziness. Why? Laziness is a hindering enemy.[1064] Not only should you rely upon the master, but toward your companions you should do as follows. To some ask, “What does this mean here in this text?” To others ask, “What is such and such?” Do not be lazy in retaining texts and the words of the master and others, or in contemplating their meanings. Why? Because laziness is an enemy that hinders such contemplation. Therefore always generate perseverance.

d.div: [595] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 6
[1064] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.98.6.

f.d: goms pa mthar dbyung ba ni/

goms pa mthar dbyung mthong thos blang ba ste/ / thams cad zhen 'dris the tshom spong bar byed/[596] / ces yi ge 'dri klog la sogs pa dang / slob dpon bsten pa dang grogs la brtson pa lhur blangs pas mkhas pa'am goms pa de mthar dbyung ba la legs par bshad pa'i cha shas mchog dman su la 'dug pa mthong ngam thos na thabs kyis zhu zhing nyams su blang ba ste/ de ltar byas pas tshig don thams cad yid la zhen cing 'dris pas the tshom gyi dri ma spong bar byed pa'o/ /

Completing your development means practicing what is seen and heard, taking, becoming familiar, and eliminating all doubt.[1065] Having learned how to read and write, devoted yourself to a master, and shown willing endeavor to your companions, you will complete that scholarship or development by ensuring that whenever you see or hear that someone, whether high or low, has even a morsel of a good teaching, you endeavor to request it and to put it into practice. In this way you take all teachings into your mind and become familiar with them, thereby eliminating the taint of doubt.

d.div: [596] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 8

f.d: gzhan don ni/

gzhan gyi bya ba la brtson nad pa de/ / de don phyi bshol bar du ma chod par/ / gyang thog mar phor bo na bsod bsdigs bzhin/ / sman dpyad dus las ma 'gyangs brtson pas sgrims/[597] / zhes gzhan gyi bya ba ni skabs 'dir nad pa ste/ de'i don lan gcig tsam las shi gson thag ma chod kyi bar du phyi bshol dang bya ba gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par rtse gcig tu bsgrim par bya dgos pa dper na gyang mthon po phra la ring ba'i thog tu mar khus gang ba'i phor pa khur nas 'gro ba la mar pho na gsod par the tshom med ces bsdigs na sgrims te 'gro ba bzhin du nad kyi tshod las dpags pa'i sman dpyad dus dus lam ma 'gyangs par brtson pas sgrims shig pa'i don dang /

Endeavor for the activities of others is effort for the sake of the patient, where without the interruption of delays— like someone under threat of death carrying melted butter on a wall— you endeavor with concentration, administering treatment at the right time.[1066] Here “activities of others” refers to the patient, for whose sake you must concentrate single-pointedly, uninterrupted by delays or by other activities, not just once but until it is certain that the patient will either live or die. Concentrate like someone walking on top of a high and narrow wall carrying a bowl full of melted butter who is threatened with certain death if he spills a drop, and endeavor to administer—at the right time and without delay—the treatment indicated by your examination of the symptoms.

d.div: [597] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 9

d.i: Wise in traditions of the world

f.d:
mi yi chos lugs mkhas par bya ba ni/ / mi chos pa dang dam pa thun mong gsum/ / dang por mkhas par bslab la gnyen gyis btsa'/ / gyong gis 'dul gsum ldan na 'dod pa 'grub/ /
dam pa'i chos lugs sna dul 'grogs pa bde/ / chog shes gyur na rang gzhan phan thogs 'gyur/ /
thun mong phongs pa rnams la snying rje bzung / / mthon po rnams kyis rag gi mdo don sgrub/ / tshogs pa drug ldan 'bras bu the tshom med/[598] / ces rgyu tha ma mi'i chos lugs la mkhas par bya ba ni/ 'jig rten mi chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba dang / dam pa lha chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba dang / de gnyis thun mong du sbyang pa gsum las

To be wise in the traditions of the world refers to worldly ethics, the spiritual, and both. For the first, become learned, care for others with gentleness, and subdue others with toughness; with these three desires are met.
With wisdom in spiritual matters comes a disciplined mind, affability, and contentment, bringing benefits to self and others.
With both comes concern and compassion for the deprived, and those on high will fulfill your needs. Endowed with these six collections, results will undoubtedly arrive.[1067] The last of the six causes is to become wise in world traditions. It is dealt with under three headings: to follow the traditions of the human world, to follow spiritual or celestial traditions, and to train yourself in both.

d.div: [598] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 10

f.d: dang po 'jig rten mi chos dang mthun par spyad pa de la thog mar mkhas par bslab pa dang / phan gdags bya'i yul du gyur pa 'ga' zhig la lus ngag gnyen po'i sgo nas btsa' ba de mgu ba bskyed pa dang / la la la rgyud gyong po'i tshul gyis 'dul ba gang la gang 'tsham pa gsum dang ldan na 'dod pa 'grub par 'gyur zhing de bzhin du dam pa'i chos lugs la'ang sna dul te shes rgyud dul ba dang 'grogs pa bde ba dang 'dod pa la chog shes par gyur na rang gzhan thams cad la phan thogs par 'gyur la/ de gnyis ka thun mong du gyur pa ni nad kyi nyam thag pa rnams dang / dbul zhing phongs pa rnams la lhag par snying brtse bas gtsang rme med par rjes su bzung ba'i tshe na 'di ni sman pa byang chub sems dpa' 'o zhes bla dpon mthon po rnams kyis rang gi mdo don mkho dgu sgrub par 'gyur la/ de ltar na blo dang ldan pa la sogs pa sman pa mkhas pa rgyu'i tshogs pa drug dang ldan na tshe 'dir snyan grags dang 'dod yon sogs gnas skabs dang mthar thug gi 'bras bu 'grub par the tshom med do//

For the first of these, you train to become learned in the behavior that conforms to the traditions of the world. Toward those you aim to benefit, use appropriate methods. For some show concern, reassuring them with gentle speech and movements. For others use tougher means to subdue them. With these three your wishes will be met. Similarly, on the spiritual path, if you have a disciplined mind, are easy to get on with, and have contentment concerning desires, you will benefit yourself and everybody else. Being learned in both worldly and spiritual ethics gives you a special compassion for those made wretched by disease and deprived by poverty, and you care for them with a pure intent. When this happens those on high, such as lamas and dignitaries, will remark, “This is truly a bodhisattva physician!” and they will ensure that all your needs are met. Therefore, endowed with this collection of six causes needed to become a learned physician—being of an intelligent mind and so on—you will gain without doubt the temporary benefits of this life, such as celebrity and wealth, as well the ultimate fruits.
sman pa'i ngo bo ni/

nyes pa gnod bya gnyen po'i mtshan nyid rnams/ / ci rigs khong du chud po ngo bor 'dod/[599] / ces gang zhig nyes pa gsum dang gnod bya bcu dang gnyen po sman dpyad kyi mtshan nyid mtha' dag rnams dbang po rab 'bring ci rigs 'thad pa'i tshul gyis khong du chud pa'i shes pa de nyid sman pa'i ngo bo yin par 'dod la/

To understand as appropriate the characteristics of humors, the vulnerable, and remedies is asserted as being the nature.[1068] The nature of a physician is asserted as being a knowledge that has understood by way of sharp or middling faculties as appropriate all the characteristics of the three humors, the ten vulnerable bodily phenomena,[1069] and all salutary medical practices.

d.div: [599] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 15

[1069] The ten vulnerable bodily phenomena, or objects of harm (gnod bya), are the seven bodily constituents—plasma, blood, flesh, fat, marrow, bone, and semen—and the three excretions or impurities—sweat, excrement, and urine.

f.d: nges tshig ni/

nges tshig nad gso lus la phan phyir sman/ / nad steng dpyad dpa' 'gro la pha ltar skyob/ / rgyal po rnams kyi rje ru 'khur bar byed/[600] / ces sman pa'i nges tshig ni nad kyi zug rngu las gso zhing lus phan 'dogs pa'i phyir sman dang / nad tshabs chen po'i steng du thur ma dang 'dral gcod kyi dpyad byed pa'i tshe dpa' zhing mi zhum pas na sman pa zhes pa dang / yang na 'gro ba rnams la pha ltar skyob pas sman pa/ gzhan yang rgyal po rnams ni 'jig rten gyi lha yin cing de rnams kyang rje ru 'khur bar byed pas lha rje zhes pa'ang rnam grangs so/ /

d.div: [600] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 16
[1070] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.98.15.

[1071] Sman pa; sman means medicine and pa as it is spelled here is usually a nominative particle indicating a male noun. Sometimes, however, it is spelled dpa’ when it means hero (as in byang chub sems dpa’, bodhisattva, in the sense of being a compassionate hero).

[1072] According to Surkhar Lodrö Gyalpo in his General Compendium of Knowledge Indispensable to Physicians (478b6), as a verb sman can also mean “to help,” and a physician is “one who helps” (sman pa). Of course sman pa could also just be read as “medicine man.”

f.d: dbye ba sman pa bla na med pa dang / / khyad par can dang phal pa gsum yin te/ / dug gsum rgyu 'bras nad sel gong na med/ / gzhan rig mngon shes byams ldan drang por srong / / gnang rigs rjes sbyangs las goms 'gro ba'i gnyen/ / 'dod pas 'phral du cha bzung srog gi gshed/ / 'on kyang mchog dang tha mar grags pa ste/[601] / zhes sman pa'i dbye ba ni sman bla na med pa dang / khyad par can dang / phal pa gsum du yod pa yin te/ de yang 'dod chags zhe sdang gti mug dang dug gsum po'i rgyu ma rig pa dang 'bras bu rlung mkhris bad kan gyi nad rnams sel ba'i sman pa ni sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das te de'i gong na sman pa gzhan med pa/

Types are the unsurpassed, the special, and the ordinary: unsurpassed in eliminating the three poisons, their causes, and their effects. clearly know the minds of others and are loving, upright, and true; those of conferred lineage, their trained followers, and those familiar with practice— these are the friends of living beings; those with desire who suddenly appear in the guise of physicians— these are the butchers of lives. However, they are identified as the best and the worst.[1073] Concerning the types of physician, there is the unsurpassed physician, the special physician, and the ordinary physician. The physician who eliminates desire, aversion, and confusion, the ignorance that causes these three poisons, together with the wind, bile, and phlegm disorders that result from the three poisons is the blessed Buddha. He is the physician surpassed by no one.

d.div: [601] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_98_yig phreng 17
[1073] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.98.17.

f.d:
'jam dpal sgyu dra las/
sman pa che mchog gtso bo ste/ / zug rngu 'byin pa bla na med/[602] / ces gsungs pa ltar ro// khyad par can gyi sman pa ni/ gzhan rgyud rig pa'i mngon par shes pa dang byams pa dang snying rje tshad med pa dang ldan pas sdug bsngal gyi nyam thag pa rnams bde ba la sbyor zhing rang rgyud drang por srong ba ste/ tsa ra kar/
drang srong chen po 'di kun yang / / mngon shas lnge dang ldan 'gyur zhing / / rig pa'i gnas mchog bco brgyad shes/[603] / zhes bshad pa dang mthun/

In the Mañjuśrī Illusory Net it says:
The best and lord of physicians, unsurpassed reliever of pain.[1074] The special physician possesses clairvoyance that knows the minds of others as well as immeasurable love and compassion. Therefore those made wretched with suffering he brings to happiness, while his own mind is upright and true.[1075] Caraka says:
All these great rishis possess the fivefold clairvoyance and know the eighteen supreme fields of knowledge.[1076]

d.div: [602] sde dge_360_bka'/ rgyud/ ka 'jam dpal mtshan brjod/ shog_6_na3
[603] tsa ra ka'i dpe cha lag tu ma son/
[1074] Found in Names of Mañjuśrī, Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti, Toh 360 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 6a3.
[1075] “Upright and true” (drang srong, ṛṣi) is the etymology of the term rishi. This is the etymology used by Clark (p. 228).
[1076] Untraced.

f.d: phal pa'i sman pa gnyis las/ dang po la don dang mthun pa'i chos rgyal rigs gsum mgon po'i sprul pa rnams kyi bla'i sman par gnang ba rigs nas rigs su brgyud pa'i sman pa dang / rgyal po'i bla sman gyi rigs ma yin kyang de dag gi rjes su zhugs nas gzhung lugs la legs par sbyangs pa'i sman pa dang / gzhung lugs la sbyangs pa'i yon tan rgya chen po dang mi ldan kyang / slob dpon gyi phyag len mthong ba brgyud pa'i las la goms pa'i sman pa dang rnam pa gsum po ni 'gro ba rnams kyi srog gi gnyen po yin la/ ci yang mi shes kyang lto gos kyi 'dod pas 'phral du sman pa'i cha lugs bzung ba ni srog gi gshed ma yin/ 'on kyang dbye ba 'di'i skabs su gnang rigs rjes sbyangs las goms kyi sman pa gsum mchog dang phyi ma la tha ma zhes yongs su grags pa ste 'jig rten nyid gtso bor byas pa'i dbye ba'i dbang gis so//

The ordinary physician is of two types, the first of which is of three kinds. There are those who have been conferred as chief physicians of genuine Dharma kings, manifestations of the three buddha families, a distinction that is passed down through their lineage. There are those who are not of the lineage of chief physicians of kings but who have followed after them and have trained well in their medical studies. Still others do not possess the qualities of being highly trained in medical studies but through observation of their master’s practice have become familiar with the work of a physician. These three are allies of the lives of living beings. Those who know nothing but, out of desire for food and clothing, suddenly appear in the guise of a physician are the butchers of life. However, among the divisions of ordinary physicians, those of conferred lineage, trained followers, and those familiar with practice are identified as the best physicians, while the second type are identified as the lowest of physicians. This division into “best” and “worst” is made primarily on the basis of worldly standards.

skabs 'dir 'bum chung gsal sgron sogs su/
gnang ba rigs kyi sman pa zhes pa/ rgyal bo rnams kyi sman par gnang ba byin nas sman pa'i rigs brgyud dang ldan pa/ rjes 'jug sbyangs pa'i sman pa zhes pa/ mkhas pa rnams kyi rjes su zhugs nas sbyangs pa/ 'dus byas las la goms pa'i sman pa zhes pa/ gzhung gi don mi shes kyang gdams ngag gi skor la brten nas/ slob dpon gyi phyag bzhes mthong ba la goms pa dang / rang gi nyams su myong ba la goms pa ste gsum dang / 'dod pas phral bslabs kyi sman pa ni/ sbyang goms med na'ang 'dod pas gdungs nas sman pa'i cha lugs 'dzin te/

On this point the Small Collection Illuminating Lamp[1077] commentary on the Explanatory Tantra says:
Physicians of “conferred lineage” refer to those conferred as physicians of kings and who then possess a physician lineage. “Trained followers” are those physicians who follow the great scholars and train accordingly. Those “familiar with practice” are those who do not know the medical scriptures but have relied on the oral traditions and have become familiar with practice by watching the master at work and developing their own practice. Physicians who train hastily through desire have no mastery or familiarization but, driven by desire, merely assume the guise of a physician.

d.div: [1077] By Sumtön Yeshé Sung.

de la bzhi/ nad pa rgan goms kyi sman pa/ yig nag bru bsgrugs kyi sman pa/ rgya pa phyogs ltos kyi sman pa'o/ / dang po ni/ nad pa rang nyid la phan goms gang byung gi rjes su dpags nas gzhan gyi nad 'chos pa dang / gnyis pa ni/ man ngag gi shog dril zab zab mo 'ga' zhig mthong ba la brten nas sman pa byed pa/ gsum pa ni/ gzhan zer dang yig mkhan dang jag pa byas pa'i yig sgum dang sman sgum la brten nas sman pa byed pa/ bzhi pa ni/ stod smad kyi sman tshong byas pas sman 'di ni 'di la phan no zhes 'ga' zhig shes pa la brten nas sman pa byed pa rnams ni srog gi gshed dmar bzhed la/[604]

The last are of four types: the physician familiar with the patients’ means, the physician limited by scrolls, the physician who has picked up a few manuscripts, and the physician who is little more than a salesman. The first is a physician who treats others having calculated the benefit the patient will be to him. The second is a physician whose practice is based on having seen a few scrolls of the profound oral tradition. The third is a physician whose practice is based on hearsay, something someone has written down, or some mediocre medicine and writings stolen by thieves. The fourth is a physician whose practice is based on knowing a little and who sells general medicines that treat all parts of the body saying, “This medicine is good for this.” These physicians are butchers of lives.[1078]
[604] g.yu thog gsar ma yon tan mgon po/ cha lag bco brgyad/ 'grel pa 'bum chung gsal sgron nor bu'i 'phreng ba/ stod cha/ shog_290_yig phreng 5
[1078] Found in Eighteen Auxiliary Texts, 290.5. The second of the four, “the physician limited by scrolls,” is missing from the text as has been added from the source text.

f.d:
mchog gi sman pa ni/
gdung btsun blo dang ldan zhing dam la gnas/ / gzhung gi don mkhas man ngag gnad du rdeg / goms thog gtso bor chos gnyer 'dod pa spangs/ / dul zhing bzo mkhas 'gro la byams sems che/ / g.yel med gzhan gyi don la rang don sems/ / gso dpyad kun la rmongs med sman pa mchog / 'gro ba nad pa rnams kyi mgon gcig pu/ / rig 'dzin drang srong rnams kyi rgyud 'dzin sras/ / 'tsho mdzad sman pa'i rgyal po'i sprul par bshad/[605] / ces rje rigs dang rgyal rigs dang bram ze'i rigs la sogs pa gdung btsun la don dang don ma yin pa so sor 'byed pa'i blo gros dang ldan zhing dam tshig la rtag tu gnas pa/

Concerning the “best physician”:
Of a venerable race, intelligent, dwelling in pledges, wise in scripture, penetrating to the essence of oral traditions, complete mastery, working primarily for Dharma, desire left behind, disciplined, skilled, a great mind of love for others, undistracted, considering the welfare of others as his own, clear and informed in all medical practices, the best physician, sole protector of the sick, a son in the lineage of the vidyādhara rishis: thus has spoken this manifestation of the life-granting medicine king.[1079] The best physician is born of a venerable race such as that of the royal, noble, or brahman classes. He has the intelligence to distinguish between what is correct and incorrect and constantly dwells within the pledges.

d.div: [605] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_99_yig phreng 3
[1079] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.99.3.

f.d: gzhung lugs mdo rgyas kyi tshig don la mkhas shing man ngag zab mo gnad du khel nges shes par brdeg pa/ lag len mtha' dag rab tu goms pa thob cing gtso bor dam pa'i chos kho na don du gnyer bas chos brgyad kyis kun nas blangs pa'i 'dod pa spangs pa/ sgo gsum dul zhing lus ngag yid gyi bzo mkhas la 'gro ba rnams la snying rje dang byams sems lhag par che ba dang / dus skad cig kyang g.yel ba med par nad pa la sogs pa gzhan gyi don la rang don las kyang gces par sems pa/ gso dpyad gzhung lugs sde mtha' dag gi tshig don kun la rmongs pa med pa ste/ de lta bu dang ldan pa gang yin pa de ni sman par khas 'che ba rnams kyi mchog dam pa dang / 'gro ba nad kyis nyam thag pa rnams kyi mgon skyabs gcig pu ba dang / sman gyi rig pa 'dzin pa'i drang srong rnams kyi brgyud pa 'dzin pa'i sras po dang / 'tsho mdzad sman pa'i rgyal po baiDUR+ya 'od kyi rgyal po'i sprul par bdag rig pa'i ye shes kyis bshad ces pa lta bu dang /

He is wise in the meanings of both small and extensive scriptural traditions and penetrates with certainty the precise essence of the profound oral traditions. He has gained complete mastery in all medical practices, and by mainly striving solely for the Dharma, he leaves behind desires motivated by the eight worldly attitudes. He is disciplined physically, verbally, and mentally and likewise skilled physically, verbally, and mentally, and he has exceptional love and compassion for others. Without being distracted for an instant, he considers the welfare of others to be more precious than his own. He is clear and informed on all the meanings of scriptures of all medical practices of all traditions. Such a one with such qualities is the best physician of all those who claim to be physicians. He is the sole protector of those beings brought down by sickness, a son holding the lineage of the vidyādhara medicine rishis. I, Vidyājñāna, manifestation of the life-granting medicine king, the beryl king, have spoken this.

le'u nyer drug par/
sman pa mkhas pa'i stegs la 'dzegs pa dang / / gzhung gi don shes las rnams mthong zhing gtsang /[606] / zhes pa'ang sman pa gang zhig mkhas pa'i stegs bu lta bu blo gros dang sbyangs pa snyan grags dang kun gyis bkur ba dang bzhi la 'dzegs pas rig pa'i gnas lnga spyi dang khyad par du gso ba rig pas mngon par mtho ba dang / rgyud dang bstan bcos dang lung dang man ngag bzhi'i sgo nas gzhung gi don mtha' dag shes pa dang / brtag pa dang sman dang dpyad dang zas spyod bslab pa dang bzhi'i las rnams ma lus pa slob dpon gyis nyams su len pa mthong ba de ji lta ba bzhin du rang gis goms pa dang / rigs ngan zhing 'tshol ba dang nad pa'i nor la brnabs sems kyi blo dang / phyogs ris can gyi snying rje dang / sman dpyad la sla thabs kyi cho ga khrag 'khrugs yid du mi 'ong ba byed pa'i skyon rnams dang bral bas gtsang ba ste sman pa'i yan lag bcu drug dang ldan dgos pa dang /

Also, as it says in the twenty-sixth chapter:
The physician ascends to the dais of the scholar, knows the scriptures, observes the work, and is pure.[1080] A physician ascends to the heights of intelligence, training, fame, and veneration—likened to the dais of a scholar—where he is elevated by his knowledge of the five sciences, especially the science of medicine. Through the tantras, treatises, transmissions, and oral traditions, he knows the meanings of all the scriptures. He has observed the work of his master in areas of examination, medicines, therapies or surgery, rules of diet, and behavior and integrated them accordingly. He is pure and clean because he is without the faults of being of poor or mixed ancestry, he does not possess a mind that covets the wealth of his patients, he is not partisan in his compassion, and he is not someone who messily spills blood in simple medical procedures. A physician must possess these sixteen attributes.

d.div: [606] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 26_shog_85_yig phreng 4

f.d:
phyi ma 'phrin las rgyud kyi yongs gtad kyi le'ur/
rgyud 'di gtad par bya ba'i snod ldan ni/ / dam tshig ldan pas bla ma spyi bor 'khur/ / nor dang srog la phangs med gtong phod nus/ / shes rab che bas tshig don 'gal 'brel 'byed/ / byang sems che bas gzhan don gtso bor len/ / chos la brang gtad g.yo sgyu zol zog med/ / sman pa'i rgyu drug tshogs pa'i skal ldan la/ / drang srong chen po'i rgyud 'di gtad par bgyi/[607] / zhes dam tshig dang ldan pas bla ma dang slob dpon tshul bzhin du spyi bor 'khur ba dang / yon tan gyi don du phra rags kyi nor dang rang nyid kyi srog la'ang 'phangs sems med par gtong ba dang 'dor phod pa dang nus pa/ shes rab che bas gzhung man ngag mtha' dag pa'i tshig don 'gal 'brel 'byed shes pa/ byang chub kyis sems shas che bas gzhan gyi don kho na gtso bor len par byed pa/ dam pa'i chos kho na la blo'am brang gtad pas gzhan bslu ba'i g.yo dang sgyu dang zol dang zog rnams med pa ste rgyu drug bshad pa zur mkhar ba phyi mas bshad rgyud bya byed sman ler bstan pa'i rgyu drug dang gcig par mdzad 'dug kyang de dang 'di gnyis tshig don mi 'dra'o//

In the Entrustment Chapter of the Enlightened Activities, or Final Tantra, of Four Tantras:
A suitable vessel for the entrustment of this tantra is possessed of the pledges and raises the guru to his crown. Able and willing to give up wealth or life, he has no sense of loss for either. Of great intelligence he discerns contradictions and connections in the text. Of great bodhi mind primarily concerned for the welfare of others, he has a mind entrusted to Dharma, with no guile and pretense. To the fortunate ones possessed of these six causes will this tantra of the great rishis be entrusted.[1081] Endowed with the pledges he will properly venerate the gurus and masters. In order to develop excellent qualities, he is willing and able to sacrifice his life and any kind of wealth without a sense of loss. Endowed with great intelligence he is able to discern all contradictions and connections in the texts and oral traditions. With a great bodhi mind he primarily works solely for the sake of others. With his mind entrusted solely to the Dharma, he is divorced of the guile and pretense that seeks to deceive others. Surkhar[1082] asserts these six causes taught in the Final Tantra to be the same as the six taught in the Explanatory Tantra in the chapter on physicians, but these two have different meanings.

d.div: [607] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 27_shog_666_yig phreng 10
[1081] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 27.666.10.
[1082] Sukhar Lodrö Gyalpo.

f.d:
gzhan yang tsa ra ka las/
sman pa blo ldan shes rab ldan/ / rang gi yon tan phun sum tshogs/ / snying rje'i sems kyis brlan pa ni/ / sman pa kun gyi gtsug rgyan yin/[608] / zhes dang /

Also Caraka:
The doctor who is intelligent and wise, whose qualities are perfected, his mind moist with compassion, is the crown jewel of all physicians.[1083]

d.div: [608] tsa ra ka'i dpe cha lag tu ma son/
[1083] Untraced.

f.d:
brgyad pa'i gleng gzhi las/
sman pa mkhas stegs gzhung don shes/ / las rnams mthong zhing gtsang ba yin/[609] / zhes dang /

In the introduction to the Treatise of Eight Branches:
The physician on the dais of the scholar, knowing scripture, observing the work, and pure.[1084]

d.div: [609] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u dang po/ shog_45_ba3
[1084] Pitṛceṭa, Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhita, chap. 1, Toh 4310 Tengyur, gso rig, he, 45b3.

f.d:
sgron gsal las/
gso ba po ni gtsang zhing shes rab can/ / rtogs dpyod brtson la dbang po zhi zhing dul/ / thos dang ngang bzang 'gro la snying rje che/ / yid gzhung lag bzo mkhas stegs gzhung don shes/[610] / zhes dang /

In Illuminating Lamp:
The healer is pure and wise, strives for understanding, has senses calm and disciplined, and is well learned and good-natured, compassionate to others, knowledgeable, and skilled; on the dais of the scholar, knows the scriptures.[1085]

d.div: [610] sgron gsal las/ gso ba po ni gtsang zhing shes rab can/ /rtogs dpyod brtson la dbang po zhi zhing dul/ /thos dang ngang bzang 'gro la snying rje che/ /yid gzhung lag bzo mkhas stegs gzhung don shes/ /gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1085] Untraced.

f.d:
yang snying bsdus par/
sman pa gzhung don la mkhas shing / / lung dang 'dris pa'i bzang po dag / las la goms shing dge ba dag / khyab ste yongs su gnas pa yin/[611] / zhes sogs pa'i yon tan dang ldan pa zhig dgos shing /

In Essence of Eight Branches:
A physician well learned in the texts is a good scholar wise in the transmissions; familiar with the practices and virtuous is the good physician, the exalted physician.[1086] Therefore, a physician must have these excellent qualities.

d.div: [611] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u/ 40_shog 334_ba4
[1086] Pitṛceṭa, Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhita, chap. 40, Toh 4310 Tengyur, gso rig, he, 334b4. Translated according to Degé reading.

f.d:
'on kyang / don dam bsnyen pa las/
rtsod ldan dbang gis bla ma skyon dang yon tan 'dres/ / rnam pa kun tu sdig pa med pa yongs ma yin/ / gang zhig yon tan lhag pa yang ni legs spyad nas/ / bu rnams kyis ni de la bsten par gyur pa'o/[612] / zhes rtsod ldan la yon tan mtha' dag ldan pa dkon pas skyon las yon tan shas che ba de bsten rung ba yin la/

However, as In Devotion to the Ultimate Truth says:
Because of these kaliyuga times of trouble, qualities and faults are mixed within gurus; none are completely without fault. Disciples will come to rely on those, discovered after careful examination, to have a predominance of good qualities.[1087] Therefore, in these kaliyuga times it is rare to find masters with all these good qualities present. Rely on those whose good qualities outweigh their bad.

d.div: [612] sde dge_1348_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na pad+ma dkar po/ dpal don dam pa'i bsnyen pa/ shog_4_ba2
[1087] Puṇḍarīka, Paramārthasevā, Toh 1348 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 4b2.

f.d: slob ma brtag pa dang slob ma'i mtshan nyid/
27. Examining Disciples and Studying with the Master
slob ma brtag pa ni/

spyir gsang sngags la/ bla ma lnga bcu pa las/
bla ma dang ni slob ma dag / mtshungs par dam tshig nyams 'gyur bas/ / dpa' bos dang por slob dpon dang / / slob ma'i 'brel pa brtag par bya/[613] / zhes dang /

On the tantra position in general, the Fifty Verses on Guru Devotion states:
Guru and disciple suffer equally any degeneration of pledges. Therefore the brave one examines the relationship between guru and disciple.[1088]

d.div: [613] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshu_slob dpon rta dbyangs/ bla ma lnga bcu pa/ shog_10_na5
[1088] Aśvaghoṣa, Gurupañcāśikā, Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10a5.

f.d:
rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba las kyang /
ji ltar rin chen brdar ba dang / / gser ni bsreg dang bcad pas brtag / de bzhin du ni slob ma yang / / lo ni bcu gnyis bar du brtag / de phyin phan tshun de lta bus/ / dus kun tu ni de ltar brtag / gzhan du bgegs ni 'byung 'gyur te/ / dngos grub 'joms shing sdug bsngal ster/[614] / zhes dang /
ji ltar seng ge'i 'o ma ni/ / sa yi snod du bzhag mi bya/ / de bzhin rnal 'byor chen po'i rgyud/ / snod min dag la sbyin mi bya/ / slob ma skad cig de la 'chi/ / 'di dang pha rol tu ni 'phung / / snod min man ngag rab bshad na/ / slob dpon dngos grub nyams par 'gyur/[615] / zhes sogs nan tan du gsungs so/ /

In the Vajra Garland Tantra:
Just as a jewel is tested by rubbing and gold by heating and cutting, the disciple is examined for up to twelve years. In this way, mutual examination should proceed. If this is not done, obstacles will arise, destroying siddhis and bringing suffering.[1089] Also:
Just as one should not pour the milk of a lioness into an earthen pot, so the Mahāyoga tantras should not be given to those vessels who are unsuitable. The disciple meets death in that moment, ruined in this and future lives. If instruction is taught to unsuitable vessels, the master suffers degeneration of siddhi.[1090] Thus, this point is forcefully made.

d.div: [614] sde dge_445_bka'/ rgyud/ ca bshad rgyud rdo rje phreng ba/ le'u/ 2_shog_212_na6
[615] sde dge_445_bka'/ rgyud/ ca bshad rgyud rdo rje phreng ba/ le'u/ 15_shog_273_na3
[1089] Vajramālābhidhānatantra, chap. 2, Toh 445 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, 212a6.
[1090] Vajramālābhidhānatantra, chap. 15, Toh 445 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, 273a3.

f.d:
lo bcu gnyis zhes pa ni brtags kyang myur du ma shes na ring mtha' de tsam zhig gi bar du rtog pa'i don yin gyi myur du shes na mi dgos so/ / rgyud nas gsungs pa'i mtshan nyid de dag ma lus par tshang ba cig kyang ma rnyed na skyon shas che ba spangs nas yan lag gtso bo rnams tshang ba'i yon tan lhag pa la brten par bya ste/ bya ba'i rgyud dpung bzang gis zhus pa las/
de lta'i yon tan ma lus ldan pa dag / rtsod pa'i dus na shin tu dkon pas na/ / yon tan phyed dam bzhi cha brgyad cha can/ / de lta bu ni sngags pa'i grogs por bsten/[616] / zhes snod rung mi legs par brtag cing /

The twelve years referred to means that if after examination you cannot come quickly to a decision, continue for a maximum of twelve years. If you are able to decide quickly, twelve years are not necessary. If it is not possible to find one with all the necessary characteristics complete, as taught in the tantras, then rely on one who has eliminated most faults and, with the most important branch qualities complete, possesses a predominance of good qualities. The action tantra called Tantra Requested by Subāhu states:
One with such qualities complete is very rare in this kaliyuga, so rely upon a mantra friend with half, quarter, an eighth of these qualities.[1091] Therefore, examine for worthy and unworthy vessels.

d.div: [616] sde dge_805_bka'/ rgyud/ wa 'phags pa dpung bzang gis zhus pa zhes bya ba'i rgyud/ le'u/ 1_shog_119_ba5
[1091] Subāhuparipṛcchā, chap. 1, Toh 805 Kangyur, rgyud, wa, 119b4.

f.d:
de yang slob ma'i skyon ni/ rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i rgyud las/
khro dang bcas shing rtog ger gus/ / na so dag ni yol ba dang / / gang yang dge slong dngos gnas dang / / zhen dang chags pas bcings pa la/ / rin thang med pa'i rin chen ni/ / de la bshad par mi bya'o/[617] / zhes dang /

On the actual faults of disciples, the Vajraḍāka Tantra states:
Those angry, too intellectual, too old, those who are actual monks, those bound by attachment and desire: jewels without worth, do not teach them.[1092]

d.div: [617] sde dge_370_bka'/ rgyud/ kha dpal rdo rje mkha' 'gro ma/ rim par phye ba so gnyis pa/ shog_70_ba1
[1092] Vajraḍākatantra, chap. 32, Toh 370 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 70b1.

f.d:
gsang ba spyi rgyud las/
ngag rtsub pa la spro thung dang / / gsod dang rku ba byed pa dang / / sdig pa'i grogs po spang bar bya/[618] / zhes dang /
gnyis spyod byed cing tshul 'chos pa/ / dad dang mi ldan brtson 'grus chung / / blo zhan nges med 'char la g.yeng / / bla ma spun zlar srid zhu chung / / de ni dbang gi snod min no/[619] / zhes sogs rgyas par 'byung la/

The General Rituals Secret Tantra states:
Leave behind those of coarse speech, of little enthusiasm, those who kill, those who steal, and false friends.[1093] Also:
Duplicitous, false ethics, little faith, little effort, a poor mind, uncertain, distracted, little respect for the master and his vajra brothers: such a one is not suitable for empowerment.[1094] There are many similar passages.

d.div: [618] sde dge_806_bka'/ rgyud/ wa gsang ba spyi rgyud/ shog_141_nas 167ba bar 'tshol zhib byed kyang rnyed son ma byung /
[619] sde dge_806_bka'/ rgyud/ wa gsang ba spyi rgyud/ shog_141_nas 167ba bar 'tshol zhib byed kyang rnyed son ma byung /
[1093] Sāmānyavidhiguhyatantra, Toh 806 Kangyur, rgyud, wa; but verse untraced.

f.d:
'o na slob ma mtshan nyid tshang ba ji lta bu zhe na/ rdo rje 'kha' 'gro las/
gang yang nga rgyal med pa dang / / sgyu med bdag tu mi 'dzin zhing / / de bzhin chos la mngon par gtad/ / de la man ngag byin par bya/ / gzhan du na ni ltung phyir ro/[620] / zhes dang /
dad dang ldan zhing brtson 'grus che/ / nyan nam slob la mi skyo ba/ / bla ma spun la bkur sti byed/ / de ni dbang gi snod yin no/[621] / zhes dang /

So what are the qualities of a true disciple? The Vajraḍāka Tantra states:
Without pride, pretense, with no clinging to self, entrusting self to the Dharma: to these impart the instructions; to others, a downfall occurs.[1095] Also:
Of faith and great striving, never tired of listening or learning, respectful toward guru and brothers: such a one is fit for empowerment.[1096]

d.div: [620] sde dge_370_bka'/ rgyud/ kha dpal rdo rje mkha' 'gro ma/ rim par phye ba so gnyis pa/ shog_70_ba2

[621] sde dge_830_bka'/ rnying rgyud/ ka de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gsang ba gsang ba'i mdzod chen po mi zad pa gter gyi sgron ma brtul zhugs chen po bsgrub pa'i rgyud ye shes rngam pa glog gi 'khor lo/ shog_344_na1
[1095] Vajraḍākatantra, chap. 21, Toh 370 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 70b2.
[1096] Found in Secrets of All Tathāgatas (Sarvatathāgataguhya). Toh 830 Kangyur, rnying rgyud, ka, 344a1.

f.d:
sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i rgyud las/
de dag sgom la dga' ba dang / / rtag tu bla ma la gus dang / / rgyun du lha rnams mchod pa yi/ / yon tan ldan na slob ma yin/[622] / zhes dang /

The Illusory Net Tantra says:
Taking joy in meditation, always respectful toward the guru, constantly making offering to the gurus: one with such qualities is a disciple.[1097]

d.div: [622] sde dge_466_bka'/ rgyud/ ja sgyu 'phrul dra ba zhes bya ba/ le'u/ 1_shog_95_na4_dge dang sdom la dga' ba dang //

[1097] Māyājālatantra, chap. 1, Toh 466 Kangyur, rgyud, ja, 95a4. Wording of first line slightly different in Degé, which states, “Taking joy in the vows and virtue.” The third line also has “deities” instead of “gurus.”

f.d:
mahA ma ya las/
yid gzhungs spro che byas la bzo/ / rigs btsun nga rgyal med pa dang / / gzugs dang lang tsho kha dog ldan/[623] / zhes dang /

The Great Illusion says:
Of intelligent mind, great enthusiasm, Of gratitude, from a good family, devoid of pride, good-looking, in the prime of life, of healthy complexion.[1098]

d.div: [623] ma hA ma ya zhes pa 'di sgyu 'phrul dra ba chen po yin nges pas lung 'di der 'tshol zhib byed kyang ma brnyed/
[1098] Untraced, but he is probably referring to the Great Illusion Tantra (Mahāmāyātantra), Toh 425 Kangyur, rgyud ’bum, nga.

f.d:
gsang ba snying po las/
dad brtson brtul zhugs rab rtogs nas/ / phan pa'i dbang sbyin nus pa'i dbang / / rim pa bzhin du sbyin par bya/[624] / zhes dang /

From the Essence of Secrets Tantra:
If possessed of faith, effort, conduct, insight, give the benefiting initiation, the power initiation, in order.[1099]

d.div: [624] sde dge_832_bka'/ rnying rgyud/ kha dpal gsang ba'i snying po de kho na nyid rnam par nges pa/ le'u/ 9_shog_120_na6
[1099] Guhyagarbha, chap. 9. Toh 832 Kangyur, rnying rgyud, kha, 120a6.

f.d:
rdo rje rtse mo las/
dkon cog gsum la dad dang ldan/ / sdig la 'jigs shing shin tu bsdam/ / dad dang dang ba phun sum tshogs/ / de la dam tshig sdom pa sbyin/[625] / zhes dang /

From the Vajraśekhara Tantra:
Belief in the Three Jewels, fear of committing wrong deeds, good discipline, faith, and pure joy: to such a one give the pledges.[1100]

d.div: [625] sde dge_480_bka'/ rgyud/ nya rgyud rdo rje rtse mo/ shog_163_na2
[1100] Vajraśekhara Tantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 163a2.

f.d:
bzhi brgya par/
gzur gnas don gnyer blo ldan pa/ / nyan po snod ces bya bar brjod/ / smra po yon tan rnam gzhan du/ / mi 'gyur nyan pa po la'ang min/[626] / zhes blo gzu bor gnas pa dang / blo tshad pa/ blo khog che ba/ blo brtan pa'o/ /

From Four Hundred Verses:
An unprejudiced, hard-working, and intelligent listener is a suitable vessel; other qualities will not be projected onto the speaker nor upon the listener.[1101] Therefore, the mind of a true disciple is unprejudiced, capable, brave, and stable.

d.div: [626] sde dge_3846_bstan/ dbu ma/ tsha slob dpon 'phags pa lha/ bzhi brgya pa/ rab byed / 12_sh+loka1_shog_13_na5
[1101] Āryadeva, Catuḥśatakaśāstra, 12:1, Toh 3846 Tengyur, dbu ma, tsha, 13a4.

f.d:
don gnyer che bas tshig bzung ba dang / don bsam pa dang / 'gal 'khrul sdebs te dri ba sogs brtson 'grus kyi lcag dang ldan zhing chos de nyid kyi tshig rtogs par nus pa'i shes rab zab pa/ gsal ba/ myur ba/ bde blag tu rtogs pa sogs blo gros kyi mig dang ldan pa'o/ / de yang rtogs par nus pa'i blo gros/ don du gnyer ba'i 'dun pa/ nga rgyal med pa'i gus pa dang ldan pa zhig dang / sgos bstan gso ba rig pa'i slob ma'i mtshan nyid ni/ tsa ra ka las/
blo ldan gtong mos byas pa bzo/ / brtse ldan chags bral dul la brtson/[627] / zhes dang /

With great endeavor he cracks the whip of perseverance in order to remember the teachings, contemplate the meanings, resolve all contradictions and errors, ask questions about them, and so on. He possesses the eye of intelligence, meaning he has an intellect that comprehends the words of the teaching profoundly, clearly, quickly, and without difficulty.
