He is someone with the intelligence to understand, the aspiration to work hard, and a respectful attitude devoid of pride. As for the qualities of the medical disciple the Caraka says:
Intelligent, happy to give, of gratitude, kindhearted, without desire, striving in discipline.[1102]

d.div: [627] tsa ra ka'i dpe cha lag tu ma son/
[1102] Untraced.

f.d:
dpa' bos yan lag brgyad par/
sbyin dang tshul khrims snying brtser ldan/ / tshangs par spyod cing byas pa bzo/ / byams ldan bcud kyi len ston na/ / tshe dang bsod nams 'phel ba'i sde/[628] / zhes gsungs pa dang ldan pa ni slob ma'i mtshan nyid la/ de las ldog pa'i snod dang mi ldan pa ni rjes su bzung bar mi bya ste/

In Eight Branches by Śūra:
Possessed of generosity, ethics, and compassion, of pure conduct,[1103] appreciative, and kindhearted, relying upon the elixirs, life and merit will increase.[1104] One with these qualities fulfills the definition of a disciple. One with opposite qualities is an unsuitable vessel and not to be accepted.

d.div: [628] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u/ 3_shog_118_na2
[1103] Tshangs par spyod pa, brahmacaryā; often refers to the chaste life of a religious student, or more specifically to celibacy.
[1104] Pitṛceṭa, Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhita, chap. 3, Toh 4310, gso rig, he, 118a2. Last line translated according to Degé.

f.d:
tsa ka ra las/
sdig can blo gros ngan pa can/ / sman pa'i gzugs brnyan de dag dang / / gtam 'brel par yang mi bya na/ / dngos su ston pa smos ci dgos/[629] / zhes dang /

In Caraka:
A bad person, of corrupt intelligence, a mere reflection of a physician should not even be spoken to, let alone taught.[1105]

d.div: [629] tsa ra ka'i dpe cha lag tu ma son/
[1105] Untraced.

f.d:
rta dbyangs kyis/
snod ngan gnas na 'phral du ni/ / ha la ha lar gyur pa yin/[630] / zhes dang / yang snying bsdus par/
bstan bcos nges pa mi shes shing / / tshig tsam la ni rjes gzhol ba'i/ / gshin rje'i zhags pa thogs pa bzhin/ / sman pa ngan pa ring du spang /[631] / zhes dang /

Aśvaghoṣa says:
Placed in a rotten vessel it immediately becomes poison.[1106] Also:
Not knowing with any certainty the treatises, absorbed merely into the words, holding in his hands the noose of Yama: cast far away this wicked physician.[1107]

d.div: [630] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u/ 40_shog_334_ba4
[631] sde dge_4310_bstan/ gso ba rig pa/ he_pha khol/ yan lag brgyad pa'i snying po bsdus pa/ le'u/ 40_shog_334_ba4

[1106] Pitṛceṭa, Essence of Eight Branches (Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhita), chap. 40, Toh 4310, gso rig, he, 334b4. The term for “poison” here (halāhala) in Sanskrit refers to the great poison spewed up by the churning of the ocean in the Vedic myth, and in Tibetan refers to the poisonous qualities of black aconite.

f.d:
man ngag khrigs sdebs gtad rgya'i skabs su/
slob dpon gsang zhing rang che 'byin pa dang / / thabs kyis rku zhing gzhogs slong byed pa dang / / g.yo sgyus 'gro ba'i nor la 'jab pa dang / / nga rgyal dregs pas bcings dang snying rje med/[632] / ces sogs dang /

Also, in the Final Tantra, in the section on entrusting the compiled teaching for safekeeping:
Keeping the master secret while promoting himself, stealing by stealth, making gains by flattery, deceitfully preying on the wealth of others, seized by pride and conceit, devoid of compassion.[1108]

d.div: [632] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 27_shog_665_yig phreng 17
[1108] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 27.665.17.

f.d:
bya ba byed pa sman pa'i le'ur/
de ltar mi ldan tha ma'i skyon/ / rigs brgyud med pa'i sman pa de/ / wa yis rgyal sa bzung ba ltar/ / kun gyis spyi bor bkur mi 'gyur/ /

In the Explanatory Tantra, from the above section on the activities of the doctor:
Not endowed with such qualities, possessing the faults of this lowest type, this doctor without a lineage, like a jackal that has seized a kingdom, is revered by no one.

d.div: gzhung don mi shes sman pa de/ / dmus long dag la rdzas bstan bzhin/ / nad rigs bcos thabs shan mi byed/ /
This doctor ignorant of scripture, like a blind person being shown various things, cannot discern various disorders and treatments.
mthong goms med pa'i sman pa de/ / rgyus med lam du zhugs pa bzhin/ / nad brtags dpyad la the tshom 'gyur/ /
This doctor without the familiarity that comes through observation, like one walking on an unfamiliar path, wonders about symptoms and surgical technique.
brtag thabs mi shes sman pa de/ / gnyen med byes su 'khyams pa 'dra/ / nad ngo shes pa gcig mi 'byung / /
This doctor who cannot diagnose, like someone wandering friendless in a foreign land, does not recognize a single disorder.
rtsa chu mi shes sman pa de/ / bya bas bya gtong mi shes 'dra/ / tsha grangs nad kyi skad mi ster/ /
This doctor ignorant of pulse and urine, like a messenger unable to carry a message, cannot articulate disorders as hot or cold.
kha smar mi shes sman pa de/ / gtso bos smra ba mi shes 'dra/ / rang skyengs grags pa ngan pa 'phog /
This doctor ignorant of prognosis, like a leader who cannot talk, is struck with embarrassment and a poor reputation.
bcos tshul mi shes sman pa de/ / mun khung 'bem la brdeg pa 'dra/ / gnyen po nad thog 'bab mi 'gyur/ /
This doctor ignorant of treatment techniques, like someone shooting at a target in the dark, his remedies never strike the disorder.
bzas spyod mi shes sman pa de/ / rang srid dgra la log pa 'dra/ / nad kyi stobs bskyed lus zungs 'joms/ /
This doctor ignorant of behavior and diet is like a king whose kingdom has become his enemy: the disorder grows in strength, the bodily constituents grow weak.
zhi sbyor mi shes sman pa de/ / so nam mi shes zhing pa 'dra/ / sman lhag log pas nad bskyed 'gyur/ /
This doctor ignorant of pacification compounds, like a farmer ignorant of farming, compounds wrongly, too little or too much, and the disorder merely increases.
sbyong byed mi shes sman pa de/ / bye mi'i ri la chu 'bebs 'dra/ / nad dang lus zungs ma rungs byed/ /
This doctor ignorant of purging techniques, like pouring water on a hill of sand: causing illness and harming the bodily constituents.
cha byad sman med sman pa de/ / go mtshon med pa'i dpa' bo 'dra/ / nad kyi dgra dpung choms mi 'gyur/ /
This doctor without surgical instruments, like a warrior without armor and weapons, cannot overcome the enemy of disease and its army.
gtar bsreg mi shes sman pa de/ / nang yan med pa'i rkun po 'dra/ / nad dang dpyad du 'dzol bar 'gyur/ /
This doctor ignorant of moxabustion and bloodletting, like a burglar without inside information, is confused about the disorder and the therapy.

f.d:
de phyir sman pa ngan pa ni/ / ci yang log par rtogs pa yis/ / gso ba lag po dag tu 'gyur/ / bdud nyid sman pa'i cha byad can/ / gshin rje'i zhags pa thogs pas na/ / srog gi gzu ba yin pa'i phyir/ / 'brel pa mi bya 'khor rnams 'phung /[633] / zhes dang /
de ltar skal med snod dang mi ldan na/ / chu srin gre bar rin chen tshud pa bzhin/ / bskal pa 'khrugs kyang kha ru mi dbyung gsang /[634] /

Therefore, such bad physicians with invariably erroneous ideas, their remedies are likewise erroneous; demons in the guise of physicians, holding the noose of the lord of death— they are the levers that topple the fortress of life. Therefore, have no connection with them, lest your circle of dependents be ruined.[1109] Also, from the Final Tantra:
To such a unmeritorious and an unworthy vessel— like a jewel in the throat of a sea monster, never emerging from its mouth though shaken for an age— it should remain secret.[1110]

d.div: [633] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 31_shog_99_yig phreng 8
[634] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ bshad rgyud/ le'u/ 27_shog_666_yig phreng 4_ma dper bskal pa 'khrugs kyang kha ru mi dbyung bas/ /zhes byung yang phyi ma'i rgyud ltar bcos/
[1109] Four Tantras, Explanatory Tantra, 31.99.8. “They are the levers that topple the fortress of life,” translated with the addition of “fortress” from Oral Transmission of Our Ancestors, 481b3.
[1110] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 27.666.4.

f.d: slob dpon las slob mas ji ltar nyan tshul/

d.i: How the disciple studies with the master

f.d: zhes gsungs pa ltar gyi skyon rnams spangs shing / yon tan de lta bu dang ldan pa'i slob ma de dag gis/ nyan pa'i tshul dngos la gnyis/ snod kyi skyon gsum spang ba/ 'du shes drug bsten pa'o/ /

With the above faults eliminated and the right qualities acquired, the way in which the disciple listens is described under two headings: 1. Eliminating the three faults using the analogy of pots 2. Developing the six recognitions
dang po ni/
Eliminating the three faults using the analogy of pots

snod kha sbub pa dang / kha gyen du bzed kyang mi gtsang ba dang / gtsang du zin kyang zhabs rdol na der lhas char phab kyang nang du mi 'gro ba dang / song yang mi gtsang ba sbags pas 'thung ba la sogs pa'i dgos pa mi 'grub pa dang / mi gtsang bas ma bslad kyang nang du mi gnas par zags nas 'gro ba'o/ / de bzhin du chos 'chad pa'i grar bsdad du zin kyang rna legs par mi gtod pa dang / gtad du zin kyang log par bzung ba'am kun slong skyon chags pa la sogs pa dang / skyon de dag med kyang nyan pa'i dus su bzung ba'i tshig dang don rnams brtan par ma byas par brjed pa la sogs pas nyams par gyur na chos thos pa dgos pa chen por mi 'gyur bas de dag dang bral ba dgos te/ de gsum gyi gnyen por mdo las/ legs par rab tu nyon la yid la zungs shig [635]ces tshig gsum gsungs pa yin no/ /

If one pot is upside down, another the right way up but unwashed, and another clean but leaky, even rain from the gods would not fall in to the first. If it fell into the second pot, it would become polluted and unfit for drinking, and so forth. It would remain clean in the third but would soon leak away. Similarly, the student may be present where the Dharma is being taught but not paying attention. He may be paying attention but understands it wrongly, his motivation is wrong, and so on. He may have been free of those two faults, but the words and the understanding gained at the time of listening were not embedded firmly in his mind, and he forgets them. If these and other similar failings occur, the great purpose of listening to Dharma will not be realized. Therefore, you should be without these faults. As a remedy for these three faults a sutra says, “Listen well, and take it to your mind.”[1111]

d.div: [635] sde dge_207_bka'/ mdo sde/ tsha glang po'i rtsal zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo/ shog_97_ba6
[1111] Girth of an Elephant Mahayana Sutra (Hastikakṣyamahāyānasūtra), Toh 207 Kangyur, mdo sde, tsha, 97b6.

f.d:
de yang byang sa nas/
kun shes par bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa dang / sems rtse gcig pa dang / rna blags pa dang / yid btud pa dang / sems kun gyis bsams nas nyan par gsungs pa ltar ro/[636] /

In the Stages of the Bodhisattva it says:
Listen with the desire to know everything, with a single-pointed mind, with attention on the teaching, with a mind of respect, and with the whole of the mind.[1112]

d.div: [636] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ shog_57_na1_lung 'di sde dge bstan 'gyur byang sa ltar bcos/
[1112] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 57a1.

f.d: Developing the six recognitions

sangs rgyas phal po che sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u bam po brgya dang bcu pa las/
rigs kyi bu khyod kyis bdag la ni nad par 'du shes bskyed do/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni sman pa'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni sman gyi 'du shes dang / nan tan nyams su blang ba la ni nad 'tsho ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/[637] / zhes bka' stsal ba bzhin 'du shes bzhi bsten pa la/

In the Flower Ornament chapter from section 110 of the Avataṃsaka Sutra:
Son of the family, develop the recognition of yourself as a sick person, of the spiritual friend as the doctor, of the teachings as medicine, and of conscientious practice as the cure for your illness.[1113] This teaches four recognitions.

d.div: [637] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a sdong po brgyan pa'i le'u/ bam po/ 17_shog_286_ba7
[1113] Avataṃsakasūtra, chap. 17, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 286b7.

f.d:
rang la nad pa lta bu'i 'du shes bzhag pa ni/ spyod 'jug las/
tha mal nad kyis btab pa yang / / sman pa'i ngag bzhin bya dgos na/ / 'dod chags la sogs nyes brgya yi/ / nad kyi rtag btab smos ci dgos/[638] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rgyun ring ba gso dka' ba sdug bsngal drag po bskyed pa'i nad chags sogs nyon mongs pas dus rtag tu na ba yin pas de la der ngo shes par byed dgos/

Recognizing yourself as a sick person is taught in Engaging in the Practices of the Bodhisattva:
If we must follow the advice of a physician even when afflicted with an ordinary illness, what need to mention when we are constantly afflicted with the manifold illnesses of desire and so forth.[1114] We need to develop this recognition because we are constantly plagued with mental afflictions such as desire that create dreadful and long-lasting sufferings difficult to cure.

d.div: [638] sde dge_3871_stan/ dbu ma/ la slob dpon zhi lha/ spyod 'jug /le'u/ 2_sh+loka54_shog_6_na3
[1114] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 2:54, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 6a3.

f.d:
chos smra ba la sman pa lta bu'i 'du shes bzhag pa ni/ dper na rlung mkhris la sogs pa'i nad tshabs po ches btab pa na sman pa mkhas pa 'tshol/ de dang phrad pa na dga' ba chen po skye ci zer nyan gus pas bsnyen bkur ba ltar chos ston pa'i bshes gnyen la'ang de ltar 'tshol ba dang rnyed nas khur du mi 'gro bar rgyan du 'dzin te ci gsung bsgrub cing gus pas bsnyen bkur bar byed pa ste yon tan rin po che sdud pa las/
de lta bas na byang chub dam pa 'tshol ba yi/ / bsam pa drag ldan mkhas pas nga rgyal nges bcom ste/ / nad pa'i tshogs kyis gso phyir sman pa bsten pa ltar/ / g.yel ba med par dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten par bya/[639] / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro//

Recognizing the Dharma teacher as the doctor is accomplished as follows. If we are seriously suffering from a wind disorder, a bile disorder, or some other ailment, and we set out in search of an experienced doctor. When we meet him we feel joy. We listen to what he says and respectfully minister to his needs. It is the same with the Dharma teacher. We seek him, and when we find him we do what he says and serve him respectfully, “wearing it as an ornament not as a burden.” In Bhagavān Jewel Qualities it says:
Therefore, by seeking the highest enlightenment, destroy the pride that comes from being learned with arrogance, and like the sick who depend on the doctor to be cured, devote yourself without distraction to the spiritual friend.[1115]

d.div: [639] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka 'phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa/ shog_13_na7
[1115] Found in Abridged Perfection of Wisdom in Verse (Prajñāpāramitāsaṃcayagāthā), Toh 13 Kangyur, shes phyin, ka, 13a7.

f.d: rjes su bstan pa la sman gyi 'du shes bskyed pa ni/ nad pas sman pas sbyar ba'i sman la gces spras chen po byed pa ltar chos smra bas gsung pa'i gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa gal po cher mthong nas 'bad pa du mas gces spras su 'dzin cing brjod pa la sogs pa'i sgo nas chud 'dza' bar mi byed pa'o/ /

Recognizing his teachings as medicine means that just as a sick person would cherish the medicine prepared for him by the doctor, you should recognize the teachings and advice given by the Dharma teacher as being of great importance, and go out of your way to cherish them and not let them go to waste by just forgetting them, and so on.

nan tan nyams su blang ba la nad 'tsho ba'i 'du shes bskyed pa ni/ nad pas sman pas sprad pa'i sman ma 'thungs na nad zhi mi nus par mthong nas 'thung ba ltar/ chos smra bas bstan pa'i gdams pa nyams su ma blangs na chags sogs gzhom mi nus par mthong nas nan tan gyis nyams su len par byed kyi nyams len med par rnam grangs mang po gsog pa'i tshig lhur mi len pa'o/ /

Recognizing conscientious practice as the cure of the illness means that just as the patient understands that if he does not take the medicine prepared by the doctor, the illness will not be cured, you should understand that without putting into practice the teachings given by the Dharma teacher, you cannot eliminate desire and so on. Therefore, engage in conscientious practice and do no pursue mere words, devoid of practice, just to build up a large collection of terminology.

de ltar na rang la nad pa lta bu'i 'du shes gal che ste/ de yod na gzhan rnams kyang 'byung la/ de tshig tsam du song na nyon mongs pa bsal ba'i phyir du gdams pa'i don mi bsgrub par nyan pa tsam zhig tu 'gyur bas sman pa btsal nas sman mi 'thung bar sman sbyor ba kho na lhur blangs na nad pa nad las mi thar ba dang 'dra ste/

In this way, seeing yourself as a sick person is very important. With that recognition the others follow. If this first recognition is nothing but words, you will not attempt to follow or put into practice the advice in order to eliminate the afflictions, and you will remain instead a mere listener. You will be like a sick person who searches out a doctor but does not take the medicine, for he only seeks the preparation of medicine; in doing so he does not recover from his illness.

ting 'dzin gyi rgyal po las/
mi dag na zhing lus ni sdug bsngal te/ / lo grangs mang por res 'ga' ma thar ba/ / de ni yun ring nad kyis nyon mongs pas/ / nad rnams gso ba'i phyir yang sman pa btsal/ /

The King of Meditative Concentrations Sutra states:
A person is sick and his body is in pain; for many years he know no relief. Tormented for so long by his illness, he seeks out a doctor in search of a cure.

d.div: yang dang yang du de yis btsal ba yis/ / sman pa mkhas shing rig pa des rnyed de/ / des kyang snying rje nye bar bzhag nas ni/ / sman 'di btang bar gyis zhes byin pa dang / /
Again and again he searches, and finally he finds a wise and learned physician, who takes great pity on him, saying, “Take this medicine,” and hands it to him.
sman mang bzang zhing phan pa de blangs nas/ / na ba 'tsho bar 'gyur ba'i sman mi 'thung / / sman pas ma len sman gyis ma nyes te/ / nad pa de nyid kyis ni nyes pa yin/ /
If he takes such excellent and beneficial medicine, he will be cured, but should he not take it, the doctor is not at fault, nor is the medicine; the fault lies with the patient himself.

f.d:
de bzhin bstan pa 'di la rab byung ste/ / stobs dang bsam gtan dbang po kun rig nas/ / bsgom pa la ni mngon par brtson mi byed/ / rigs par mi brtson ga la mya ngan 'da'/[640] / zhes dang /
ngas ni rab tu bzang ba'i chos bshad kyang / / khyed kyis thos nas yang dag ma spyad na/ / nad pa sman gyi rkyal pa thogs pa dag / bdag gi nad ni gso bar mi nus bzhin/[641] / zhes dang /

Likewise, having been ordained into this doctrine, having learned about all the powers, concentrations, forces, putting no actual effort, no proper effort into the practice of meditation, how will nirvana be attained?[1116] Also:
I teach this excellent Dharma but if you, having heard it, do not apply it well, you are like the sick person holding a bag of medicine unable to cure his illness.[1117]

d.div: [640] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da 'phags pa ting nge 'dzin gyi rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_27_ba4
[641] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da 'phags pa ting nge 'dzin gyi rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 4_shog_14_na5
[1116] Samādhirājasūtra, chap. 9, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 27b4.
[1117] Samādhirājasūtra, chap. 4, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 14a5.

f.d:
spyod pa la 'jug pa las kyang /
lus kyis 'di dag spyad par bya/ / tshig tsam brjod pas ci zhig 'grub/ / sman dpyad bklags pa tsam gyis ni/ / nad pa dag la phan 'gyur ram/[642] / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro//

In Engaging in the Practices of the Bodhisattva:
I will put these into practice, for what is achieved by mere words? Is merely reading the medical texts of any use to the sick person?[1118]

d.div: [642] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug /le'u/ 5_sh+loka109_shog_14_ba2
[1118] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 5:109, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 14b23.

f.d: des na nan tan la ni nad sel ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i nan tan ni/ bshes gnyen gyis gdams pa'i blang dor gyi gnas rnams la lag len du byed pa ste/ de yang byed pa la shes dgos shing / de la thos dgos pa dang thos nas shes par byed pa'i dgos pa'ang byed pa yin pas/ thos pa'i don la nus pa dang bstun pa'i lag len re gnad du che zhing /

The term “conscientious”[1119] in the line “Recognition of… conscientious practice as the cure of your illness” applies to putting into practice that to be cultivated and that to be discarded as taught by your spiritual friend. To do that you have to know these practices. To know them you have to learn them. Therefore, this term also applies to the necessity of learning and of gaining understanding from that learning. Therefore, adopting a practice that accords with your learning capacity is an important principle.

d.div: [1119] Nan tan: conscientious, earnest, careful.

f.d:
slob dpon dbyig gnyen gyis rnam bshad rigs par/
nga rgyal dang ni ma dad dang / / don du gnyer ba med nyid dang / / phyi rol rnam g.yeng nang bsdus pa/ / skyo ba nyan pa'i dri ma yin/[643] / zhes pa'i skyon rnams spangs shing / sgrub bya sems can thams cad gnas skabs su nad kyi sdug bsngal las skyob pa dang / mthar thug bla na med pa'i byang chub la 'god pa'i phyir/ gso ba rig pa'i gzhung lugs la thos bsam dang 'chad nyan byed snyam pa'i bsam pa bzang pos/ bla ma'i mdun drang por dma' ba'i stan la 'dug cing / dga' spro dang ldan pas yid dul ba dang / slob dpon dang chos la gus pa chen pos nyan dgos te/

Vasubandhu in his Science of Explanation says:
Arrogant, lacking faith and aspiration, distracted, withdrawn, and bored— these are the contaminants of listening.[1120] The true disciple has abandoned these faults. With the aims of protecting living beings from the sufferings of sickness in the short run and of bringing them ultimately to peerless enlightenment, the medical student holds the virtuous thought of wanting to study, contemplate, and teach the great texts of the medical tradition, and sits upright on a low seat in the presence of the master. There, with joy and a disciplined mind, he should listen with great respect for the teacher and the teachings.

d.div: [643] sde dge_4061_bstan/ sems tsam/ shi_slob dpon dbyig gnyen/ rnam bshad rigs pa/ bam po/ 4_shog_65_ba4
[1120] Vyākhyāyukti, Toh 4061 Tengyur, sems tsam, shi, 65b4.

f.d:
sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo las/
gcig tu dad cing gus pas chos mnyan gyi/ / de la 'phya zhing skur par mi bya'o/ / chos smra ba la mchod pa bya ba ni/ / sangs rgyas 'dra bar de la 'du shes bskyed/[644] / ces dang /

d.div: [644] sde dge_239_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_sa'i snying po'i 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_223_na5
[1121] Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra, chap. 7, Toh 239 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 223a5.

f.d:
skyes rabs su/
rab tu dma' ba'i stan la 'dug / dul ba'i dpal ni rnam par bskyed/ / dga' dang ldan pa'i mig gis blta/ / tshig gi bdud rtsi 'thung ba bzhin/ /
gus pa bskyed cing rtse gcig tu/ / rab tu dang ba'i dri med yid/ / nad pas sman pa'i ngag nyan bzhin/ / rim gro bskyed la chos nyon cig[645] / ces dang /
dus su 'tshogs shing bar ma chod/ / sdod sa 'dug lugs tshugs thub cing / / gus pas yid 'ong rna bar 'jug[646] / ces gsungs pa ltar dang /

In the Garland of Past Lives:
Sit on a very low seat, generate the serenity of a disciplined mind, gazing with eyes of happiness, drinking in the nectar of words.
Have respect and with concentration and a mind pure and joyful— like a patient listening to a doctor— show reverence and listen.[1122] Also:
Come together at the right time without interruption, sit still with firmness of purpose, and with great devotion welcome the teachings to your ears.[1123]

d.div: [645] sde dge_4150_bstan/ skyes rabs/ hu dpa' bo/ skyes pa'i rabs kyi rgyud/ so gcig pa/ shog_125_na1
[646] dus su 'tshogs shing bar ma chod/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1122] Aśvaghoṣa, Jātakamālā, no. 31, Toh 4150 Tengyur, skyes rabs, hu, 125a1.
[1123] Untraced.

f.d:
tshig don thams cad rna bar lhan cing / yid la bsam pa dang / ngag tu'ang zlos pa rim par bya dgos te/
yid gzhung tshig chod don go longs/ / me long med cing rtag tu sems/ / ma 'dres bar du zlos pa rem/ / 'dzin pa so so'i chos yin te/ / de las ldog pa spang bar bya/[647] / zhes bshad pa dang /
'o na sems gzhan du yengs pa dang / brjed ngas su gyur pa dang / sems dge sdig lung ma bstan had por lus pa rnams la/ chos kyi byin rlabs mi 'jug cing don med du 'gyur ba yin te/ brjed nges blo la rdo rje sems sogs pa/ / bde bar gshegs pa rnams kyis byin mi rlob/[648] / ces dang /

Every word should be heard, comprehended, and contemplated—and even repeated aloud—with concentration:
With clear mind ascertain the words and understand meanings and contemplate them constantly without laziness;[1124] until familiarized, repeat and concentrate. These are the factors for remembering teachings; abandon those which are their opposites.[1125] Also:
However, mind wandering off elsewhere, forgetfulness, vagueness on what are virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral minds— these do not receive the blessings of Dharma and render all as meaningless: Vajrasattva and other tathāgatas do not bless a forgetful mind.[1126]

d.div: [647] tshig don thams cad rna bar lhan cing / yid la bsam pa dang / ngag tu'ang zlos pa rim par bya dgos te/ yid gzhung tshig chod don go longs/ /me long med cing rtag tu sems/ /ma 'dres bar du zlos pa rem/ /'dzin pa so so'i chos yin te/ /de las ldog pa spang bar bya/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/

[648] 'o na sems gzhan du yengs pa dang / brjed ngas su gyur pa dang / sems dge sdig lung ma bstan had por lus pa rnams la/ chos kyi byin rlabs mi 'jug cing don med du 'gyur ba yin te/ brjed nges blo la rdo rje sems sogs pa/ /bde bar gshegs pa rnams kyis byin mi rlob/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1124] The Tibetan has me long (mirror) which seems strange. As the text is untraced, I have emended it to the more probable le lo (laziness). The whole verse is difficult to comprehend.
[1125] Untraced.
[1126] Untraced.

f.d:
spyod 'jug las/
sems gzhan g.yeng bas byas pa ni/ / de nyid rig pas don med gsungs/[649] / zhes pas/ sems gzhan du ma g.yeng bar chos kyi tshig don la spro ba gal che/ 'di ltar/ chos nyan du yod pa ni rnyed par dka' zhing / bskal pa du mar tshogs bsags pa las 'byung ste/

In Engaging in the Practices of the Bodhisattva:
That done by a wandering mind becomes meaningless, the knower of reality has said.[1127] It is very important to have great enthusiasm for the words and meanings of the Dharma devoid of any mental wandering. Listening to Dharma is a very rare occurrence and arises from eons of merit accumulation.

d.div: [649] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la slob dpon zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug /le'u/ 5_sh+loka16_shog_10_ba6
[1127] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra, 5:16, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 10b6.

f.d:
gsang ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i mdo las/
kye ma dad pa dang ni chos nyan pa/ / 'di 'dra bskal pa brgyar yang rnyed mi 'gyur/[650] / zhes dang /

The Sutra of Inconceivable Secrets says:
Alas! Faith and the listening to Dharma such as this will not be found in a hundred eons.[1128]

d.div: [650] sde dge_47_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ka gsang ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa bstan pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 5_shog_119_ba1 grogs po gang dag dad dang chos nyan pa/ /'di 'dra bskal ba brgyar yang rnyed par dka'//
[1128] Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa, chap. 5, Toh 47 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ka, 119b1. Degé has slightly different wording.

f.d:
rgya cher rol pa las/
gal te bskal pa khrag khrig tu/ / chos thob mi 'gyur srid pa ste/ / khyod kyis de ring rnyid zin gyi/ / bag med ma lus rnam par spongs/[651] / zhes gsungs pas/ lus ngag yid gsum bag dang ldan pa'i sgo nas chos nyan pa'i kun spyod rnams lhur len pa gal che zhing /

d.div: [651] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha rgya cher rol pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 26_shog_198_na2
[1129] Lalitavistarasūtra, chap. 26, Toh 95 Kangyur, mdo sde, kha, 198a2.

f.d:
de ltar thos pa'i phan yon kyang 'phags pa byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las/
dge ba dang ni sdig pa'i chos/ / ma thos par ni shes mi 'gyur/ / thos pas chos kun rnam par shes/ / thos pas sdig pa bsten mi byed/ / thos pas gnod pa spong bar byed/ / thos pas mya ngan 'das pa thob/ / thos pa 'dod pas thos pa 'phel/ / thos pas shes rab 'phel bar 'gyur/[652] / zhes dang /
thos pas chos rnams shes par 'gyur/ / thos pas sdig las ldog par 'gyur/ / thos pas don ma yin pa spong / / thos pas rnam par grol ba thob/[653] / ces pa dang /
mig ldan mar me yod gyur na/ / gzugs rnams mthong ba ji lta bar/ / de bzhin dge dang mi dge chos/ / thos pas rnam par shes par 'gyur/[654] / zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang /

As for the benefits of listening in such a way, the Bodhisattva Basket of Scripture states:
Virtuous and nonvirtuous dharmas— without listening you will not know them. Through listening you know all dharmas; listening you do not engage in wrong, listening you eradicate harmful acts, listening you pass into nirvana; wanting to listen, your listening increases, and listening increases your wisdom.[1130] Also:
Listening one comes to know Dharmas, listening one turns from the nonvirtuous, listening one eradicates the meaningless, listening one gains liberation.[1131] Also:
One with sight and a lamp sees forms. Similarly, through listening, one knows virtue and nonvirtue.[1132]

d.div: [652] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ kha byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod ces bya ba'i mdo/ le'u/ 11_shog_160_ba5
[653] sde dge_326_bka'/ mdo sde/ sa ched du brjod pa'i tshoms/ thos pa'i tshoms te nyer gnyis pa/ shog_228_ba2
[654] sde dge_326_ka'/ mdo sde/ sa ched du brjod pa'i tshoms/ thos pa'i tshoms te nyer gnyis pa/ shog_228_ba1
[1130] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, chap. 11, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, kha, 160b5.
[1131] Udānavarga, chap. 22, Toh 326 Kangyur, mdo sde, sa, 228b2.

f.d:
lung rnam 'byed las/
mang du thos pa la phan yon lnga yod de/ phung po la mkhas pa dang / khams la mkhas pa dang / skye mched la mkhas pa dang / rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba la mkhas pa dang / de'i gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa gzhan la rag ma las pa yin no/[655] / zhes dang /

Detailed Vinaya Presentations states:
Much listening has five great benefits: you will be learned in the aggregates, learned in the sensory realms, learned in the sensory sources, learned in dependent origination, and for giving teaching and advice on these, you will not have to rely on others.[1133]

d.div: [655] sde dge_3_bka'/ 'dul ba/ nya lung rnam 'byed/ bam po/ 71_shog_119_na7
[1133] Vinayavibhaṅga, Toh 3 Kangyur, ’dul ba, nya, 119a7.

thos pa gti mig mun sel sgron me yin/ / rkun po la sogs mi 'khyer nor gyi mchog / kun tu rmongs pa'i dgra 'joms mtshon cha yin/ / thabs tshul man ngag ston pas grogs gyi mchog / dpal dang grags dang gter gyi mchog kyang yin/ / ya rabs rnams dang phrad na skyes kyi mchog / tshogs kyi nang na mkhas pa dga' bar 'gyur/ / phal kyi rgol la nyi ma'i 'od dang 'dra/[656] / zhes dang /
dul zhing rab tu gsal ba'i spobs pa skye/ / grags pa chen po 'phral du 'byung bar byed/ / smra lce bde 'gyur khyad par can gyi rgyu/ / thos pa'i dpa' goms don gsal rtogs par 'gyur/ / thos pa ldan na 'gal ba med pa yi/ / 'khor gsum lam la rab tu gnas par 'gyur/ / thos pa'i rjes 'jug sgrub pa snying por byed/ / skye ba'i rdzongs las tshegs chung thar bar 'gyur/[657] / zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang /

d.div: [656] sde dge_4150_bstan/ skyes rabs/ hu_dpa' bo/ skyes pa'i rabs kyi rgyud/ so gcig pa/ shog_122_na1
[657] sde dge_4150_bstan/ skyes rabs/ hu dpa' bo/ skyes pa'i rabs kyi rgyud/ so gcig pa/ shog_122_na4
[1134] Aśvaghoṣa, Jātakamālā, chap. 31, Toh 4150 Tengyur, skyes rabs, hu, 122a1.

f.d:
rgyud bla mar/
gang zhig byang chub don du gnyer bas gser zhing nor bus spras pa ni/ / sangs rgyas zhing rdul mnyam pa nyid de chos rgyal rnams las rtag 'bul na/ / gzhan gang 'di las tshig tsam thos shing thos nas kyang ni mos na ni/ / sbyin pa las byung dge ba de las bsod nams ches mang 'thob par 'gyur/ /

From the Uttaratantra:
Should one person, striving for the highest enlightenment, offer constantly to the great Dharma king golden realms adorned with jewels, as many as atoms in a Buddha realm, and should another hear words from this treatise, and on hearing them take great liking to their meaning, the latter would bring much more merit than the virtue produced by the giving.

d.div: blo ldan gang gis byang chub 'dod pas bskal ba du mar yang / lus ngag yid ni 'bad pa med par tshul khrims dri med bsrung byed pa/ / gzhan 'di las ni tshig tsam thos shing thos nas kyang ni mos na 'di/ / tshul khrims las byung dge ba de las bsod nams ches mang 'thob par 'gyur/ /

Should persons of intelligence, wishing for enlightenment, protect effortlessly through their body, speech, and mind, and without the slightest taint, their ethics for many an eon, and should another hear words from this treatise, and on hearing them take great liking to their meaning, the latter would bring much more merit than the virtue produced by this guarding of ethics.

gang zhig 'di ni srid pa gsum gyi nyon mongs med 'byil bsam gtan ni/ / lha dang tshangs gnas mthar son rdzogs pa'i byang chub 'pho med thabs sgom la/ / gzhan gang 'di las tshig tsam thos shing thos kyang ni mos na 'di/ bsam gtan las byung dge ba de las bsod nams ches mang thob par 'gyur/ /

Should a person with the meditative absorption meditation that smothers the fires of afflictions of the three realms gain the realms of the gods and of Brahmā as a method to attain enlightenment without the process of death, and should another hear a few words from this treatise, and on hearing them take great liking to their meaning, the latter would bring much more merit than the virtue produced by this meditative absorption.

f.d: gang phyir sbyin pas longs spyod dag ni sgrub byed cing / / khrims kyi tshul khrims sgom pas nyon mongs spong byed la/ / shes rab nyon mongs shes bya kun long de'i phyir/ / 'di mchog nyid de de yi rgyu ni 'di thos yin/[658] / zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang /

d.div: Why is this? Giving produces wealth, ethics gains high birth, and meditation suppresses the afflictions, but because wisdom eliminates all afflictions and all obstructions to omniscience, it is supreme, and its cause is listening to this.[1136]
[658] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_rje btsun byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 5_sh+loka9_shog_72_na2
[1136] Maitreya, Uttaratantra, 5:9, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 72a2.

f.d:
ting 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo las/
yang dag ji bzhin mkhyen pa yin/ / sangs rgyas de bzhin gshegs pa yis/ / mang du thos pa'i legs pa ni/ / bcu po 'di rnams rab tu bshad/ / bcu po gang zhe na/ kun nas nyon mongs pa mi byed pa dang / gnod sems mi skye ba dang / the tshom rnam par 'byed pa dang / lta ba drang por byed pa dang / lam log pa spong ba dang / lam la gnas pa dang / mi 'chi ba'i sgor gnas pa/ byang chub tu bsnyen pa dang / sems can kun la snang bar 'gyur ba dang / ngan 'gro thams cad kyis mi 'jigs pa rnams so/[659] / zhes bya ba la sogs te rgya cher 'byung ngo / /

From the King of Meditative Concentrations Sutra:
The knower of reality as it is, the Tathāgatha Buddha, has taught that there are ten good qualities of much listening and learning. What are these ten? One will not engage the mental afflictions, one will not develop a harmful state of mind, one will separate from doubt, one’s views will become pure, one will abandon wrong paths, one stays on the path, one stands at the door of no death, one becomes closer to enlightenment, one shines among all living beings, and one is no longer frightened by the lower realms.[1137] There are many similar passages.

d.div: [659] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da_'phags pa ting nge 'dzin gyi rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_91_ba2
[1137] Samādhirājasūtra, chap. 9, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 91b2.

f.d:
de ltar yang theg pa'i go rim bzhin du phan yon che zhing / mthar nges pa'i don gyi gsung rab rnams thos nas mi skrag na de bas kyang phan yon che ste/ bskal pa bzang po'i mdor/
'jig rten khams 'di'i sems can gang su dag / de rnams thams cad byang chub bkod pa bas/ / gang gis phung po med pa'i tshig thos nas/ / skrag med de yi bsod nams khyad par 'phags/[660] / zhes dang /

There are great benefits of listening in accordance with the stages of the various vehicles, and finally if you listen to the definitive teachings and are not afraid, the benefits are even greater. The Sutra of the Good Eon says:
Greater than bringing to enlightenment all the beings of these world realms is the special merit of one who hears the teaching on no aggregates and is not afraid.[1138]

d.div: [660] sde dge_94_bka'/ mdo sde/ ka 'phags pa bskal ba bzang po zhes bya ba'i mdo/ le'u/ 2_bam po/ 2_shog_18_na5
[1138] Bhadrakalpika, chap. 2, Toh 94 Kangyur, mdo sde, ka, 18a5.

f.d:
mdo sdud par/
gang la shes rab pha rol phyin mchog mi dmigs shing / / byang chub sems dpa' mi dmigs byang chub sems mi dmigs/ / de skad thos nas rmongs pa med cing skrag pa med/ / byang chub sems dpa' de ni bde gshegs shes rab spyod/[661] / ces gsungs/ [336-7]

In the Abridged Perfection of Wisdom in Verse:
The supreme perfection of wisdom is not seen, the bodhisattva and the bodhicitta are not seen; those who hear this and are not confused, not afraid, are engaging in the wisdom of the Sugata.[1139]

d.div: [661] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa/ shog_2_na2_lung 'di mdo sdud pa ltar bcos/
[1139] Prajñāpāramitāsaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 2a2.

f.d: sde srid rang nyid kyis sman lag len du bstar tshul/
28. Chakri Medical College and the Author’s Own Practice of Medicine

de lta bu'i 'chad nyan dang rigs lam tshul bzhin du bskyangs ba dka' na'ang rang rtsom gyi bstan bcos dag 'chad nyan gyis gtan la 'bebs pa gtsor gyur rig gnas che chung gi grwa tshang lcags ri baiDUR+ya 'gro phan lta na ngo mtshar rig byed gling thog ma rgan pa kha shas la dpe 'dzin gyi bskul ma'i dge rgan bcol ba the ba'i sum cu skor dang / da lta je rgyas kyi gra ba bdun cur longs pa gsar du btsugs pa rgyud dang lhan thabs kyi rgyugs sprod dang tshogs mchod smon lam du sman rams pa byed mi yang mi nyung zhing / sngo sman gyi rigs chig rgyud yin nges rnams gza' skar dus la sogs pa dmigs bsal nges med du rang rang gi dam tshig dang bstun btu dgos pa dang /

Although it was difficult to nourish the development of such a teaching environment and methodical approach as described above, I nevertheless began the Chakri Vaidūrya Drophen Tana Ngotsar Rikjé Ling (Vaidūrya Sustenance to Living Beings, the Wondrous to Behold Center of Knowledge),[1140] a college for the major and minor sciences, with an education based on the works I have composed. The numbers in the beginning, including some senior monks appointed as memorization teachers, came to about thirty, whereas these days it has grown to about seventy monks. Examinations on the tantra and its supplements are held, and during the great offering and prayer festivals, many are conferred as Menrampa medical scholars. Those medicinal plants found in one-to-one lineages that lack any special stipulations of time, stellar, and planetary position, and so on, are collected according to each lineage’s own stipulations.

d.div: [1140] Lcags ri bai dūrya ’gro phan lta na ngo mtshar rig byed gling.

f.d:
byings phyi rgyud las/
btu dus rtsa ba yal ga sdong po gsum/ / sdong po'i rigs yin rus rtsa sha nad sel/ / ston ka rtsi skam dus su btu bar bsngags/ /

Generally, however, the Final Tantra says:
Roots, branches, and stems—all classified under stems— cure diseases of the bones, channels, and flesh. When the sap[1141] has dried in the autumn is the recommended time for collecting.

d.div: [1141] Rtsi, short for rtsi tog/thog, according to Surkhar Lodrö Gyalpo.
lo ma zho dang myu gu rnam pa gsum/ / lo ma'i rigs yin snod rkang lha nad sel/ / 'dab rgyas char gyi dus su btu bar bsngags/ /

Leaves, milk, and shoots—all classified under leaves— cure diseases of the hollow organs, marrow, and spirits. When leaves and petals are fullest in the rainy season is the recommended time for collecting.
me tog 'bras bu rtse mo rnam pa gsum/ / 'bras bu'i rigs yin mig don mgo nad sel/ / ston ser smin pa'i dus su btu bar bsngags/ /
Flowers, fruits, and tips—all classified under fruits— cure diseases of the eyes, solid organs, and head. During autumn winds, the time of ripening, is the recommended time for collecting.
skogs pa bar shun tshi ba rnam pa gsum/ / shun pa'i rigs yin lpags rgyas yan lag sel/ / kha 'bus dpyid kyi dus su btu bar bsngags/ /
Bark, inner bark, and resins—all classified under bark— cure diseases of the skin, fibers, and limbs. When buds appear in the spring is the recommended time for collecting.

f.d: bshal sman rtsi skams nus pa gting 'gro'i dus/ / skyugs sman kha 'bus gyen 'dren dus su btu/ / khyad par zla ba yar ngo'i dus bzang la/ / gtsang ma'i byis pa khrus byas mdzes par brgyan/ / gzungs sngags rten 'brel snying po bzla bzhin btu/[662] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rang rang gi dus dam tshig dang bstun te btus pa dang / dkyus ma phal che ba rnams sngar nas r-i Sh-i'i gdong du tshang che ba'i lo rgyus dang bcas 'thu ba'i rgyun snang ba 'gal cha cher mi 'dug pas lo star sman ngo dang sgrags yer pa nyang dogs nye kor gyis mtshon pa tshor btu bar btang / rang nyid kyis r-i Sh-i'i dus su long dang bstun rgyud sogs kyi lung dang de'i don gyi ngo sprod dag bshad ci rigs su byas pa sogs nas sman ngor mtshon na sngon chad gnyug mar gnas pa dang phyogs kyi sman pa rnams phal cher gyi sman ngo shes pa las 'dab 'gyur gyis mang ba sogs mu 'thud na gso rig gi bstan par 'phel rgyas 'byung nges su mchis kyang /

Gather purgatives when sap dries up and the force of the plant fades, and emetics when buds are drawn upward. Ideally, during the auspiciousness of the waxing moon, these should be gathered by a pure child, washed and adorned, while reciting mantra and auspicious words.[1142] Therefore, medicinal plants are to be collected according to various stipulations of time. Supported by traditional accounts stating that the majority of plants are ready during the time of the face of rishis,[1143] the usual collecting times for most ordinary medicines are not hugely contradictory. Therefore, each year students were sent out to gather as well as to identify medical plants from neighboring areas such as Drak Yerpa and Nyangdok. When I had the time, during the time of the rishis I gave, as appropriate, transmissions of the tantra and other works, and introductions to their meanings. All this has resulted in a significant contribution to the continuing growth of medical science. For example, the number of medical plants identified is more than twice the number previously identified by local and outlying doctors of the past. However,

d.div: [662] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ phyi ma rgyud/ shog_605_phreng 13
[1142] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 12.604.13.

[1143] The time of the rishis is either the first or the third month of autumn. According to Prof. Losang Tenzin, the “face of the rishis” may refer to the appearance of the rishi constellation in the night sky.

f.d:
yul 'khor skyong gis zhus pa'i mdo'i le'u dang po las/
ngo tsha khrel dang 'dzem pa bral ba dang / / khwa ltar spyi brtol che la rgod gtum zhing / / phrag dog nga rgyal rgyags pas 'tshig pa yi/ / dge slong dag ni nga yi bstan la 'byung /[663] / zhes snyigs ma las kyang ches snyigs pa'i dus gang zag cha lugs dge slong du 'chos pa bsam pa dang spyod pa khyim pa bas kyang ngan pa'i khrel 'dzem dang bral ba du ma 'byung ba dang /

as the first chapter of the Sutra Requested by Rāṣṭrapāla says:
Lacking modesty, consideration, and care, shameless like crows, coarse and uncultured, spiteful with jealousy, pride, and arrogance: monks like these will enter my doctrine.[1144] At a time even more degenerate than the age of degeneration, people dressed in the garb of fully ordained monks will have minds and behavior displaying a lack of shame and modesty even worse than lay men and women. The passage continues:

d.div: [663] sde dge_62_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga yul 'khor skyong gis zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 1_shog_240_na6
[1144] Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā, Toh 62 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, nga, 240a6.

f.d:
de dag khyim pa lta bur sogs 'gyur zhing / / 'tshog chas rnams dang g.yog 'khor mang bar 'gyur/[664] / zhes ngan spyod mkhan de rnams gzhan las longs spyod dang ldan zhing g.yog 'khor mang ba'i rgyus skye bo kun dad pa dang mos pa byed la/
gang dag tshul khrims dang ni yon tan ldan/ / chos 'dzin skye bo'i don la mngon brtson pa/ / dul zhing yang dag lam la gnas de dag / phyi dus sems can rnams kyis brnyas par 'gyur/[665] / zhes bag dang ldan pa'i chos la brtson pa dag nag phyogs la mngon par dga' ba'i lha rnams kyi mthus 'gro ba rnams kyi yid tu mi 'ong zhing brnyas thabs las dad 'dun mi byed par gsungs pas dper mtshon nas deng sang gi chos byed spyi la mtshungs pa ltar/

They will increase in number like the laity, with accumulated possessions, servants, and entourages.[1145] These people of sordid conduct, with their wealth and possessions gained from others and their many servants and helpers, will entice the people to have faith and a great liking for them. However:
Those with pure ethics and endowed with good qualities, who hold to the Dharma and work for the good of others and who are disciplined and abide on the perfect path, will in later times be abused by sentient beings.[1146] By the power of spirits who delight in evil, those who conscientously pursue the Dharma will no longer be attractive in the minds of others and, far from being objects of faith and aspiration, will simply become objects of abuse. Such an illustration has parallels in general to the practice of Dharma these days.

d.div: [664] sde dge_62_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga yul 'khor skyong gis zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 1_shog_241_na7
[665] sde dge_62_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga yul 'khor skyong gis zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 1_shog_241_na5
[1146] Ibid., 241a5. Degé wording somewhat different.

f.d:
lha rje yang sman pa'i rgyu drug tshang zhing sems can gyi don rgya chen po sgrub nus pa skyes sbyangs shes rab kyi rtsal dang ldan pa rnams rgyal po bka' chems las/
de tshe nag po'i phyogs rnams dar gyur zhing / / gang zag rnams kyi shes pa bsgyur nas kyang / / mi dge'i spyod pa sna tshogs byed par 'gyur/[666] / zhes dang /

For the great Lhajé physicians also, with the six causes of a physician complete, capable of vast accomplishments for the welfare of others, possessed of the innate or developed skills of wisdom, the King’s Chronicle Extracted from a Pillar says:
At that time evil forces will spread and change the minds of people, who will engage in nonvirtuous behavior.[1147]

d.div: [666] jo bo a ti shas gter nas bton pa/ bka' chems ka khol ma/ shog_280_phreng 13
[1147] Atiśa (revealer), 280.13.

f.d:
byang gter rang byung rang shar gyi lung bstan las/
tshe tshad lnga bcu kha ral gyi dus na bod du bdud dang 'gong po chen po pe har gyis byin gyis brlabs pa'i log chos spyod pa 'ga' yar 'byung /[667] zhes dang /

In the Teachings on the Self Arising Self Appearing from the northern Treasure tradition:
In the decrepit times when the lifespan is fifty years, there will come to Tibet māras and all kinds of wrong practices endorsed by the great spirit Pehar.[1148]

d.div: [667] byang gter dgongs pa zang thal dang ka dag rang byung rang shar gyi chos skor/ pod/ trAM_skye med ma bcos rang byung rang shar ba rin po che phrin las kyi rgyud/ khu_shog_6_ba5

[1148] Unborn, Uncontrived, Self-Arising Self-Appearing Precious Enlightened Activities Tantra, vol. khu, 6b4; from Unobstructed Enlightened Mind and Primordially Pure Self-Arising Self-Appearing Collection, vol. trāṃ.

f.d:
bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen po'i bka' las/
sngon byung gdon tshogs zad pa med pa'i steng / / gsar skyes dam sri dbyar mtsho ltar 'phel ba'i/ / dus 'dir [668] zhes stsal pa ltar rgyal 'gong dam sri sogs mtha' dbus 'dre ngan gyis rgyud bsgyur te shes bya spyi las kyang tshe'i rig byed 'dir blo mi 'jug par yon tan gzhan la mgo gtogs tsha ran lta bu'i slob sbyong sna tshogs byed pa dang / gal te lam 'dir blo zhugs nas tshul ldan yod rigs rnams kyang /

My guru the Great Fifth also said:
Alongside the never-ending demons of the past, the new hostile spirits of these times rise up like a lake in summer.[1149] Everywhere, demons such as pledge-breaking spirits and troublesome spirits are changing things, and people are turning away from this Āyurveda science of life even more than from the study of knowledge in general. They pursue their various other studies by merely nodding toward achievements and studying them as they would taste food to check saltiness.[1150] Even those who do engage in this field of study and conduct themselves properly suffer much harm and abuse and do not get the things they wish for.

d.div: [668] bdag gi bla ma lnga pa chen po'i bka' las/ sngon byung gdon tshogs zad pa med pa'i steng / /gsar skyes dam sri dbyar mtsho ltar 'phel ba'i/ /dus 'dir/ rgyal mchog lnga pa chen po'i gsung 'di gang las drangs ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[1149] Untraced.
[1150] In other words, barely studying at all.

f.d:
zla ba snying pos zhus pa'i mdo las/
dam pa'i chos ma nor bar spyod pa rnams la ni bskrun cing skur pa 'debs/ longs spyod dang yo byad nyung / nad dang 'tshe ba mang /[669] zhes pa ltar gnod pa dang 'tshe ba mang la 'dod yon sogs yid bsam ltar mi 'byung ba dang /

The Sutra Requested by Candragarbha says:
Those who unerringly walk the way of the sacred Dharma are slandered and disparaged. They have little wealth and few possessions and suffer much harm and illness.[1151]

d.div: [669] sde dge_356_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_'phags pa zla ba'i snying pos zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_217_na6
[1151] Candragarbhaparipṛcchā, Toh 356 Kangyur, mdo sde, ah, 217a6.

f.d:
sa paN gyis/
blun po'i drung na mkhas pa bas/ / spre'u 'dzin pa khyad par 'phags/ / spre 'dzin zas dang nor gyis mchod/ / mkhas pa lag pa stong par 'gro/[670] / zhes dang /

Sakya Paṇḍita says:
Fools hold the monkey entertainer in higher regard than the scholar. The monkey owner is showered with food and money; the scholar goes on his way empty-handed.[1152]

d.div: [670] sa skya paN+Di ta kun dga' rgyal mtshan gyi gsung 'bum/ tha_legs par bshad pa rin po che'i gter zhes bya ba'i bstan bcos/ rab byed gsum pa/ shog_5_na4_sa skya'i bka' 'bum pod lnga pa/ tha
[1152] Treasury of Wise Sayings, chap. 3, Collected Works, tha, 5a4.

f.d:
dpal mgon klus/
bzhad gad mkhan dang mkhas pa gnyis/ / blun la bzhad gad byed pa mchog / bzhad gad mkhan gyis nor rnyed kyis/ / mkhas pa nor med stang por 'gro[671] / zhes dang /

The glorious protector Nāgārjuna:
Of the joker and the scholar, the foolish hold the joker in higher regard. The joker is bestowed with wealth, the scholar goes without.[1153]

d.div: [671] sde dge_4329_bstan/ lugs kyi bstan bcos/ ngo mgon po klu sgrub/ shes rab sdong bu zhes bya ba/ shog_109_na7
[1153] Shoots of Wisdom (Nītiśāstrajantupoṣanabindu), Toh 4329 Tengyur, lugs kyi bstan bcos, ngo, 109a7.

f.d:
thams cad mkhyen pa bu ston zhabs kyis/
kye ma kho bo sngon gyi bsod nams dman/ / chos nub log chos dar ba bod kyi yul/ / blun po bkur zhing mkhas rnams rtswa ltar 'dor/ / chos ldan brnyas pa'i gangs ri'i khrod 'dir skyes/[672] zhes gsungs pa ltar mkhas blun dbye ba ma phyed pas 'gro don 'phrin las chung ba dang / zog po snying khams can bslab sbyong gi yon tan til 'bru tsam med pa rang nyid kyi sman 'thu ba dang sbyor ba'i lag len gang yang mi shes par man ngag gi sman gzhan las bslangs te nad brgya sman gcig lta bur sbyin rigs du ma'ang /
blun pos bya ba legs 'grub kyang / / stes dbang yin gyis bsgrubs pas min/[673] / zhes pa bzhin ltar snang 'phral gyi nad sogs dang thug ste 'phrin las kyi sgo bye ba sogs

The omniscient Butön also:
Alas, I have so very little merit, born in this snowy realm, this land of Tibet, where Dharma declines and wrong teachings increase, where those engaged in Dharma are abused, where fools are revered and scholars cast aside like grass.[1154] Not differentiating the fool from the true scholar has led to a lessening of beneficial activity for sentient beings. There are many who are deceivers at heart without an iota of the qualities that come from knowledge or learning, who have not the slightest idea of the practices involved in collecting and compounding their own medicines, but procure oral-tradition medicines from others and hand them out as if they were “one medicine to cure a hundred diseases.” These people may open the door of beneficial activity when they come into contact with minor illnesses that do not actually require treatment.[1155] However, as it is said:
Fools may accomplish good works, but it is by luck and not by design.[1156]

d.div: [672] bu ston rin chen grub kyi gsung 'bum/ dza lta ba ngan sel/ shog_31_na2_bdag ni sngon tshe las ngan bsags pa yis/ /chos nub chos min dar ba gangs ri'i khrod/ /mkhas smod blun po bkur ba'i kha ba can/ /chos ldan khyi ltar 'khyams pa'i bod 'dir skyes//
[673] sa skya legs bshad/ rab byed gsum pa/ shog_4_ba2_sa skya'i bka' 'bum pod lnga pa/ tha
[1154] Eliminating Wrong Views, Collected Works, dza, 31a2. Wording slightly different in Collected Works.
[1155] Ltar snang nad; a disorder that has the appearance of an illness and from which the patient will recover without treatment; one of the four types of disorder.
[1156] Sakya Paṇḍita, Treasury of Wise Sayings, chap 3, Collected Works, tha, 4b2.

f.d:
mdor na/ zla ba snying pos zhus pa'i mdo las/
nga'i bstan pa nub par nye ba'i dus dam pa'i chos kyi srung ma dag kyang mi dga' bar 'gyur te/ chos ma yin par spyod pa rnams ni sngon pas mthu dang stobs skye/[674] zhes dang /
de'i dus na chos la dga' ba'i lha klu rnams kyis sa gzhi bor te mi gnas shing / bdud kyi ris la sogs pa chos kyi bgegs rnams der 'byung ste/ chos ma yin pa mthu dang stobs skye bar 'gyur ro/[675] / zhes dang /

To summarize, the Sutra Requested by Candragarbha says:
During the period when my doctrine is drawing to a close, the protectors of the Dharma will also not be happy, and non-Dharma practices will increase in strength and power.[1157] Also:
During those times the gods and nāgas that delight in the Dharma will leave the land. Māras and other hinderers of the Dharma will take their place, and the power and force of non-Dharma will increase.[1158]

d.div: [674] sde dge_356_bka'/ mdo sde/ aH_'phags pa zla ba'i snying pos zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_217_na2
[675] gong mtshungs/ shog_217_ba1
[1157] Candragarbhaparipṛcchā, Toh 356 Kangyur, mdo sde, ah, 217a2.

f.d:
slob dpon ma ti tsi tras mdzad pa'i rtsod dus kyi gtam las/
da ltar rtsod pa'i dus na 'jig rten rnams la g.yo sgyu'i mtshon drag stobs dang ldan/ / bcud rnams sas 'thung dngos rnams stobs chung lha rnams char ni 'bebs mi byed/ / rlung rnams rab tu drag ldang lo tog rnams ni mi smin skye mi 'gyur/ / skyes la ser 'bab sa rnams rtsod pa'i dus kyis dbang sgyur 'bras bu med/[676] / ces sogs dang /
yon tan mkhan la mi bkur nor ldan rnams ni mchod bya min par mchod/ / skye rmongs mchod byed gshin rjes 'jig rten sdug bsngal nges 'khrid gang gis bzlog / tshul khrims 'chal ba stobs ldan tshul khrims ldan pa bsdigs shing tshar gcod byed/ / sdig la dga' ba'i stobs ldan g.yon can rnams kyis dam chos bsnub par 'gyur/ /
legs spyad brgya phrag dri yis bsgos pa yi/ / skal ldan nub cing dus ni 'das par gyur/ / gang na yon tan rnams kyi stobs phra la/ / yon tan la bdud 'bab pas gcod par byed/[677] / ces sogs mang ba dang /

In Tales of the Kaliyuga by Maticitra:
In the world in these Kaliyuga times, weapons of pretense and deceit are strong. The goodness of the soil is consumed by the earth, all natural materials lose their power, and the gods do not send the rain. Fierce winds blow, harvests do not ripen, and crops fail, while those that grow are struck by hail. Under the weight of the Kaliyuga the earth produces no fruit.[1159] Also:
Those with great qualities are not revered, whereas to the wealthy, unworthy of offering, confused beings make offerings. Yama is undoubtedly leading the world to suffering. How will he be stopped? Those possessed of the force of immorality threaten and wipe out those of pure ethics. The deceitful, with the power of their love of evil, will destroy the sacred Dharma.[1160] Also:
All good works smeared by corruption, the meritorious disappear, their time passes. Everywhere the force of goodness is weak; māras descend upon it and destroy it.[1161] There is much more of the same in this work.

d.div: [676] sde dge_4170_bstan/ skyes rabs/ ge_slob dpon ma ti tsi ta/ rtsod pa'i dus kyi gtam/ shog_192_na6
[677] gong mtshungs/ shog_192_ba1
[1159] Kaliyugaparikathā, Toh 4170 Tengyur, skyes rabs, ge, 192a6.
[1161] Ibid., 193a1. The line sequence is different in Degé.

f.d:
blon po bka' thang las/
lha yi khengs log byung tsa na: rdzun lung mkhan la yid ches gtod: dkar po'i phyogs de mun par 'gyur: zhes pa nas/
skyes pa'i snying la rgyal 'gong 'jug: bud med snying la bsen mo 'jug: byis pa'i snying la te'u rag 'jug:[678] ces sogs dang /

In the Chronicles of Ministers:
By the perverted pride of the deities, trust is placed in those with false teachings. The light changes into darkness. And so on until:
Troublesome spirits enter the hearts of men, demonesses enter the hearts of women, and air spirits[1162] enter the hearts of children.[1163]

d.div: [678] bka' sde lnga/ blon po'i bka' thang / phyi ma ci 'gyur ba'i skabs/ shog_517_phreng 21
[1162] The’u brang/rang. Type of spirit that flies through the air, or a kind of ghost (Great Tibetan-Chinese Dictionary, p. 1187).
[1163] Orgyen Lingpa, Five Chronicles, Future Occurrences chapter, 517.21.

f.d:
blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo las/
nag po'i phyogs la grogs ni brgya stong phrag kyang mang / / dkar po'i phyogs ni gang la'ang grogs por gcig pur 'gyur/[679] / zhes dang /

From Sutra Requested by Sāgaramati:
Though there be thousands of companions on the dark side, this is my sole friend on the bright side.[1164]

d.div: [679] sde dge_152_bka'/ mdo sde/ pa blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 2_shog_18_ba2
[1164] Sāgaramatiparipṛcchā, chap. 2, Toh 152 Kangyur, mdo sde, pa, 18b2.

f.d:
'phags pa na gA rdzu nas/
skal pa zad 'dod skye bo ngan pa bsten/[680] / zhes gsungs pa ltar/

Ārya Nāgārjuna states:
Devoting themselves to evil beings who seek the destruction of virtue.[1165]

d.div: [680] sde dge_4329_bstan/ lugs kyi bstan bcos/ ngo mgon po klu sgrub/ shes rab sdong bu zhes bya ba/ shog_105_ba3
[1165] Shoots of Wisdom (Nītiśāstrajantupoṣanabindu), Tengyur 4329, Tengyur, lugs kyi bstan bcos, ngo, 105b3.

f.d: spyir dus kyi snyigs ma lnga brgya'i tha ma/ sgos nag phyogs la dga' ba'i rgyal 'gong dam sri ma rungs pa rnams mthu che bas 'gro ba rnams 'khrul bcug ste log lam 'ba' zhig spyad pas bsod nams sam skal ba zad pas ma 'ongs par yid bsam dang mthun pa'i bstan 'gror phan slebs ma byung dogs/ rang ngos nas 'brum pa mched che ba snga phyi'i dus dang mchod sdong 'dzam gling rgyan gcig rten dang brten par bcas pa bzheng skabs bya ba las kyi 'khor lor gtogs pa'i 'go ba/ bzo rigs/ 'u lag yan chad du thang phye ril bu sogs phon ma chungs pa sbyar te sman byin rgya chen po bgyis/ lo star 'chi gsos bdud rtsi'i mdzod du zla ba nyi ma/ gza' skar/ 'phrod sbyor/ sa bdag la sogs pa zhib rtsis dang / khyad par klu rigs ldan dang bdud rtsi'i thun gnyis gtso bor bzung /

Therefore, during the period of the degeneration in the final five hundred years of the doctrine, and specifically when powerful malicious spirits arise who delight in the dark side and push living beings into the ways of error, where they will only follow wrong paths and diminish their store of virtue, there is great doubt that in the future the help and assistance needed for living beings and the preservation of the doctrine will transpire as wished. From my own side, I engaged in the extensive provision of medicine by compounding not-insignificant quantities of medical powders, pills, decoctions, and so forth for smallpox sufferers, who had increased in number over time, and for the supervisors and craftsmen, including laborers, who were involved in the construction of the central and ancillary structures of the Ornament of the World reliquary for the Great Fifth.[1166] Every year, for the treasury of death-destroying ambrosia medicine, I performed detailed calculations concerning the sun and moon, planets and constellations, their elemental combinations, land guardians, and so on. In particular the nāga and kulika and the two ambrosia periods are given prime importance.[1167]

d.div: [1166] The reliquary constructed for the Fifth Dalai Lama’s remains.
[1167] These are astrological calculations made for the purpose of determining auspicious times for medical procedures, compounding medicines, and so on.

f.d: rgyud dang lhan thabs su dngos su bshad pa dang shugs bstan chig brgyud kyi rigs sogs bsnan te 'ol spyi hol rgyugs ma yin par phra zhib kyi sbyor tshad 'degs kha tshad dang ldan pa lag tu bstar te sbyar/ ji ltar rang rang gi bshad khungs dang mthun pa'i rab gnas dang / so so'i nus pa bskyed byed kyi gzungs kha yar bzlas/

In accordance with actual instructions found in the tantra and its oral-tradition supplements, and aided by instructions received indirectly from various one-to-one lineages and so on, I measured, weighed, and compounded with great precision and great care various medical substances. I performed the consecration rituals according to the authoritative source for each of these compounds and repeated the individual mantras to develop their powers.

go sa'i stabs kyi slong mi la la dag lugs kyi bstan bcos las/
khral brkos pa na nor rtsis 'debs/ / 'gro dgos byung na nad bu ldang / / bza' btung mthong na nan gyis 'jug / dka' ba mthong na thabs kyis 'jol/[681] / zhes pa ltar gcong chen du khas 'tshe ba dang nad pa yin tshul gyi dgos dbang can kha shas dang / don la gnas pa'i gcong dang nad pa lha rje sna tshogs du mas sman dpyad ji snyed byas kyang bskyed med blos btang du thug nas ma gtogs thog ma nas slong ba po'i rigs mi yong 'dug cing / gang byung yang thos pa sgra rig gis brtag pa tsam las/ mthong ba yul rig dang spyod pa don rig gnyis ga'i sgo nas rang ngos kyis brtag ma thub pas nad babs dang lha rje 'dra'i brjod rigs la brtag nas rang blos tsha grang ha lam mi 'gal lam snyam pa kha yar gtad cing / tshur gtugs sogs ma byung yang bcos mtha' dag gis rdugs pa 'tsho byed kyi blos btang dang / dbul ba'i blta mi med rigs la phan nam bsams pa'i sman bskyel mi btang ba ji snyed nas/ dar mo sman rams pa dang skyid spe ba e pa lhun grub sogs mang bar bstan pa mi 'thon par kha smar gdags te bor bas 'chi bdag gi khar chud par nye ba lam pa bla ma sog po ngag dbang bstan 'dzin/ mo nad rtsa byer lha rje du mas ngos ma zin par bcos kyi phan pa lar ma byung ba dgung gseb nor lha sogs phan rngo thogs kyang re mang byung /

Of those who came to me begging for medicine because of my position, there were those who for some reason claimed to be chronically ill or feigned illness. As Wise Counsel says:
When taxes are levied, they count their wealth, when they have to go, they don’t feel well, when they see food and drink, they rush in, when they see hardship, they skillfully avoid it.[1168] Others who came begging were actually chronically ill, and some had received treatment from various physicians, but it had not worked and they were abandoned. They were not beggars from the beginning. No matter who they were, I examined them using only the question-and-answer technique, because I was unable to conduct visual or physical examinations through urine and pulse.[1169] Therefore, I looked at their condition and examined what other doctors had said, and satisfied my mind that their hot and cold elements did not seem seriously out of balance.[1170] For those who had been abandoned by their doctors because they had exhausted all treatments, and for the poor who had no one to examine them, I sent via messengers medicine that I thought would help them, even though they had not made contact with me first. I helped Lampa Lama Ngawang Tenzin from Mongolia. He had seen many doctors—Darmo Menrampa, Kyipewa, Epa Lhündrup, and others—who had examined him and made contradictory prognoses and then abandoned him, placing him almost in the mouth of the lord of death. I was able to help Gungsep Norlha, who was suffering with a particular menstrual illness that had gone unrecognized and was treated unsuccessfully by many physicians. These and other helpful treatments I have given.

d.div: [681] sa skya legs bshad/ rab byed gsum pa/ shog_5_na6_sa skya'i bka' 'bum pod/ 5
[1168] Sakya Paṇḍita, Treasury of Wise Sayings, chap. 3, Sakya Collection, vol. 5, 5a6.
[1169] Desi Sangyé Gyatso was a great medical scholar but, as Prof. Losang Tenzin points out, he was not a qualified doctor.
[1170] Rang blos tsha grang ha lam mi ’gal lam snyam pa kha yar gtad. I am still not sure if my understanding of the second half of this sentence is correct.

f.d:
gzhan yang tshogs mchod smon lam sogs kyi dus rig gling ba dang sman pa rnams la sman sbyar ba dang sbyor ba'i rgyu cha sprad de sman byin/ der ma zad nad pa'i don la 'gro nges kyi sman bzang drug sogs rin thang can slong mi gang byung la sprad pa sogs gzhung lugs dang 'gro ba'i don lhag bsam ston gyi zla ba ltar sgrubs pa ni/ gzhung lugs 'di gar yang /
nor dang srog la phang med gtong phod nus/[682] / zhes sogs rgyu drug gi nang dang /

During the offering and prayer ceremonies, I gave compounded medicines and the compounding ingredients to the medical college students and doctors. Also I gave to all those who requested a variety of precious medicines, such as the six excellent medicines,[1171] which are of definite benefit to the sick. I have developed, like the autumn full moon, an exalted state of mind that works on behalf of the medical tradition and of living beings. As it has been said in this literature:
Able and willing to give up wealth or life, with no sense of loss for either.[1172] This passage is from the section on the six causes of a doctor.

d.div: [682] sman gyi rgyud bzhi las/ phyi ma rgyud/ shog_666_phreng 10
[1171] Bamboo concretion, saffron, clove, nutmeg, small cardamom, and greater cardamom (Pasang and Clark).
[1172] Four Tantras, Final Tantra, 27.666.10.

f.d:
bya ba'i rgyud dpung bzang gis zhus pa'i le'u dgu par/
sems can nad kyis gdungs dang sdug bsngal la/ / rtag tu byams pa'i sems ni yid la bya/[683] / zhes dang /

Also, in the ninth chapter of the action tantra Requested by Subāhu:
Always place your mind in love for those living beings tormented by illness.[1173]

d.div: [683] sde dge_805_bka'/ rgyud/ wa 'phags pa dpung bzang gis zhus pa zhes bya ba'i rgyud/ le'u dgu ba/ shog_135_ba2
[1173] Subāhuparipṛcchā, chap. 9, Toh 405 Kangyur, rgyud, wa, 135b2.

f.d:
dkon cog ta la'i mdo las/
rgyal po blon po mdun 'don pho nya dang / / sman pa 'jig med bstan bcos cho ga mkhas/ / de dag dgon par ljon shing chen por 'gyur/ / sman dang rin chen mi zad gter rnams dang / / yid bzhin nor bu 'od 'byin sdong po dang / / lam gol dong pa rnams la lam ston 'gyur/[684] / zhes dang /

In the Jewel Lamp Dhāraṇī:
There will be kings, ministers, envoys, and fearless physicians, wise in text and practice, and they will be great trees in the wilderness, an endless supply of medicine and jewels, wish-fulfilling jewels, wish-granting trees, showing the way to those who lose the path.[1174]

d.div: [684] sde dge_145_bka'/ mdo sde/ pa 'phags pa dkon mchog ta la la'i gzungs zhes bya ba'i mdo/ shog_69_ba4
[1174] Ratnolkādhāraṇī, Toh 145 Kangyur, mdo sde, pa, 69b4.

f.d:
li tsa byi dri ma med par grags pas bstan pa'i mdo las/
nad kyi bskal pa bar ma la/ / de ni rtsi mchog dam par 'gyur/ / des ni sems can rnams grol zhing / / nad rnams med cing bde bar 'gyur/[685] / zhes dang / mkhas mchog dpa' bos phar phyin bsdus par/
'jig rten 'di dag rga shi med bstabs par/ / sman gyi mchog rnams grangs med sbyin par byed/[686] / ces gsungs pa ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa brlabs po che dag gi rjes su 'gro'am snyam mo//

The Liccavi Vimalakīrti Sutra says:
In the intermediate eon of illness, he becomes the supreme ambrosia, liberating sentient beings, restoring health, and bringing happiness.[1175] And in the Pāramitā Synthesis by the great scholar Śūra:
Bringing no aging and no death in this world, supplying countless stores of the best of medicines.[1176] In this way I think I have followed the great waves of bodhisattva conduct.

d.div: [685] sde dge_176_bka'/ mdo sde/ ma 'phags pa dri ma med par grags pas bstan pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_217_na2
[686] sde dge_3944_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_slob dpon dpa' bo/ pha rol tu phyin pa bsdus pa/ le'u/ 4_shog_220_na1
[1175] Vimalakīrtinirdeśa, chap. 7, Toh 176 Kangyur mdo sde, ma, 217a2.
[1176] Pāramitāsamāsa, chap. 4, Toh 3944 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 220a1.

f.d: mjug rtsom/
Conclusion
29. Dedication

smras pa/ ma rig las skyes nad do cog gi dgra bor bzhengs pa'i sman pa che mchog bcom ldan 'das/ gang gi bka' drin ye shes srog gi bdud rtsir 'thul bas nad med 'tsho ba'i dngos por grub pa yi/ / tshe yi rang bzhin ring po'i tshad du mthar phyin pa dang chos nor bde ba mtha' dag 'byung ba'i gzhi/ / kun shes rgyu yi rig kun rtser son yid can rjes 'dzin lus sems gso ba'i rig pa mchog de rgyal/ /[*]

Bhagavān, supreme physician, arising as the enemy of disease born of ignorance: from your kindness exalted wisdom arises as the ambrosia of life to produce the phenomenon of health, free of disease, the foundation for a life extended to its fullest, for Dharma, for wealth, and for all happiness; the peak of all sciences—causes for knowing all things, that cares for sentient beings, the supreme science for the healing of body and mind!

d.div: [*] bsam pa rgya che ba'i rgyan dang yan lag gnyis gzugs 'dres pa/

f.d: gang gi rang srol mchog tu dge ba tshul bzhin rtogs nas ma nyams 'dzin pa'i lhag bsam gyis/ / 'gro ba'i rgyud la lhan skyes zug rngu lus srog gnyis 'thungs sdig pas drag por khros pa'i so/ / dag pa'i snying stobs blo gros sor mos drungs nas 'byin mkhas gzhon nu'i mtshan sogs bla na med/ /[*]

Having fully understood its supremely virtuous doctrine, exceptionally virtuous minds work to preserve it without decline, their fingers of pure and courageous wisdom skillfully pulling out the fierce and angry teeth of the evil deeds that drink bodies and minds, causing the pain endemic to living beings. Those peerless beings—Kumāra[1177] and others,

d.div: [*] gsos dang gzhon nu gdong drug sbyar ba/

[1177] The whole dedication has annotations inserted in the text explaining poetical references. Here it states that this verse makes reference to the story of Kumāra pulling out the fangs of Gaṇapati.

f.d: khyad par gnang rigs rjes sbyangs sman pa'i tshogs la blo ldan gang zhig yid ni cis mi dad/ /[*]
especially the ranks of lineage and trained follower physicians— why would the intelligent not have faith in them?

d.div: [*] gzhon nu gdong drug gis tshogs bdag gi mche ba phyungs pa'i gtam dang sbyar gzugs/

f.d: rgyud don tshul bzhin rtogs pa'i blo gros nyin mo'i rgyu skar tshul bzung yang / / grags snyan longs spyod 'brug sgra tsam la 'tsho byed ming gi mngal brten pa'i/ / 'gro srog 'tsho 'chi ma nges som nyis tshod len byed pa'i gshin rje'i spun/ / sman pa'i rigs la dad pa'i 'gram chu rmi lam du'ang ldang ma yin/ /[*]

Their wisdom of comprehending the tantra exists like stars in the daytime, yet at the mere sound of the thunder of fame, reputation, and wealth, they are conceived in the womb of “physician in name alone.”[1178] On whether patients will live or die they are uncertain, riddled with doubt, merely guessing, these brothers of Yama: for such doctors, not even in dreams does the saliva of faith arise.

d.div: [*] 'brug sgra thos pa na rma bya mo rnams mngal 'dzin pa'i gtam dang sbyar ba'i dpe gzugs/
[1178] Annotation here states that the allegory is of the peahen who conceives at the sound of thunder.

f.d: phyogs lhung drag po'i chags sdang spang pa'i tshig don mtha' gcod dang / / lung rig tshad ma'i srang gis blang dor lci dang yang ba'i dngos/ / gzhal byar mi byed rang rang rmongs zhen pha yis gsol ba'i snod/ / kun la dga' ba'i dper mtshon chos 'byung mkhan rnams ngal gso mdzod/ /[*]

Not determining the meanings of texts free of the fearful prejudice of attachment and aversion, nor weighing the goods to be discarded or cultivated with the scales of scripture and valid perception: you writers of history, each preferring the cups used by their old father of blind partisanship, you can rest easy now.

d.div: [*] sngon byon gi gtam dang sbyar ba'i cha shas gzugs can dang nges bstan 'dres pa/

f.d: ka ye 'di na phyogs lhung ldem po'i ngag spangs shing / / 'phags bod la grags phyi nang lha dang drang srong gi/ / lugs kyi bka' bstan rgya mtshor rnam 'byed ded dpon che/ / mang thos grur zhon gso dpyad gting mtha' yangs pa'i khungs/ /[*]

Friends, here the crooked speech of prejudice is left far behind, with the navigator of investigative intelligence aboard a boat of great learning upon the ocean of Buddha word and commentary on the traditions of the outsider, Buddhist, Deva, and Rishi, greatly famed in the lands of India and Tibet, a vast resource plumbing the depths of medical science,

d.div: [*] ting nge 'dzin gyi yon tan dang ldan pa'i gzugs can 'dres pa/

f.d: lung rigs mi ldog drang srong dmod pa'i mtshon/ / tshe rig dbang po'i lus la lhungs pa'i mod/ / nges par dpyad pa'i gtam gyis 'khrul pa'i rma/ / dag pa'i mig bsgyur dpal ldan gso ba yi/ /[*]

not to be refuted by scripture and reason, the wound of error inflicted by the knife of the rishi curse piercing the body of the science of life, transformed immediately by incisive writing into a pure eye,

d.div: [*] brgya byin gyis drang srong gi chung mar log g.yems spyad pa'i gtam dang sbyar gzugs/

f.d: rig pa rgya cher dri ma med pa'i gnas/ / gangs can mtsho ltar shin tu zab pa'i khog / 'bugs pa'i legs bshad sngon med gzugs gsar pa/ / 'dzin pa'i baiDUR+ya'i me long che/ /[*]
this well-explained history of the glorious science of medicine, a vast and pure realm, deep as a Himalayan mountain lake, a great mirror of beryl reflecting a form never before seen,

d.div: [*] chos dpe dang lhan cig pa'i dpe gzugs/

f.d: nyes snyoms lus ngag yid kyi spyod pa dag / drang srong rnams kyang dgyes pa'i spyan ras zur/ / tshangs pa rang snang las mched bu mor bzhin/ / chags par byed pa'i dga' don 'di brtsams pas/ /[*]

its humors in balance, its activities of body, speech, and mind pure, pleasing even the rishis who from the corners of their eyes are attracted— like Brahmā to his daughter born from his own imagination. By the merit of composing this festival of joy,

d.div: [*] tshangs pa rang gi sprul pa'i bu mo thig le mchog mar chags pa'i gtam dang sbyar ba'i chos dpe/

f.d: mtha' dag 'gro ba'i tshogs kyi mig gi nad/ / phyogs lhung gdon gyis bskyed pa'i ling tog dag / lhag ma med phyis gzur gnas blo gros kyis/ / rtog cing dpyod pas zhib mor gzigs gyur te/ /[*]

I pray that the cataracts in the eyes of all beings, brought on by the demon of prejudice are erased forever, and that by examining and investigating with nonpartisan intelligence, they come to see clearly,

d.div: [*] yan lag gnyis gzugs dang bya ba mtha' gsal 'dres pa/

f.d: bde dang thar pa 'dod pa'i 'bab stegs che/ / rig lam nor bu'i khyim 'dir sman pa yi/ / rgyu yi khyad par rdzogs pa'i blo gsal rnams/ / gzhan la phan pas tshul bzhin rab zhugs shing / /[*]

and that those of clear minds with all causes of a doctor complete will enter this jeweled house of the path of the sciences, built on its foundation of desire for happiness and freedom, with the wish to benefit others.

d.div: [*] mi mnyam pa'am mdzes pa'i gzugs can dang bya ba mtha' gsal 'dres pa/

f.d: de yi mthu stobs drang srong skar mig gis/ / sbyin pa'i sgo nga rim bzhin smin pa las/ / 'gro mang 'dul byed ma ma dus min du/ / 'chi bas nyam thag bran g.yog las thar te/ /[*]
By its power may many beings be free— as the egg given by Rishi Tārakākṣa gradually matured, and Damayantī was freed from the lowly state of servitude when her mother died an untimely death—

d.div: [*] rgyal po gcig la chung ma gnyis byung ba'i 'dul byed ma'i gtam dang sbyar gzugs/

f.d: tshe yi gnas skabs mthar phyin dgung zla'i 'od/ / shin tu ches dkar chos nor bde ba yi/ / rab zhi bsim ba'i dpal ldan ga bur rgyun/ / rtag tu 'dzag pa'i yar ngor rgyu bar shog /[*]
and may they live their lives to completion, and the bright white light of the winter moon, with its glorious camphor stream of pacifying coolness of Dharma, wealth, and happiness, wax forever.

d.div: [*] mtha' dag gzugs can la sngon med gzugs kyis spa ba/

f.d: de sogs rnam dkar 'dis mtshon pha mes kyang / / srid zhi'i dngos grub rin chen dbyig gi char/ / 'bebs mkhas drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma mchog / sangs rgyas sems dpa'i tshul bzung lnga pa che'i/ /[*]

For my forebears, too, this virtue is dedicated. The false images drawn with the inks of ordinary provisional meanings in the form of wicked deeds, the faults and downfalls of my supreme root guru, the Great Fifth,

d.div: [*] bsam pa rgya che ba dang lhan cig pa'i yan lag gcig gzugs/

f.d: thun mong drang don tshon gyis bris pa yi/ / ltar snang sdig pa'i gzugs can nyes ltung rnams/ / dag ste bstan 'gror phan pa 'ba' zhig pa'i/ / bzhed dgongs rnam dag ji bzhin 'grub par shog /[*]

buddha in the guise of a bodhisattva, master in bringing the jewel rains of siddhis of samsara and nirvana: may they be erased, and may his pure wish solely to benefit the Dharma and living beings be fulfilled.

d.div: [*] gnyis gzugs dang bya ba bar gsal 'dres pa/

f.d: mgon de bsam bzhin mkha' spyod 'og min nas/ / dus babs bstan 'gro'i dris bzang ut+pal kha/ / 'byed phyir phebs pa drug pa chen po yi/ / nyin byed zhing 'di'i sgron mer zhabs brtan cing / /[*]

As the intention of this great protector was to blossom the sweet-smelling utpala lotus of benefit to doctrine and living beings when the time is apt, may the sun of the Great Sixth shine from the great sky realm of Akaniṣṭha as a light in this world forever.

d.div: [*] bsam pa rgya che dang gnyis gzugs 'dres pa la ting nge 'dzin gyi yon tan gyis spa ba/

f.d: gnam bskos gser gyi 'khor lo mkhar 'gro ba'i/ / grib mas dga' ba rdzogs ldan pho brang gi/ / chos srid bka' rtags nor bus mtshan pa'i gdugs/ / mi nyams srid pa'i tshad du 'khor ba'i mthus/ /[*]

With the shade offered by its golden wheel, heaven-ordained and arcing across the sky, may the parasol of the rule of the Palace of Completion of Joy[1179] adorned with jewel of sovereign authority never fall and remain for all existence.

d.div: [*] gcig gzugs dang lhan cig pa'i rigs rgyu/

[1179] Dga’ ba rdzogs ldan pho brang, which is usually written dga’ ldan pho brang (Ganden Podang), referring to the rule over Tibet established by the Fifth Dalai Lama. Ganden usually refers to the celestial realm of Tuṣita and is an alternative name for the Geluk (dge lugs) tradition and of course the monastery of the same name. By inserting rdzogs here, the author also offers the possibility of reading the term rdzogs ldan, which is a translation of the Sanskrit kṛtayuga (era of completion) or caturyuga (era of four), the first and best of the four eras. This is again referred to in the last line.

f.d: gangs kyi sa 'dzin ra bas khor yug ljongs/ / sdig pa'i shing rtar 'thul ba'i 'thab rtsod dang / / 'khrug pa g.yul 'gyed dal yams mu ge sogs/ / mi 'byung rdzogs ldan dus kyis 'tsho bar shog /[*]

By its power may this land ringed by snow mountains be free of civil strife arising as chariots of evil, of disturbance, wars, epidemics, and famines, and may all come to dwell in an era of completion.

d.div: [*] cha shas gzugs can/

f.d: tshul 'di lhag bsam stobs kyi byed pa po/ / bag chags 'chad rtsom smra ba'i sa ra yang / / gdug pa'i yid can mi dang mi min gyi/ / bar gcod dgra sde'i g.yul ngo las rgyal te/ /[*]
